articleTitle: MAPCON 2024 Breaker Page
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This work represents the Design of ML Assisted Reconfigurable MIMO Antenna for a 5G Application. Wide- band sensing modes are achieved by using all three PIN diodes in ON Condition and Varactor diode in Reversed biased OFF condition. Reconfigurable Communication modes are achieved by using a Varactor diode which is modeled as a Variable Capacitor and used to select the spectral holes. The suggested patch antenna has a small volume of 11.52 cm3 (120mm×60mm×1.6mm). The proposed patch antenna has a wideband sensing range 1GHz to 5GHz and a Reconfigurabil- ity range of 1.8GHz to 4.2GHz. S11 parameter is optimized using machine learning algorithms. In this study the S11 parameter of a reconfigurable antenna is calculated utilizing a frequency range of 1 to 5 GHz. To optimize the parameter, several ML algorithms are employed. Different algorithms are utilized in this study to compare the results, including To shorten the simulation’s iteration process, algorithms including decision trees, KNN, the Random Forest, and XGBoost ML is applied. Instruction and validation of these algorithms are done by using the CST generated data set. The outcomes of the KNN, and Random Forest are better than the XGBoost and Random Forest.

articleTitle: MAPCON 2024 Breaker Page
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Several clinical studies have shown hyperthermia (HT) as an effective adjuvant for standard cancer treatment modalities such as radiotherapy and chemotherapy. Selective tissue heating is achieved using water-cooled microwave antennas to improve power delivery during an hour-long HT treatment. Mechanical design aspects are often overlooked in the electrical design of antennas meant for HT. In this work, we present the design of water-loaded 434 MHz cavity-backed antenna using metal stamping process to address the mechanical design issues. The probe fed patch is modified as metal stamped antenna (MSA) for mechanical rigidity without compromising the near-field power coupling characteristics. A prototype of the MSA is fabricated and assessed on tissue equivalent phantom. The MSA has >95% power coupling to tissue at 434 MHz with 15 MHz bandwidth (‒10 dB), >85% tangential electrical field and specific absorption rate of 7.6 W/kg.

articleTitle: Microwave-based Safe Alternative for X-ray Scans for Pleural Effusion
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Pleural effusion and high water content abnormality in the lungs require either continuous monitoring or frequent monitoring. Conventional techniques, such as X-ray scans, pose safety concerns due to their ionizing nature. In this work, we propose a methodology combining a wideband high-gain antenna with a raster scanning technique for imaging high water content anomalies within the lungs. The low-profile antenna operates over a wide bandwidth of 2.98 to 6 GHz, including the 5.8 GHz ISM band. Enhancements to the raster scanning technique have been made to improve resolution and accuracy. The proposed methodology has been applied on a multilayer tissue model. Additionally, a comparison between microwave imaging and X-ray scans is presented, demonstrating the potential of the proposed technique for safely and effectively detecting high water content abnormalities in the lungs.

articleTitle: Design of Fully Integrated & linear PHEMT Voltage controlled Oscillator at 2240 ± 145 MHz
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: The design and development of a fully integrated monolithic microwave integrated circuit (MMIC) voltage controlled oscillator at center frequency of 2.2 GHz are presented here. The VCO was fabricated on a GaAs substrate with 0.25um-pHEMT technology from UMS foundry and is based on pHEMT-varactors in order to achieve a very small chip size. The VCO is designed especially for telemetry tracking and control applications at a frequency of 2.2 GHz. Realized buffered VCO MMICs deliver output power of 10 dBm at 2.2 GHz while consuming $228 m W$ DC power. The VCO has measured phase noise of -90 dBc at 100 kHz and $-113 \mathrm{dBc} / \mathrm{Hz}$ at $1 M H z$ offset from the carrier frequency. The VCO has a frequency tuning bandwidth of $\sim 12 \%(2.1 G H z-2.38 G H z)$ with a tuning voltage sensitivity of $290 \mathrm{MHz} / \mathrm{V}$ in linear region. The realized VCO has good measured Frequency pulling and frequency pushing characteristics.

articleTitle: Optimizing OAM Beams by Varying Refractive Index of Hemi-Spherical Dielectric Lens
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents the study on hemi-spherical dielectric lens to minimize the divergence angle and optimize the gain of orbital angular momentum (OAM) beam. An eight element Uniform Circular Array (UCA) antenna is designed to generate +2 and +3 OAM modes at resonance frequency of 5.2 GHz WLAN band. The refractive index of hemi spherical lens is varied to converge the beam direction of UCAs from $\pm \mathbf{2 8}^{\boldsymbol{0}}$ to $\pm 12^{\mathbf{0}}$ and simultaneously increases the directivity from 7.44 dBi to 14.4 dBi while maintaining side-lobe level below 15 dB for OAM mode +2. OAM mode +3 is not supported by dielectric lens of refractive index less than 1.5 and above refractive index of 1.5, the beam converges from $\pm 44^{0}$ to $\pm 16^{0}$ with the gain of 11 dBi.

articleTitle: Design and Fabrication of Out of Plane MEMS Actuator Driven by Lorentz Force
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents an out-of-plane micro actuator driven by Lorentz force achieving good vertical stroke on low resistivity silicon wafer. The actuator was made up of electroplated copper having a thickness of $1-1.2 \mu \mathrm{~m}$. A deflection of approx. $4 \mu \mathrm{~m}$ has been achieved with the magnetic flux density of 0.45 T and applied current of 1.4 A. The vertical deflection has a linear dependence on the driving current because the Lorentz force is proportional to both the driving current and the magnetic field. Simulated RF results of the switch with a similar configuration of the actuator show an insertion loss of $\mathbf{- 0. 8 4}$ at $\mathbf{1 0 0} \mathbf{~ G H z}$ and an isolation loss of $\mathbf{- 3 6. 8}$ dB at $93 \mathbf{G H z}$.

articleTitle: Fluid-Driven Pattern Reconfigurable Antenna With Cavity-Backed Slot
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This work introduces a novel cavity-backed slot antenna design operating at 10 GHz, employing a shorted monopole as the feed mechanism. The cavity structure is realized by integrating PLA (Polylactic Acid) posts filled with liquid mercury, enabling dynamic beam steering capabilities. By selectively emptying sets of eleven consecutive PLA posts, the antenna achieves 360 -degree scan coverage without any degradation in scanning efficiency. Furthermore, to enhance the antenna’s directivity, cone structures are integrated at the upper and lower extremities of the cavity. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed antenna achieves complete 360degree azimuth coverage with a directivity of 12 dBi. The proposed design is realizable and can be employed in various applications where beam steering is required such as communication and radar.

articleTitle: Wideband Highly Efficient Cross Polarization Converter based on Metasurface
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper introduces a bow-tie shaped reflective cross-polarization converter that demonstrates high polarization conversion efficiency (PCE) across a broad bandwidth. The suggested converter is designed to achieve a wide polarization conversion bandwidth of $75 \%(14.5-32 \mathrm{GHz})$ with over 90% PCE. The converter exhibits an ultrathin thickness of $0.07 \lambda_{0}$, at the lowest operating frequency. Detailed simulation and theoretical analysis of the converter is executed to validate the polarization conversion performance. A prototype comprising of $25 \times 25$ converter unit cells is fabricated and its characteristics are tested to verify the simulated results. The converter finds applications in K-band, and parts of Kuand Ka-bands.

articleTitle: Efficient Data-Driven Simulation of Microwave Interaction With Complex Plasma Profiles
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Microwave interactions reveal electromagnetic properties of complex materials like plasma that aid in under-standing plasma’s wide range of applications in manufacturing, aerospace, and more. The interactions generally comprise transmission, absorption, and scattering of microwaves with the dense plasma profile. Traditional computational methods face a challenge in simulating the complex interaction between the microwave and asymmetric plasma profiles due to the trade-off between the number of computations and the accuracy of the result, which encourages exploring other techniques. Data-driven deep learning techniques due to their ability to decipher hidden pattern from input data finds application in solving various advanced scientific/engineering problems. The technique has been applied to investigate complex microwave plasma interactions. The proposed deep learning model, trained on different asymmetric plasma profiles and corresponding scattered microwave E-field patterns, achieved 300-500 times faster and accurate predictions that are within acceptable limits. Thus, affirms the model’s applicability in accelerating future studies on plasma dynamics.

articleTitle: Non-contact RADAR-based Approach for Dielectric Material Characterization of Impure Water Samples
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This work introduces a non-contact Radio Detection and Ranging (RADAR) approach for characterizing the dielectric properties of water samples, aimed at chemical detection applications. Utilizing the TI IWR6843 RADAR module, the proposed method enables non-contact dielectric measurement-based material characterization. This approach establishes a foundation for the precise characterization of contaminated wastewater samples from the semiconductor industry, facilitating early detection of contamination levels exceeding acceptable limits to mitigate adverse health effects. By providing real-time dielectric characterization, this RADAR-based approach enhances the efficiency and effectiveness of chemical detection in wastewater, contributing to improved environmental monitoring and regulatory compliance in semiconductor manufacturing environments. The proposed system demonstrated significant improvements in detection sensitivity and speed compared to traditional methods, offering a novel solution for environmental monitoring.

articleTitle: Wideband Orthogonal Mounting Antenna design with Minimal Physical Footprint for 5G Smartphones
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A dual port antenna system with wide bandwidth and high isolation is proposed in this paper which works in the $\mathbf{5 G} \mathbf{m m W a v e}$ band. The individual array antenna is a simple series fed patch array with simple microstrip feeding with electrically small with dimensions of $3.73 \lambda \times 0.466 \lambda \times 0.046 \lambda$ at 28 GHz. It offers wide impedance bandwidth of 50% in the range 21 GHz to 35 GHz. The antenna system has two identical series fed patch array antennas each working in the mmWave frequency with an impedance bandwidth of 45.6% from 22 GHz to 35 GHz, offering high gain with high pattern integrity across the wide operating bandwidth. The system supports orthogonal mode of operation which ensures seamless data transmission irrespective of the phone’s orientation. The compact dimensions of the antenna system make it suitable for orthogonal panel mounting for portable handsets.

articleTitle: A Polarization Insensitive Wideband 1-Bit RIS Unit Cell Design Using Printed Dipoles
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: While designing reconfigurable unit cells for Reconfigurable Intelligent Surface (RIS) applications, polarization insensitivity and oblique incidence angle stability are two of the major challenges. As practical scenarios involve incident waves with any polarization, the RIS design must have identical behaviour for any polarization. In this paper, a PIN diode loaded dipole based design is explored to implement a one bit reconfigurable unit cell. The phase difference between the ON and OFF states is close to $\mathrm{1 8 0}$ deg. Four dipoles oriented along two diagonals ensure polarization insensitive behaviour. The reflection response of metasurface unit cell changes with the variation in incidence angle. Thus, a reflection response that is stable up to a high angle of oblique incidence is desirable for RIS unit cell designs. The proposed reconfigurable unit cell has a stable oblique incidence response up to $\mathrm{4 5}$ deg for both TE and TM polarizations over a wide frequency range from 3.57 GHz to 4.38 GHz.

articleTitle: Silver Nanowire based Highly Flexible Lightweight Optically Transparent Thin Film for EMI Shielding Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A flexible, optically transparent and lightweight silver nanowires (AgNWs) based thin film is demonstrated for the electromagnetic interference (EMI) shielding applications. The process involves the synthesis of silver nanowires with a length of $60 \mu \mathrm{~m}$ and a diameter of 169 nm using the polyol process. These AgNWs are then deposited on polyethylene terephthalate (PET) sheet via drop-casting to create a silver nanowire-polyethylene terephthalate (AgNWPET) layer. The resulting thin film forms AgNW networks with a sheet resistance ($R_{\mathrm{s}}$) of $70.73 \Omega / \mathbf{s q}$, which provides conductive paths for the EM waves in the specified frequency band thereby providing adequate shielding. This film is found to be quite effective as the EMI shielding layer, providing a total shielding effectiveness ($\mathrm{SE}_{\mathrm{T}}$) above 10 dB in the X-band ($8.2-10.5 \mathrm{GHz}$), for a thickness of only $100.8 \mu \mathrm{~m}$. The proposed AgNWPET film is also simulated using the CST Microwave Studio to optimize various parameters, and the measured $\mathrm{SE}_{\mathrm{T}}$ agrees well with the simulated results. The high aspect ratio (355) of AgNWs allows optical frequencies to pass through, thereby making it optically transparent. The proposed thin sheet is lightweight, highly flexible, and optically transparent, making it ideal for EMI shielding applications in the aerospace and defense industry.

articleTitle: Design, Development and Characterization of mm/sub-mm wave Receivers at 220-230 & 330-345GHz for radio astronomical applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents design, development and characterization of $\mathrm{m m}$ /sub-mm wave receivers at $220-230 \mathrm{GHz}$ and 330-345 GHz for radio astronomical applications. The receivers are designed for observing CO transitions from first $\mathrm{m m} / \mathrm{s u b}-\mathrm{mm}$ wave telescope of India, proposed to be deployed at Hanle, Himalayan region. The receiver comprises of Schottky-diode based RF front-end and Monolithic Microwave Integrated Circuit (MMIC) & Microwave Integrated Circuit (MIC) based IF back-end with two levels of down conversion. In first stage down conversion in RF front-end (FE), double sideband (DSB) configuration is followed whereas sideband separating (2SB) configuration is adopted in second stage down-conversion. Local oscillator (LO) signal at certain offset from band center aids in distinguishing the CO spectral lines in the lower side band (LSB) and upper side band (USB) after sideband separation. RF front-end comprises of Schottky barrier diode (SBD) based sub-harmonic (SHM) mixer at 230 GHz (WR- 4.3 interface) & 345 GHz (WR-2.8 interface) followed by IF low noise amplifier (LNA). The IF back-end receiver has side-band separation mixing circuit, amplification stages, filtering stages and electronic gain control circuitry. Measured results of both 230 and 345 GHz receivers demonstrate side-band separation better than 20 dB across the IF bandwidth.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of a Low-Profile Transmissive/Absorptive Rasorber for Ku-Band Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This article proposed a novel frequency selective rasorber (FSR) structure based on transmissive and absorptive for Ku-Band applications. The proposed FSR is printed on a polyethylene which has, flexibility, and robustness with a low dielectric constant (2.25). The presented FSR consists of two different designs printed on a single substrate, with lumped resistors incorporated on the top layer to achieve 100% absorptivity. Simultaneously, the bottom layer acts as a bandstop frequency-selective surface. Also, this configuration has a simulated transmission bandwidth of 9.54 GHz ranging from 13.04 to 22.58 GHz and an absorption bandwidth of 2.04 GHz ranging from 16.36 to 18.40 GHz. The proposed FSR exhibits polarization-independent characteristics, with a constant frequency response and oblique angles under the transverse electric (TE) incident mode. The presented FSR is suitable to utilization in radar target scanning, Ku-Band microwave imaging and modern 5G-mm wave.

articleTitle: Wide band reconfigurable salt water column antenna for RF communication
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Audio communication is tested in the frequency range (5 MHz to 4 GHz) over a distance of 56.3 m. Experiments are conducted at different salinity and height of salt water column to cover the frequency range. Salt water antenna is tested with two different base materials, Teflon and Acrylic. Salt water antenna is used on either side for transmission and reception of RF signal. Received signal strength is measured and heard using spectrum analyzer.

articleTitle: 200W Solid-state Pulsed RF Power Amplifier at S-Band
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper describes the design and performance of a 200 W solid-state pulsed RF (radio frequency) power amplifier, operating in S-band at a duty cycle of 0.1% and with a pulse width of $10 \mu \mathrm{s}$. The solid-state pulsed power amplifier has been configured with a series of 3 -stage cascaded power amplifiers with different RF output power levels at each stage. This paper also describes a new biasing scheme that has been developed for biasing the pulsed power amplifier. Also, the temperature stability of the integrated system has been recorded while keeping on the system for a long duration at room temperature and has been reported in this paper.

articleTitle: Multiband Jamming Waveform Design for Advanced GNSS Receivers and UAVs
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents the design of multiband waveforms for software-defined radio (SDR) based jamming applications. The proposed waveforms comprise frequency-swept continuous wave signals with band-switch properties. With appropriate in-band sweep rate and inter-band hop delay, the waveforms show a strong potential for use in agile jammers. As a use case, a dual (L1 and L2) and tri-band (L1, L2, and L5) waveform is designed for navigation receiver jamming working on L1 (1575.42 MHz) and L2 (1227.6 MHz) bands. The proposed waveforms are generated using GNU radio and a commercially available SDR. The jamming experiment shows the successful jamming of two different types of receivers: one with a ublox receiver working on both L1 and L2 bands and another on a DJI FPV drone working on L1 and L2 bands.

articleTitle: A Resistive ink based Circular Swastika-Shaped Radar Absorbing Structure for Stealth Application
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This study presents a design for a radar-absorbing structure that has a combo of circular and swastika-shaped surface designs capable of absorbing X and $K u$ bands. The structure has been created using a specifically developed resistive material with an outer layer resistance of $210 \Omega / \square$, while the substrate material used is Roger RO3003 laminate. A metallic plate (copper) has been used for the bottom layer. The proposed structure has been designed and simulated for its performance. The result showed a minimum of 10 dB reflection loss (90% absorption) over $8-20 \mathrm{GHz}$, covering X, Ku, and a portion of the K band. The structure has a fractionalbandwidth (FBW) of 85.71%, with a $0.102 \lambda R$ ($\lambda R$ is the corresponding wavelength to maximum reflection) intermediate layer thickness. The structure has angular stability of up to 50 degrees and polarization insensitivity of up to 90 degrees. The study also examines the performance of power loss and surface current distribution in the structure. It is slim in its architecture and can be fabricated using a customized surface resistive ink, making it an ideal candidate for the aero-stealth application.

articleTitle: Decoupling Dynamics in MIMO DRA: The impact of Metallic Sheets on H-Plane & E-Plane Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This article presents a novel technique that utilizes metallic sheets to improve the inter-port mutual coupling in dual-port multiple-input-multiple-output (MIMO) dielectric resonator antenna (DRA) systems. Two structures were analyzed: a MIMO setup with decoupled H-plane and E-plane. Utilizing metallic sheets can have a substantial impact on the distribution of the electromagnetic (EM) field within the dielectric resonator (DR). This results in concentrating the most intense EM energy in the adjacent slot, leading to a significant enhancement in inter-port isolation. By utilizing two DR elements and incorporating metallic sheets within the sidewall of the DR element, there is no requirement for additional footprints. This results in a compact and straightforward MIMO antenna setup. The results indicate that the H-plane decoupled MIMO configuration achieved a maximum inter-port isolation enhancement of around 21 dB, while the E-plane decoupled MIMO arrangement achieved roughly 20 dB of enhancement across the operational frequency spectrum.

articleTitle: Multiple Wideband Reflective Polarizer With Simultaneous Linear-Circular and Linear-Linear Conversion Ability for X to Ka-band Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A novel linear-circular and linear-cross reflecting types wideband polarization converter applicable for the X-Ka band frequency range is suggested in this article. A resonant electric dipole is printed on the grounded low-loss dielectric substrate and a circular patch that makes up the top metallic resonator in the polarizer’s unitcell. From 10.31-11.54 GHz, $\mathbf{1 2. 0 4 - 2 9. 5 6 G H z}, 33.26-40.69 \mathrm{GHz}$, and $41.75-43.78 \mathrm{GHz}$, the proposed converter executes linear-circular conversion with an effective $\mathbf{3 d B}$ axial ratio of $\mathbf{8 5. 3 3 \%}, \mathbf{2 0. 0 9 \%}$, and $\mathbf{4. 7 5 \%}$ fractional bandwidth, respectively. Furthermore, this design is capable of linear-cross conversion in three distinct frequency ranges: 11.56-12.03 GHz, 29.96-33.26 GHz, and $40.06-41.74 \mathrm{GHz}$, all with a $\mathbf{9 0 \%}$ polarization conversion ratio. Surface current distributions, which reveal the plasmonic resonances that generate the multiple conversions, are investigated to study the polarization conversion mechanism. The design’s performance is evaluated at various oblique angles under the Transverse Electric and Magnetic modes. With a total thickness of $0.041 \lambda_{L}$ and dimensions of 0.206 $\lambda_{L} \times 0.206 \lambda_{L}$, the proposed polarizer is modest in electrical terms. Here, $\lambda_{L}$ is the free-space wavelength at the lowest operational frequency. The proposed unitcell is ideal for real-time applications due to its distinctive compactness and polarization conversions; here is where the concept’s novelty resides.

articleTitle: Miniaturized RF Power Distribution Network for space borne SAR payload
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper discusses the miniaturization techniques adopted to realize a 1:256 Vertical & Horizontal polarization (V-pol and H-pol) Imaging and Calibration signal RF Power Distribution network for an space borne payload operating at X-band. The RF Power Distribution Network scheme employs a 1:4 Panel level distribution, 1:2 Tile level distribution, 1:8 Transmit Receive Integrated Block (TRiB) level distribution and 1:4 Transmit receive module (TRM) level distribution. For footprint weight and volume reduction, the Tile and TRiB distribution power dividers are realized in a vertical mounting configuration and the TRM level distribution is implemented in a vertically stacked configuration on a single 9-layer Low Temperature Co-fired Ceramic card housed inside TRiB package along with 4 V -pol and 4 H -pol TRMs.

articleTitle: 3D Printable GRIN Lens for C-band Circularly Polarized Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Circularly polarized (CP) antennas maintain consistent signal quality regardless of orientation and vital in wireless communication systems. However, increasing the size of array antennas to achieve a lower axial ratio poses challenges due to bulkiness and design challenges in the feed network. This study explores the design of a 4x4 CP antenna array using a diagonal corner truncation method, enhanced with a Gradient Index (GRIN) dielectric lens. The CP antenna array is designed with corporate feed network. The GRIN lens, which is 3D printing compliant, consists of five layers with varying infill densities obtained by phase equalisation method to achieve desired dielectric constants thus enhancing the antenna gain. The designed CP array with the feed network were executed by Ansys HFSS and lens slicing is performed using Ultimaker Cura software. Detailed design, mathematical modelling and unit cell analysis of the GRIN lens, along with performance results are discussed. In addition to this, performance analysis and a comparison of the Linearly Polarized (LP) and CP antenna arrays with GRIN lens is presented in this paper.

articleTitle: An On-chip Fractal Antenna using Defective Ground Structure for Compact RFIC Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Radio frequency integrated circuits (RFIC) are the vital component of electronic devices utilizing system-on-chip (SoC) architecture for communication. To make these devices truly wireless and miniaturized, an on-chip antenna (OCA) plays a significant role. This paper presents the design of a miniaturized OCA for Ku-band applications. In general, at lower microwave frequencies, to achieve efficient radiation characteristics from compact OCA is quite challenging. Here, the combination of DGS along with fractal design methods is employed to boost the antenna’s bandwidth (BW) to 7.22 GHz across the entire 12 to 18 $\mathrm{GHz}(\mathrm{Ku}-\mathrm{Band})$ range at center frequency of 15 GHz. The OCA is integrated within a compact area of $\pi 2^{2} \mathrm{m m}^{2}$ and reflects a gain and efficiency of $\mathrm{- 1 9. 7 6} \mathrm{dBi}$ and $\mathrm{5 5. 6 \%}$, respectively. Moreover, the outcomes of simulation and characterization of fabricated design display very good alignment together.

articleTitle: A Compact Wideband Polarized Insensitive Frequency Selective Absorber
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents a novel design of a polarization insensitive frequency selective absorber (FSA). Its unit cell features a modified Jerusalem cross metallic structure with a central square loop, printed on a dielectric substrate and backed by an air spacer and metal reflector. To enhance absorptivity, four lumped resistors are embedded within the FSS design. The unit cell has dimensions of $0.22 \lambda_{0} \times 0.22 \lambda_{0} \times 0.2 \lambda_{0}$, with a substrate thickness of $0.014 \lambda_{0}\left(\lambda_{0}\right.$ is the free space wavelength corresponding to the central frequency). The proposed absorber achieves a reflection coefficient ($S_{11}$) of less than −10 dB across the frequency range of 2.82 GHz to 8.41 GHz. It maintains an 100% absorptivity bandwidth under normal incidence when absorption is maintained more than 90%. The design is polarization-insensitive, lightweight, and compact, making it suitable for various applications in electromagnetic wave absorption.

articleTitle: Sun Inspired Tri-Band FSS based Absorber with High Angular Stability and Polarization Insensitivity Used for RF Energy Harvesting Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A compact and low profile FSS based absorber incorporating sun inspired geometry enclosed within a slotted rectangular ring is reported in this paper. The proposed triple layered(patch-substrate-ground) geometry yielded a closely spaced tri-band response centered at resonants 3.1 GHz, 4.2 GHz and 6.1 GHz with near unity absorptivities. The proposed meta cell exhibits four-fold symmetry leading to the structure being insensitive to change in polarization. The meta atom designed using the impedance matching theorem shows stable characteristics over a wide range of oblique incidence angle. The geometrical structure is designed in such a way so that it can be employed as a device for RF energy harvesting applications for the 5G and 6G technology which falls in the Sub Gigahertz.

articleTitle: A 5-18 GHz Medium Power Amplifier MMIC with High Gain for Electronic Warfare
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this work, the design and implementation of a broadband, high-gain medium power amplifier using $0.13 \mu \mathrm{~m}$ GaAs pHEMT technology in $\mathbf{5 - 1 8} \mathbf{G H z}$ frequency band is presented. The two-stage amplifier design uses feedback topology with a low quality (Q)-factor input/output impedance matching network. The measured performance shows a median gain $\gt19 \mathrm{~dB}$ and a minimum output power $\gt19 \mathrm{dBm}$ at 1 dB compression point. The achieved performance makes the circuit useful for electronic warfare applications.

articleTitle: Gain Enhancement of Substrate Integrated Waveguide based Cavity-Backed Slotted Planar Antenna Array using FSS Superstrate
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Substrate Integrated Waveguide (SIW) technology based rectangular cavity-backed slotted antenna and antenna array is designed to perform at 5.52 GHz in the dominant TE101 mode with an impedance bandwidth of 5.51 – 5.53 GHz. A simulated gain of 4.8 dBi is obtained with a reflection coefficient of -18 dB for a single element antenna. It is further modified to delineate planar antenna array operating at the same resonating frequency of 5.52 GHz. The reflection coefficient and simulated gain of –26.92 dB and 10.4 dBi is obtained for 2×2 planar antenna respectively. Frequency selective surface (FSS) is used as a superstrate on planar antenna arrays leading to an increase in the gain to 14.2 dBi. Antenna and FSS fabrications are done using Arlon AD270 and AD320 substrates respectively. Parametric studies on antenna gain and reflection coefficient are executed for better results. All the simulations are carried out using ANSYS HFSS v19.0.

articleTitle: Integrated Dual 8-port MIMO Antenna for Sub-6 GHz and mm-Wave 5G-NR Communications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this paper, an integrated dual 8-port substrate-integrated-waveguide (SIW) based MIMO antenna for sub-6 GHz and millimeter wave 5 G -NR communications is presented. Two 8-port MIMO antennas are incorporated efficiently on the same substrate. The overall dimensions of the proposed MIMO antenna is $\mathbf{9 2} \times \mathbf{9 2} \times \mathbf{0. 5 0 8} \mathbf{~ m m 3}$. The sub- $\mathbf{6} \mathbf{~ G H z}$ MIMO section of the proposed antenna consists of four square QMSIW cavity resonators (SQMSIW) and four triangle QMSIW cavity resonators (TQMSIW) arranged side-by-side that resonates at the frequency of 5.75 GHz. Whereas the millimeter wave MIMO section is nested inside central part of the sub-6 GHz section, which comprises of four SQMSIW cavity resonators and four rectangular patches which resonates at 28.4 GHz. The open-ended rectangular slots are loaded in both the SQMISW and TQMSIW cavity resonators in sub-6 GHz MIMO section to lower down their resonant frequencies that lead to the overall size reduction. The designed dual MIMO antenna possess the excellent port-to-port isolations (better than 40 dB) in both the operating frequencies of sub- 6 GHz and millimeter wave. The MIMO characteristics of the designed antenna are evaluated in terms of envelope correlation coefficient (ECC) and it is well below its acceptable limits

articleTitle: Investigation into Different Materials for Designing a Radome Wall for Airborne Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Radomes, are the protective enclosures serving as cover or shell for airborne radar antennas, to achieve structural integrity, environmental protection, and electromagnetic transparency. This paper investigates various materials suitable for designing radome walls in airborne applications and emphasizes the importance of selecting appropriate materials for radome wall design. We analyse the key properties of conventional materials, followed by exploring advanced options like composites and metamaterials. We discuss material selection based on factors like mechanical strength, electromagnetic performance, and cost. Finally, we highlight promising future directions for radome material development.

articleTitle: Multiband Antenna System based on Complementary-Ring Bethe-Hole Array as Superstrate
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A penta-band antenna system based on the concept of the complementary-ring Bethe-hole array is presented in this paper. The antenna comprises a monopole antenna element and a complementary-ring Bethe-hole array as a superstrate. An air gap separates the antenna and superstrate to achieve penta-bands with enhanced gain. A commercialgrade FR4 substrate is utilized for both the antenna and superstrate to achieve multiple bands at $4.67 \mathrm{GHz}, 7.11 \mathrm{GHz}$, 7.86 GHz, 9.92 GHz, and 12.02 GHz, with reflection coefficients of $-16.25 \mathrm{~dB},-14.78 \mathrm{~dB},-17.73 \mathrm{~dB},-29.78 \mathrm{~dB}$, and -13.91 dB, and gain values of $5.7 \mathrm{~dB}, \mathbf{2. 2 ~ d B}, 1.7 \mathrm{~dB}, \mathbf{3. 5} \mathrm{~dB}$, and 2.5 dB, respectively. The overall size of the antenna system is $28 \times 28 \times$ $11.305 \mathrm{~mm}^{\wedge} 3\left(0.436 \lambda_{0} \times 0.436 \lambda_{0} \times 0.176 \lambda_{0}\right.$ at 4.67 GHz). The proposed antenna system is eventually verified using the transmission line circuit model for C - and X -band applications.

articleTitle: Design and Eigen Analysis of Diagonal Tensor Based Holographic Metasurface Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A comprehensive eigen analysis and design procedure of a low profile, diagonally tensor meta unit-cell loaded Holographic Metasurface Antenna (HMSA) is discussed in this article. Using Irreducible Brillouin Zone (IBZ) theory, an effective tensorial surface impedance ($Z_{s u r f}$) is extracted for proposed diagonally tensor meta unit-cell. Furthermore, a linearly polarized HMSA (LPHMSA) is designed using axially sectored phase inversion method. Proposed LPHMSA, having an overall dimension of $12.5 \lambda_{0} \times 12.5 \lambda_{0}$ is composed with nonlinearly distributed $50 \times 50=\mathbf{2 5 0 0}$ diagonally tensor meta unit-cell. A single, highly directive beampattern towards ($\theta_{0}$, $\left.\varphi_{0}\right)=\left(0^{\circ}, 0^{\circ}\right)$ is realized with a peak gain $\left(g_{max }\right)=22.11 \mathrm{dBi}$. Proposed LPHMSA is operated at $f_{r}=25 \mathrm{GHz}$.

articleTitle: Elliptical shaped MIMO antenna with asymmetric fins for mmWave application
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In the proposed research, a compact 2 port MIMO antenna is designed for $n 257(26.5-29.5 \text{GHz}$) and $n 261$ (27.5 – 28.35 GHz) 5 G mmWave band. The proposed antenna is designed on Rogers 5880 dielectric substrate of size $51.75 \times 17.02 \times 0.79$ millimeter cube. The proposed design covers the 2:1 VSWR frequency band of 24.96 - 29.50 GHz with bandwidth 4.54 GHz and 3-dB axial ratio band of 28.86 - 29.32 GHz with axial ratio bandwidth 0.46 GHz. The gain is more than 4.68 dBi and radiation efficiency is more than $82.16 \%$ in the operating band. The peak gain is 5.58 dBi.

articleTitle: Broadband Time-Modulated FSS for C, X, and Ku Band Radar Countermeasures
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This article presents the design of a broadband time-modulated frequency selective surface (FSS) for radar countermeasures. The FSS operates in the C, X, and Ku frequency bands and is intended to deceive Doppler radar systems by mimicking the velocity of a moving target. The time-modulated FSS is meant to modulate EM waves that are reflected from it, resulting in the production of multiple sideband frequency components. This modulation occurs within the frequency range of 4.5 GHz to 19.3 GHz, with a fractional bandwidth of 124%. The modulation of the EM wave is achieved by altering the reflection coefficient of the FSS over time. The unit cell design of the time-modulated FSS being shown includes two layers. The top layer features a capacitive ring, while the middle switching layer consists of two PIN diodes positioned on each side of the layer. To achieve a time-varying reflection coefficient, a periodic biasing signal is applied to the PIN diodes. As a result of the proposed FSS, the sideband frequency components of the reflected waves exhibit greater power compared to the incident frequency component.

articleTitle: Wideband Compact Circularly Polarized Patch Antenna Array Using Non-uniform Metasurface
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A circularly polarized wideband non-uniform metasurface integrated $2 \times 2$ antenna array is designed for C-band applications. The wideband performance is achieved through the use of non-uniform metasurface. A sequentially rotated phase network is utilized for uniform power distribution in the $2 \times 2$ array antenna. Stubs are employed in patch design to enhance impedance bandwidth. The parameters of the antenna array are $1.24 \lambda_{0} \times \mathbf{1. 2 4} \lambda_{0} \times \mathbf{0. 0 7 3} \lambda_{0}\left(\mathbf{6 8} \times \mathbf{6 8} \times 4 {~mm}^{3}\right)$ at a center frequency of 5.5 GHz. Dual orthogonal feeds are used to generate circular polarization in the proposed antenna. As a result, the achieved bandwidth covers from 4.68 to 7.17 GHz in the C -band, with an axial ratio remains less than 3 dB over the range of 3.11 to 6.55 $\mathbf{G H z}$ and a peak gain of 13.03 dBic. Simulations indicate that the array exhibits right-hand circularly polarized radiation in the broadside direction, characterized by a symmetrical profile, minimal side lobe levels, and an 80% radiation efficiency.

articleTitle: Radar-Based In-Home Monitoring System for Supporting Aging and Wellness
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This study presents a novel approach to continuous, in-home gait analysis using Multiple Input Multiple Output Frequency-Modulated Continuous Wave (MIMO FMCW) radar, with a specific focus on step length and step count detection within naturalistic environments. Traditional gait monitoring methods are often intrusive and impractical for continuous use, particularly in personal living spaces. Our system was designed to address these limitations by enabling reliable, non-invasive monitoring of gait patterns in cluttered, real-world environments. The study is the first of its kind to successfully detect and analyze varying step lengths and counts in non-linear walking paths within a small apartment setting. The results demonstrate that our radar-based system can accurately capture step length and count with minimal error, offering a promising solution for autonomous, continuous athome gait monitoring. The experimental results demonstrate the method’s robustness in detecting gait parameters in a small apartment, highlighting its potential for long-term, nonintrusive monitoring of individuals at risk of falls or other mobility issues. This study marks a significant advancement in deploying non-invasive gait analysis systems in naturalistic home settings, with promising applications in healthcare, rehabilitation, and elderly care.

articleTitle: Plasma based Self-Reconfigurable Energy Selective Surface for High-Power Protection
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents an energy-dependent self-reconfigurable frequency selective surface (SRFSS) without an additional biasing network or tuning elements. The proposed FSS can switch the operation frequency with incoming high-power microwaves. The plasma technology is integrated into the FSS design to achieve this reconfigurability. The structure is designed to resonate at $\sim \mathbf{6. 0} \mathrm{GHz}$ during the plasma OFF (low power) mode. The resonance shifts to $\sim 3.0 \mathrm{GHz}$ In the presence of a high-power input, plasma ON mode, thus resulting in an independent reconfigurable performance. A prototype is fabricated and tested as proof of the concept, with a unit cell size of $0.15 \lambda \times 0.15 \lambda \times 0.012 \lambda$, which is ultra-thin and compact.

articleTitle: A 2-bit Reconfigurable Intelligent Surface with Wide Beam Steering Angles
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents a 2-bit reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS) with an aperture size of $4.4 \lambda_{0} \times 4.4 \lambda_{0}$ aiming for wide angle beam steering applications. The proposed geometry is based on a periodic arrangement of metallic patterns printed on an FR4 substrate, where a varactor diode is mounted between two rectangular patches in each unit cell for regulating the electromagnetic wave. An air spacer terminated with a ground plane is stacked below the dielectric substrate to obtain a high reflection characteristic. By carefully tuning the diode voltage across unit cell, four distinct coding states are generated with different reflection phase values $\left(-165^{\circ},-75^{\circ},+15^{\circ}\right.$, and +105°). Subsequently, a 2-bit RIS structure is designed from the phase profiles such that a normally incident plane wave can be reflected in specific directions, ranging from -50° to +50° at 4 GHz. The simulation result shows that the structure achieves angular reciprocity for the entire beam steering range and holds great potential for use in various 6G and future wireless communication networks.

articleTitle: Polarization Reconfigurable inverted F antenna for Multiband Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A polarization reconfigurable antenna having an inverted-F shape is proposed in this communication which is designed on an FR4 substrate and is simulated using HFSS. An RF switch, capable of changing the mode from linear to circular orientation and vice versa is used for this antenna design. By modification of the patch, it becomes an F-shape which was initially an L-shape. Being a basic layout, it gives an impressive result that its impedance bandwidth ranges from $2.72-3.51 \mathrm{GHz}$ (25.4%), 4.92-6.48 GHz (27.4%) and 8.23-10.78 GHz (26.8%) while the 3 dB axial ratio bandwidth ranges from $2.72-3.46 \mathrm{GHz}$ (24%), 4.95-5.98 GHz ($\mathbf{18.9\%}$) and 8.38-8.63 GHz (3%) which indicates that the antenna is circularly polarized and using the PIN diode as a switch it can change its polarization which has many real-life applications in the communication field.

articleTitle: Transparent and Flexible Wideband Polarization Conversion Metasurface for Aircraft Windows
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A transparent and flexible wideband metasurface featuring a reflective cross-polarization converter is proposed in this paper. The metasurface is designed with a singlelayered rectangular and circular-shaped resonator unit cell. The proposed converter achieved wide bandwidth from 8.48-22.76 GHz by combination of three adjacent frequency bands: ${1 0. 4 4}$ $\mathrm{G H z}, 15.06 \mathrm{GHz}$, and 20.52 GHz. The physical mechanism of the polarization converter is analyzed by using the surface current distributions. The proposed polarization converter is fabricated and a high polarization conversion ratio (PCR) $\gt97 \%$ is achieved across the entire operating band. Additionally, the metasurface maintains stable performance at incidence angles up to 60°. Additionally, a conformability of the polarization converter is analyzed with a curvature radius of 60 mm and achieved a PCR $\gt95 \%$ within the frequency range of 8.65 22.76 GHz. With these advantages, the proposed reflective crosspolarization converter is suitable for airplane smart windows system applications.

articleTitle: Few-shot Learning for Defect Classification from Terahertz Images using Siamese Network with Triplet Loss Function
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Terahertz imaging is emerging as a potential technique for the non-destructive testing of various materials ranging from traditional timber wood to highly advanced composite materials. The capability of THz radiation to penetrate through these materials to identify defects is the rationale behind this wide spectrum of applications. However, there are system-dependent limitations that restrict the image quality in the THz images. Hence, an artificial intelligence algorithm will be of greater significance in aiding in automatic classification and defect identification. However, to employ traditional CNN-based models for image classification, large image datasets are required. Typically, the THz image dataset is small, so few shot-learning techniques are attractive for these applications. Here, the authors have explored the defect classification in the THz images using a Siamese network, which learns to optimize the similarity metrics with a small dataset. Various distance metrics and loss functions have been attempted to optimize the model performance. The triplet loss function has been found to be the best, yielding better classification. Validation of the Siamese network has been carried out using two different small $\mathbf{T H z}$ datasets - one with defects in timber wood and the other with defects in GFRPs.

articleTitle: A 42 dB Gain, 16 W X-Band MMIC Power Amplifier with 46% PAE for Satellite Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper details the development of a X-band, high-gain ($\mathrm{4 2} \mathrm{~ d B \text {), }} \mathrm{1 6} \mathbf{W}$ output, class AB Monolithic Microwave Integrated Circuit (MMIC) power amplifier, which utilizes a $0.15-\mu \mathrm{m}$ gallium nitride (GaN) high electron mobility transistor technology (HEMT) grown on silicon carbide (SiC). It has been specifically designed for next generation SDR-based telemetry for satellite and nano-satellite applications. The amplifier, which consists of three stages, shows good performance in matching, gain, output power, stability and efficiency in the frequency range of $9.4-10.4 \mathrm{GHz}$. The device achieves a peak gain of 42 dB and a peak power added efficiency (PAE) of 46%, with a saturated output power of 42 dBm. The overall chip size is $7.41 \mathrm{~mm}^{2}$.

articleTitle: Alford Loop Inspired Phase-Gradient Metasurface Lens for X-Band Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Phase-gradient metasurface (PGMS) lenses have emerged as a promising technology in transmitarray antenna systems to satisfy the high-gain demands in modern wireless and satellite communication systems. PGMS use a spatial phase gradient to collimate the incident wave to enhance the gain of the system. In this work, a 4-layered slot type phase gradient metasurface lens separated by airgap has been proposed using a novel Alford loop inspired unit cell. The lens has been designed to operate at 11 GHz for X-band applications. The unit cell achieves a 360-degree phase variation by parametrically varying the arm length of the Alford loop. The performance of the lens-antenna system has been investigated by adjusting the position of the source antenna. The $13 \times 13$ metasurface measuring $155 \mathrm{~mm} \times 155 \mathrm{~mm}$ enhances the gain of the source antenna up to 18.7 dBi at 11 GHz with a 66-degree reduction in half-power beamwidth in the E-plane.

articleTitle: Miniaturized Circular Slotted Crossovers with Defected Ground Structures
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this paper, a novel Circular Slotted Crossover (CSC) with enhanced performance characteristics is proposed. The study aims to develop and harness the concept of incorporating symmetrical rectangular slotted patterns into planar circular patch crossovers. Additionally, it introduces intentional alterations in the ground plane to form a Defected Ground Structures (DGS), to further enhance crossover performance parameters. By utilizing the proposed technique, it is aimed to improve bandwidth, reduce insertion loss, and achieve a high level of isolation for existing circular patch crossovers. In the presented design, rectangular slots of same dimensions are introduced into both the signal and ground planes, facilitating ease of design and fabrication. The proposed method for augmenting crossover performance demonstrates that the presented device achieves a fractional bandwidth of $\mathbf{9. 3 5 \%}$, a miniaturization factor (Area $/ \lambda^{2}$) of 0.04, and an insertion loss of less than 0.6 dB, while maintaining an isolation of 25 dB or more across the entire bandwidth, surpassing most of the recent reported crossover configurations.

articleTitle: Fractal T-Square Antenna for Radar Application
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This article presents a T-Square fractal antenna with multiband characteristics. The radiator shape design is based on 2nd order T-Square fractal geometry. The multiband antenna exhibits three resonant frequencies $7.84 \mathrm{GHz}, 8.64 \mathrm{GHz}$ and 10.98 GHz. The inclusion of defected ground plane(DGS) technique that comprises a circular slit cut in the ground plane helps further to enhance impedance bandwidth. The achieved bandwidth is $7.74-7.96 \mathrm{GHz}, 8.49-8.83 \mathrm{GHz}$ and $10.72-11.14 \mathrm{GHz}$ respectively. An FR4 epoxy has a permittivity of 4.4 substrate is the foundation on which the radiator is embedded. In addition to it, coaxial feeding is adopted for excitation for best impedance match of $50 \Omega$. The dimension of the investigated radiator is 62 mmx 62 mmx 1.6 mm. The peak realized gain $4.76 \mathrm{dBi}, 5.43 \mathrm{dBi}$ and 2.04 dBi attained by the radiator at $7.94 \mathrm{GHz}, 8.64 \mathrm{GHz}$ and $\mathbf{1 1. 1 2 \mathbf { G H z }, \text { respectively. Therefore, this radiator is suitable for }}$ radar application.

articleTitle: A Multi-Functional Triple-band Reflection Type Polarization Converter
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this work, a triple-band reflection type polarization converter is proposed that converts a linearly polarized incoming wave into an orthogonal linearly polarized reflected wave in the frequency ranges of $6.3-11.2 \mathbf{~ G H z}$ and $16.2-17.6 \mathbf{~ G H z}$, while a circularly polarized reflected wave is obtained within the frequency range of $12.2-15.6 \mathbf{~ G H z}$. The performance of the polarization converter is studied experimentally by carrying out measurements on a fabricated $28 \mathbf{x} 28$ array of the $\mathbf{4 5}^{\circ}$ rotated Split Ring Resonator (SRR) structure. Additionally, a $12 \times 12$ array arranged in a checkerboard configuration is designed and integrated with a patch antenna to arrive at the design of a low RCS radiating system.

articleTitle: Cavity Backed Cross Dipole Dual Band (L1+L5 Band) Active Antenna for GNSS Reflectometry Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this paper, a cavity backed cross dipole antenna design at L-band integrated with active circuitry is proposed. The proposed RHCP design has complementary elliptical shape and are fed by ring shaped phase delay line for providing quadrature phase. A cavity with non-uniform fins have been used for enhancing front to back ratio. Active circuitry containing LNA, filters, DC-biasing network and lumped components is designed and integrated with an antenna, so as to enhance the Carrier to Noise ratio ($\mathrm{C} / \mathrm{N}_{\mathrm{o}}$). Active antenna has been tested with GNSS receiver and $\mathrm{C} / \mathrm{N}_{o}$ better than $40 \mathrm{~dB}-\mathrm{Hz}$ is achieved. Design and development of antenna, active circuitry and integrated active antenna are carried out and results are presented.

articleTitle: Design of an Inductorless Wideband Noise Cancelled Capacitor Cross Coupled Balun-LNA for Satellite Communication Application
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this manuscript a wideband noise cancelling inductorless and gain boosted low-noise amplifier (LNA) is reported. The design is based on common-gate-common-source (CG-CS) topology with capacitor cross-coupled (CCC) feedback for transconductance $\left(g_{m}\right)$ boosting and noise cancellation. The CCC topology enhances the $\boldsymbol{g}_{\boldsymbol{m}}$ of transistors which provides for an additional headroom for transistor sizing. The wideband matching is achieved by sizing the 65 nm MOSFETs. The gain is 19 dB across a 3-dB bandwidth of $0.5 \mathrm{GHz}-3.5 \mathrm{GHz}$; The Noise Figure (NF) is less than 4.6 dB; The power consumption is 1.87 mW with 1.2 V power supply; The input-referred third order intercept (IIP3) is 2.35 dBm.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of Logistic Impedance Taper for Distortion less Pulse Transmission
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Transmission line Impedance Tapers are critical components in signal transmission systems, aiding in impedance matching and minimizing signal reflections. In this work, we have proposed novel logistic taper lines which can be utilised for low-distortion pulse transmission. These tapers will help to transmit signals effectively with less ringing.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of a Conformal Series fed Microstrip Patch Antenna Array with Unequal Power Division and Delay Lines
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents a novel design and analysis method for a $4 \times 4$ Series-fed Microstrip Patch Antenna Array (SFMPAA) tailored for satellite launch vehicles, featuring a beam-shifting mechanism using transmission lines. The design incorporates Wilkinson’s unequal power divider to reduce side lobe levels, achieving unidirectional radiation patterns at 0 and 45 degrees with a progressive phase shift. The antenna array is conformed on a curved surface, enhancing aerodynamic efficiency and minimizing structural impact. With overall dimensions of $2.1 \lambda \times 3.2 \lambda$, the proposed SFMPAA yields a directive central beam $\left(\phi=\boldsymbol{\theta}=0^{\circ}\right)$ and a directive angular beam at $\phi=0^{\circ}, \theta=42^{\circ}$, with maximum gains of 16.06 dBi and 14.02 dBi at a frequency of 2.4 GHz.

articleTitle: A Modified Hexagonal Shaped Sub-6 GHz 5G Antenna in MIMO Configuration
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A line-fed Modified Hexagon shaped 2-port planar antenna is presented for 5G application. The MIMO antenna is designed through combining the techniques of a modifying the radiator and defected ground structure. In the MIMO configuration, two replicas of the MIMO element are arranged orthogonal to ensure the pattern diversity. A cross shaped structure is integrated with the ground to enhance interelement isolation. The size and operating bandwidth of the MIMO antenna are $28 \times 56 \mathrm{~mm}^{2}$ and 2.54 GHz to 5.46 GHz, respectively. This design advantageously offers a wide $\mathbf{- 1 5} \mathbf{~ d B}$ bandwidth from $3.3 \mathbf{~ G H z}$ to 5.0 GHz with a percentage bandwidth of $\mathbf{4 0. 9 6 \%}$ and a peak realized gain of 3.1 dBi at 3.3 GHz. Maximum isolation value of 33.55 dB is achieved while it is never less than $\mathbf{1 6. 8 5} \mathrm{dB}$ for the frequency of interest. The envelope correlation coefficient (ECC) ${\lt}0.003$, mean effective gain (MEG) ${\lt}\mathbf{- 3} \mathbf{~ d B}$, and diversity gain (DG) approaching to 10 have been achieved. The MIMO design is fabricated and experimentally tested for S-parameter analysis and the results matches satisfactorily. This antenna will be highly suitable for sub-6 GHz 5G communication applications in today’s world.

articleTitle: Design of Ridge Waveguide Based 16-Way Wideband Radial Power Combiner/Divider
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents design, simulation and implementation of a 16-way low loss wide band ridge waveguide based radial power combiner. The radial combiner comprised of three section transformer and coaxial to ridge waveguide transition. A three-section transformer is designed to match $\mathbf{8 0 0 0 h m}$ to 50 Ohm impedances. The designed transformer is radially arranged to build a 16-way power combiner/divider. The combiner uses a coaxial port with stepped impedance matching as a common port. Full wave 3D EM model is simulated using ANSYS HFSS. Measured results are in good agreement with experimental results. The designed radial combiner offers very low insertion loss of 0.3 dB and return loss better than 15 dB over 3.5 GHz to 6.5 GHz. The amplitude and phase imbalance of the combiner are within 0.35 dB and 2.5 deg respectively. The proposed design is suitable for high power wireless radio communication.

articleTitle: Development of Cryogenic Technologies and Systems for mm and sub mm wave receivers for Ground based Astronomical Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents details of cryogenic system envisaged and being realized for cooling of low noise millimeter (mm) and submillimeter wave receiver front-end components. Cryogenic system for ground based astronomical observation consists of a vacuum enclosure i.e. Cryostat, which will be evacuated using two stage vacuum pumping system, and a closed cycle mechanical cooler to achieve and maintain cryogenic temperature. Cryogenic system will cool the RF front-end components to $\sim 35 \text{K}$ and $\sim 100 \text{K}$, to reduce their thermal noise. This reduction in temperature of front-end components will provide a significant improvement in sensitivity of complete system enabling it to measure CO transitions in Milky Way and nearby galaxies. In addition to reducing the thermal noise, this cryogenic system also offers a very high reliability and stable operating environment for all components placed inside the vacuum enclosure.

articleTitle: A Circularly Polarized Wearable Antenna for X-band Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper introduces a geometrically simple, compact and flexible circularly polarized wearable antenna with bidirectional radiation characteristics for off-body communication in X-band. The proposed antenna is based on a simple microstrip feeding technique with a rectangular C-shaped parasitic strip which excites two orthogonal modes for circular polarization (CP). The proposed antenna maintains the axial ratio bandwidth (ARBW) below 3-dB within a wide range in the X-band by utilizing the combined asymmetric geometry of a straight feed line with a parasitic stub and a slotted ground, while also maintaining a compact footprint. The proposed structure has overall footprint of $\mathrm{0. 6 4 \lambda} \times \mathrm{0. 3 2 \lambda o}$ at the lower cut off frequency. The proposed antenna, achieves a 25% impedance bandwidth (IBW) from 9.8 GHz to 12.6 GHz and an ARBW of approximately $\mathrm{2 1. 0 5 \%}$ from $\mathrm{1 0. 2} \mathrm{~ G H z}$ to $\mathrm{1 2. 6} \mathrm{~ G H z}$. Within the CP radiation operating band, the realized gain is $\mathrm{3. 8}$ dBic. Experimental results closely align with simulations, validating the effectiveness of the proposed design.

articleTitle: Impedance Transforming Inline Bandpass Filter with High Selectivity using Internal and External Frequency-Variant Couplings
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this paper, a technique is introduced to design impedance transforming inline microstrip bandpass filters with high selectivity. The proposed technique is based on employing frequency variance in both internal and external couplings. The frequency-variant couplings allow creation of transmission zeros close to the passband increasing the filter’s selectivity. The external frequency-variant coupling topology allows the core filter structure to be matched to real or complex termination impedance values. Therefore, the proposed circuit can be used as an impedance transformer with highly selective bandpass filtering response. To validate the proposed technique, a third order filter with 50 Ohms input termination and 100-j100 Ohms output termination is designed and fabricated for $2.4-2.5 \mathrm{GHz}$ band. The measured return loss is better than 11 dB over 100 MHz of bandwidth with insertion loss better than 2.9 dB. The achieved selectivity factor, defined as the ratio of the 3-dBc to $20-\mathrm{dBc}$ bandwidths, is $\mathbf{0. 6 7 9}$ providing $20-\mathrm{dB}$ roll-off rates higher than $360 \mathrm{~dB} / \mathrm{GHz}$ at the band edges. The size of the filter prototype is 0.36 by 0.25 times the wavelength at the center frequency.

articleTitle: Polarization Agile Multibeam Holographic Metasurface Antenna with Variable Excitation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A dual beam, polarization agile holographic metasurface based leaky-wave antenna (HMA) is reported in this article. The location of primary phase center (i.e. excitation point) is optimized meticulously to obtain the polarization agility into dual beam pattern. A brief and compact study on the modulation of polarization state and beam pattern are portrayed in this work. Proposed HMAs contain $60 \times 60=3600$ metaunit-cells with an overall surface dimension of $15.5 \lambda_{0} \times 15.5 \lambda_{0}$. Both center and diagonally, near edge fed HMA is designed and beam pattern characteristics are compared in this work. Dual beam pattern towards $\left(\theta_{n}, \varphi_{n}\right)=\left\{\left(-30^{\circ}, 0^{\circ}\right)\right.$ $\left.;\left(30^{\circ}, 0^{\circ}\right)\right\}$ is obtained with polarization agility. Proposed HMAs exhibit an average gain $g_{\text {avg }}=21.3 \mathrm{dBi}$ for each beam pattern at $f_{r}=15.5 \mathrm{GHz}$. Sufficient simulated results are compared and discussed in this article.

articleTitle: Design of a Power Amplifier with Enhanced Power Added Efficiency using GaN at 60 GHz
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A highly efficient power amplifier is a critical component of an RF transmitter, particularly at higher frequencies, where gain and efficiency decrease due to noise. The primary objective of this research is to design an efficient power amplifier (PA) with improved Power-Added Efficiency (PAE) for V Band ($40-75 \mathrm{GHz}$) applications at 60 GHz using Gallium Nitrate (GaN) substrate. The high-frequency parameters of GaN device are extracted through circuit design and analyzed. In PA design, the driver stage utilizes a common-source configuration to boost output power using single-stage contours. The load stage employs back-to-back MOS connections to maximize output. A class AB power amplifier is chosen for its superior power efficiency and improved linearity. The results conclude that the proposed GaN device is suitable for V-band applications as it can withstand very high voltages without breakdown and thus yield high power. The obtained PAE for GaN PA is 32.2% which reflects its effectiveness compared to some of the previously reported works of literature. Moreover, the results are compared with the CMOS-based PA model designed for the 60 GHz frequency, and the proposed GaN design demonstrates an excellent improvement in PAE by $\mathbf{1 1. 7 \%}$ over the CMOS device.

articleTitle: Design of Two-Port Wideband MIMO Antenna With High Isolation for Sub-6 GHz (5G), ISM Band, and WLAN Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Due to immense applications in the Sub- 6 GHz, ISM band, WLAN, and LTE bands, wireless communication is vital in transmitting and receiving data between end nodes. However, there are specific challenges in transmitting and receiving the data. Different theories and models have been proposed to mitigate these challenges using the MIMO antenna system, but attaining higher isolation between antennas for the above applications is always challenging. In this paper, we design a two-port wideband antenna with enhanced isolation between the antennas to overcome interference and improve the overall throughput for the mentioned applications. The designed antenna has two ports with an operating frequency of ${1. 2 0 - 5. 0} \mathrm{~ G H z}$ and is fabricated on an FR-4 substrate having a dielectric constant of 4.3, with the dimensions $56 \times 70 \times 1.6 \mathrm{~mm}^{3}$. The gain of the designed antenna falls in the range of 2.10 to 4.45 dBi with a limited variation of 2.35 dBi for the entire operating range. Moreover, the proposed MIMO antenna design is simple to operate. The design of the proposed approach has been validated using CST Microwave Studio software.

articleTitle: Multi-turn Loop Antenna for Monitoring Internal Brain Temperature
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Design of a multi-turn loop antenna for monitoring the internal brain temperature of a subject using microwave radiometry is presented. The antenna model consists of a 4 turn circular loop of 40 mm diameter in a PTFE dielectric substrate with 80 mm diameter ground plane to reduce electromagnetic interference. The antenna was designed using Ansys HFSS software and has a return loss greater than 10 dB at the center frequency of 2.9 GHz with 10 dB return loss bandwidth of 84 MHz. Further, the volume loss density in human head was computed for different placements of the antenna radially outward from the human head to account for human head hair thickness and an optimal placement was identified. The optimal air gap for brain temperature monitoring was determined as 10 mm. The VLD calculated at 2.9 GHz within the human head model for 10 mm air gap was found to be sufficient for estimating the temperature of human cortex located at a depth of 20 mm.

articleTitle: Reliability Analysis of Ku-Band 2-watt Solid State Power Amplifier
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents the reliability analysis carried out for a Ku-Band 2W (watt) SSPA (Solid State Power Amplifier). The 2 W SSPA is a driver amplifier to TWTA (Travelling Wave Tube Amplifier). This configuration along with an EPC (Electronics Power Conditioner) is used as a transmitter for a space-borne Mini SAR (Synthetic Aperture Radar). To ensure the SSPA meets the life of the mission in space, internationally recognized method of electronic equipment defined in MIL-HDBK-217 is used. Using this standard published by the US Department of Defense, the component and system reliability analysis was carried out. The stress values for the individual military, space and commercial components were included to calculate the Failure Rate and MTBF (Mean Time between Failures) of the SSPA. The Part Stress Analysis was considered to predict reliability of the SSPA under specified operating conditions. For a mission time of 10 minutes per day and a span of 5 years, the reliability of the SSPA is calculated to be $\mathbf{9 9. 9 \%}$.

articleTitle: A CPW-Fed Triple band Slot Antenna with symmetrical Stubs for WLAN/WiMAX Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents a novel compact CPW-fed slot antenna designed for Triple-band operation. It features a segmental shaped rectangle with two symmetrical stubs placed inside a larger rectangular slot to achieve triple-band operation spanning 2.28-2.74 GHz, 2.87-3.26 GHz, and 4.11-5.89 GHz. The proposed antenna is designed on FR4 substrate of thickness $\mathbf{1. 6}$ mm and dielectric constant of 4.4. The overall size of the antenna is $\mathbf{4 5} \mathrm{mm} \times 60 \mathrm{~mm}$. Simulated Results demonstrate favorable broadside radiation patterns across all three bands, indicating the antenna’s suitability for WiMAX, WLAN applications and other wireless communication needs.

articleTitle: Low-Cost Ultra-Wideband Fractal Antenna Array For L-Band Beam Squint Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents a low-cost, ultra-wideband fractal array antenna, designed for beam squint applications at the L-band frequency ranges from 1 to 2 GHz. The detail design process, simulation results, measured results and potential applications of the proposed antenna array is projected here. For beam squint applications usually higher frequency bands are preferred since achieving higher impedance bandwidth is easier at higher frequencies. The proposed design allows the utilization of the entire L-Band, thereby making beam squint applications possible even at L-band. The prototype of the microstrip antenna is fabricated on single layer FR4 substrate, it makes the design cost effective. The measured reflection coefficient is better than $\mathbf{1 0. 0} \mathbf{~ d B}$ across entire L-Band. These features make it particularly suitable for various communication systems and radar technologies that require ultra-wide bandwidth at lower frequencies.

articleTitle: Coaxial Measurements for EMI Characterization of Dielectric Powders as Inclusions for Low Frequency Cement Based EMI Shielding Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Coaxial transmission line-based technique to explore suitability of dielectric powders as fillers for cement-based EMI shielding is presented, in frequency range $100 \mathrm{MHz}-1 \mathrm{GHz}$. Low frequency characterization mandates large antennas and huge samples. The proposed technique provides rapid initial estimates on EMI shielding performance of powders, enabling easier filler identification, reducing cost and time. Dielectric fillers considered are ash by-products from varied units of steel plants including Argon-Oxygen Decarburization (AoD), Acid Recovery Station (ARS) and Electric Arc Furnace (EAF) units. Plane wave skin depth of powders is computed from S matrix measurements on ash filled coaxial structure. The coaxial line includes provision to vary dielectric material. ARS ash exhibits skin depth less than 20 cm in entire frequency analysis range. AoD and EAF ashes provide good skin depths less than 40 cm in the upper UHF range above 500 MHz. Validation of results though plane wave experiments are necessary. Industrial and agriculture by-products in powder form, which are at present explored as sustainable options, can be easily characterised through the present technique, for customized EMI mitigation solutions, and for other emerging cement based applications in electrical engineering.

articleTitle: An Ultrawide Band 5G Millimeter Wave Antenna Using Square Loop Ring Resonators
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this paper, a dual-band antenna for the millimeter wave (mm-Wave) application is designed. The single-element design offers several advantages, including simple construction, large operational bandwidth, and high gain. The antenna is designed on a Rogers RT/Duriod 5880 substrate and has a compact footprint of $8 \times 6 \mathbf{~ m m}^{2}$. The UWB spectrum achieves $\mathbf{- 1 0}$ dB impedance bandwidths of 6.3 GHz and 19.8 GHz, covering $\mathbf{3 7. 2 - 4 3. 5 ~ G H z}$ and 54.7-74.5 GHz. The antenna exhibits a peak gain of 8.93 dBi and a consistent radiation pattern within the operational bandwidth. Due to these properties, the suggested antenna is considered suitable for future 5 G and mm-Wave communications.

articleTitle: Wideband RCS Reduction of a microstrip antenna in Ku Band
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper describes RCS reduction of a wideband microstrip antenna by employing a multiband microwave absorber designed at Ku Band. The copper backed absorber is constructed by integrating dodecagonal, hexagonal and circular truncated apertures circumscribed by a square copper loop for exhibiting absorption above $\mathbf{9 7 \%}$ at $14.2 \mathrm{GHz}, 14.6 \mathrm{GHz}$ and 16.8 GHz respectively. The CPW fed microstrip antenna operates from 5.1-18 GHz. Monostatic RCS reduction of the antenna occurs from $\mathbf{1 2 - 1 8 ~ G H z}$ due to absorber loading. The current distribution at the resonance frequencies has been numerically studied for investigating the electric and magnetic resonances in the absorber. All simulations have been conducted using finite integration technique.

articleTitle: Electronically Reconfigurable Band Pass Filter for Vehicular Application
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this manuscript, an electronically reconfigurable compact Band Pass Filter (BPF) is presented. A $4^{\text {th }}$-order microstrip BPF, based on a ring resonator with coupling sections, has been designed. Band tuning is achieved by incorporating a varactor diode, allowing for dynamic adjustment of the filter’s passband. Additionally, a biasing network has been developed to isolate the RF and DC power sources effectively. The filter’s response has been analyzed and optimized through a parametric study. The proposed filter offers a 220 MHz frequency tuning range for the pass band with a bias voltage range of $\mathbf{0 - 2 0}$ Volts. The group delay between ports is less than 3 ns in the passband, and the design also validates the positions of transmission poles (TP) and transmission zeros (TZ). The current distribution across the structure confirms the filtering path, and the design is compact, occupying a footprint of just $0.38 \lambda \mathrm{~g} \times 0.36 \lambda \mathrm{~g}$.

articleTitle: Imaging with Deep Sub-Wavelength Resolution using Metasurface
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this paper, we have introduced a biomedical imaging system with deep sub-wavelength resolution utilizing a low-frequency electromagnetic field metasurface. Our experimental results demonstrate that this system can detect an inclusion of approximately 2 cm in size, highlighting its high resolution of around $\lambda / 75$.

articleTitle: A Metasurface-based Bandpass Filter in Ka-Band for Space Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this paper, a multi-layered metasurface (MS) structure has been proposed as Ka-band filter having extremely low insertion loss and sharproll-off characteristics towards space application. Three identical distinct layers of RT Duroid 6010 substrate have been used in which the proposed structure has been designed. The unit cell of the structure consists of a square metallic slot together with a square metallic ring slot in the top and bottom surfaces of the middle layer of RT Duroid 6010 substrate. The proposed design offers bandpass characteristics over 27.5 GHz to 30.5 GHz combined with a sharp rejection of $4 \mathrm{~dB} / \mathrm{GHz}$ out-of-band. The proposed filter offers $0.3 \mathrm{~dB}, 1 \mathrm{~dB}$ and 3 dB bandwidths of $2.08 \mathrm{GHz}, 3.17 \mathrm{GHz}$ and 4.36 GHz respectively. The extremely low insertion loss lesser than 0.4 dB has been achieved in the passband. The structure offers angular stability up to $\mathbf{3 0}^{\circ}$ along with polarization independent feature. Being compact in nature, the structure is suitable for space applications.

articleTitle: Design of RF Biosensor for Blood Glucose Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this study, a Planar Inverted-F Antenna (PIFA) array is designed as a RF bio-sensor in the ISM (Industrial Scientific Medical) band for blood glucose monitoring.
