The proposed antenna sensor consists of two PIFA elements with each element consisting of a parasitic patch and designed onto FR4 substrate. The microstrip corporate feed is used to excite the radiators. The antenna sensor resonates at 2.45 GHz with an impedance bandwidth of 293 MHz. The bio-sensor is designed for the ex-vivo environment. The corresponding sensitivity of the antenna with respect to the change in glucose concentration in blood has been found to be $\mathbf{1 9. 6 4 2 ~ K H z /(m g / d L). ~}$

articleTitle: Experimental Demonstration of SIC in a Co-linearly Polarised Full-Duplex Antenna for 6G and its Multi-Element Implementation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this paper, we showcase an affordable in-house experimental setup to demonstrate the antenna domain self-interference-cancellation in a co-linearly polarized full-duplex antenna with 1-Tx and 1-Rx configuration. The experimental setup uses off-the-shelf devices such as MATLAB Simulink-operated software-defined radio and spectrum analyser with the developed FD antenna. Experiments are conducted for different propagation environments such as indoor and anechoic chamber to validate the design effectiveness of the developed FD antenna. Further, the FD antenna design is extended to a multi-element configuration having 1-Tx and $2-\mathrm{Rx}$ configurations. $\left|S_{i j}\right|$ of less than −30 dB and −70 dB are achieved between $2-\mathrm{Rx}$ antennas and between Tx-Rx for a three-element FD configuration respectively. Further, it is validated using fabrication and measurements.

articleTitle: Development of Ku-Band Frequency Generator of OCEANSAT-3 Payload
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper demonstrates novel techniques used for the performance optimization during development of onboard Ku-band Frequency Generator subsystem for OCEANSAT-3 payload which is successfuly operational in orbit. It demonstrates how various high frequency RF and Microwave circuits from 50 MHz to Ku-band viz. Amplifiers, Multipliers, Mixers, Modulators, Band pass filters, Low pass filters and Link cards can be optimized under single circuit to integrated tray level assembly and finally at subsystem level assembly to improve the overall performance viz. oscillations, thermal shifts, spurious rejections, power variations, improvement of return losses and stability of the onboard Ku-band Frequency Generator subsystem.

articleTitle: A Compact Five-Port Hybrid Network with Electronic Control of Both Magnitude and Phase
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This work presents a microstrip line-based 5-port hybrid network with tunable magnitude and phase outputs. The network is constructed by incorporating an additional output port into the traditional 3 dB branch – line hybrid coupler and integrating two varactor diodes. The proposed beamforming network offers a 30° progressive phase variation with amplitude variations of at least $\pm 3 \mathrm{~dB}$ over the $2.25-2.55\ \mathrm{GHz}$ range using only one varactor diode, while the other is set to a fixed bias. Thus, it is ideal for adaptive beamforming in wireless LAN applications. Since it is based on a transmission line model, higher-order beamforming networks can be easily obtained. Measurements show that the 5 – port coupler maintains at least 15 dB isolation and a 10 dB return loss over the $2.2-2.8\ \mathrm{GHz}$ range. The overall size of the structure is $0.125 \lambda_{g}^{2}$.

articleTitle: Improved Boresight Gain in Slotted Trapezoidal Ground UWB Monopole with Non-Concentric Circular Loops
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: The design and performance analysis of a microstrip-fed circular ring-based planar monopole Ultra Wide-Band (UWB) antennas are investigated in this paper. Three non-concentric circular rings are inserted within the microstrip-fed circular ring monopole antenna backed by reduced ground planes of distinct shapes such as rectangular ground (RG), elliptical ground (EG) and trapezium ground (TG) respectively. The non-concentric rings are scaled optimally, for a comprehensive analysis of their impact on impedance bandwidth and antenna gain in boresight direction. By integrating such structures, the study addresses significant challenges associated with traditional UWB monopole antennas, particularly the degradation of radiation performance at higher frequencies. It is found that non-concentric ring based UWB monopole antenna offers UWB impedance band while demonstrating positive gain in boresight direction up to 8 GHz. Thus, the proposed antenna structures exhibit enhanced UWB impedance bandwidth and improved boresight gain, thereby overcoming the limitations of conventional designs.

articleTitle: Two-stage reference-free fault diagnosis in phased array antennas
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Fault diagnosis in an antenna array without any reference pattern is a new topic of interest, particularly for practical scenarios. We propose a two-stage fault diagnosis in phased array antennas without the need for information on fault-free arrays. In the first stage, we use low rank + sparse matrices recovery to separate electric fields and faulty elements of an antenna array. This allows us to obtain the approximate true electric fields of all elements in an antenna array, including mutual coupling effects. The field information serves as a reference for a healthy array in the second stage, eliminating the need to repeat the initial stage. This efficient method not only makes the fault diagnosis process entirely free from reference data but also enhances the efficiency of the second stage by using the approximate true field information as a reference.

articleTitle: A millimeter wave Circularly Polarized Dielectric Resonator Antenna for Ka-band applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this article a millimeter wave (mm-wave) circularly polarized dielectric resonator antenna (DRA) has been proposed for Ka-band applications. The projected antenna comprises of a rectangular shaped dielectric resonator (DR) and a microstrip patch, which offer $\left|S_{11}\right|$ frequency band of (27.17 40.44) GHz and an axial ratio frequency range of (37.16 - 37.98) GHz. Around 16 dB isolation has been obtained between right hand (RH) and left hand circular polarization (LHCP) in a broadside direction. The presented design is appropriate for radar and satellite applications. The Ansys HFSS simulation software (2023 R1) has been applied for simulating and analyzing the projected antenna design.

articleTitle: Analysis of a Concave Cylindrical Rectangular Microstrip Antenna for GSM-band Application
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Microstrip antennas are popular for their conformability on non-planar mounting surfaces. A Plethora of investigations is present in the open literature. However, the main focus of those contributions has been on convex structured conformal antennas. In this work, we take the opportunity to investigate on concave microstrip antenna. In this work, a rectangular microstrip antenna on a concave cylindrical surface is designed and simulated using commercially popular 3D EM software HFSS. Input impedance, reflection coefficient, and radiation patterns are also shown here. The antenna is designed for GSM-band applications. Finally, the effect of different curvatures on the radiation pattern is presented.

articleTitle: Novel Coupling Design For Substrate Integrated Waveguide Bandpass Filter
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents a novel coupling design for substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) bandpass filter. The coupling structure is formed by a rectangular slot cut on the top metal surface and inductive post. This design is based on the mixed coupling structure, where magnetic and electrical coupling play the filter formation with two transmission zeros at both sides of the pass band. For the validation, fabrication, and testing of the model is performed.

articleTitle: Multibit Quasi Confromal Chipless RFID for Wideband Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper introduces square-shaped chipless RFID tags, providing an in-depth exposition of their design and development. A thin grounded substrate (0.254 mm) composed of FR-4 renders the tags bendable. Conformity and cross-polarization tests are simulated at various rotation and tilt angles to validate the tag’s positional independence. The proposed tags operate within the 2 GHz to 8 GHz frequency range, accommodating a 10-bit capacity. Modifying bit sequence techniques are elucidated, showcasing transformative potential.

articleTitle: A Wideband Polarization-Insensitive Metasuraface Absorber For Harvesting RF Energy & Wireless Power Transmission
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper introduces an energy harvesting technique through a polarization-insensitive metasurface absorber over a wideband from 19.8-23.5 GHz. The proposed wideband metasurface absorber consists of an F4B substrate (sandwiched between split ring resonators (SRRs) & Cu ground plane) and 350 ohms resistive loads to improve energy capturing capability over wideband. The metasurface absorber’s design allows more than $\mathbf{9 0 \%}$ absorption of energy over the whole absorption bandwidth of 3.7 GHz. The absorbed RF energy is then passed to an integrated rectifying circuit to convert it into DC. The maximum simulated rectification efficiency of the integrated rectifier obtained is 59.9% at 15 dBm of input power.

articleTitle: Design of an MMIC Medium Power Amplifier at 47 GHz
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: An MMIC medium power amplifier is designed at 47 GHz with 0.15 μm gate length pHEMT-based GaAs process. An innovative topology with a novel biasing arrangement has been adopted to realize the MMIC amplifier with nominal active devices while maintaining efficient real estate utilisation. Simulation results show that the amplifier gives 16dB of small signal gain with 17.5 dBm output P1dB over 45-49 GHz. The amplifier is stabilized over 0 to 60 GHz by utilizing a feedback loop. The amplifier can be used to produce an LO signal in a W-band sub-harmonic mixer for cloud RADAR application.

articleTitle: System Design, Integration and End-to-End Characterization of 220-230GHz & 330-345GHz Heterodyne Spectrometer Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents system design, integration and end-to-end characterization of 220-230GHz and 330-345GHz heterodyne spectrometer systems for ground based sub-mm wave telescope, proposed to be deployed at Hanle, India. This telescope will generate the first comprehensive survey maps of molecular clouds in the Milky Way and nearby galaxies from the northern hemisphere at these frequencies. This telescope consists of low-noise cryo-cooled sideband separating heterodyne receivers with wideband high speed digital FFT based spectrometer system to observe (J: 2 → 1 and J: 3 → 2) rotational transitions of different isotopes of CO (i.e. 12CO and 13CO) with 54” and 36” angular, and 1.6MHz spectral resolution. Noise Temperatures for 230GHz and 345GHz RF Frontends will be 450K and 525K at cryotemperatures and are at-par with state-of-the-art Schottkybarrier diode (SBD) based receivers. Spectrometer system is a 4-channel instrument providing total 8GHz bandwidth with a spectral resolution of 1.6MHz, which can be further optimized to 400KHz. End-to-end performance of the 230GHz and 345GHz integrated systems with 0.5m reflector in ambient lab environment is demonstrated. Current paper discusses system configuration design and specifications, hardware configuration, integration methodology and end-to-end characterization results of integrated 230GHz and 345GHz heterodyne spectrometer system at ambient temperature.

articleTitle: Compact Linearly Polarized Resistor Loaded Bow-Tie Antenna for GPR System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents a resistor-loaded cavity backed modified elliptical bow tie antenna, tailored for rover based Ground Penetrating Radar (GPR) applications. The antenna’s distinctive flared design delivers a wide bandwidth and high impedance, essential for achieving high-resolution subsurface imaging. Here centre section of the bow tie antenna is modified to match it with Coplanar Strip-line (CPS). Further, a miniaturized meandered matching network is employed to match it with a microstrip line and cavity is incorporated to have broadside radiation. Antenna radiates linearly polarized waves with return loss better than 10 dB in $0.5-3 \mathrm{GHz}$, exhibits good radiation performance in our desired band of $\mathbf{0. 5 - 2} \mathbf{~ G H z}$ and achieves maximum gain of 5 dBi. As ringing is a crucial parameter for GPR systems, two resistors are loaded on both the sides of bow tie antenna to suppress it. We assess the antenna’s time domain performance by examining its impulse response and pulse distortion. Proposed antenna produces minimal ringing resulting in precise and clear signal transmission. An antenna prototype of size $0.33 \lambda_{1} \times 0.25 \lambda_{1} x$ $0.05 \lambda_{1}$ (with $\lambda_{1}$ corresponds to 0.5 GHz) has been fabricated to validate it’s performance. Results suggest that the bow tie antenna offers optimal performance favourable for GPR systems.

articleTitle: Design of a planar multilayer reconfigurable SIW Band Pass Filter for 5G Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A multilayer tunable SIW based reconfigurable band pass filter using varactor diodes as switching element is designed in this paper. Firstly, a two-pole band pass filter is constructed using SIW coaxial resonator sections. An inset feeding mechanism is used to match the filter section to 50 Ohm input and output microstrip ports. Frequency reconfigurability of the filter is achieved by varying the effective electrical lengths of resonators with help of voltage-controlled varactor diodes loaded at the metallic posts in the center of the resonator cavity. The frequency reconfigurable filter is experimentally developed using a 4-layer PCB with low loss substrate Taconic TLY (dielectric permitivity $=2.2$, tan delta $=0.0009$) backed by FR4 with 70 mm by 36 mm circuit area. The two-pole filter provides tuneablity in the $5 \mathrm{G} \mathrm{n78}$ band from 3.2 GHz to 3.8 GHz with fractional bandwidth of 4 percentage. Experimental filter has return loss greater than 17 dB and insertion loss less than 7dB over the all the tune able bands of operation. The reconfigurable filter can be used in 5G NR for high data rate communication.

articleTitle: Coaxial Cavity Tunable Bandpass Filter for Radar Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents a low-loss, post-manufacturing coaxial cavity tunable bandpass filter(BPF). A BPF with 5th degree Chebyshev bandpass response is discussed. It resonates at 2.8 GHz with a Bandwidth of 450 MHz. The lowpass prototype is used as a starting point in the bandpass filter design. Particularly in the passband, insertion loss of 0.2 dB, return loss greater than -20 dB are attained. A good spurious response and better rejection of -50 dB characterized. The tuning screws are used to adjust the bandwidth and coupling screws are used to decrease the ripples in the filter. These kind of microwave cavity filter is beneficial for base stations, radar, and satellite transceivers and systems requires low insertion loss and good selectivity, The BPF is fabricated and validated.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of 5-18 GHz Planar Coupled Dipole Array Antenna for Phased Array Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents the design and analysis of 5 to 18 GHz compact planar coupled dipole array antenna for phased array applications. The antenna array is required to operate over 5 to 18 GHz band and to provide scan coverage of 45 deg in Az and El planes. The main objective of this work is to enhance the impedance and pattern bandwidth and to provide the broad scan coverage. The efforts has made to optimize the comb structure of coupled elements and for utilization of stacked layers to make it compact and wideband. Initial design and optimization of the proposed antenna carried out using 3D electromagnetic solver, CST Microwave studio. To analyze the functionality of proposed array antenna, a planar array of total 64 radiating elements (8 by 8) distributed over a rectangular aperture of 76.8 mm by 76.8 mm size is used. The proposed structure makes the Active Array Antenna Unit (AAAU) compact and is suitable for Tile based TR Module Active Array Units.

articleTitle: Staggered Panel Based Approach for GLL Improvement in Large Phased Array for Spacebrone SAR Application
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This manuscript describes the new and simple approach of grating lobe improvement in large phased array antennas designed for spaceborne synthetic aperture radar (SAR) applications. The subarraying scheme on such a large phased array antenna restricts the scanning range due to the grating lobe appearance, resulting in degraded ambiguity performance in SAR systems. In this paper, a simple staggering based approach is presented. When it is applied on the tile or panel of the antenna, the energy concentrated in the grating lobe divides, reducing its amplitude level. Here, the $3.08 \mathrm{~m} \times 3.17 \mathrm{~m}$ sized large phased array antenna working at X-band and having $8 \times 8$ array as subarray is presented, along with its modularization. Such array has been evaluated for ±2 degree conical beam scan. 2 cases of the subarray’s row staggering in azimuth and elevation direction and 2 cases of the panel level staggering in azimuth direction are discussed in detail along with their scan performance ±2 degree conical beam scan. It has been proved that the simple panel staggering in the azimuth direction improves the grating lobe level by 3.62 dB.

articleTitle: A Low Loss High Isolation SPDT MMIC Switch at 145 GHz
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: The design of a passive single-pole double-throw (SPDT) switch has been presented in a 0.1 um GaAs pHEMT technology for D-band communication system for future 6G applications. A simple topology has been adopted and the simulation result of the MMIC shows insertion loss of 1.76 dB and isolation of 31.78 dB at 145 GHz along with 20 dB isolation bandwidth of 15 GHz. The die size of the proposed switch including all RF and DC pads is 1 mm x 1 mm only.

articleTitle: Planar Array Antenna with Reconfigurable Feed Network for Wide-Angle Beam Switching
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Two reconfigurable beam steering antennas are designed using a parallel corporate feed network and PIN diode switches with possible applications in 5G, Satcom, or IOT. The main beam of the initial $4 \times 1$ array antenna is tilted to the desired direction by introducing phase difference between array elements. For the Design I, two PIN diodes are incorporated to realize beam steering of ± 20° in the H -plane with a maximum peak gain of 7.9 dBi. With parametric study it has been shown that a higher value of beam tilt is possible with increase in phase difference of the corresponding radiating subarray elements. The desirable beam steering up to ± 22° is achievable by just changing the extended feed path length in Design I. In Design II, four PIN diodes have been introduced in parallel fed array with some modification in spacing between array elements. Using combinations of the different states of diode switches, $\pm \mathbf{3 2 ^ { \circ }}$ beam steering has been realized in $\mathbf{H}$-plane. Both designs utilize the array feed network and the overall gain increases because of the array configuration. The proposed antenna is completely planar with dimensions of $2.08 \lambda \times 0.83 \lambda$, where $\lambda$ is the wavelength corresponding to the operating frequency of $\mathbf{4. 2} \mathbf{~ G H z}$.

articleTitle: P-Band Frequency Synthesizer for Airborne Synthesis Aperture Radar
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper describes the design, development and characterization of a microwave P-band frequency synthesizer for airborne synthetic aperture radar applications. The frequency synthesizer uses a direct frequency multiplication technique using a temperature compensated crystal oscillator (TCXO) as a source to generate multiple signal coherently. The signals generated by the frequency synthesizer are a 50 MHz reference signal from TCXO, a clock signal of 250MHz, 2 nos. of 450 MHz local oscillator signal and a linear frequency modulated (LFM) signal of $450 \pm 25 ~\mathrm{MHz}$. The LFM signal is synthesized by quadrature modulation of 450 MHz signal with modulating chirp input of 25 MHz bandwidth. The modulated transmit chirp signal exhibits side band suppression of $\gt20 \mathrm{dBc}$ and frequency response of $\lt \mathrm{2} ~\mathrm{d B}$ over the operating temperature range of $-10^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$ to $55^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$. The in-band and out-of-band spurious signals are $\gt20 \mathrm{dBc}$ and >40dBc, respectively. The frequency synthesizer is realized using microwave integrated circuits using space hardware development guidelines.

articleTitle: Progress in ICRF antenna and feeder system research in Tokamak Experiments at IPR
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Ion Cyclotron Resonance Frequency (ICRF) system is employed at tokamak experiments at IPR. These frequencies are in the MHz range depending on the operating magnetic fields for plasma experiments. Two of the important component of the system are antenna and the feeder that injects power to the plasma. Various upgradations have been carried out based on the experiments conducted and experiences obtained on their shortcomings. The interface system that feeds power to the antenna has been considerably improved and replaced by a compact feeder by removing the features that were either not required for the present operating conditions. The new direct antenna feeder system is designed in electromagnetic simulation software and is fabricated as per the modified design. The system is integrated and used in tokamak experiments by successfully injecting 100 kW of RF power in pulsed and 80 kW for more than 10 s. The improved antenna system are designed and ready to be integrated for future experiments.

articleTitle: Series-Fed Binomial Tapered Microstrip Antenna with Low Side Lobe Level for Automotive MIMO RADAR Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this paper, a compact multiple input multiple output (MIMO) antenna system with two transmitters and four receivers (2Tx-4Rx) is designed using a five-element series-fed binomial tapered (SFBT) microstrip antenna (MA) at 24 GHz millimeter-wave band, aimed at autonomous driving applications. A feedline configuration employing edge feeding is implemented to enhance integration capabilities with various devices. The study comprehensively evaluates a stand-alone series-fed array antenna configuration alongside two distinct MIMO antenna configurations such as traditional and sparse MIMO arrangement. The proposed SFBT-MA has a side lobe level of -23 dB with a maximum gain of 11.2 dBi. It is studied that the traditional and sparse MIMO arrangement exhibits increased SLL of -21.44 dB and -20.78 dB respectively compared to the stand-alone antenna due to the inter-element coupling.

articleTitle: Simplified Doherty Power Amplifier With Harmonic Suppression
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Communication radio need back-off power efficient amplifier with harmonic suppression. Efficiency and harmonic suppression are two contradicting requirements. While Doherty’s architecture improves back-off efficiency, the cascaded harmonic suppression filter nullifies the benefits. Moreover, a UHF Doherty would be space constrained by the matching network each at carrier (to $100 \Omega$) and peaking amplifiers. This paper demonstrates a simplified design methodology for UHF Doherty amplifier with harmonic suppression features. The impedance inverter is implemented at transistor’s load line impedance and the matching network at carrier and peaking amplifier’s drain are eliminated. After load modulation, an impedance transforming filter, embedded with harmonic suppression features, performs the final translation to $50 \Omega$. Similarly at the input, an impedance transforming wilkinson power divider reduces gate matching networks. The simplifications have resulted in a compact Doherty amplifier which is a form-fit replacement for class AB modules while significant back-off efficiency improvement of $15 \%$ and $18 \%$ at $\mathrm{6 d B}$ and 10 dB back-off have been achieved. Besides, harmonic suppression levels as low as $\mathrm{- 7 3 d B c}$ have been recorded in the $\mathrm{2 2 0 - 3 0 0 M H z}$ fabricated demonstrator circuit. The module delivers $49.4-50 \mathrm{dBm}$ of CW power with $\mathrm{6 5 \%}$ efficiency at peak output power, $47 \%$ efficiency at $\mathrm{6 d B}$ back-off and $\mathrm{3 8 \%}$ efficiency at 10 dB back-off output power.

articleTitle: A Lightweight 3D Printed Metasurface for Wideband RCS Reduction
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This work presents a lightweight, 3-D printed metasurface for radar cross-section (RCS) reduction applications. The proposed unit cell geometry is based on a circular shaped metallic patch printed on a polylactic acid substrate terminated with a ground plane. Two different sets of unit cells are designed by varying the dielectric height to obtain a reflection phase difference of $180^{\circ} \pm 37^{\circ}$, such that a complete metasurface is resulted from these unit cells exhibiting a $10-\mathrm{dB}$ RCS reduction bandwidth ranging from 8.1 GHz to 19.5 GHz. The novelty of the method lies in the utilization of the 3-D printing technique to vary the dielectric volume instead of only using different unit cell patterns, unlike used in the conventional phase cancellation method for RCS reduction. The proposed metasurface has been simulated using the finite element boundary integral technique and is observed as polarization-insensitive as well as angularly stable up to 30° incident angle.

articleTitle: Automation of Conducted Susceptibility Testing According to IEC 61000-4-6
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this paper, we detail the automation of the conducted susceptibility (CS) test in accordance with IEC 61000-4-6 standard. The automation process was implemented for both power line and signal line testing using Coupling-Decoupling Network (CDN), EM clamp, and Bulk Current Injection (BCI) modules. This was accomplished by controlling the signal generator and spectrum analyzer through MATLAB and Python via a USB interface. Our software is optimized to reduce calibration and testing time.

articleTitle: Tolerance Analysis of W-Band Slotted Array Monopulse Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper discusses the effect of fabrication tolerances on the broader dimension (width) of a slotted waveguide that has been incorporated in a monopulse slotted array antenna designed and developed to operate in the Wband. Initially, a monopulse antenna has been configured, consisting of $\mathbf{2 4 0 0}$ radiating slots. A sum pattern gain of $\mathbf{4 0} \mathbf{d B}$ has been obtained with a side lobe level of $\mathbf{- 1 6. 2} \mathbf{d B}$ in the $\mathbf{H}$ plane and - $\mathbf{1 8. 4} \mathbf{~ d B}$ in the E-plane. For this antenna, tolerance analysis of $\pm 10 \mu$ to $\pm 20 \mu$ in waveguide channel width has been carried out. For a variation of $10 \mu$, a gain value around 39 dB has been obtained in the $\mathbf{H}$-plane and E-plane sum patterns. Respective side lobe level values are around $\mathbf{- 1 5} \mathrm{dB}$ and $\mathbf{- 1 7} \mathrm{dB}$ in $\mathbf{H}$ and E-planes. For a change of $20 \mu$, the gain has reduced to $\mathbf{3 6 ~ d B}$ with side lobe levels of $\mathbf{- 1 2} \mathbf{d B}$ and -7dB in H and E planes.

articleTitle: High Power Compact Doherty Power Amplifier for n8 and n106 5G Base-Station
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents a novel design of a high-power compact Doherty Power Amplifier (DPA) optimized for n8 and n106 5G base-stations (BSs). The proposed methodology innovatively eliminates the traditional output matching network and with a post-matching network to achieve a compact design with high efficiency and gain. The design operates efficiently over the frequency band of $\mathbf{8 8 0}$ to $\mathbf{9 5 0} \mathbf{~ M H z}$. Detailed simulation results demonstrate that the designed DPA not only reduces size and complexity but also maintains high efficiency and gain across the targeted frequency range. Achieved peak power is more than 57.5 dBm for an efficiency more than $\mathbf{7 0 \%}$ over the band. At an average power of 50.6 dBm attained efficiency is above $\mathbf{6 0 \%}$. The gain is above 18 dB over the frequency band. The size of the proposed DPA is 150 mm X 100 mm. This approach provides a promising solution for next generation 5G infrastructure, addressing the need for compact, high-performance high power amplifiers.

articleTitle: Compact Hexagonal shaped Multiband Patch Antenna Loaded with Complementary Split Ring Resonators for THz Frequency Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A compact hexagonal patch antenna designed to achieve efficient performance in the THz frequency range is presented in this paper. Departing from conventional designs, in this antenna ground plane and patch are loaded with four hexagonal shape complementary split ring resonators (HCSRRs) on each. The proposed antenna operates at five resonating frequencies below $\mathbf{- 1 0} \mathrm{dB}$ reflection coefficients. These frequencies are $0.9 \mathrm{THz}, 1.12 \mathrm{THz}, 1.37 \mathrm{THz}, 2 \mathrm{THz}$, and 2.7 THz, with corresponding bandwidth of $60 \mathrm{GHz}, 60 \mathrm{GHz}, 280$ GHz, 510 GHz and 440 GHz, respectively. Moreover, the antenna provides gains of $6.9 \mathrm{dBi}, 5.8 \mathrm{dBi}, 5.4 \mathrm{dBi}, 9.5 \mathrm{dBi}$, and 8.9 dBi at the aforementioned frequencies, respectively. The overall floor area of the proposed antenna is $\mathbf{4 0 0} \times \mathbf{4 3 0} \times \mathbf{2 0} \mu^{3}$. Radiation patterns for the antenna are also presented, showcasing its suitability for various THz applications.

articleTitle: 1GHz x3 Frequency Multiplier with Integrated Filter for Space Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Design and development of an active $1 \mathbf{G H z X} 3$ frequency multiplier with an integrated filter is presented in this paper. The proposed frequency tripler is designed using BFY193 bipolar junction transistor (BJT) on 25mil alumina substrate with distributed networks. Multiplier is designed to achieve better than 40 dBc harmonic rejection along with good input and output return loss which is the cornerstone of the design. The fabricated $\mathbf{x} 3$ multiplier provides conversion loss of 9.5 dB, input and output return losses better than 15 dB, and has stable performance over $-15^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$ to $55^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$. The entire hybrid circuit is fit into 41.5mmx25.4mm size. The reported space grade tripler has extremely good return loss and harmonic suppression when compared to state-of-the-art designs and has been successfully used in S band frequency generator for NASAISRO Synthetic Aperture Radar (NISAR) mission.

articleTitle: A Multilayer Stacked Patch Antenna Tile for Octal Digital Transmit/Receive Module of S-Band Dual Polarized Phased Array Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A low profile multilayer stacked patch antenna tile is proposed. It is to be integrated with an octal digital transmit receive module (ODTRM) of S-Band dual polarized phased array antenna. Stacking of conductive patches is used in designing radiating element for this antenna tile. Each radiating element is provided with two probe feeds to generate linear orthogonal polarizations. A $\mathbf{2 X 2}$ sub-array of radiating elements is designed with two incorporated 1-to-4-way power dividers with outputs connected to probe feeds of radiating elements. Four such sub-arrays are arranged along y-axis to form antenna tile. Antenna tile is provided with BMA connectors perpendicularly connected at inputs of 1-to-4-way power dividers to blindly integrate it with ODTRM. Designed antenna tile is realized and validated in near field antenna test range. Measured gain is better than 15.8dB for both V and H polarizations with cross polarization less than -20 dB over frequency band of 2.9 GHz to 3.3 GHz. Measured isolation between ports of orthogonal polarizations of antenna tile is less than -20dB and VSWR measured is 2.4 (max) at all ports of antenna tile. Realized antenna tile is a promising modular tile for building large dual polarized phased array antennas.

articleTitle: Characterization of Materials to Realize Metasurface Design Through 3D Printing
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This manuscript discusses methods for determining the relative permittivity and loss tangent of dielectric filaments. The study focuses on three-dimensional (3D) printed structures made from Vero, a multi-color 3D printing material, PREPERM 10, and Acrylonitrile Butadiene Styrene (ABS) filaments. The design frequency is set at 12 GHz, with the operational range maintained within the Ku-band. User-defined cylindrical and rectangular structures fabricated using Vero filament are characterized using the dielectric probe (DP) method. Similarly, another set of cylindrical and rectangular structures is 3D printed from ABS filament and subsequently coated with copper paint to simulate metallic properties. The copper-coated ABS structures are used to measure a dark resin sample’s reflection and transmission coefficients using the NNIC method. The simulated and measured results are analyzed to emphasize the importance of combining 3D printing techniques with metallic coatings to enhance feed-source performance.

articleTitle: Aerosol Jet Printing on Kapton for Affordable Millimeter Wave Antenna Prototyping
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this work, we have examined the feasibility of 3D printed antennas on Kapton for mm-wave applications. Initially, a series-fed patch antenna array at 47 GHz was designed and fabricated on a low-loss Rogers substrate. Subsequently, aerosol jet printing was employed to prototype the antenna on Kapton film, which was adhered to the Rogers substrate. Experimental results showed that the Kapton antenna demonstrated similar performance to the copper etched Rogers antenna. Therefore, this method can be adopted for prototyping high-frequency antennas on expensive low-loss substrates, enabling rapid prototyping and allowing the substrates to be reused by peeling off the Kapton films.

articleTitle: A CPW-Fed Super Wideband Antenna with Triple Band Notch Characteristics
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A unique CPW-fed microstrip patch antenna with the band-notch feature is developed. The designed and analyzed antenna has minimal dimensions with a wider bandwidth. The proposed antenna is mounted on an FR-4 substrate, having a relative permittivity of 4.4. The design of the antenna consists of a radiating element as a regular inverted pentagon fed with a co-planar wave-guided line feed with the partial ground which is circularly etched corners on either side of it. This resulted in a super wide band of 2.98 GHz to more than 40 GHz with an S11 magnitude under -10 dB and VSWR<2 with a fractional bandwidth of 172.2%. Further, rectangular U-shaped slots are etched from the patch to introduce the notching feature. As a result, three slots with a particular dimension cause three notch bands at WiMAX, WLAN, and X-band frequencies. The results indicate a substantial consistency between the simulated and measured. This antenna can be used for many wireless applications that require wide bandwidth and where interference of the bands is a concern.

articleTitle: Compact SIW Backed Antenna With Integrated Multiplexer for Quad-Band Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This article presents a simple and compact substrate-integrated waveguide backed self- quadruplexer antenna design for quad band applications. The upper surface of the substrate is engraved with a modified slot which has four radiating patches of different lengths. Each radiating patches are fed independently by four $\mathbf{5 0 - o h m}$ microstrip feed lines and when simulated it operates at $5.2 \mathrm{GHz}, 5.9 \mathrm{GHz}, 6.88 \mathrm{GHz}$, and 7.66 GHz respectively. This antenna architecture makes it possible to modify each resonant frequency in accordance with the requirements of the application by manipulating a single parameter and without affecting the system performance. The proposed EM model shows good isolation and is simulated on 3D electromagnetic simulator Ansys HFSS.

articleTitle: Importance of Common Grounding for Tightly Coupled Dipole Array and Its Feed Network
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents an ultra-wideband tightly coupled dipole array (TCDA) and highlights the importance of common grounding for both the TCDA and its feed network to ensure optimal performance. The TCDA consists of a dipole layer, a resistive frequency selective surface (FSS) layer, and baluns designed using a tapered microstrip line (MSL) to feed the dipole elements. Semi-rigid coaxial cables are used to connect the feed network to the baluns. However, it is found that if the ground planes of the baluns and the TCDA are not properly connected, it leads to undesired resonance within the operational bandwidth. This resonance can significantly degrade the performance of the array due to the issues such as increased return loss and reduced gain of the TCDA, resulting in a decrease in the operational bandwidth. Therefore, ensuring a common grounding between the TCDA and its feed network is critical to maintain desired performance across an ultra-wideband frequency range.

articleTitle: A Cylindrical Dielectric Resonator Antenna Based on Apollonian Gasket of Circles
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: First time a cylindrical Dielectric Resonator Antenna (DRA) is proposed for wide bandwidth and compact size based on the Apollonian gasket of circles. First, a cylindrical DRA is designed to resonate at 1.78GHz by exciting $\mathrm{HEM}_{11 \delta}$ mode. The dielectric constant is 10.2 and for excitation offset co-axial probe is used. The apollonian gasket of circles is a self-similar fractal technique. This technique upto third iteration is performed and resonant modes are identified in each iteration stages. An improvement in the bandwidth upto $56 \%(2.57-4.14 \mathrm{GHz})$ at 2.78 GHz is obtained with a compact size in the proposed cylindrical DRA. The bandwidth is improved due to the merging of two resonant modes, $\mathrm{TM}_{11 \delta}$-like mode and $\mathrm{TM}_{21 \delta}$-like mode in the bandwidth of operation. The compactness is achieved due to the fractal technique and proposed antenna is suitable for applications such as 5G, WiMAX and part of S-band (2.58 – 4.0 GHz). Also, gain and efficiency of the proposed cylindrical DRA are within the limit in the bandwidth of operation.

articleTitle: A Badge Shaped Tri Band Microstrip Patch Antenna for Wireless Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A badge shaped microstrip patch antenna with truncated ground plane is proposed for a tri-band operation at frequencies covering the Industrial, Scientific, and Medical (ISM) band and C band for sub 6GHz communication technology. The proposed antenna has a simple structure and also has the feasibility for using it as a wearable antenna since it can be easily integrable on textiles. The overall dimension of the proposed antenna is around $50 \mathrm{~mm} \times 43 \mathrm{~mm} \times 1.6 \mathrm{~mm}$. Firstly, the antenna is simulated and analyzed in terms of performance parameters like return loss, current distribution, radiation pattern and gain using Ansys High Frequency Structure Simulator. This is followed by the fabrication of the antenna with its optimal dimensions and measurements are carried out. The fabricated antenna is also investigated for wearable applications by taking measurement with different fabrics in background. The results are found to be in good agreement.

articleTitle: Resonator-Based Wearable System for Efficient Intra-Body Communication through Fat Tissue for Biomedical Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents the design and analysis of a resonator-based wearable fat intra-body communication (Fat-IBC) system for biomedical applications. The proposed Fat-IBC system is designed to operate in the industrial, scientific and medical frequency band (ISM) of $2.40-\mathbf{2. 4 8} \mathbf{~ G H z}$. A resonating structure is designed by a planar circular spiral structure with notch enclosed and excited by a loop antenna. During numerical study, a three-layer human body tissue model (skin, fat, and muscle) is used to optimize the resonator. In addition, a polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) coating layer is considered all around the resonator to eliminate direct contact with the human body. The FatIBC system is constructed by using two identical resonators, which act as transmitting ($\mathbf{T x}$) and receiving ($\mathbf{R x}$) elements that have been placed on tissue models at different distances to show the energy transmission. To reduce the loss of energy in an undesired direction and stop the surface wave propagation over the skin tissue, the backside and side walls of the PDMS were shielded by the ferrite substrate. The concept of the proposed resonator-based Fat-IBC system has been established by numerical simulations and validated by experimental studies.

articleTitle: Development of Advanced Vircator and its Experimental Results
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: New configuration of Virtual Cathode Oscillator (VCO) has been studied for the generation of High Power Microwaves through simulation and experiments. Critical parameters such as sheet transparency and voltage variation are optimized to obtain maximum output power. The proposed design is simulated for maximum output power of 200 MW with beam parameters of $350 \mathrm{kV}, 10 \mathrm{kA}, 60 \mathrm{~ns}$. The experiment results are obtained by using D-dot probes and achieved maximum power of 159 MW in S band.

articleTitle: Optimization of 4X2 Slot Array Antenna Based on Gap Waveguide Using Machine Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper compares different machine learning models to optimize 4X2 slot array antenna based on the Gap waveguide technique. Different regression models like KNN, Decision tree, Support Vector, XGBoost, Random forest, and deep learning cascaded models were used to optimize the slot dimensions of the antenna using training datasets obtained from CST simulation software. So according to the different parameters, for this kind of dataset random forest shows the best performance which can be further used to optimize these types of complex structures at higher frequencies to save simulation time.

articleTitle: Design of a Compact Dual Layer Filtenna With Good Frequency Selectivity
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: The paper covers analysis of a compact substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) filtenna that has a two layered design aiming to improve frequency selectivity. On the common wall between the two stacked cavities are etched two slots for coupling so that four radiation nulls are developed. The radiating slot is etched in the upper cavity. Simulation software is used to analyze the structure. The operating frequency is 4.42 GHz and an out-of-band rejection of around 23 dB is achieved, which is acceptable.

articleTitle: Low RCS Antenna Array Design Using Checkerboard Arrangement of Antenna Elements
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this work, antenna elements are used to design a low RCS (radar cross section) antenna array along with a good radiation performance. Two antenna elements are designed distinctly in geometry but have similar radiation characteristics within the desired operating band. The analysis of radiation and scattering performances of antenna elements is studied to design a low RCS antenna array. The top layer of the design serves as the scattering layer, while the bottom layer provides the radiation performance of the antenna. The reflection magnitude of one and phase difference of $180^{\circ} \pm 37^{\circ}$ are ensured to achieve a condition of phase cancellation of the checkerboard array. For the radiation performance, the overall gain of both antenna elements exceeds 4 dBi and return loss is below -10 dB for frequency range of 5.2 to $5.8 \mathbf{G H z}$. A significant RCS reduction is observed over the array of element A, element B and perfect electric conducting (PEC) sheet under X and Y polarization for different frequency bands. To validate the proposed antenna array simulated results, an antenna array is fabricated with size of $160 \mathbf{x} 160 \mathrm{~mm}$. The measured and simulated results show a good agreement in RCS reduction under X and Y polarizations.

articleTitle: Theoretical Insights into mm-Wave Metasurface Behaviour
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this paper, a theoretical analysis and methodology for the design of wavefront manipulating metasurfaces that achieve radiation for a desired angle at 26 GHz and 72 GHz for mmWave communications is presented. The resulting complex surface impedance and admittance can be approximated by purely imaginary functions, leading to a passive and lossless prototype. However, there are limitations in this design for large angles of incidence and higher frequencies. For this reason, we employ Bianisotropic Huygen’s Metasurfaces, which introduces an additional degree of freedom into the design. Since highfrequency beamforming modules involve complex circuitry and significant losses, it necessitates the use of low-profile metasurfaces. The feasibility of these surfaces, emphasizing the importance of achieving an ideal unity transmission coefficient magnitude are demonstrated.

articleTitle: Tapered Cavity-Backed Drooped Crossed Dipole Antenna for Precise GNSS Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents a dual-feed, drooped crossed dipole antenna fed through a broadband feed network. The proposed antenna offers consistent performance across the complete L-band GNSS spectrum. The gain, beamwidth and cross-polarization at low elevation angles are controlled by precise design of the tapered cavity. The measured return loss is better than 17 dB in $1.15-1.62 \mathrm{GHz}$. The measured peak gain and boresight axial ratio are better than 5.5 dBi and 1.5 dB respectively, in the desired band. The measured gain roll-off is also better than 15 dB from zenith to 15° elevation. The proposed antenna was integrated with an active circuit and was tested with a GNSS receiver. The link was established with multiple GNSS satellites.

articleTitle: Orientation Independent Wireless Power Transfer System Design Utilizing Negative Refractive Index Metasurface
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This article proposes a new octagram-shaped meta-atom design having a negative refractive index (NRI) across its operating region 5.71 GHz to 5.90 GHz in the industrial, scientific and medical (ISM) band (5.72 – 5.87 GHz). The corresponding periodic metasurface (MTS) can enhance the power transfer efficiency (PTE) of a circular polarization (CP) based wireless power transfer (WPT) system operating at 5.81 GHz by 9.07%. The proposed NRI MTS can focus the incident waves from the transmitting antenna onto the receiving antenna placed at the focus of the MTS, thereby enhancing the PTE of the system. A circularly polarized square-shaped microstrip antenna (MSA) having orthogonal mode excitation and a diagonally fed rectangular-shaped MSA have been designed to operate as the transmitting and receiving elements, respectively for this proposed rotational orientation independent (CP-based) WPT system. A detailed design flow, along with the parametric study of the proposed meta-atom design as well as the WPT system has been presented based on results from the electromagnetic simulation environment and experimental validation.

articleTitle: Impact of unit cell variation on visible spectrum multiband metamaterial absorbers
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This study explores the design and parametric analysis of a dual-band metamaterial absorber optimized for the visible optical range. The absorber enhances tunability and efficiency across frequency bands by utilizing a periodic sub-wavelength unit cell. Comprising a metal-dielectric-metal structure with Silver layers and a magnesium fluoride dielectric, it operates in the $1-10 \mu \mathrm{m}$ wavelength range. The design’s effectiveness for dual-band infrared emission is analyzed using the finite element method in the frequency domain. The terahertz absorption peaks (89% and 65%) are detected, characterized by narrow line widths and significant absorption coefficients at discrete resonance frequencies ($1.54 \mu \mathrm{~m}$, and $6.1 \mu \mathrm{~m}$). Notably, the temperature-dependent variations in IR stealth capabilities are illustrated, achieving a remarkable reduction in infrared radiation signatures at 750K within specific atmospheric windows, exceeding 95.90% and 95.47%, without significant heat dissipation in the non-atmospheric window. Comprehensive parametric studies, varying patch structures to circular and triangular shapes with consistent dimensions, reveal the trade-offs between absorption bandwidth, efficiency, and spectral radiation. These findings provide key insights for developing advanced metamaterial absorbers with applications in electromagnetic stealth and thermal dissipation management.

articleTitle: Enhancing Border Surveillance Efficiency through Edge Computing and Anomaly Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This research work focuses on enhancing the efficiency of border surveillance through the integration of edge computing and advanced anomaly detection algorithms. By processing data locally at the edge, the system reduces the latency and bandwidth requirements associated with transmitting large volumes of sensor data to centralized servers. Furthermore, the research examines the impact of edge computing on energy consumption in Wireless Sensor Networks (WSNs). This reduction is achieved by minimizing data transmission and leveraging local computation, thereby prolonging the lifespan of the network and improving the overall efficiency of the surveillance system. The findings of this study underscore the importance of integrating edge computing with advanced anomaly detection algorithms like Isolation Forest in border surveillance systems. This approach not only enhances detection capabilities but also optimizes energy consumption, making it a viable solution for long-term, real-time monitoring of borders.

articleTitle: Design of Various Stacked Configurations of Hexagonal Shaped Microstrip Antennas for Broadband Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this paper, various stacked configurations of hexagonal MSAs are discussed for broadband applications. The simulated results show an impedance bandwidth of 46% for $\mathbf{- 1 0} \mathrm{dB}$ reflection coefficients. A peak gain of 11.2 dBi has been achieved with +- 1dB variations over the entire bandwidth. The front-to-back ratio is improved to 25 dB compared to $\mathbf{1 7} \mathbf{d B}$ for simple HMSA.

articleTitle: Sub-array based Tile Array Antenna for Beam Forming and Multi-Beam Radar Applications in X-Band
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This work asserts the design of a sub-array based tile antenna array for a CW RADAR in X Band. The CW target detection requires beam forming ability with adaptable beam scan area / multiple beam formation. This is achieved by controlling the source of signaling at the tile /sub-array/ element level of a large aperture. The sub-array presented in this work comprises multi-layered uniform-fed antenna elements arranged in a 4 × 4 planar structure, operating over a broad bandwidth of 400 MHz ($10.1-10.5 {GHz}$). The proposed sub-array configuration achieved an impedance matching better than $-10 \mathbf{d B}$, gain of $17.9 \mathbf{d B i}, 3 \mathbf{d B}$ beamwidth of $22.1 \mathbf{d e g}$, and side lobe level $\lt -13 \mathbf{d B}$ over the operating band. The sub-array beam steering performance is demonstrated up to 45°. The sub-array is extended to an 8 × 8 tile array aperture with beam switching configuration S1, S2, S3 & S4, demonstrating four beams from a single array aperture. The sub-array and tile antenna array are fabricated, and the simulated performance is validated through measurement.

articleTitle: A Wrench-Shaped Wideband Monopole Antenna for Wireless Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents a compact wrench-shaped wideband linearly polarized planar monopole antenna. Circular monopole structures are typically employed to offer large bandwidth. To improve the impedance bandwidth, the upper portion of this circular monopole structure is modified by etching I-shaped open-ended slot, creating a wrench-shaped monopole structure. According to the simulated results, the proposed antenna radiation efficiency is around 75 percent throughout the whole frequency range and its fractional impedance bandwidth is 87.45 percent in the range of 2.82 GHz to 7.24 GHz frequencies. The radiation pattern is omnidirectional with $\mathbf{3 0} \mathbf{d B}$ of cross polarization. The antenna has a maximum realized gain of 4.25 dBi, with an overall dimension of $0.68 \lambda_{0} \times 0.51 \lambda_{0} \times 0.03 \lambda_{0}$ at resonant frequency 5.02 GHz where $\lambda_{0}$ represents the wavelength in free space. Measured results are also used to verify the simulated reflection coefficients. The performance characteristics of the proposed antenna are suitable for the wireless applications.

articleTitle: High-gain Wideband Circularly Polarized Dielectric Resonator Antenna Array for X-Band Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper puts forward a low-profile high gain wideband circularly polarized (CP) dielectric resonator antenna (DRA) array for various X-band applications. Initially, we fed a $1 \times 2$ element DRA with a quarter-wave transformer to achieve circular polarization. The structure has a footprint of $1.46 \lambda \times 0.82 \lambda$ and provides an impedance bandwidth (IBW) of 1.93 GHz (7.66-9.57 GHz) and $1.85 \mathrm{GHz}(10.34-12.2 \mathrm{GHz})$. It is fed via a rectangular slot in order to excite the radiating modes in DRA. Two dielectric materials are placed together to enhance IBW. A maximum gain of 9.8 dBic is attained with an average gain of $7.63 \mathbf{d B i}$ throughout the operating bandwidth. The axial ration bandwidth (ARBW) has also achieve around $1.3 \mathrm{GHz}(10.78-12.08 \mathrm{GHz})$ in upper side of X-band. The proposed DRA has a simple geometry and it is fabricated for experimental validation. The simulated & measured results are in good coherence with each other. The DRA can be put to use in weather forecasting, radar communication, defense & satellite applications.

articleTitle: A Y-Shaped Dielectric Resonator Antenna Excited With a Microstrip-Fed Aperture For Multiband Circular Polarization
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: The paper introduces a novel antenna design featuring a circularly polarized Y-shaped dielectric resonator (DRA). The proposed DRA is excited by a diagonally oriented asymmetric cross-shaped slot and fed via a microstrip line. The asymmetry in the cross-shaped slot and orientation of Y-shaped DRA generate circular polarization at multiple frequency bands. The antenna structure is analyzed using commercially available EM simulation software, and a parametric study is discussed in the paper. The proposed DR antenna structure demonstrates a $3-\mathrm{dB}$ axial ratio bandwidth of $1.7 \%(7.69-7.83 \mathrm{GHz}), 3.37 \%(8.27-8.55 \mathrm{GHz}) \&$ $1.4 \%(8.78-8.91 \mathrm{GHz})$ and impedance bandwidth of $2.2 \%$ (7.707.88) and $8.9 \%$ (8.22-9.00) has been achieved for overlapping circularly polarized band.

articleTitle: Design and sensitivity studies of 4D Radar Waveguide antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: 4D Radar is high-resolution, long-range sensor technology that identifies the elevation information of the object in addition to measuring range, azimuth, and velocity. The key technology in 4D radar is to use waveguide antennas. The trend is to make this antenna by SMT soldering 3 to 4 injection molded plates that are metallized either by vacuum metallization or electroplating. The automotive industries are very specific about the 4D radar antenna material requirement. SABIC’s LNP<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">™</sup> THERMOCOMP<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">™</sup> material portfolio provides material solutions for 4D imaging radar waveguide antennas. Compared to incumbent thermoplastic materials, the LNP<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">™</sup> THERMOCOMP<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">™</sup> materials provides additional benefits of lower warpage, lower CLTE, higher operating temperature and SMT capable which meets the key requirement for the next generation radar antenna. In this paper various simulation studies were carried out to understand the antenna design/architecture and demonstrate effects of various manufacturing sensitivities such as warpage, airgap, CLTE, etc. on the antenna performance. Through sensitivity analysis, we showcase LNP<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">™</sup> THERMOCOMP<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">™</sup> materials advantage in 4D Radar antenna applications.

articleTitle: Real-Time Direction of Arrival Tracking of Drone Utilising Radio Frequency Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Drone/RF-emitter tracking finds many applications from commercial to strategic. This paper presents digital beamforming with phased array antennas to estimate the Direction of Angle of a radio frequency (RF) source. This technique was realized using an FPGA-based setup of Software-Defined Radio receivers. This paper presents a comprehensive drone tracking system, starting from the RF front end and employing a monopulse tracking algorithm.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of a Compact Filtenna for C Band Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents novel design and simulation of a filtenna system for C Band applications. A rectangular shaped patch, end-coupled microstrip slow wave resonator, and a feeding microstrip line are integrated to form the filtenna. The proposed filtenna configuration has total bandwidth of 1.464 GHz with higher selectivity. The Filtenna is implemented on FR4 substrate with dielectric constant of 4.4 and thickness of 1.6 mm. The optimal VSWR and gain of filtenna are 1.0829 and 8.444 dB respectively at 7.635 GHz frequency. This integration of filter and antenna leads to compact size $(56 \mathrm{mmx} 50 \mathrm{~mm})$ of overall design with improved system performance suitable for $\mathbf{C}$ Band applications such as weather radar system, telemedicine, satellite communication etc.

articleTitle: GNLMD-Net: Gaussian Non-Local Means Despeckling Network for ISAR images
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Inverse Synthetic Aperture Radar (ISAR) Imaging is severely affected by speckle noise, leading to the targets in the generated ISAR images being obscured/unidentified. Because of the multiplicative property of speckle noise, it is difficult to remove it. This paper presents a convolution neural network called Gaussian Non-Local Means Despeckling Network (GNLMD-Net) aided by Gaussian non-local means filtering to remove the speckle noise from the ISAR images. The experimental results show that the proposed networks perform better than the existing methods in the literature. The proposed model without the Gaussian non-local means filtering is also used for comparison to show its effectiveness.

articleTitle: Effect of resonator-coupled control line on microwave transmon qubit gate operations
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper investigates the effect of a resonator-coupled microwave control line on transmon qubit operations. It is shown that introducing an intermediate resonator and appropriately positioning the qubit along the length of the microwave control line increases the relaxation-time at the qubit resonant frequency, which is highly desirable for executing high-fidelity quantum operations reliably. It is further highlighted that even though an intermediate resonator increases the qubit relaxation-time, it causes pulse-broadening of the microwave control signal leading to non-ideal quantum gate operations.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of n8 and n106 UHF Band High Power Inverted Doherty Power Amplifier
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this article, the design and implementation of a high peak power Inverted Doherty Power Amplifier (IDPA) are demonstrated for n8 and n106 UHF applications. The study explores how the low values of the required optimum impedances for input and output of high-power devices can utilized to extract the maximum output power and efficiency since lower characteristic impedance transmission lines are wider to realize the matching network if they are purely resistive. In this paper, these bulky lines are replaced with higher characteristic impedance loaded by shunt capacitors to reduce the aerial dimensions of the transmission lines. The proposed IDPA achieves a high peak output power of 57.1-57.6 dBm with a Drain Efficiency (DE) of 68-76% over the 850-975 MHz frequency range and 51-65% at 50.6 dBm output back-off power.

articleTitle: A-Sandwich Tangent Ogive Radome Operating in X-Band for Airborne Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this paper a Tangent Ogive Radome has been proposed which operates in the X-Band frequency range of 812 GHz. The proposed Radome consists of an A-Sandwich structure which consists of two skins with high dielectric constants and a core in between them with a low dielectric constant as compared to the skin. The skin of the Radome has been made using Quartz Cyanate Ester with $\varepsilon=3.2, \rho=1198$ $\mathrm{Kg} / \mathrm{m}^{3}$ and core consists of Rohacell-110WF with $\varepsilon=1.16$, $\rho=110 \mathrm{Kg} / \mathrm{m}^{3}$. An FSS structure has also been introduced between the skin and core on both sides to reject frequencies that do not fall in the desired operating spectrum. The FSS structure incorporated in the Radome structure resembles a split ring resonator structure. For testing the characteristics of the Radome material, a $10 \times 10 \mathrm{~mm}^{2}$ unit cell has been designed with core and skin material to evaluate the desired operating frequency by analyzing the $S_{11}$ of the unit cell. The simulation and Design have been done using ABAQUS and CST (Computer Simulation Technology).

articleTitle: Cavity Backed Dual-Band Polarization Reconfigurable Slot Antenna for RFID Readers
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper proposes a low-profile printed cavity-backed slot antenna suitable for Radio Frequency Identification (RFID) readers with polarization reconfigurability. The designed antenna can switch the antenna’s polarization between left-hand circular polarization (LHCP) and right-hand circular polarization (RHCP). The polarization reconfiguration is achieved by using PIN diodes. The operational bands for the proposed antenna are the UHF RFID band and the $2.4 \mathbf{G H z}$ ISM band. The backing of the cavity ensures the directivity of the proposed antenna into the desired direction making it useful for Indoor/Outdoor RFID applications. The measured performance showed the effectiveness of the proposed antenna.

articleTitle: Design of a High Power S-band Multiple-Beam Klystron
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Design of a 6 MW, S-band Multiple-beam Klystron (MBK) is presented in this paper. The cold circuit design of the cavity and coupling circuits has been carried out. 3D Particle-In-Cell (PIC) simulations have been performed to compute the RF performance of the MBK. 3D PIC simulation indicates that a stable output power of 6 MW at the desired operating frequency can be achieved with the proposed design. An electronic efficiency of about 45%, with a gain of about 58 dB could be achieved with the proposed design.

articleTitle: Radiated Mode Characterization of NISAR in CATF-An Overview
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: NASA-ISRO Synthetic Aperture Radar (NISAR), a joint mission between NASA and ISRO has undergone various phases of testing and is gearing up for launch from Indian spaceport Sriharikota. It is a unique and first of its kind earth-observation dual frequency radar imaging satellite with a 12-day repeat cycle which aims to provide unprecedented observations of Earth’s surface. The science data generated from this mission helps researchers to understand phenomena like glaciers movement, land-slides, earthquakes etc. A critical aspect of its operation is the characterization of payload performance in radiated mode ensuring the spacecraft’s communication systems efficiency and minimizing interference with other electronic systems. In this paper, an overview on different configurations of NISAR observatory, challenges faced and details on various radiated mode tests of L & S-SAR payloads, at compact antenna test facility (CATF) is presented.

articleTitle: Widebeam Four-element Filtering Magneto-electric Dipole MIMO Antenna for X/Ku-bands
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this paper, a four-element filtering ME-dipole MIMO antenna with high isolation and wide beamwidth has been achieved. The filtering ME-dipole antenna is composed of magnetic and electric dipoles coupled with a modified dual H-shaped slot (two inner and two outer slots), which provides impedance bandwidth from 10.8 GHz to 14.8 GHz. The dual radiation nulls are also observed in the ME-dipole antenna, which is explained using traditional transmission line theory. Also, inner H-shaped slot is inserted on the ground to achieve additional null, which is responsible for anti-parallel surface current and hence no radiation. The proposed MIMO antenna (using the same element) is positioned orthogonally with an isolation of more than 25 dB.

articleTitle: Two-Dimensional Beam Scanning using Transmitarray Antenna for X-band Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this research a pyramidal horn feed two dimensional (2-D) transmitarray aperture is proposed for X-band applications. A novel circular patch embedded in circular ring printed on both top and bottom layer of substrate and a shorting via in the center is designed and numerically validated. The proposed transmitarray antenna is designed with five different unit-cell. An overall phase difference of 174° while maintaining a high transmission magnitude of more than $\mathbf{7 0 \%}$ at 9.74 GHz is realized. Transmitarray aperture is constructed using $5 \times 5$ unit-cell with varying size of the central patch for independent control over transmission amplitude and phase. The novel designed aperture realizes the beam-scanning in both the elevation $\left(-19^{\circ}\right.$ to $\left.-56^{\circ}\right)$ and azimuthal plane (+75° to +157°) by varying the angle of feed antenna $\left(-30^{\circ}\right.$ to $\left.30^{\circ}\right)$. The simulated results in the form of transmission amplitude and phase response, shows its significance in designing the compact, high gain, low side-lobe-level (SLL), easy fabrication, and low cost transmitarray antenna. The beam-scanning in the form of 2-D polar plot and 3-D gain pattern proves the efficacy and usefulness of the proposed idea for X-band beam-scanning applications.

articleTitle: Antenna Arrays with Time-Modulation for Generating Beams in Two Directions at Harmonic Frequencies and Scanning Capabilities
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A technique for beamforming and scanning in time-modulated linear antenna arrays (TMLAAs) by sideband patterns is presented in this paper. Cost-effective beam scanning across various angles is enabled through asymmetric timing schemes. By managing groups of array elements to shift the phase center unidirectionally, comprehensive scanning coverage is achieved without affecting the main beam. Additionally, the technique is applied to enhance beamforming for secure single-channel communication by reducing sideband levels using element groups. The study of a 10-element linear array offers thorough findings and comparisons that demonstrate the success of the approach. This research provides a feasible method for safe and economical beamforming and scanning in wireless networks.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of Compound Reconfigurable Antenna for IRNSS Band Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this paper, a compound reconfigurable microstrip patch antenna with multi-functional characteristics is investigated for the Indian Regional Navigation Satellite System (IRNSS) band applications. The proposed antenna consists of a three layer and arranged in stacked configuration. The lower and upper radiating patch is printed on Layer 1 and Layer 2, respectively, and fed with quad coaxial probes. RF PIN diodes loaded octagonal parasitic ring is placed on Layer 3 for pattern reconfiguration. By controlling the switching mechanism of RF PIN diodes, the proposed antenna reconfigures the pattern beamwidth in a highly variable environment. The frequency and polarization is reconfigured by appropriately selecting the coaxial probes and providing equal and progressive phase difference of ± 90°. The suggested antenna can reduce interference by lowering beamwidth by 6 – 8 dB close to the horizon.

articleTitle: High Gain Decagon shaped Tri-Band Patch Antenna for K/Ka band Satellite Communications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Compatibility plays a major role in our modern life as it fosters innovation and flexibility in development. In this paper tri-band, decagon-shaped is designed for the size of 12 mm x 12 mm. To achieve the multiband a small decagon with a length of 3.5mm is slotted from the outer decagon patch antenna with a circular center patch of radius 1.5mm with a rectangle is used to connect the outer decagon. Applications involving satellite communication in the K,-Ka-band are the focus of the proposed antenna. The decagon-shaped patch antenna on the RT Duroid Rogers 5880 substrate measures 12 mm x 12 mm overall and has a 1.5 mm height. The designed antenna resonated for three frequencies which are 23GHz, 30.9GHz, and 37.5GHz. The proposed DSPA achieves steady and symmetric radiation with a peak gain of 6.1dBi at 23GHz, 9.5dBi at 30.9GHz, and 6.3dBi at 37.5GHz. The suggested antenna structures gain, radiation pattern, VSWR, reflection coefficient, and field distribution are among the antenna properties that can be simulated and examined using HFSS software. The suggested antenna is ideally suited for wireless applications that demand small dimensions, increased directivity, high gain, and exceptional radiation characteristics.

articleTitle: Dual Band Dual Polarised Stacked Reflectarray Antenna at Ku-Band for GEO TT&C on-orbit Application
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this paper, a light weight, dual linearly polarized stacked microstrip reflectarray antenna for Ku-Band satellite on-orbit telemetry, tracking and commanding (TT&C) application that can be placed on Earth Viewing (EV) side of GEO satellite is presented. Unit element that will suit both downlink and uplink frequencies which are separated by ratio of 1.15 is chosen and reflectarray is generated based on optimal phase value compensation technique. Simulated peak gain of 26.7 dB is achieved for downlink frequency with cross polarization of 28 dB. At uplink frequency, simulated peak gain of 27.3 dB is achieved with cross polarization of 28 dB.

articleTitle: Millimeter-wave slotted metal cavity resonator circular polarized antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A multi-layered circularly polarized all-metal slotted waveguide antenna is demonstrated in this work. The design utilizes an array of $3 \times 3$ crossed dipole-shaped slots on the top wall of a rectangular resonator cavity. This resonator cavity in the back end of the aperture antenna is fed by a standard rectangular metal waveguide for operation in the $\mathbf{K}_{a}$-band. The antenna has been designed from low-cost aluminum metal using conventional micromachining. A broadside gain in excess of 14 dBi, impedance bandwidth more than 9%, and axial ratio bandwidth greater than 2% centered at 30 GHz has been measured which closely matches the simulated expectations. The proposed antenna is easy-to-assemble and robust in design which can find application in harsh environment conditions.

articleTitle: A Compact Microstrip Band-pass Filter for S/C-band Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents a compact planar ultrawideband (UWB) band-pass filter (BPF). Initially, it employs a compact BPF with a reversible notched band to reject unwanted signals. The second phase entails determining and establishing the conventional microstrip feed’s input impedance at a fixed value of 50 ohms. Then, to eliminate the unwanted signal, a triangleshaped patch is etched from an L-shaped parallel linked transmission line. The bottom part of the BPF receives grounding. The BPF is designed, simulated, and fabricated in the laboratory. The measured fractional impedance bandwidth of 4.42 and 25.83%, minimum insertion loss of 1.40 and 0.32 dB, and minimum total loss of 15 and 8%, along with flat group delay at first and second resonant frequencies, respectively. Notably, BPF exhibits minimal loss, exceptionally low distortion, and acceptable speed. It demonstrates that the simulation and experimental results support the conclusions. The proposed BPF is suitable for S/C-band applications.

articleTitle: Tweaked Triangular Monopole Antennas for Wide Band Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive study on the design and performance of tweaked triangular monopole antennas, highlighting their enhanced operational characteristics and potential applications. The paper focuses on modifications in the traditional triangular monopole design aimed at improving impedance bandwidth and overall compactness. Through a combination of theoretical analysis, numerical simulations, and experimental validations, this paper demonstrates that specific geometric alterations such as chopping the vertex of triangular monopole significantly enhances the bandwidth of the antenna by nearly 8 times.
