Another modified configuration, Orthogonal Tweaked Triangular Monopole Antenna is discussed which gives better omni-directional radiation pattern along with increased bandwidth. The findings reveal that these tweaked designs offer a superior balance of broad frequency coverage and miniaturization.

articleTitle: Design of a Distributed Coupled-Line Nonreciprocal Bandpass Filter with Constant Insertion Loss and Tunable Phase Shift via Hybrid Coupler
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This work presents a unique microwave design integrating band pass filtering (BPF), unidirectional transmission/isolation, and continuously programmable phase shifting into a single system. The spatio-temporal modulation of progressively shifted AC signals modulates the resonance frequencies of the coupled-line-based BPF resonators, thereby enabling propagation of radio frequency (RF) signals in one direction (e.g., from port 1 to port 2) and substantially suppressing the propagation in the other direction. A hybrid coupler is incorporated to enable controllable phase shifting with almost constant insertion loss throughout the design. The proposed microstrip-based nonreciprocal bandpass filter with variable phase shift is designed and simulated at 2.4 GHz. In the forward direction, the insertion loss is 3.7 dB, exhibiting nearly constant insertion loss across all phase tuning states, as electromagnetic simulations show. On the other hand, the isolation in the opposite direction is as high as 24.3 dB at the centre frequency. Return loss is 33.1 dB at the centre frequency. The control voltage ranges for which the phase shifting changes are between 1 V and 10 V, from 179 degrees to -105.6 degrees. Combining several RF signal processing operations into a single RF component, this nonreciprocal filter with a tunable phase shifter opens the door for extremely compact RF front-ends

articleTitle: A Low Profile Planar Metasurface for Near-Field Focusing
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Electromagnetic (EM) wave focusing using metasurface at near-field with the phase compensation method has emerged as a cutting-edge approach for concentrating EM waves at a specific location. A novel near-field focusing (NFF) metasurface design for EM wave concentration is presented in this paper. The proposed metasurface includes $16 \times 16$ array of unit cells which are further categorized in $8 \times 8$ supercells. Each supercells are designed such that they introduce specific phase differences to the reflected wave from that supercell. The basic unit cell consists of a crossed shape with an arc-shaped metallic resonating structure placed on a metal-backed F4B substrate. By employing phase compensation techniques, each supercell of the metasurface is uniquely designed to achieve near-field focusing at 11 GHz at coordinates of $(0,0,100) \mathrm{mm}$. The proposed NFF planar metasurface provides an efficient means of EM wave concentration with potential application in both medical and engineering fields.

articleTitle: Design and Optimization of Featherweight, UltraThin, Flexible PET/CNF/PU Multilayered Sandwich Structure for Absorption-Dominant EMI Shielding
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In the present work, thin, lightweight, and flexible multi-layer sandwich structure (FMSS) nanocomposite is designed and developed for next-generation EMI shielding which can be used in complex environments and conformal surfaces. Such type of FMSS nanocomposite is fabricated by encapsulating the carbon nanofiber (CNF) between the polyethylene terephthalate (PET) and polyurethane (PU). FMSS has tri-layered structure which work as an absorber-reflector-absorber. The $2 \mathrm{wt} \%$ CNF (FMSS2) displays both enhancement in the conductivity and shielding effectiveness $(S E T) ~ i n ~ t h e ~ \mathrm{X}$-band. The maximum SET of $\mathbf{- 2 4. 8 0} \mathrm{dB}$ is observed for FMSS2 at just 0.15 mm thickness. The micrographs and electrical conductivity of the fabricated FMSS are explored further for the absorption dominating mechanism for EMI shielding. The stacked layers of FMSS2 (0.3 mm thick) display the maximum $S E S T_{T}$ of $\mathbf{- 3 2. 6 1 ~ d B}$, showing high resistance towards two hours of water sonication, bending horizontally/vertically, and 1000 mechanical bending cycles. The CST simulation was performed in at $8.2-12.4 \mathrm{GHz}$ using the materials microwave properties and $S E_{T}$ is verified numerically with the experimental values. The fabricated FMSS are flexible, lightweight, thin and showing advancement in the $S E_{T}$ values can be used in conformal electronic packaging and coating in civil, defense, and aerospace applications.

articleTitle: 1.5-bit Passive RIS for Single Beam Anomalous Reflection
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Conventional reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (RISs) or anomalous reflectors are known to use two or more bits to reconfigure the reflected beam towards a desired direction, essentially using four or more states to represent the phase distribution on the surface. In this work, a 1.5-bit (three state) gradient metasurface based passive RIS has been proposed to provide single anomalous reflection for normal incidence. The unit cell design is simple with only one parameter to distinguish between the three states. The $18 \times 18$-unit cell RIS provides a narrow reflected beam at the desired direction of +34° with a measured beamwidth of 12.5°. The sidelobes are lower than 10 dB and the level of the undesired reflection is 13.22dB. This RIS can find its application in providing connectivity to a stationary target with a blocked line-of-sight path.

articleTitle: Two-Port Elliptical Shaped Monopole MIMO Antenna Array with High Isolation using DGS Technique
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A compact and symmetrical monopole antenna with an elliptical-shaped patch is initially designed. The designed monopole antenna is further converted into two-port MIMO type with small edge-to-edge distance of 0.14 lambda. The overall size of the proposed two-port MIMO antenna is $60 \mathrm{~mm} \times 30 \mathrm{~mm} \times 0.9 \mathrm{~mm}$. The proposed antenna operates in the n78 (3.3-3.8 GHz) 5G band. Defected Ground Structure (DGS) technique is used to enhance the port-to-port isolation between two antenna elements. The isolation remain $\gt22 \mathrm{~dB}$ over the entire band of operation with $\mathbf{- 3 6. 8 d B}$ of peak isolation. Index Terms-monopole antenna, two-antenna MIMO, isolation enhancement, defected ground structure (DGS)

articleTitle: Computerised Numerical Control Machined Fresnel Zone Lens for Efficient Radiative Microwave WPT at 5.8 GHz
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this paper, the authors fabricated and tested the Fresnel Zone lens (FZL) using subtractive manufacturing (CNC machining) at 5.8 GHz. The FZL is machined from the low dielectric loss polymer, i.e., Polypropylene (PP) $\left(\epsilon_{r}=2.2, \tan \delta=1.39 \times 10^{-3} \pm\right.$ $2 \times 10^{-4}$) having an overall diameter of 307.58 mm ($5.94 \lambda$ where $\lambda=51.72 \mathrm{~mm}$). The focal point is $\mathbf{8 0}$ cm from the aperture of the conical horn antenna. A total of 8 subzones (P = 8) for the single full zone ($N=1$) is used taking into consideration the optimal size and fabrication facility. A $4 \times 4$ patch array is used on the receiver side to measure the received power. The measurements are done at 2 m from the horn antenna aperture which is in the Fresnel zone of the Horn+FZL. An improvement of 5.6 dB in the received power is achieved with this arrangement. The use of CNC manufacturing is advantageous for the design of FZL with higher overall dimensions due to single block manufacturing and the homogeneous $\epsilon_{r}$ and $\tan \delta$ across the FZL.

articleTitle: Improved RF Subsurface Imaging Under Complex Terrain by Synergistic Use of Radar and LiDAR
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: The conventional Ground Penetrating Radar (GPR) usually requires the system to be in direct contact with the ground surface, which becomes challenging to be utilized for subsurface imaging of undulating and risk-prone terrain. The subsurface image of the terrain in this kind of situation is typically obtained using the synthetic aperture radar (SAR) algorithms by assuming a homogenous half-space with a planar interface. However, such types of complex terrains are non-planar in most situations. In this work, a novel LiDAR assisted RF imaging methodology is proposed to retrieve the subsurface image of complex terrains by considering their non-planarity and utilizing a non-contacting measurement procedure. The effectiveness of this approach is demonstrated through laboratory experiments carried out using an automated subsurface imaging testbed with a monostatic radar and a co-located LiDAR sensor. The conventional imaging algorithm is successfully modified to integrate both radar and LiDAR data to compensate for the terrain induced errors. Comparative study of results from the modified and the conventional imaging algorithm reveals improvement in reconstruction of the target’s geometry, its reflection amplitude as well as accurate localization. The proposed scheme can potentially be utilized for various real world applications such as the rockmass inspection in underground mines.

articleTitle: Ultrawideband Metasurface Microwave Absorber based on Laser Induced Graphene
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this work, the laser induced graphene (LIG) based novel metasurface structure for microwave absorber (MWA) applications is proposed. The measured performance of the proposed absorber is outstanding, as it provides 90% absorption bandwidth ranging from 8 GHz to 11.5 GHz covering 87.5% of X -band. The proposed metasurface structure is designed and simulated using the CST Studio, and various structural parameters are optimized to achieve better absorption performance. It is observed that the sheet resistance of LIG is an important property, and hence a detailed analysis is carried out to investigate its effect on the performance of the MWA. The unit cell of the designed structure is especially chosen to make it polarization and incident angle insensitive, thereby making it more attractive from practical perspective. Finally, the prototype based on the optimized design is fabricated and tested for X-band, and a good agreement is observed between the simulated and the measured response. The proposed LIG based absorber working in X-band, appears to be a viable low cost alternative for applications in the stealth technology and satellite communication etc.

articleTitle: A Novel Bi-directional Dipole Antenna Array for UAV-Based Back-haul Link at C-band Frequency Range
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A novel aperture-efficient bi-directional antenna is proposed to support a back-haul link for unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) in the C-band frequency range. The bi-directional antenna radiation is achieved through a double-sided E-dipole structure. This E-dipole combines two vertical stubs on both sides of the antenna. The stubs are slanted at 45 degrees, making them perpendicular to each other and forming an L-shaped structure when viewed from the top, thereby achieving elliptical polarization (EP). The proposed 5G antenna array is designed for dual resonating frequency bands n79 and n96, with fractional bandwidths (FBW) of $\mathbf{2 0 \%}$ (4.2-5.12 GHz) and $\mathbf{3 5 \%}$ ($5.2-7.37 \mathbf{G H z}$), respectively. Unlike traditional designs that utilize dipole elements, the optimized dipole antenna array can attain a bidirectional distribution of broadside gains of $25.1 \mathbf{~ d B i}$, while maintaining a smaller size of $41 \times 41 \mathrm{~cm}^{2}(5.47 \lambda \times 5.47 \lambda)$ with a side lobe level (SLL) better than 21 dB maintaining radiation efficiency more than 80%.

articleTitle: A Modified Octagonal Ring-Loaded Cross Dipole FSS for mmWave Electromagnetic Shielding
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper discusses a novel design of an ultrathin conformal modified octagonal ring-loaded cross dipole frequency selective surface (MORCD-FSS). The proposed FSS offers multifunctional properties such as in-band passband and out-of-band electromagnetic interference (EMI) shielding. Equivalent circuit model analysis has been performed for insight working and validating the simulated results. In addition, the conformal analysis of the FSS has also been carried out on the cylindrical surface at different radii to check its shielding effectiveness (SE) performance. The proposed MPRCD-FSS offers a 3-dB passband response from 13.5 GHz to 24.6 GHz and 26.62 GHz to 29.5 GHz, respectively. Moreover, out-of-band EMI shielding has been observed from 8.3 GHz to 11.55 GHz (SE $=87.3 \text{dB}$), from 25.5 GHz to $26.4 \text{GHz}(\text{SE}=44.10 \text{dB})$ and 31.2 GHz and $35 \text{GHz}(\text{SE}=76.6 \text{dB})$.

articleTitle: Metamaterial-loaded MIMO Antenna on Swastika Substrate for DSRC Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This study introduces a pioneering method to enhance isolation in a metamaterial-loaded multiple-input-multiple-output (MIMO) antenna system for DSRC (Dedicated short-range communication) band applications by adopting a Swastika-shaped substrate instead of the conventional square one. By integrating metamaterial-based CSRRs (Complementary split ring resonators) into MIMO antenna designs, precise control over electromagnetic responses is achieved, facilitating the development of compact and efficient antennas. Renowned for their ability to suppress surface waves, CSRRs often lead to improved isolation within MIMO antennas. Focused on the design and testing of a $4 \times 4$ MIMO antenna operating in the dedicated short-range communication band (5.850-5.925 GHz) for vehicular communication, this research demonstrates a significant enhancement in isolation with the Swastika-shaped substrate, while maintaining other antenna performance parameters.

articleTitle: Novel All-Metal Dual-Band Phase-Shifting Cells: A Generic Design and Their Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Phase-shifting cells are the building blocks of radio frequency (RF) components that allow for the flexible manipulation of electromagnetic waves. They are typically constructed based on a 360° phase-range database, which expands the search space and necessitates significant computational simulations. This further complicates the design challenges of cells employed for dual-band applications. A general design approach for an all-metal dual-band cell is presented in this article. First, databases for phase vs. magnitude operating at two selected frequencies are built. From there, every phase pair combination functioning at dual bands can be generated without simulating and creating a full 360° phase database for each phase pair combination. These cells can be widely employed in creating various RF components, including phase-correction and phase-gradient metasurfaces, transmitarrays, and planar lenses.

articleTitle: A Triple Band Implantable Antenna for Wireless Power Transfer and Bio-Telemetry Application
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A compact triple band muscle implantable antenna is realized at $1.86 \mathbf{G H z}, 2.45 \mathbf{G H z}$ and $5.8 \mathbf{G H z}$ for wireless power transfer (WPT) and bio-telemetry applications. The proposed antenna is made multi-band and compact by loading the top patch with slits and modified Hilbert curve shaped slots. The physical volume of the antenna is $10 \times 10 \times 0.54 \mathrm{~mm}^{3}$ where profile of the antenna is $0.003 \lambda_{0}$ at the lowest resonance frequency. The proposed antenna avoids any use of shorting pin that makes it simple and stable polarized structure for biomedical communication. Moreover, the antenna can be safely used for an maximum input power of 3.5 mW. The performance of the fabricated antenna is measured in the muscle gel environment. A decent agreement of the return loss response is observed amongst the human hand model, phantom model and the invitro environment.

articleTitle: Ground Size Optimization for High Boresight Gain in Offset-Fed Wide Slot Antennas
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents a microstrip-fed wide rectangular slot antenna that achieves improved boresight gain while functioning in the $\mathbf{6 - 8. 5} \mathbf{~ G H z}$ frequency band. The radiation and impedance characteristics of the slot antenna for distinct dimensions of ground plane are examined and analyzed. It is observed that optimizing the ground plane size enhances the gain of a wide rectangular slot antenna. This occurs when direct waves from the slot radiator interfere appropriately with the waves that are diffracted from the ground plane edges. The optimized rectangular slot antenna utilizing an FR-4 substrate, with a slot size of $0.31 \lambda_{0} \times 0.22 \lambda_{0}$, has overall dimensions of $1.2 \lambda_{0} \times \mathbf{0. 7 7} \lambda_{0} \times \mathbf{0. 0 4} \lambda_{0}$, where $\lambda_{0}$ denotes the free-space wavelength at the midpoint frequency of the operating band. Measurements of the fabricated antenna prototype reveal an impedance bandwidth ranging from 5.96 to 8.54 GHz and a bidirectional radiation pattern. The antenna exhibits an average boresight gain of 5.33 dBi within this range, with a gain variation of 1.35 dBi. The key advantage of the proposed method is the precise selection of the ground plane size, which allows for nearly uniform gain improvement across the entire impedance bandwidth, while maintaining a bidirectional radiation pattern.

articleTitle: Parametric Insights into Square Loop-Based Artificial Magnetic Conductors
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This study investigates the band-stop frequency in both Transverse Electric (TE) and Transverse Magnetic (TM) modes by examining a square loop Artificial Magnetic Conductor (AMC) with varying inner edge widths, while keeping the distance between unit cells and their dimensions constant. The analysis focuses on the reflection and transmission characteristics to determine the band-stop frequency, bandwidth, and phase attributes. These insights are critical for the antenna design community, enabling the precise adjustment of the inner edge width to meet specific application requirements. The findings facilitate the selection of appropriate AMC unit cell dimensions, ensuring optimal performance in various electromagnetic environments. This research provides a valuable reference for engineers and designers in the field of antenna technology, aiding in the development of more efficient and tailored electromagnetic solutions.

articleTitle: Dual Polarized Beam Switchable 1-Bit Coded Reflective Metasurface
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this paper, a dual polarized 1-bit coded metasurface is presented. It can electronically steer the beam in both xz and yz planes in the desired direction. The unit cell of the metasurface consists of ring loaded square patch with two PIN diodes connected across the gap between ring and patch in x and y direction. It has a ground plane sandwiched in-between two Rogers 5880 substrate layers. Furthermore the RF is isolated from DC using properly designed radial stubs. A phase difference of 180 -degree has been achieved at 6.32 GHz between on and off conditions for both polarisation. An array of $16 \times 16$ such unit cell elements has been used to make the metasurface with different coding schemes. A good agreement is observed between the MATLAB simulated radiation pattern and full-wave simulated far field radiation pattern.

articleTitle: Substrate Integrated Waveguide Technology Based Cavity Backed Antenna for Millimeter Wave Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) technology-based cavity backed antenna is presented for millimeter wave (mmW) applications. The antenna geometry consists of two layers thickness of 0.508 mm RT/Duroid substrate. The lower level consists of the ring slot inside the SIW cavity and upper layer consist of rectangular patch antenna with a rectangle slot. The antenna is fed at lower layer between SIW structure and ground plane. The patch on upper layer is fed through EM coupling. The simulation results of antenna have a large -10 dB impedance bandwidth of 23.6% with three resonances at $49.2 \mathrm{GHz}, 53.8 \mathrm{GHz}$ and 59.38 GHz. The radiation patterns of antenna at three resonances are observed to be symmetrical with cross polarization level below -30dB. A maximum gain of 5.37 dB is achieved at 49.2 GHz. The proposed antenna would be promising for millimeter wave applications.

articleTitle: A Wideband Quasi Hybrid 180° Circulator for Satellite and Radar Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents a wideband quasi-hybrid 180° circulator ($\mathrm{QH}-\mathrm{C}$) of multiband with maximum isolation, bandwidth using appropriately unified out-of-phase and in-phase dividers the device is formed. The multiband 180° hybrid is employed to attain wideband high isolation between the transmitter and receiver (Tx-Rx). It consists of two layers substrate FR4 of size $44.44 \times 22 \mathrm{~mm}$ with relative permittivity of 4.4, with four ports and ground slot. The hybrid indicates good quality return losses of the in-phase (summation) and out-of-phase (difference) ports throughout the band, as well as a well-balanced power division between the output ports. More than 40 dB separates the difference and summation ports, and the phase characteristics are almost ideal $1 \mathbf{1 8 0}^{\circ}$ and 0°. The multiband QH-C is designed using HFFS software with an operating frequency of $1.2 \mathrm{GHz}, 3.2 \mathrm{GHz}, 4.6 \mathrm{GHz}$ with the bandwidth of 74%, 12%, 14% (L, S, C Band), simulation results indicating promise in satellite, Wi-Fi, WiLAN and radar applications.

Author Keywords: out of phase and in phase

articleTitle: Dual Band Polarization Insenstive Metasuface Absorber
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A Metasurface Absorber exhibiting dual-band behavior across the C band has been proposed in this article. Metasurface unit cell having dimensions $0.17 \lambda_{0} \times$ $0.17 \lambda_{0} \times 0.03 \lambda_{0} \mathrm{~mm}^{3}$ ($\lambda_{0}$ is free space wavelength at lower resonance frequency) was developed on a Glass Epoxy FR4 dielectric substrate, achieving remarkable absorptivity and impedance matching properties exceeding 90% for absorption peaks at 4.4, and 6.8 GHz. Simulated results demonstrate stable absorption across incidence angles for both TE and TM polarizations, making it polarization insensitive at the two resonant bands.. The proposed metasurface absorber demonstrates very low radar crosssection, making it suitable for stealth technology, military aircraft, and ships. Additionally, it finds applications in wireless communication systems such as WLAN, Wi-Fi, 5G networks and Weather Radar System etc.

articleTitle: Design of a High Power and High Gain Slotted Array Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper describes the design of a high power and high gain slotted waveguide array antenna operating in the S-band. The radiating slots have been created in the narrow wall of the standard WR-284 rectangular waveguide. A common feed with a power divider has been designed to feed all the slotted waveguide sections with the same phase. Simulations of the antenna element and whole array antenna have been carried out in CST studio. Simulation results of the array antenna provide a gain of $\sim 41 \text{dB}$ with beamwidth of 0.4° and 2° in azimuth and elevation, respectively.

articleTitle: Design of Dual Band Circular Slot Patch Antenna on Various Textile Substrates for Biomedical Applications in Sub-6GHz
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: The dual-band microstrip circular slot patch antenna designed for sub- $\mathrm{6} \mathrm{~ G H z}$ biomedical applications is presented in this study along with its analysis and design. Using the HFSS software, the antenna with dimensions of $58.8 \times 41.5$ $\times 1.6 \text{mm}^{3}$ was constructed. The functioning frequencies of the antenna were noted as follows: 2.41 GHz and 3.70 GHz for Jean, 2.43 GHz and 3.70 GHz for Lycra, 2.40 GHz and 3.63 GHz for Teflon, 2.81 GHz and 4.18 GHz for Felt. The sub-6 GHz band, which is particularly beneficial for biomedical applications, offers several advantages, including improved penetration through biological tissues, better signal stability, and lower latency. These features make it ideal for real-time health monitoring and telemetry. The performance of each substrate was evaluated to determine the most suitable material for the designed antenna. In addition to the operating frequencies, other performance parameters, such as return loss, gain, bandwidth, and radiation patterns, were also analysed. The results indicated that each substrate provided distinct advantages, in terms of gain and performance consistency.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of Interconnected Square Ring FSS for C-band Shielding Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this article, an interconnected square Ring FSS is presented. The FSS unit cell consists of an interconnected square ring enclosed by an outer square loop which provides shielding at the C-band frequency range. The symmetric structure of the proposed FSS design offers polarization-insensitive characteristics, ensuring a stable response at normal and oblique incidence for both TE and TM modes. It provides an angular stability of 50° for both TE and TM modes. The FSS unit cell size is $0.136 \lambda_{0} \times 0.136 \lambda_{0}$, where $\lambda_{0}$ denotes the free space wavelength at the lowest resonant frequency.

articleTitle: Estimation of Antenna Factor for Printed Circular Monopole Antenna for EMI/EMC Testing
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Traditional antennas used for EMC testing, such as log-periodic, horn, and biconical antennas, often present challenges due to their large size, which complicates setup. Additionally, many of these antennas have limited bandwidth. To address these issues, a proposed solution is an ultra-wideband Printed Circular Monopole Antenna designed to operate across the 0.5 to 6 GHz range for EMC testing. Printed antennas, typically made on FR4 substrates, are highly cost-effective and well-suited for UWB technology-based, low-cost systems. The design, simulation, and laboratory measurements of this antenna have been completed to determine key parameters such as return loss and gain. The antenna factor of these monopoles has been analyzed for use in EMC testing, as it plays a crucial role in ensuring accurate measurements. The antenna factor relates the incident electromagnetic field to the antenna’s voltage output, making precise calibration vital for reliable testing.

articleTitle: Design of An Efficient GaN Power Amplifier Using Harmonic Suppression Technique
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this paper, a compact, high-efficiency power amplifier is designed and realized in the frequency range of 290 MHz to 320 MHz using a GaN HEMT transistor for satellite communication. The design is accomplished with a stability network, conjugate input matching, and output matching using loadpull analysis to achieve optimum output power and efficiency. To validate the design, a prototype is fabricated on a printed circuit board. The amplifier is analyzed under both small signal and large signal conditions. The measured small signal return loss is better than 13.45 dB, while the gain variation ranges from 23.2 dB to 22.6 dB over the operating frequency. The measured maximum output power is 85 W and power added efficiency is greater than 68 percent. The achieved harmonic suppression is better than 55 dBc for the second and third harmonics and $\mathbf{6 8. 4} \mathbf{d B c}$ for all higher order harmonics.

articleTitle: Cross-Polarization Insensitive 1-bit Unit Cell to Design a Reconfigurable Intelligent Surface for Beam Scanning Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper proposes a new 1-bit unit cell design for Reconfigurable Intelligent Surface (RIS) with beam scanning capability. The designed unit cell has $0.53 \lambda_{0} \times 0.53 \lambda_{0}$ dimension comprising four truncated circular-shaped patches arranged in a cross-shaped pattern and loaded with 4 PIN diodes in orthogonal directions. The unit cell responses can be varied by switching ON/OFF the PIN diodes. It exhibits high reflectivity of $0.95(-0.24 \mathrm{~dB})$ and $0.61(-2.41 \mathrm{~dB})$ in the ON and OFF states, respectively, with a phase difference of 180° between the two states at 6.17 GHz. The proposed unit cell is operable within a frequency range of $6.14-6.21 \mathrm{GHz}$ while maintaining a phase difference of 180°±30+30° and high reflection coefficient. It also exhibits incidence angle independency from -30° to +30+30° for cross-polarized (TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">00</inf> and TM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">00</inf>) waves impinged onto the unit cell’s surface. A $10 \times 10$ array of the proposed unit cell has also been designed to create a RIS that can steer a vertically incident beam from 0° to +22°. A detailed design analysis and parametric response study are presented based on results from the floquet simulation environment.

articleTitle: A Unique Hourglass-shaped Patch Integrated, Compact Monopulse Antenna for Orthogonal Target Detection and Tracking
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents the design and implementation of a compact monopulse antenna utilizing a unique $2 \times 2$ hourglass-shaped patch integrated with a comparator circuit realized by four rat-race coupler. The antenna is designed to operate at a frequency of 10.3 GHz a gain of 12 dB is achieved at the sum port, with azimuthal and elevation difference ports yielding gain of 9.65 dB and 11 dB, respectively. A null depth of $\mathbf{- 2 4} \mathrm{dB},-15 \mathrm{~dB}$ is observed in azimuthal and elevation respectively, indicating precise signal discrimination. The design achieves a fractional bandwidth (FBW) of 2.3%, from 10.24 GHz to 10.485 GHz. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed antenna design in X -band target detection and tracking radar application.

articleTitle: Polarization-Resolved Speckle Correlations in Scattering Birefringent Films
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this work, we experimentally investigate the polarization-resolved speckle cross-correlations in scattering birefringent films fabricated from liquid crystal elastomers (LCE). The order-induced optical birefringence in fabricated samples was confirmed from polarized microscope images of aligned and random LCE films. Thereafter, a comparative evaluation of speckle cross-correlations was performed for a ground glass, random LCE, and aligned LCE films. We find that the polarization information in the speckle correlations is completely lost in random LCE film, while the aligned LCE film preserves partial correlations. Our findings may pave the way for biomedical applications, sensing, and imaging microscopy.

articleTitle: Cavity Backed MIMO Antenna with CSRR Resonator for n257/n258 5G mmWave Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this paper, a compact wideband 2-element cavity backed MIMO antenna is presented for 5G millimeter-wave (mm-wave) applications aiming at n257 and n258 bands. The proposed antenna element is based on a complementary split ring resonator element printed on a low loss dielectric substrate Rogers 5880 of size 22.58 mm × 12.09 mm × 0.79 mm. The design exhibits a 2:1 VSWR response from 26.13 to 28.80 GHz, a peak realized gain of 8.78 dBi, and a radiation efficiency above 97.13% in the presented band. A few MIMO parameters are also investigated, such that channel capacity loss is observed less than 0.3 bits/s/Hz and the envelope correlation coefficient is observed in the range of 0.001 as per ITU standards for the mmwave applications.

articleTitle: Error Analysis & optimisation Techniques in Wide Band T/R Module based 1 X 16 Plank
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This study investigates amplitude and phase errors in a Transmit/Receive (T/R) based 1 X 16 Plank operating in the C-Ku band for radar EW applications. It focuses on mitigating these errors using both Least Squares (LS) and Stochastic Gradient Descent (SGD) optimization strategies. The analysis covers amplitude and phase variations across the 16 Transmit/Receive (T/R) modules in the plank. LS and SGD algorithms are implemented in MATLAB to optimize T/R module performance by minimizing errors across operational frequencies. Simulation results demonstrate significant improvements in Plank performance and robustness in diverse electromagnetic environments. Additionally, the simulations are validated through measured data, reinforcing the findings and validating practical applicability.

articleTitle: Dual-Frequency, Polarization-Dependent Beam Steering With a Novel Phase-Profiled Metasurface
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: For metamaterial-based Reconfigurable Intelligent Surface (RIS) design nowadays, researchers are investigating novel active/passive unit cell geometries, which may offer polarization-diverse performance. This article presents a novel, passive unit cell design which demonstrates controlled phase-reflection performance at both X and Y-polarized modes of operation. The proposed unit cell shape operates at two different frequencies, for the two different polarizations, and keeping the periodicity of the element constant - the other geometric dimensions of the chosen shape can be controlled to achieve suitable phase variation performance during reflection. By controlling its dimensions, two sets of unit cell elements with identical periodicity are obtained to generate the layout of two separate reflecting metasurfaces of the same size, which operate at 7.15 GHz and 30.875 GHz respectively. The controlled beam-tilt performance of the gradient phase-profiled surfaces is validated quantitatively against the calculated beam-tilt as computed using the Generalized Snell’s Law equation. Such a passive, reflective unit cell shape, which is later used to generate phase-profiled RIS layouts for controlled beam-tilt operations, and that individually responds to both the orthogonal polarization modes and supports multi-frequency performance, is rare in literature as per the authors’ understanding.

articleTitle: Design of L band High Power Coaxial line Bandpass Filter With Wideband Harmonic Rejection
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents a design and implementation of L band high power tubular filter. The designed filter consists of high $\mathbf{Q}$ air core inductor, metal dises and dielectric material. Here, fifth order tubular filter having passband frequency ranges from 960 to 1240 MHz is presented. The complete 3D model of the filter is designed, simulated and optimized using ANSYS HFSS. A prototype of the filter is fabricated to validate the design. The measured result shows maximum insertion loss of 1 dB and return loss is better than 10 dB. The measured stopband rejection is better than 54.6 dBc below 550 MHz and better than 76.5 dBc beyond 1700 MHz. The filter offers high selectivity and provides harmonic suppression up to 4 times of the center frequency in the operating band. The experimental results are in good agreement with simulation results. The predicted power handling of filter through simulation is 200 W.

articleTitle: A 4x4 MIMO SIW Antenna for Vehicular Communications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This work introduces a chamfer patch substrate integrated square cavity (SISC) MIMO antenna. One $4 \times 4$ MIMO antenna optimised for the 5.80-6.03 GHz Dedicated Short Range Communication (DSRC) band is used for vehicle communication. The antenna is designed with a SISC construction and has four $50 \Omega$ inset feedlines. Between each element, the envelope correlation coefficient (ECC) is below 0.004, and the diversity gain is 9.99 dB. Furthermore, throughout a-10 dB impedance bandwidth, the antenna exhibits superior gain and radiation efficiency of over 6.73 dBi and 98.5%, respectively. It has a broad range of frequency tuning capabilities. The compact prototype makes it appropriate for vehicle communication, and the isolation between the ports is higher than 18.23 dB.

articleTitle: A Compact Bandpass Filter Based on a Multi-Mode Re-entrant Cavity for 5G Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A bandpass filter utilizing a multi-post, triple-mode re-entrant cavity is developed. This design enables miniaturization without losing bandwidth efficiency by incorporating three modes into a single cavity and precisely adjusting their coupling. This filter is cost-effective, simple to produce, and offers uncomplicated adjustment, correction, and tuning of the bandpass frequency. The filter provides a passband suitable for sub-6GHz 5G applications while filtering out the altimeter frequencies. A passband ranging from 3.4 GHz to 4 GHz was accomplished with excellent rejection from 4.2 GHz to 4.4 GHz.

articleTitle: Design of a Sub-6 GHz Wideband Antenna with Metasurface-Based Gain Enhancement for 5G Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents a new metasurface (MS) antenna design based on a superstrate arrangement with a high gain. The antenna combines a ground plane with a rectangular slot (Defective Ground Structure) and a slotted patch loaded with a stub. The FR4 dielectric creates MS by arranging unit cells in a periodic pattern. A central patch with a C-type pattern and two outer patches with L-type patterns make up the unit cell’s structure. The conventional patch antenna is designed over the FR4 dielectric. A spacer separates the MS from the antenna, which acts as a superstrate. The proposed MS antenna has a figure of eight radiation patterns and offers suitable impedance matching from $2.52-4 \mathrm{GHz}$. Using MS, over $\mathbf{8 0 \%}$ of the gain improvement is achieved. With MS, the antenna achieves a maximum gain of 6.8 dB when operated at 3.7 GHz. The proposed antenna is better suited for 5G Sub 6GHz uses because of its increased efficiency.

articleTitle: A Miniaturized Tunable Dual-band BPF With CABW Using Stub-Loaded Multi-Mode Single Resonator
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents a novel multi-mode single resonator-based dual-band tunable bandpass filter (BPF). The layout is designed with a half-wavelength resonator centrally loaded with stubs. To tune the odd and even mode resonance frequencies, two varactors are connected at the open ends of the half-wavelength resonator that participate in the formation of two different passbands. A centrally loaded stub connected at one end to a varactor tunes only the even mode. The ends of the feed lines are also connected to varactors that produce two different resonance frequencies and these frequencies help create two passbands with dual modes. Additionally, transmission zero is generated next to the passband using fixed capacitors between the input and output feed lines. Individual control over the resonance frequencies helps to achieve constant absolute bandwidth (CABW) tunable BPF to both passbands. An example filter has been designed for two different passbands. The first passband is tuned from 1.58 GHz to 1.68 GHz with a CABW of $90 \pm 3 \mathrm{MHz}$ and an insertion loss of 3.1 dB. The second passband is tuned from 2.16 GH to 2.31 GHz with a CABW of $190 \pm 5 \mathrm{MHz}$ and an insertion loss of 0.9 dB.

articleTitle: Design and Simualtion of Hexagonal Dual Circularly Polarized X-Band Sub-Array With Beam Steering Capability using High Performance Patch Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This article presents the design and simulation of a X-band dual circularly polarized, multilayer microstrip patch antenna characterized by wide bandwidth and low cross-polarization levels. The dual polarization feature is achieved through a 90-degree hybrid aperture coupled with a patch and a slotted ground plane. Dumb-bell shaped slots are employed to enhance cross-polarization isolation & to achieve the lower back radiation levels. The antenna exhibits a return loss greater than 10 dB, with a gain of 8.2 dBi, and cross-polarization isolation exceeding 18 dB within the operational frequency band. The array is designed for a 91 -element hexagonal sub-array functioning in the X -band ($8.0-8.5 \mathrm{GHz}$). The sub-array demonstrates a peak gain of $\mathbf{2 8} \mathbf{d B i}$ and a maximum scan loss of $\mathbf{2. 5} \mathbf{d B}$ for a scan angle of $\mathbf{3 0}$ degrees. This article also includes simulations of the sub-array with beam steering capabilities. This sub-array is intended to be incorporated into a larger array structure for receiving satellite data from LEO satellites.

articleTitle: Realization of MMIC Based Electronically Tunable mm-Wave Local Oscillator Sources for Sub-Harmonically Pumped Receivers at 230 & 345GHz
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents an overview of electronically tuned local oscillator (LO) sources at 112.68 GHz and 169.2 GHz for astronomical applications. In order to maintain signal stability, 50 MHz Temperature Compensated Crystal Oscillator (TCXO) is used as an input reference signal. Phase Locked Loop (PLL) based indirect synthesis technique, followed by frequency multipliers is used for mm-wave LO signal generation. The output of the PLL is further fed to successive signal amplification stages followed by filtering & suitable multiplications stages (Multichip drop-in module (DIM) configuration is used) to generate 37.56 GHz and 28.2 GHz. Finally, Gallium Arsenide (GaAs) Monolithic Microwave Integrated Circuit (MMIC) based frequency multipliers are used for pumping sufficient input power to sub-harmonic mixers at 230 GHz and 345 GHz. All the low frequency modules are fabricated and housed in single package (i.e TCXO, PLL, DIM and frequency multipliers up to Ka-band) whereas Schottky diode based frequency doublers and frequency triplers are fabricated using GaAs substrate and packaged in Copper Tellurium (CuTe) material based housing. The measured final output power and conversion efficiencies of frequency triplers are $12.64 \mathrm{dBm} \& 23 \%$ and $13 \mathrm{dBm} \& 18.2 \%$ at 112.8 GHz and 169.2 GHz respectively.

articleTitle: An Artificial Magnetic Conductor backed Cylindrical Dielectric Resonator Antenna for portable Wireless Communications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A compact Cylindrical Dielectric Resonator Antenna (CDRA) is proposed for the portable wireless communication in this paper. CDRA is in high demand by various smart wireless devices, due the low less, moderate gain and compact size. The proposed antenna structure is realized using simulation followed by fabrication using a high dielectric material ($\varepsilon_{r}=9.9$) alumina on a Rogers RT Duroid substrate $\left(\varepsilon_{r}=2.2\right)$. A microstrip feed line is used to excite antenna for radiation. The CDRA resonates at a frequency of $\sim 2.9 \mathrm{GHz}$ with a $10-\mathrm{dB}$ bandwidth and gain of 250 MHz and 3.3 dBi, respectively. To enhance the gain of the antenna and reduce the back-lobe radiation, an artificial magnetic conductor (AMC) is proposed which can be placed at the back of the antenna. The simulation results show that integration of AMC helps to achieve a gain up to 6.6 dBi and improve the impedance matching, as well. The proposed CDRA can be used in smart portable wireless devices for applications like body-area-network, wireless sensing, and low power automative RADAR.

articleTitle: Non-Invasive Sensor for Hyperglycemia Detection and Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This study presents a novel octagonal-slotted defective ground structure (DGS) patch antenna for noninvasive monitoring of elevated blood glucose (hyperglycemia). The antenna operates at a resonant frequency of 2.4 GHz within the ISM band and features an innovative octagonal slot forming the DGS, resulting in a wide impedance bandwidth from 1.4 $\mathbf{G H z}$ to 2.9 GHz, with a measured $S_{11}$ of $\mathbf{- 1 6 ~ d B}$ and a gain of $3.77 \mathbf{~ d B i}$ at $2.8 \mathbf{~ G H z}$. This antenna is specifically engineered for application on various body parts, including the foot, thumb, and arm, facilitating effective glucose measurement. Simulation and experiments show the antenna can detect blood glucose levels (BGL) between 200 and $500 \mathrm{mg} / \mathrm{dl}$. Notably, the S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf> amplitude variation observed is approximately 11 dB across this glucose range when applied to the human leg, arm, and thumb. These promising results indicate high accuracy in readings, underscoring the potential of this technology for continuous blood glucose monitoring systems. Furthermore, the strong impedance matching between the microwave sensor and the human body enhances the efficacy of glucose detection. This work shows promise for advancing non-invasive blood glucose monitoring and managing hyperglycemia.

articleTitle: Dual Polarized Vivaldi Antenna for Ground Penetrating Radar for Interplanetary Rover
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents a dual polarized vivaldi antenna designed specifically for rover based Ground Penetrating Radar (GPR) systems with polarimetric capability. It integrates the Ultra Wide Band (UWB) behaviour of the vivaldi antenna with dual polarization capabilities to enhance the performance of GPR systems in terms of subsurface imaging. In this configuration, four vivaldi antennas are arranged in a trapezoidal shape to maintain the homogenous pattern at high frequencies. It is combined with square coaxial lines power divider and teflon as well as aluminium support structure to produce rugged hardware for rover based GPR systems. Antenna operates from $0.3 \mathrm{GHz}-3 \mathrm{GHz}$ with a maximum gain of 10.5 dBi and cross-pol isolation better than $\mathbf{2 5 d B}$ while maintaining its performance for both polarizations. Antenna of size $0.24 \lambda \times 0.24 \lambda \times 0.18 \lambda$ ($\lambda$ corresponds to 0.3 GHz) is fabricated to validate its performance. Further, the antenna is incorporated into a rover model to address and account for scattering effects. Time domain analysis of the antenna is carried out by taking three scenarios of two dielectric layers (changing dielectric constant and loss tangent) kept below two antennas (Tx-Rx). A Gaussian modulated bandlimited impulse is transmitted and the impact of dielectric constant and loss tangent is analysed.

articleTitle: Design and Development of Active Frequency Doubler MMIC at X-Band
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Design and development of a wideband active frequency doubler Monolithic Microwave Integrated Circuit (MMIC) at X-band using a single GaAs based pseudomorphic High Electron Mobility Transistor (p-HEMT) is presented in this paper. In this design, emphasis is given to achieve minimal conversion loss, better harmonic suppression along with a good return loss over the desired band of operation. The fabricated MMIC has a conversion loss of 2.5 dB at 9.6 GHz with flatness of 2.5 dB over 600 MHz bandwidth for an input power level of $\mathbf{- 1}$ to +3 dBm and consumes only 46 mW. The MMIC die has harmonic suppression better than 19 dBc, input return loss better than 18 dB and output return loss better than 12.5 dB over the operating frequency band. The actual circuit fits into the compact size of $1.8 \mathrm{~mm} X 1.8 \mathrm{~mm}$, it is fabricated in $2.5 \mathrm{~mm} X$ $\mathbf{2. 5} \mathbf{~ m m}$ limited by tiling of other circuits in the same wafer.

articleTitle: Novel Probe-fed SIW to Dielectric Waveguide Transition for Ku-Band Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents a novel transition to a low-index core dielectric waveguide (LICDW) from a lightweight, low-profile, and compact probe-fed substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) for Ku-band applications. The proposed transition design employs a tapered SIW section that efficiently excites the dominant $E_{11}^{y}$ mode in the LICDW section using the dominant $TE_{10}$ mode of the SIW section. Comprehensive simulation results of a Ku-band back-to-back prototype, along with extensive field analysis, confirm the effective excitation of the dominant mode within the LICDW. The transition has been fabricated and experimentally validated, with results matching the simulations. It demonstrates excellent performance, achieving a transmission coefficient better than $3.2 \mathrm{d}\mathrm{B}$ and a reflection coefficient better than $14 \mathrm{d}\mathrm{B}$ across the entire Ku-band, underscoring its suitability for Ku-band applications.

articleTitle: Fractal Inspired Dual-Band Compact UWB MIMO Radiator with Wideband Isolation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this paper a compact dual-band Ultra-wideband (UWB) multiple-input-multiple-output (MIMO) antenna covering the 2.4 GHz ISM band and the UWB spectrum (3.511.5 GHz) is designed and investigated. The antenna owns a compact dimension of $26({L}) \mathrm{mm} \times 40 \mathrm{~mm}({W})$ with an interelement spacing of $6.6 \mathrm{~mm}\left(0.05 \lambda_{0}\right.$ at 2.4 GHz). For enhancing the isolation of the diversity antenna, a combination of extended ground stubs, a neutralization line, and the 2nd-order Koch fractal boundaries are exercised. Isolation of 40 dB and $\gt15 \mathrm{~dB}$ is attained in the 2.4 GHz ISM band and the UWB band respectively. The antenna achieves a maximum realized gain of 4.5 dBi and a peak efficiency of 82%. The investigation of the simulated diversity parameters demonstrates an $\mathbf{E C C}\lt0.2$. The antenna demonstrates desirable impedance, radiation, and diversity traits, making it a suitable contender for portable wireless applications.

articleTitle: Studies on Metasurface Geometries for Scan Enhancement in Phased Array Antennas
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper investigates the application of Phase Gradient Metasurfaces (PGMS) in Phased Array Antennas (PAA) to enhance beam steering capabilities, which is crucial for achieving rapid and precise control over radiation patterns. A comprehensive analysis of various geometrical topologies of PGMS unit cells is carried out focusing on optimizing both transmittance and phase distribution to maximize the performance. By identifying the optimal unit cell design, PGMS supercells and arrays tuned to operate at frequencies of 5.65 GHz and 8 GHz are designed. The integration of these PGMS structures atop the PAA is validated via full-wave simulations in Ansys HFSS, demonstrating significant improvements in beam scanning range.

articleTitle: Circular SIW Microwave Sensor for Methanol Detection in Spurious Liquors
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Local or spurious liquors are alcoholic drinks being illicitly produced in crude settings with very less control on dual step production process, i.e., fermentation and distillation. Due to the uncontrolled manufacturing setup, the concentration of a byproduct like methanol in these types of spurious liquors may also be substantially higher, in addition to the potable psychoactive solvent i.e., ethanol. It may be noted that the presence of methanol of above 5% concentration in alcoholic drinks can cause visual impairment and mortality, and hence its concentration level should monitored and regulated. The conventional chromatography-spectroscopy requires exorbitant equipment and highly skilled personnel, limiting its widespread usage for this purpose. In this work, a circular SIW based microwave sensor operating in S-band with a high-quality factor (Q) of 195 is proposed to accurately detect the methanol concentration in alcoholic drinks. The structure is simulated using CST-MWS, and the prototype is fabricated and tested. The fabricated RF sensor is able to provide good sensitivity to facilitate detection of $1.1 \mathrm{MHz} /$ unit percent concentration of methanol in ethanol ($\mathbf{v} / \mathrm{v}$) with a minimum detected methanol concentration of 5%(v/v) in ethanol i.e., the maximum permissible limit of methanol in alcoholic beverages.

articleTitle: TEM to TE11 Mode Converter Using Step Waveguide Transformer Section
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: The authors present coaxial transverse electromagnetic TEM to circular $\mathbf{T M}_{01}$ mode conversion using a conical shaped central conductor and step waveguide transformer section for mode conversion from TM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">01</inf> to TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf>. The mode converter is designed for an operating frequency of 3 GHz. The proposed mode converter is designed to have a compact structure. A theoretical study is performed to determine the values for design parameter of TEM to TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf> mode converter and the results are validated using CST microwave studio. The S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf> for the TEM input mode is $\mathbf{- 2 0. 9 6} \mathrm{dB}$, the mode conversion in TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf> mode is $\mathbf{9 7. 8 \%}$, the conversion in other mode is less than $\mathbf{4. 1 \%}$, and bandwidth for conversion efficiency more than $\mathbf{9 0 \%}$ is 141 MHz $(\mathbf{4. 6 6 \%})$. The mode converter also exhibits peak electric field concentration of $2375.14 \mathrm{~V} / \mathrm{m}$ which corresponds to the high-power microwave handling of 388 MW. To improve the high-power handling capability of the mode converter, a simulation study is carried out by varying the radius of chamfer which is applied to the sharp edges.

articleTitle: A CPW-Fed Tri-Band Parasitic Patch Antenna for 5G, WLAN and Satellite Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This work proposes a compact CPW-fed tri-band linearly polarized antenna for wireless applications, which consists of a tri-notched square slot filled with four parasitic elements. The actual size of the designed antenna is $25 \mathrm{~mm} \times 25 \mathrm{~mm} \times 1.6 \mathrm{~mm}$, with electrical dimensions of $0.27 \lambda_{0} \times 0.27 \lambda_{0} \times 0.017 \lambda_{0}$. The proposed multi-band antenna is developed and simulated on an FR-4 substrate. The two conducting stubs are connected to the radiating patch along both sides of the feed line for impedance matching. The antenna’s impedance bandwidths (IBWs) are 2.74-4.44 GHz, 5.02-5.69 GHz, and 7.234-8.346 GHz to cover the mid-band 5G $(3.2-3.5 \mathrm{GHz})$, WLAN $(5 / 5.2 / 5.5 \mathrm{GHz})$ and $\mathrm{C}(7.2-7.8 \mathrm{GHz})$ band. The antenna structure is also incredibly simple, compact and with a low profile. The proposed antenna can be used in compact and portable devices that operate in various frequency bands, such as 5G, WLAN, and C-band satellite bands.

articleTitle: Optimization of Side Lobe and Side Band Reduction in Time-Modulated Elliptical Antenna Arrays Using CRPSO and NPSO Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents an approach to design a 12-element time-modulated asymmetric elliptical antenna array (ATMEAA) for optimum far-field radiation pattern synthesis. By minimizing the sidelobe levels (SLLs) and sideband levels (SBLs), the far-field radiation pattern is designed to minimize the interference of ATMEAA. For achieving the ultra-low SLLs and SBLs, an optimal combination of switch-ON time sequence and progressive phase delay is determined using metaheuristic techniques, which are craziness-based Particle Swarm Optimization (CRPSO) and novel particle swarm optimization (NPSO). ATMEAA is also considered for the practical antenna at fundamental frequency 2.4 GHz to calculate SLLs, SBLs, feed network efficiency, and directivity using the CRPSO and NPSO techniques.

articleTitle: Dual-Polarized Broadband Inverted Dipole Antenna Design for Base Station Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper introduces a dual-polarized base station antenna designed for 5G communications which prioritizes high gain. The antenna features two pairs of perpendicular planar inverted bowtie antennas along the central axes, an optimized coaxial feeding structure, and a square $50 \mathrm{~mm} \times 50 \mathrm{~mm}$ ground plane used as a reflector. Together with its dual-polarization properties, the planar inverted-bowtie antenna’s two inverted-bowtie-shaped planar dipoles can increase bandwidth. The antenna design results in a 10 dB return loss bandwidth from 2.8 GHz to 4.03 GHz by employing uniform open-sleeve dipole configurations. The isolation between the first and second ports is more than 35 dB, across the whole bandwidth. Results from the suggested antenna indicate that the cross-polarization is maintained below -15 dB and the FBR (front-to-back) ratio in the operating band is better than 22 dB. The gain of the proposed antenna is $\mathbf{7. 5 5 2 4 d B i}$ and $\mathbf{6. 3 6 6 4 d B i}$ at the two resonating frequencies.

articleTitle: Binary Particle Swarm Optimization for Design of a Reconfigurable Transmissive Unit Cell
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Ensuring connectivity between pixels and the switching element on a pixelated unit cell is challenging using binary particle swarm optimization (BPSO). Here, a design approach is formulated to utilize BPSO for a reconfigurable unit cell design, and then a novel random walk-based initialization is proposed to reduce computation cost. The proposed initialization scheme has shown several-fold improvement in the computation time. This approach may be extended for metasurface unit cell designs for various other applications.

articleTitle: Characterization of Fiber-optics Based Composite Signal Distribution for Phased Array Radar
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: We present development and characterization of an optical signal distribution unit for the phased array radars. The signal distribution is based on radio-over-fiber technology and is capable of distributing a combination of radio frequency (RF) as well as digital signals to the antenna elements of the phased array radar. It comprises of an optical transmitter unit (OTU) and an optical receiver module (ORM). The OTU comprises of eight electrical-to-optical (e/o) conversion modules whose outputs are combined to generate the composite signal that feeds the antenna elements. The e/o modules are integrated and housed in a rugged enclosure and have been qualified as per military standards (MIL-STD) for ground-based deployment and operations.

articleTitle: Diagonally Polarized Dual Beam Holographic Metasurface Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A dual beam, Linearly Polarized Holographic Metasurface Antenna (LPHMSA) with a diagonally cross-polar isolation is proposed in this article. Comprehensive numerical characterization to realize the surface impedance expression of diagonally cross-polar LPHMSA is discussed here. A strategic transformation between single beam to diagonally cross-polar LPHMSA is numerically analyzed in this paper. Proposed LPHMSA has an overall dimension of $12.5 \lambda_{0} \times 12.5 \lambda_{0}$, composed with $55 \times 55=3025$ scalar meta unit-cells. A high gain, linearly polarized (LP) dual-beam pattern at $\left(\theta_{n}, \varphi_{n}\right)=\{(-$ $\left.\left.20^{\circ}, 0^{\circ}\right);\left(20^{\circ}, 0^{\circ}\right)\right\}$, with a peak gain $\left(g_{\text {max }}\right)=15.13 \mathrm{dBi}$. Equal co-cross polar gain pattern is observed at proposed beam position while $\approx \mathbf{2 5 d B}$ cross-pol isolation is reported at an diagonal beam position.

articleTitle: Cascaded Quarter-Circular Mushroom Resonators loaded to Substrate Integrated Waveguide for Semi Selective Bandpass Filter
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A bandpass filter with partial sideband selectivity based on two cascaded quarter-circular mushroom resonators (QcMRs) loaded to substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) is presented in this paper. Two cascaded mushroom resonators having shapes of quarter-circular metal patch are placed face to face along their linear edges and loaded into a SIW cavity. The direct electrical coupling between the excited fundamental modes of these two QcMRs controls the maximum power transfer within the resonators loaded into the SIW cavity. A dual-pole passband with a transmission zero (TZ) at a higher sideband is generated after carrying out an EM simulation. The proposed compact filter structure occupies an area of $0.5 \lambda_{0}$ $\times 0.3 \lambda_{0}$ and has its center frequency (CF) at 4 GHz with a 0.75 dB of minimum insertion loss.

articleTitle: Offset-Fed 3D-Printed Zoned Reflectarray Antenna for Ultra-Wideband Millimeter-Wave 5G Satellite Communication Links
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents design and development of a lightweight and cost-efficient 3D-printed zoned reflectarray (ZRA) antenna achieving ultra-wideband beamforming performance intended for millimeter-wave satellite communication applications. The proposed design features a dielectric metamaterial element (DME) with bottom layer covered with copper tape which reflects the incident electromagnetic (EM) waves with different phase delay. Further, a ZRA is diligently designed comprising of $\mathbf{2 5} \times \mathbf{2 5}$ different forms of proposed DMEs. The zoning on reflectarray aperture takes into account the incident angle of EM ray for each DME to minimize reflection phase error across the complete aperture. Finally, the ZRA is offset fed by a 3D-printed dielectric pyramidal horn positioned at a focal point located at $(0,-15,67.5) \mathrm{mm}$. Weighing only 35 grams, the prototype is suitable for satellite communications, offering a practical halfpower gain bandwidth of 41.5% with practical peak gain of 25.4 dBi and an antenna efficiency of 56.6% at 28 GHz.

articleTitle: A Double Slotted Antipodal Vivaldi Yagi-Uda Antenna for 5G mmWave MIMO Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this paper, a four-element multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) antenna employing a double slotted antipodal vivaldi yagi-uda antenna (DSAVYA) is proposed for mmWave MIMO applications, targeting the n257 and n261 5G FR2 bands specifically. The use of a double slotted antipodal vivaldi structure (DSAVS) as gain-enhancing component, makes this approach unique, which results in a notable 3.1 dB boost in the gain of the proposed antenna. The DSAVYA has an impedance bandwidth of 27.4% ($25.68-33.83 \mathrm{GHz}$) with gain varying from 6.9 to 8.7 dBi. The DSAVYA is subsequently utilized further in a four-element MIMO with orthogonal arrangement that boasts a wide impedance bandwidth of 27.6% (25.63-33.82 GHz) with a gain varying from 7.3 to 9.2 dBi. The MIMO configuration of the DSAVYA offers 1.9 dB gain-bandwidth over the entire band covered.

articleTitle: Textile Based Polarization Reconfigurable Aperture Coupled Microstrip Patch Antenna For Wearable Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper introduces a textile-based polarization reconfigurable aperture-coupled microstrip patch antenna designed specifically for real time health monitoring. Operating at ISM band 2.45 GHz, the antenna utilizes strategically placed slots over a concentric circular slot on the patch to achieve three distinct polarization states at 0° and ± 45° polarization angles. Its innovative design includes textile materials for lightweight and flexible integration. The antenna architecture comprises the antenna structure itself, slot actuators functioning as switches, and a grounded plane, ensuring simplicity and reliability. Rigorous simulations with bending analysis validate the antenna’s performance within the specified frequency band with around 2.8 dBi of gain, highlighting its suitability for dynamic polarization adjustment in confined environments. Additionally, the proposed textile-based antenna is kept into a meshed human hand model to evaluate Specific Absorption Rate (SAR) value in a practical manner.

articleTitle: Design and Development of C + Ku Band Shared Aperture Monopulse Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents a design of dual-band microstrip /waveguide shared aperture monopulse antenna in C+ Ku-band for semi-active seeker application. The proposed antenna is a six-layer configuration which is a first of its kind providing a new idea of two monopulse antennas on same aperture in two different band and is suitable for compound guidance systems. A single layer C-band printed monopulse array with miniaturized series-fed patch array and compact branch-line coupler design is realized on the top of five layer Ku-band monopulse slotted waveguide array antenna. The electrical performance of microstrip patch antenna array with hybrid network in presence of Ku-band slotted array is presented with EM simulation results. Similarly, the simulated performance of Ku-band monopulse slotted waveguide array in presence of microstrip patch antenna array is also presented here. The design approach has been validated and proven with both ANSYS HFSS and CST EM simulation software. A proto unit is developed and is meeting all the technical specifications of both C-band and Ku-band shared microstrip/waveguide monopulse antenna.

articleTitle: Development of High Power X-band MMIC SPDT switch using single series GaN HEMT switching device
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper present design of highly linear twenty-watt MMIC SPDT switch for X-band transmit/receive switch application based on 0.25μm GaN/AlGaN HEMT technology using customized single series device and its measured results. The measured S-parameter of X-band SPDT switch demonstrates insertion loss less than 1 dB, isolation more than 38 dB and return losses better than 12 dB in 9 GHz to 10 GHz frequency band. This circuit can transmit 44.2 dBm input power at 0.1 dB compression and can handle 45.4 dBm input power at 1 dB compression.

articleTitle: Planar Array Antenna with a simple Feed Network for Beam Steering
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A simple beam steering technique has been proposed and analyzed for two designs, consisting of a planar $2 \times 1$ array antenna which can be used for 5 G communication in FR1 band, IOT, Fixed-Satellite Service (FSS). In Design I, two elements are isolated along the H-plane, while in Design II, the elements are separated along the E-plane. For both designs, a simple microstrip feed network with two ports has been conceived to control the direction of radiating beam. Utilization of two ports introduces phase differences between radiated signals from patches, resulting in beam steering in three different directions based on excitation of the ports. Both designs can be operated in three modes: either both ports or only one of them is excited simultaneously. Design I provides a maximum beam tilting of ± 22° in the H -plane with maximum gain of 7 dBi. Design II exhibits a maximum beam tilting of $\pm \mathbf{2 0 ^ { \circ }}$ in the E-plane with maximum gain of 6 dBi. The proposed designs are completely planar with a dimension of $1.38 \lambda \times 0.55 \lambda$, where $\lambda$ is the wavelength corresponding to the operating frequency $(4.2 \mathrm{GHz})$. A prototype of Design I is fabricated and measured, which validates the simulation results.

articleTitle: Design of a Metasurface-based Bifunctional Folded Transmit/Reflect Array Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: We present a bifunctional folded reflect/transmit array antenna (FRA/FTA) utilizing a low-profile metasurface (MS) array. The design incorporates four linear phase variants of the transmit array (TA), facilitating cross-polar transmission at high frequencies ($30-40 \mathrm{GHz}$) and x-polarized wave propagation at lower frequencies ($\mathbf{1 0 - 2 2} \mathbf{~ G H z}$). Furthermore, a dual-band reflect array (RA) is implemented, operating as a folded reflect array (FRA) antenna in the lower frequency range ($11-22 \mathrm{GHz}$) and serving as a polarizer converter for the FTA at higher frequencies ($28-40 \mathrm{GHz}$). The proposed design achieves peak realized gains of 22.7 dBi and 28.1 dBi, with aperture efficiencies (AEs) of 42% and 31% at 16 GHz (FRA) and 35 GHz (FTA), respectively. It also provides 3-dB gain bandwidths (GBWs) of $\mathbf{4 2. 9 \%}$ and $\mathbf{2 8. 5 \%}$, maintaining frequency separation ratio of $1: 2.19$. The profile-to-diameter ratio (H/D) has been minimized to 0.27, with side lobe levels (SLLs) suppressed by 12 dB and 15 dB across the specified frequency bands. This design applies to satellite communication, synthetic aperture radar (SAR), radio astronomy, and related fields.

articleTitle: Design of a Multilayer Transmissive-Reflective Frequency Selective Surface with Wide Stop-band for mmWave Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A 2-D dual-polarized second order based band-pass transmissive-reflective frequency selective surface (TR-FSS) exhibiting desirable selectivity and wider out-of-band wave rejection characteristics is being proposed in this paper. The band-pass TR-FSS has been designed to span the whole $n 258$ band which ranges from 24.25 GHz to 27.5 GHz. The design offers a flat 3 dB pass band response from 24.08 GHz to 27.50 GHz. An insertion loss as minimal as 0.2 dB has been achieved at 26 GHz. The $\mathbf{- 1 0} \mathbf{~ d B}$ out-of-band suppression bandwidths are obtained from 18 GHz to 23.58 GHz and 28.43 GHz to 58 GHz. An equivalent circuit modeling (ECM) approach has been discussed to illustrate the aperture coupled-based concept, which aids in achieving the required responses.

articleTitle: A wire monopole with secondary current suppression for microwave imaging of biological tissues
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: The design and simulation of wire monopole antenna inside an imaging tank are presented for biomedical applications. The performance of the proposed monopole is evaluated in the coupling liquid used for impedance matching with tissue. Surface current density along the inner and outer conductors of wire monopole was analyzed to evaluate antenna performance. Electromagnetic (EM) simulations indicated that antenna $\left|S_{11}\right|$ in the presence of secondary current induced on the outer conductor ranges from $- \mathbf{1 4 . 4 3 2}$ to $\mathbf{- 1 7 . 0 4} \mathbf{d B}$ over 0.9 to 1.5 GHz. With the addition of a ferrite sleeve, these values improved from $\mathbf{- 2 0 . 5 6}$ to $\mathbf{- 2 3 . 3 4} \text{dB}$ over 0.9 to $\mathbf{1 . 5} \mathbf{~ G H z}$. The secondary current induced on the outer conductor that extended up to 70 mm in length was reduced to 7 mm when a ferrite sleeve of length 18 mm was positioned at 14 mm distance from the antenna junction. Additionally, mutual coupling between the antenna array inside the imaging tank reduced by 0.7 to 3.5 dB in the presence of ferrite choke. Numerical simulations indicate the feasibility of using the wire monopole with ferrite choke for microwave imaging applications.

articleTitle: Multilayer Fourth Order Single Band Aperture Coupled Bandpass Frequency Selective Surface
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this paper, a Band Pass Frequency Selective Surface (FSS) is presented with an aperture-coupled single band fourth order. Firstly, a pair of square and triangular truncations are introduced in a square patch along the rightside diagonal and left-side diagonal, respectively, forming a structure that appears as two tilted hexagons cascaded together. With simultaneous excitation, the symmetry of this structure introduces two orthogonal degenerative modes. However, perturbations in the form of square and triangular truncations split the orthogonal modes into two different frequencies. This approach can be used to implement a compact bandpass FSS. Subsequently, a composite resonator is employed by strategically rotating the patches by 90 degrees between adjacent patches, designed to remove the cross-polarization reflection produced by the two orthogonal modes. Building upon this groundwork, a three-layered structure is designed, with the top and bottom conducting layers serving as composite resonators and the middle conducting layer coupled through a circular aperture. Finally, using the proposed FSS element, a fourth-order single band bandpass FSS is designed.

articleTitle: A Compact Planar Wideband Antenna with Higher-Order Modes Suppression for 5G NR n79 band
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents a planar wideband microstrip patch antenna (MPA) with the suppression of spurious higherorder modes for $\mathbf{n 7 9}$ band. The MPA is capacitively fed through a $\lambda / 4$ resonator which not only helps to suppress higher-order modes but also plays a significant role in the enhancement of the impedance bandwidth. A series of metallic vias is placed at the central plane of the structure which facilitates the propagation of $\mathrm{TM}_{1 / 2,0}$ mode along with the fundamental TM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">10</inf> mode. Therefore, two radiating modes of the MPA, namely $\mathrm{TM}_{1 / 2,0}$ and $\mathbf{T M}_{10}$, resonate in close proximity of each other along with the non-radiating $\lambda / 4$ resonator which results in a wider impedance bandwidth ($\mathrm{FBW} \sim \mathbf{1 4 \%}$). A prototype of the designed wideband antenna is fabricated to validate the proposed concept. The measured result indicates that the proposed antenna has an impedance bandwidth of $4.6-5.2 \mathrm{GHz}$. Moreover, the higherorder modes of the MPA are successfully suppressed in the proposed structure due to the presence of $\lambda / 4$ resonator and an array of metallic vias.

articleTitle: Battery-less Reconfigurable Intelligent Surface Powered By Energy Harvesting Rectenna Array
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents a re-configurable intelligent surface (RIS) powered by an energy harvester rectarray. A battery-operated complex circuitry is needed in conventional RIS communication to bias different phase states. The RF (radio-frequency) energy harvesting approach provides a solution to the aforementioned problem. The unit cell of battery-less RIS is designed with the varactor diodes to alter the reflection phase and amplitude. The unit cells are distributed to provide phases from 90° to -90°. The rectarray is a parallel connection of 4 hybrid (serially and parallelly) connected rectenna. The $4 \times 4$ energy harvester rectarray is suitable for powering RIS as it harvests approximately $9 \mathbf{V}$ when 25 dBm RF power impinges on it. The proposed design is a promising concept because it can be fabricated using the conventional fabrication process, and it is cost-effective compared to a conventional phased array antenna. A RIS with a $6 \times 6$ array was manufactured and experimentally characterized to verify the altering properties of unit cells by varying transmitted power.
