articleTitle: Metasurface Lens Antenna for Microwave Subsurface Anomaly Detection and Imaging
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: The subsurface anomaly detection using the conventional ground-penetrating radar (GPR) is usually done in the bistatic mode, where the antennas are kept very close to the surface. In this work, a transmissive metasurface lens along with a probe-fed patch antenna is designed and developed for improved subsurface anomaly detection and imaging using the monostatic configuration, without requirement of the antenna being in direct contact with the surface. The applicability of the proposed scheme is shown by scanning the designated area comprising three metallic and dielectric objects buried under 3 cm of sand, using the antenna without and with the metasurface lens. The reflection coefficient data are measured at each scan point using the antenna with and without lens, and finally the microwave image of the test area in terms of the measured reflected data is formed in both cases. It is observed that when the antenna is used along with proposed metasurface lens, then various objects buried inside the sand can be detected and accurately located. However, when the scanning is carried out using the same antenna without lens, then it becomes difficult to distinguish various objects from the background medium.

articleTitle: Flexible wideband microstrip patch antenna using DGS for MIoT/ healthcare applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: The design and implementation of the antenna as a component of a Medical Internet of Things (MIoT)-based healthcare monitoring system are presented in this study. Sensors acquire and deliver data to the IoT platform, requiring interaction with the Wi-Fi module to ensure data availability. A $48 \times 40 \mathrm{~mm} 2$ polyamide substrate manufactures a wideband ($\mathbf{5. 8}$ $\mathbf{G H z}$) microstrip patch antenna. To achieve wideband operation at 5.8 GHz, a ladder-shaped slot is etched to the patch, along with two oval-shaped slots, resulting in a 1.08 GHz bandwidth at 5.8 GHz frequency. The S 11 at 5.8 GHz is -42.77 dB and gain is 5 dB.

articleTitle: Design of a Dual Polarized Amplifying Reflectarray Element
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This work presents a novel design for a dual-polarized, amplified reflectarray antenna element. The proposed element comprises of two identical unit cells placed orthogonal to each other, each featuring an aperture-coupled square patch layered on a slotted plane, integrated with microstrip lines and a power amplifier chip. Incident waves couple to the square patches on the top layer, are guided onto the microstrip line for amplification and are subsequently re-radiated through the slotted plane. Simulation results demonstrate an active gain of 13 dB within the $5.10-5.45 \mathrm{GHz}$ frequency band.

articleTitle: Low-RCS Reflectarray Co-Designed With Phase Controllable Absorptive Frequency-Selective Reflection Structure
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This article presents an approach to reducing a reflectarray’s radar cross section (RCS). A polarization-insensitive absorptive frequency selective reflection structure (AFSR) is used for the proposed design. The AFSR design consists of a circularshaped broadband absorber and ring resonator on the top and back sides of a dielectric which is separated by the ground plane through an air spacer. The proposed AFSR design provides a reflection window at 8.2 GHz within two broad absorption bands, which ranges from 4.19 to 7.10 GHz and from 9.21 to 11.51 GHz. The phase response within the reflection window is achieved by changing the size of metallic patches loaded on the top AFSR structure. The proposed 1-bit reflectarray with reduced RCS, using phase controllable AFSR structure is designed, fabricated, measured and compared with a reference reflectarray. When compared to a conventional reflectarray, the low-RCS reflectarray showed nearly the same radiation performance, achieving a gain of $21.8 \mathbf{~ d B i}$. A significant reduction in RCS of proposed reflectarray over conventional reflectarray has been achieved both in lower and higher bands with fractional bandwidths of $\mathbf{7 8 \%}$ and $\mathbf{2 0 \%}$ respectively.

articleTitle: One-bit Coded Near-field Corrected Metasurface for Beam Steering Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this paper, one-bit coded near-field corrected metasurface antennas for beam-steering applications are critically examined, with studies on various feeder antenna locations. Initially, the reflection phase profile necessary for 1-bit coded metasurface is analytically generated using MATLAB, which provides scattered beam in the desired direction of $\mathbf{2 0}$ degrees, for far-field illumination. Then, near-field correction factor considering feeder antenna position at a quarter wavelength height at 10 GHz is analytically computed using MATLAB. Subsequently, the one-bit coded metasurface is synthesized in Ansys EM solver using MATLAB HFSS API, considering patch-type unit cells. Furthermore, effect of half wavelength dipole antenna as feeder for this fixed metasurface is explored, considering different heights quarter wavelength, half-wavelength and one-wavelength. It is observed that the 1-bit coded near-field corrected metasurface when excited with dipole-fed antenna placed at a height of quarter-wavelength, generates a beam in the direction of 16 degrees with directivity of 9.55 dBi and a half-power beamwidth (HPBW) of 37 degrees. In the other two cases, the incident field splits into multiple directions. Such coded metasurface based antennas useful for beam steering in future 6 G wireless communication and Radar applications.

articleTitle: Quantum-Driven Collaborative UAS Beam-Reforming: A Novel Approach for Congested Spectrum Environment in NextG Communications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: The increasing congestion in spectrum environments demands enhanced capacity, reliability, and coverage in NextG communication systems. Distributed beamforming, assisted by collaborative unmanned aerial systems (UASs), offers a promising solution for improving spectrum efficiency and system robustness. However, this approach encounters significant challenges due to electronic and mechanical issues. We present a pioneering quantum computation method designed to develop distributed beam-reforming strategies for UAS systems experiencing hovering instability. To address the drawbacks of current distributed beamforming systems, which are constrained by positioning and synchronization inaccuracies, we introduce a new concept: the quantum-position-lock loop (Q-P-LL) for real-time tracking of USAs. The proposed framework harnesses quantum superposition, entanglement, and amplitude amplification to accurately detect the states of UASs, leading to more efficient and resilient collaborative positioning. We validate the feasibility of our quantum framework by constructing a quantum computing network that mitigates beam distortion caused by rapid changes in UAS positions due to hovering. The system collects real-time positioning data and uses quantum phase inversion and measurement circuits to generate a joint control signal for beam-reforming. In addition, the convergence analysis is presented. Our results indicate that our framework significantly reduces real-time beam distortion, establishing a reliable framework for UAS-assisted NextG communications.

articleTitle: A Low Profile Dual Circularly Polarized Leaky Wave Antenna at W-Band
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A low-profile, all-metal, dual circularly polarised leaky wave antenna operating in the W band is proposed in this work. The combination of the transverse and longitudinal slot pattern is perforated along the broad wall of a WR-10 waveguide to generate circular polarization. This antenna is designed for 92 GHz to 96 GHz frequency bands and shows gain above 19 dBi in the entire operating band. The designed antenna HPBW is 1.9°, and its SLL is less than -12 dB. To create dual polarization, two feeds have been utilized. By changing the feed from port 1 to port 2, left-hand to right-hand circular polarization or vice-versa can be accomplished. The proposed antenna is an excellent candidate for space application because of its robust all-metal design.

articleTitle: Ultra Wide band low noise amplifier with Gain Equalizer
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This technical paper presents a wide band low noise MMIC amplifier with gain equalizer realized on a depletion mode indium gallium arsenide pHEMT technology. The MMIC demonstrates 17 dB of typical gain and less than 3.5 dB of noise figure and minimum 12 dBm of output P1 dB over a wide frequency band of $\mathrm{C}, \mathrm{X}$ and Ku. It is realized using a two stage distributed cascade topology with a form factor of 2.2 mm X 1.5 mm X 0.1 mm. It operates on dual supply of 3 V drain and a negative 0.5 V gate supply with current consumption of 58 mA. This circuit has an on chip gain equalizer with positive slope to improve the overall gain flatness. This design has integrated DC blocking capacitors at the input and output as part of matching circuit.

articleTitle: A High Gain GaAs pHEMT Low Noise Amplifier for Ka-Band Active Phase Shifters
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A two-stage common source topology, 36 to 38 GHz GaAs pHEMT Low Noise Amplifier (LNA) was designed, fabricated, and tested. This LNA is an essential part of the proposed active phase shifter for soil moisture radiometer phased array antenna. The LNA provides 23 dB gain. A typical noise figure (NF) of 5 dB was measured at 37 GHz. DC power consumption is about 154 mW. The MMIC chip was fabricated by using $0.15 \mu \mathrm{~m}$ GaAs pHEMT process. The total chip area including all the pads and scribe lines is about $1.5 \mathrm{~mm} \times 0.9 \mathrm{~mm}$. Measured gain flatness is about $\pm 1 \mathrm{~dB}$ within $36-38 \mathbf{G H z}$ bandwidth. The high gain, small gain flatness makes this device well suited for the phase shifters in the soil moisture radiometer phased array antenna.

articleTitle: Compact Triple-Band Bandpass Filter Using Coupled Resonators With Transmission Zeros
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this work, a triple-band band-pass filter utilizing quarter-wavelength coupled resonators with transmission zeros is proposed. The filter design incorporates four resonators, including two short-ended quarter-wavelength modified coupled resonators. The proposed filter achieves three passbands with bandwidths of $1.67 \mathrm{GHz}-1.97 \mathrm{GHz}, 4.2 \mathrm{GHz}-$ 8.67 GHz, and $9.45 \mathrm{GHz}-10.45 \mathrm{GHz}$. The return losses for these passbands are $20 \mathrm{~dB}, 15 \mathrm{~dB}$, and 14 dB, respectively, with corresponding insertion losses of $0.5 \mathrm{~dB}, 0.2 \mathrm{~dB}$, and 1 dB. To validate the design, we fabricated the filter using Rogers 4003 material, which has a dielectric constant of 3.55 and a height of 0.8 mm. The measured results show good agreement with the simulations. Additionally, the approximated lumped equivalent circuit was extracted, and the results were plotted, confirming the design’s accuracy. The proposed filter exhibits a flat group delay of less than 1 ns within the passbands and achieves five transmission zeros, enhancing attenuation near the passbands. The overall size of the proposed filter is $17 \times 22.6 \times 0.8 \mathrm{~mm}^{3}$.

articleTitle: Gap-coupled and Hybrid-coupled Half Hexagonal Microstrip Antennas for Dual Frequency Operations
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents two configurations of compact half hexagonal microstrip antennas (HHMSA) employing gapcoupled and direct and gap coupling techniques to achieve dual band performance. Extensive parametric studies on the effects of feed point location and coupling gap have been conducted through simulations and practical experiments, yielding accurate results. For the HHMSA with feed along y-axis, dual frequency ratios ranging from 1.047 to 1.075 for gap-coupled and 1.186 to 1.295 for hybrid-coupled HHMSA were achieved by varying the size of the parasitic antenna. In the HHMSA with feed along x -axis, frequency ratios varied from 1.115 to 1.174 for gap-coupled and 1.217 to $\mathbf{1 . 3 3 7}$ for hybrid-coupled HHMSA. Optimization of the feed point and strip width for direct and gap coupling was crucial in achieving better resonance. These findings demonstrate the potential for tuning dual band performance in HHMSA through precise control of geometric and coupling parameters. The simulated results are validated experimentally.

Author Keywords: direct and gap coupled microstrip antenna

articleTitle: Polarization Insensitive Angularly Stable and Frequency Reconfigurable Programmable Metasurface based RIS for B5G/6G Communication
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A novel polarization insensitive, angularly Stable, frequency reconfigurable reflective metasurface for Reconfigurable Intelligent Surface aided Wireless Communication applications has been proposed in this article. This reflecting metasurface operates at frequencies of 2.3 GHz and 3.9 GHz for 5G NR S-band and C-band respectively. Separate aperture technique is utilized to achieve independent reconfiguration between both bands. A novel biasing technique has been proposed to provide individual and simultaneous dual-band operation. Multi-bit operation of 3-bit and 2-bit phase states is exhibited in both the bands for both TE & TM polarization. The full wave simulations of the proposed unit cell are performed, and reflection magnitude and phase response are analyzed. The characteristics of polarization insensitivity and angular stability are verified from the results. The unit cell is extended to the metasurface design and its properties of beam steering are analyzed.

articleTitle: Breast Cancer Detection Using a Metasurface of 3 mm Cell at 200 MHz
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: We introduces a metasurface sensor designed to detect Breast Cancer (BC) by operating at sub-microwave frequency. Each cell of the metasurface gives rise to a voltage difference that can be measured at the back of the metasurface. Thus, the metasurface has the ability to generate an impression that relates to the constituents of the breast. Simulations were performed to capture and analyze a collection of images using Machine Learning (ML) methodologies. The findings of this testing stage demonstrated the device’s capability in identifying anomalies in the breast that may or may not be cancerous.

articleTitle: Design and Development of Dual Transmit Receive Module (DTRM) with Variable Phase and Gain for Beam Forming Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this paper, The Design architecture of Integrated Dual Transmit Receive Module is presented. The Module is designed for active phased array radar for air surveillance. The radar is proposed to be mounted on ship surface. Module consists of RF front end Transmitter and Receiver. The configuration is based on hybrid MIC/MMIC architecture. The transmitter chain is realized using GaN (Gallium Nitride) devices. The T/R module has bandwidth of 400MHz. To control phase and Amplitude digital phase shifter and digital attenuator is used respectively. The receiver noise figure is 3.5 dB (max) and gain is 30 dB (±2dB). The transmitter power is 50dB (min) over the frequency range with better than 40% efficiency. FPGA based control card provides sequencing control for GaN devices and T/R switching signals depending upon the PRT. Electrical performance of TR module is tested and measurement results are in accordance with design specifications.

articleTitle: A Novel Software-Defined Radio Transceiver System with a Dynamic and Adaptive Digital Pre-distortion Solution
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper introduces a high-value Software Defined Radio (SDR) transceiver system implemented on the zc706 and ad9371-based embedded System-on-Chip. This system has real-time modulated signal generation capabilities and the ability to apply a dynamic and adaptive digital pre-distortion technique(DA-DPD). It continuously calculates the Normalised Mean Square Error (NMSE) and performs further iterations of the Digital Pre-distortion (DPD) only when the NMSE reduces below a particular threshold in the DA-DPD configuration. The memory depth and non-linearity order can be dynamically changed during the execution according to the Power Amplifier (PA) requirements, making the proposed DA-DPD system adaptable to any PA class. For the proof of concept, a 10 MHz LTE signal is transmitted through a 50W GaN Doherty Power Amplifier (DPA) at 3.3 GHz, operating at 8 dB output power backoff (OPBO). The coefficients are extracted in real-time from the received amplified signal. Before performing DPD, the subjected DPA has an Adjacent Channel Leakage Power Ratio (ACPR) of -28.6 dBc (lower) and -29.7 dBc (upper), with NMSE of $\mathbf{- 1 2. 2} \mathbf{d B}$. When the PA is tested with the DA-DPD system, the ACPR and the NMSE have been improved to $\mathbf{- 4 7} \mathbf{d B c}$ and -34 dB, respectively.

articleTitle: A Compact inverted I-Shaped HMSIW Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This research represents the design layout and development of the planar inverted I-shaped slot antenna using semi-circular half-mode substrate integrated waveguide technique. The design prototype is realized using inverted ‘I’ slot on a patch, which resonates at 5.8 GHz with a gain of $\mathbf{6. 2 5 ~ d B}$ with bandwidth of 90 MHz. All simulations of the designed are executed using high frequency structure simulation software. The proposed design is fabricated on FR-4 substrate with semi-circular cavity having size of $\mathbf{6 0}$ $\mathrm{mm} \times 60 \mathrm{~mm}$, the prototype exhibits high gain and a front to back ratio.

articleTitle: Machine Learning Approach to Reduce Phase Quantization Error in Transmitarray
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A non-linearly spaced phase quantization utilizing the k-means clustering method has been presented in this paper. Phase quantization is usually performed to limit the number of unique unit cells required for the design of a transmitarray. This quantization introduces significant phase error, which in turn reduces the gain and bandwidth of the transmitarray along with higher sidelobe levels. Traditionally, a fixed state quantization (1-bit, 2-bit, 3-bit, etc.) is adopted, which adds quantization error to each unit cell’s phase. k-means clustering-based machine learning (ML) algorithm reduces quantization errors by forming high-density clusters without increasing the number of unit cells required.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of Moon-Shaped CPW-Fed Antenna for Ultra-Wideband Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents a planar, low-cost, moonshaped, coplanar waveguide-fed antenna designed for ultrawideband (UWB) applications, fabricated on an FR4 epoxy substrate with dimensions of $0.31 \lambda_{L} \times 0.36 \lambda_{L} \times 0.0082 \lambda_{L}$. The proposed antenna achieves a remarkable fractional bandwidth of 150.6% across the frequency range of 3.1 to 22 GHz, demonstrating excellent agreement with measured values. Additionally, the antenna exhibits a maximum gain of $4.4 \mathbf{d B i}$ and a maximum radiation efficiency of 87.4%, indicating robust performance. Comprehensive analyses of the antenna’s E and H plane radiation patterns, group delay, and transfer function were conducted, all of which yielded favorable results. These findings underscore the antenna’s suitability for UWB frequency applications, making it a strong candidate for various communication systems requiring wide bandwidth and high efficiency.

articleTitle: Compact and Highly Isolated QMSIW Based Self-Diplexing Antenna for Smart Traffic V2V Communication Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this paper, a self-diplexing antenna based on quarter-mode substrate integrated waveguide (QMSIW) is introduced for Vehicle-to-Vehicle (V2V) communication applications. The antenna achieves diplexing functionality through a cross-shaped slot integrated into its top metallic plane. Operating at resonant frequencies of 4.86 GHz and 5.26 GHz, it achieves high port isolation of 35 dB while offering gains of 4.85 dBi and 5.52 dBi, respectively. These performance metrics are enabled by the integration of a T-shaped slot and metallic via, which provide capacitive loading, ensuring effective signal isolation and compactness. The antenna, designed on a substrate with a thickness of 0.787 mm, optimizes its electrical size to $0.05 \lambda_{0}^{2}$, where $\lambda_{0}$ represents the free space wavelength at the lowest resonant frequency. Importantly, the antenna is optimized to function within the NR 46 and NR 79 bands, aligning perfectly with the requirements of smart traffic management systems. This design facilitates robust communication essential for enhancing traffic safety and efficiency in urban environments, addressing the growing demand for reliable V2V communication solutions.

articleTitle: Optimizing Ultra-Low Sidelobe Level Radiation in Concentric Circular Array Antennas Using Evolutionary Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper describes the Ultra-Low Side Lobe Radiation of Concentric Circular Array Antenna, which employs evolutionary optimization techniques. Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO), which has gone through the prose inspired by the meta-heuristic algorithm, is employed to obtain the radiation beam pattern properties of a Concentric Circular Array Antenna, Far-Field radiation beam pattern generated. Current trending applications include next-generation wireless communications and the Internet of Things—the optimization variables to attain preferable radiation pattern characteristics of CCAA. The approach illustrated by $\mathbf{4, 6, 8}$ and $\mathbf{8, 1 0, 1 2}$ elements three rings of a concentric circular array antenna with and without a centre element. The obtained simulation results dissipated the domination of this address on the side lobe level, resulting in maximum reduction. By suppressing the side lobe level, undesired signals and interference signals in the same frequency band are suppressed. The results are justified; the PSO algorithm grasped lower side lobe level values compared with existing methods in previously published papers.

articleTitle: Performance Enhancement of Ku-Band Receiver for SCATSAT-1 Scatterometer
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A Ku-band receiver was developed for space borne pencil beam Scatterometer sensor for different Indian remote sensing programs. It is a low noise and high gain receiver catering to wide input dynamic range over narrow bandwidth of 1.6MHz. Receiver is designed in heterodyne configuration employing double down-conversion and digitally controlled gain facility operated by tele-commanding. An additional low noise amplifier tray with waveguide interface was developed, replacing the coaxial interface in earlier OSCAT, thereby achieving around 0.5dB of noise figure improvement in the receiver. The receiver flatness was also improved in SCATSAT-1 by 0.5dB, thereby improving overall system performance. The paper touches upon the design aspects, assembly, integration and optimization methodology adopted for the development of the receiver. Detailed results taken at each stage are presented in the paper. Developed receiver had successfully being flown in SCATSAT-1 mission, successor of OSCAT.

articleTitle: Forward and Backward to Forward Beam Scanning Bow-tie Slot Loaded SIW Leaky-Wave Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A planar low-profile periodic leaky-wave antenna (LWA) is presented. A substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) with a bow-tie slot in each unit cell is used to design the antenna. Vias of two different spacings are used at each edge of the top plate to allow radiation. Radiation via the fundamental mode results in beam scanning only in the forward directions. Furthermore, continuous backward-to-forward beam scanning occurs when the antenna radiates via the $n=-1$ space harmonic. The measured results verify the beam scanning from +23° to +65° (fundamental mode) and -81° to +20° ($n=-1$ space harmonic) when frequency sweeps from 5.375 to 6.25 GHz and 8 to 11.5 GHz, respectively.

articleTitle: Compact and Wideband Antenna Array for Surveillance Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A compact and wideband antenna array operating in the $\mathbf{C}, \mathbf{X}$ & $\mathbf{K u}$ bands is presented here. A planar array of eight identical wideband radiating elements is realized and then it is tested with the help of a $1: 8$ wideband power combiner. The performance of the complete passive network is tested after integrating it with the transmit-receive module. Additionally, the phase shifters were used with the transceiver module to switch the main beam of the array from - 10 to 10 degrees. The proposed solution is planar compact and has a stable radiation pattern over the entire operating frequency range.

articleTitle: Microstrip Patch Antenna Design with Improved gain using Geometric Optimization
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents a novel cut microstrip patch antenna (MSP) for enhanced gain. The design suggests a special defected ground structure (DGS) in the microstrip patch antenna for a wide frequency range. The design is tested using CST microwave studio and measured at a frequency of 4 GHz. The improved antenna operates in the frequency range of 3.8 GHz to 4.22 GHz providing 11% impedance bandwidth. The paper discusses the evolution of the final prototype and the simulated and measured results agree. The final prototype provides a high gain of 3.3 dBi for a simple yet effective design.

articleTitle: Nonlinear Impairments in Short-Range Linear FM Radar Frequency Translation Units
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Linear FM radar systems using phase locked loop synthesizers or free running oscillators as the frequency translation entity is attractive for implementation of short range radars, such as proximity fuses. This paper presents the theoretical background of the nonlinear impairments in open loop and close loop implementations for linear FM systems. An evaluation setup was developed to assess the system implementation, providing empirical validation against simulation results. Our study contributes to a deeper understanding of the impact of nonlinearities in linear FM radar systems, offering insights valuable for their effective deployment.

articleTitle: A Narrowband Polarization Insensitive Multifunctional Frequency Selective Surface
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents a polarization-insensitive frequency selective surface (FSS) switching between different electromagnetic (EM) operations with the help of p-i-n diodes. The proposed unit cell geometry consists of four-fold symmetric metallic patterns etched on two sides of a single FR4 dielectric substrate, and p-i-n diodes are appropriately placed across the design supported with biasing lines. Based on different combinations (ON and OFF states) of top and bottom diodes, four different working states are obtained in the proposed design. When diodes on both top layer (PD<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>) and bottom layer $\left(\mathrm{PD}_{2}\right)$ are in the OFF state, the geometry exhibits a transmission response with an insertion loss of 1.8 dB at 5.43 GHz. In the OFF $\left(\mathrm{PD}_{1}\right)$-ON (PD<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>) state, the FSS works as an absorber with an absorptivity of 91.39% resonating at 5.59 GHz. In the same way, the proposed configuration provides a complete reflection for the entire frequency range under the $\mathrm{ON}-\mathrm{ON}$ state. The detailed methodology of achieving multiple characteristics (absorption, transmission, and reflection) under different polarization angles has been clearly explained and provided with various applications in the practical scenarios.

articleTitle: A Compact PCB Antenna for 433 MHz Band: Design, Simulation, and Experimental Validation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents the design, simulation, and experimental validation of a compact PCB antenna optimized for the 433 MHz frequency band, with dimensions of approximately $0.066 \lambda \times 0.032 \lambda \times$ $0.0023 \lambda \mathrm{~mm}^{3}$. The antenna uses meandered traces and a shorting pin to achieve a compact form factor while maintaining effective performance. Simulations were conducted using CST Microwave Studio, and the antenna’s S11 parameter was measured in a laboratory environment. The antenna demonstrates a peak gain of approximately -21 dBi at 433 MHz, making it suitable for short-range wireless communication applications, such as remote controls, wireless sensors, and IoT devices.

articleTitle: Design and Optimization of Rectangular Dielectric Resonator Antenna for C-Band Frequencies Using Machine Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: The use of machine learning (ML) to optimize the design process of a wideband circularly polarized (CP) stacked rectangular dielectric resonator antenna (RDRA) is proposed in this article. The antenna uses two dielectric resonators (DRs) separated by an air gap, with the upper resonator rotated by 45°. The rotation creates a left-hand circular polarization at 6.75 GHz, 7.8 GHz, and 10.7 GHz frequencies respectively. The 3 dB AR bandwidth and 66.7% overlap in the 10 dB impedance region along with high gain makes this design suitable for 5G applications. Machine learning is used to reduce the antenna design simulation times by training the models on the antenna’s datasets. Two datasets corresponding to the return loss and the axial ratio (AR) were derived using CST Microwave Studio to train the ML models to predict the antenna’s return loss and AR. The algorithms employed were Random Forest (RF), K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), Decision Trees (DT), Gradient Boosting, and Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) algorithms. KNN and RF performed significantly better for the prediction of S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf> with accuracy values of 99.91% and 99.86%, respectively. The role of ML integration is to ensure efficient and accurate antenna design optimization.

articleTitle: Shared Radiator Full Duplex Antenna for Wi-Fi Application
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This study aims to introduce a novel shared radiator patch antenna operating at Wi-Fi 2.4 GHz of frequency. Two feeding ports placed at a distance of only $0.08 \lambda_{g}$ directly excite the shared radiator in the design. The coupling pins with circular slots on the antennas are strategically positioned on the symmetry plane of the radiator. These coupling pins play a crucial role in decoupling the self interference signal between the feeding ports, thereby enhancing the antenna’s performance. The simulated results show an improvement in isolation from 5 dB to around $16.5-22 \mathrm{~dB}$ in the first $\mathrm{Wi}-\mathrm{Fi}$ channel at a resonant frequency of 2414 MHz. Furthermore, the study of various geometrical factors and parametric analysis that affect the performance of the antenna is also investigated.

articleTitle: Design and Development of Groove Gap Waveguide Filters for High-Power Space Applications at Q-band Using Space-Mapping Technique
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents the design and development of Chebyshev as well as quasi-elliptic filters using groove gap waveguide technology for high-power space-applications at Q band. The filters are optimized using space-mapping technique which reduces the optimization time in case of complex structures like the groove gap waveguide. A sixth order Chebyshev filter and a fourth order cascaded quadruplet filter using TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">102</inf> overmoded cavity-based resonator are designed with 1.97% fractional bandwidth at 38 GHz. The designed filters can handle more than 7.5 kW peak power. The designs are validated through the S -parameter measurements of the fabricated hardware using performance network analyzer (PNA).

articleTitle: A Unique Rectangular Shaped CP THz MIMO Antenna for High Speed Vehicular Communication
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In the proposed research, a MIMO antenna is designed for the circular polarization THz band to resonant at 0.654 THz frequency. The MIMO antenna for the high speed vehicular communication is designed on polyimide dielectric substrate. The proposed design covers the 2:1 VSWR frequency band of 0.624- 0.679 THz with bandwidth of 55 GHz. The proposed THz MIMO antenna covers the 3-dB axial ratio band of 0.618- 0.671 THz with a wide axial ratio bandwidth. The MIMO antenna has gain of more than 5.29 dBi in the operating band and radiation efficiency is more than 88.46% in band. The maximum value of the gain in band is 5.97 dBi at 0.654 THz resonant peak. The ECC in the band is in the range of 0.004132.The MEG is tested for indoor and outdoor activities in Isotropic and Gaussian conditions.

articleTitle: Design and Optimization of a Dual-Band THz Antenna for 6G Wireless Communication Using Interpolated Quasi-Newton Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This study investigates the development and optimization of a dual-band terahertz ($\mathbf{T H z)}$ antenna designed for next-generation 6 G wireless networks, operating at 0.35 THz and 0.41 THz. The antenna utilizes a Rogers RO3210 substrate with a relative permittivity of 10.8, an electric loss tangent of 0.0027, and a thermal conductivity of $0.81 \mathrm{~W} / \mathrm{K} / \mathrm{m}$. The dimensions of the antenna is $900 \mu \mathrm{~m} \times 570 \mu \mathrm{~m} \times 100 \mu \mathrm{~m}$. After the initial design phase, the antenna was optimized using the Interpolated Quasi-Newton Algorithm in CST Studio Suite, focusing on minimizing reflection coefficients and maximizing gain. The optimized antenna showed effective impedance matching with return losses of $\mathbf{- 2 8. 9 8 d B}$ at 0.35 THz and 31.19 dB at 0.41 THz. The 3D and far-field radiation pattern analyses revealed robust directional characteristics and efficient power distribution at both frequencies. This research highlights the potential of innovative antenna designs and advanced optimization techniques to address the challenges associated with THz frequencies. The findings confirm the antenna’s suitability for high-frequency applications, such as smart cities, connected vehicles, IoT ecosystems, and precision sensing, providing a promising pathway to achieving high performance in future 6G networks. Continued research and development will be essential to fully realize the transformative potential of THz frequencies in wireless communication systems.

articleTitle: Precision Beamforming for SAGIN Networks: A Reinforcement Learning Approach to Combat UAV Hovering Instability
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this study, we explore a novel approach to beamforming in a Space-Air-Ground Integrated Network (SAGIN) by utilizing a single unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) equipped with a mounted antenna array. The UAV dynamically adjusts its beamforming weights in real-time to address the challenges posed by UAV hovering, which can impair the beam’s performance. We propose a model-free reinforcement learning (RL) framework, integrated with a neural network, to predict the optimal beamforming weights and enhance the received signal-to-noise ratio (SNR). Traditional RL methods face difficulties with continuous action spaces, as they require explicit representation and updating of Q-values for each possible action, which is infeasible in complex scenarios like UAV beamforming. Our approach leverages deep reinforcement learning (DRL) to learn high-level decision-making strategies, demonstrating significant improvements in beamforming efficiency and energy utilization. The DRL framework showcases remarkable performance in mitigating beam distortion and optimizing SNR, thus advancing the state-of-the-art in UAV-assisted mmWave communications within SAGIN networks.

articleTitle: High Performance Dual-Band THz Metamaterial Absorber for Versatile Biosensing Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper describes a novel polarization insensitive metamaterial absorber-based terahertz sensor for versatile biosensing applications. According to the simulation studies, the sensor offers sharp dual-band resonance at $\mathbf{0. 5 6}$ THz ($f_{1}$) and $0.67 \mathrm{THz}\left(f_{2}\right)$ with peak absorbance and half power bandwidth of $\mathbf{9 9. 5 4 \%}$ and $\mathbf{0. 7 6} \mathbf{G H z}$ at $f_{1}$ while $\mathbf{9 9. 8 3 \%}$ and 1.59 GHz at $\boldsymbol{f}_{2}$. It is found that the high intensity electric field confined to inner and outer edges of the meta-atom has resulted into such exceptional absorption properties. Owing to the extremely narrow spectra, it possesses very high Q-factors of 736.84 and 421.38 at the two peaks. Further, the sensor performance is evaluated by assessing the resonant frequency shift while modifying the refractive index (RI) of analyte layer, placed atop the meta-atom, from 1.34 to 1.41 with superb resolution of 0.01. The sensitivity and figure-of-merit are recorded as $0.07 \mathrm{THz} / \mathrm{RIU}$ and $92.10 \mathrm{RIU}^{-1}$ at $f_{1}$ while 0.141 THz/RIU and 88.68 RIU $^{-1}$ at $f_{2}$. Consequently, our sensor has huge prospect in detection and characterization of the biomedical samples including blood, skin, cervical, jurkat, breast, MCF-7, and PC-12 cancers; malaria, tuberculosis, dengue, and herpes viruses, and esophagus tumor since their RI lies in the range of $\mathbf{1. 3 4}$ to 1.41.

articleTitle: A Composite Dense Dielectric Patch Antenna with Improved Radiation Characteristics in Diagonal, Principal Planes and Other Different phi cut Planes
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In the present work, a new composite dense dielectric patch antenna (DDPA) structure has been proposed to achieve improved Co-polar to Cross-polar isolation in diagonal, principal H plane, other different phi cut planes. Also, the radiation patterns are symmetric. The simulations have been done in Ansys Electronic Desktop Suite 19. The antenna consists of a simple T shaped DDPA with three brick shaped quasi-planar brick shaped dielectric resonators. The DDPA and brick shaped resonators have permittivity 78. The structure has been designed and perceived judiciously and the materials have been chosen keeping in view future developments and fabrication possibilities. This is perhaps the first work, in which CO-XP isolation improvement in different phi cut planes of a DDPA has been judiciously addressed.

articleTitle: X-Band Circularly Polarized Quadrifilar Helix Antennas for Spacecraft TT&C and Data Transmission Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Circularly polarized quadrifilar helix antennas are designed at X-Band for Low earth orbit Data transmission and TT&C applications. The proposed antennas provide a broader coverage on earth compared to that of circularly polarized patch antennas with return loss better than 15 dB for around 10% bandwidth. For Data antenna, ± 62° coverage gain of 1 dBi, minimum peak gain of 6 dBi is achieved and for TT&C antenna, ± 90° coverage gain of 0 dBi is achieved. The larger coverage area implies seamless data reception for longer periods of time. In this letter, design and experimental validation of impact on the radiation pattern with change in the take-off angle of the filars along with fabrication criticalities are discussed in detail.

articleTitle: An Antenna With A Sectoral Radiation Pattern Based On A Modulated Metasurface Ground Plane
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Various applications such as Global Navigation Satellite Systems, sensors, automotive radars, and millimetre wave imaging systems require broad fields of view of antennas. Such a requirement leads to antennas with sectoral radiation patterns where the level of radiation pattern outside of the field of view area should be as small as possible. Such radiation patterns can be realized using an omnidirectional antenna installed on a ground plane. The ground plane suppresses the undesired radiation. Creating a sectoral radiation pattern is possible using various metasurface-based ground planes. This paper investigates a modulated metasurface ground plane with a three-dipole antenna to achieve a sectoral radiation pattern. A semitransparent surface located near the ground plane’s edges suppresses undesired radiation. We investigate the effect of back radiation suppression while using resistive or inductively resistive semitransparent edge.

articleTitle: Design a Super Wideband Antenna with Dual Band Notch Characteristics and its MIMO Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This work presents a compact super wide band (SWB) antenna with dual band notch features. The proposed antenna tenders the SWB characteristic by tapering the rectangular radiator at its bottom corners and fedline along with defected ground plane. The antenna initially designed for SWB applications afterwards dual band notch characteristic is introduced by inserting an inverted F-shaped stubs beside the feedline and folded T-shaped notches in the patch. The results show that antenna achieved 178% impedance bandwidth ranging between 2.33 GHz to 40 GHz with dual band notch at WiMax and WLAN band. The electrical equivalent circuit is also realized. The antenna’s simulated and its equivalent circuit’s results are found in well agreement. Further, two elements MIMO antenna using a decoupling structure is designed.

articleTitle: GaAs-Based Multi-Functional Beamforming MMIC for X-Band SAR Applications: Design, and Performance Evaluation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents the development of a miniaturized GaAs-based multi-functional monolithic microwave integrated circuit (MMIC) designed for X-Band synthetic aperture radar (SAR) applications. Utilizing the OMMIC D01PHS process with a 130 nm gate length, the MMIC integrates phase shifting, amplification, and attenuation functionalities using 98 numbers of microwave transistors in a compact size of $\mathrm{6 m m x} \mathbf{~} \mathrm{4.5 m m}$. In the transmit path, the MMIC incorporates a 6-bit digital phase shifter (DPS), a small signal amplifier and a driver amplifier, achieving a gain of $\gt15 \mathrm{~dB}$ with a phase error of ${\lt}6^{\circ} \mathrm{rms}$, providing precise beam steering capabilities. The receive path features small signal amplifiers (SSAs), a 6-bit DPS, and a 6-bit digital phase shifter (DPS), delivering a gain of $\gt12 \mathrm{~dB}$, with a phase error of ${\lt}6^{\circ} \mathrm{~ r m s ~ a n d ~ a ~ g a i n ~ e r r o r ~ o f ~}{\lt}0.5 \mathrm{~dB}$ rms. The paper details the design and simulation process, fabrication, and testing of the MMIC, highlighting its performance in comparison with prior studies. Compared to previous GaAs-based designs that employed separate MMICs for different functionalities, this work demonstrates superior miniaturization and integration, effectively reducing system complexity and size.

articleTitle: Multi-Band and Multi-Functional Reflective Type Polarization Converting Metasurface
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents a single-layer multi-band polarization converting metasurface for both cross and circular polarization conversion. This proposed multi-band polarization converting metasurface (MPCM) behaves as a reflective-type linear-to-cross polarization converter with a minimum 90% polarization conversion ratio (PCR) over the frequency bands of $3.43-3.45\ \mathbf{G H z}, 3.75-3.81\ \mathbf{G H z}$, and $4.72-4.82\ \mathbf{G H z}$. On the other hand, for a linearly polarized incident wave on the MPCM, the reflected wave would be circularly polarized for the frequency bands of $3.41-3.42\ \mathbf{G H z}, 3.46-3.50\ \mathbf{G H z}, 3.67-3.73\ \mathbf{G H z}, 3.84-3.91\ \mathbf{G H z}, 4.55-4.67\ \mathbf{G H z}$, and $4.87-4.97\ \mathbf{G H z}$. The MPCM unit cell consists of two diagonally placed square-shaped rings joined by a meandered microstrip line on the top of a metal-backed Rogers RT5870 substrate. The unit cell is compact with periodicity $0.158 \lambda_{0} \times 0.158 \lambda_{0}$ and low profile with a thickness of $0.018 \lambda_{0}$. The proposed MPCM offers a promising platform for applications in radar cross-section reduction, communication systems, and remote sensing technologies.

articleTitle: Advanced Step Tracking Technique for Improved Satellite Path Prediction
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents a gradient-based step tracking algorithm implemented in MATLAB and Arduino. By interfacing two-axis gimbals, a reflector antenna, a power meter, and an Arduino, we demonstrated the algorithm’s effectiveness in the CATF test range. Our system successfully tracks the signal peak, even with the antenna platform in motion and in the presence of modulated signals. We achieved a tracking accuracy of $\mathbf{0. 0 5}$ degrees and a tracking speed of $\mathbf{0. 0 5}$ degrees per second, enhancing real-time satellite path prediction and monitoring for both commercial and scientific applications.

articleTitle: Metal-Only Reflectarray Based on Polarization Conversion Element for W-Band
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A polarization rotation element based metalonly reflectarray is proposed for (W-band) spectrum. The unit cell has a double-arrow slot on a metallic sheet that has a periodicity of $1 \mathrm{~mm}\left(\lambda_{0} / 3\right.$ at 100 GHz) and thickness of 0.2 mm. The required phase shift is achieved by rotating the slot on the metal sheet by ± 45°. The reflectarray features a circular aperture having a diameter of $\mathbf{3 0} \mathbf{~ m m}$ and is engineered to operate in the sub-millimeter-wave frequencies and the early terahertz spectrum. A pyramidal horn antenna that has a gain of $\mathbf{1 3 ~ d B i}$ at 100 GHz is used to excite the reflectarray. The focal length is $\mathbf{2 4}$ mm, resulting in an $\mathrm{F} / \mathrm{D}$ ratio of 0.8. The reflectarray achieves a gain of 21.7 dBi with an aperture efficiency of 15% at 100 GHz. Additionally, it features a 3-dB gain bandwidth of the aperture spans 14%, covering frequencies from 93 GHz to 107 GHz, underscoring its capability for early THz applications.

articleTitle: Magnet-Free Circulator Using BAW Filters Based on Spatiotemporal Modulation for Full-Duplex Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents the design and measurement of a magnet-free circulator based on bulk acoustic wave (BAW) filters, employing spatiotemporal modulation techniques for full-duplex communication systems. BAW filters are recognized for their high-quality factors, which allow for a reduced modulation frequency compared to previous LC implementations. The appropriate modulation frequency and amplitude facilitate the routing of electromagnetic signals to the desired port without using a magnet. Simulations were conducted using the Advanced Design System (ADS). Commercial off-the-shelf BAW filters and varactors were integrated onto a Rogers RT/duroid 5880 substrate. The measured results of the proposed circulator indicate an insertion loss (IL) of 9 dB, isolation of 18 dB from port 1 to port 3, a 15 dB isolation bandwidth (IX-BW) of 8 MHz, and a return loss (RL) of approximately 33 dB at 2.5 GHz with 19 MHz sinusoidal modulation signals.

articleTitle: Fresnel Zone Number for Localization of Ground Plane
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Concept of Fresnel zone number is used to localized the ground plane of aperture antenna. A finite circular ground plane with slots has been used to improve the gain of an openended waveguide (OEWG). Dimension of ground plane and the positions of slots on the ground plane are based on the Fresnel zone number. The slots are introduced corresponding to even Fresnel zone number and their width are optimized to improve the gain of the OEWG. Next, the Fresnel zone number is used for elliptical ground plane with elliptical slots to demonstrate the E-plane and H-plane symmetrical beam pattern from an OEWG.

articleTitle: Highly sensitive Si/h-BN exotic avalanche photo detector for applications in IR detection: A Detailed Numerical Investigation and Experimental Verification
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper reports the superiority of superlattice Si/h-BN exotic Avalanche Photodiode over its flat profile Si counterpart in IR wavelength region. A Quantum Modified Schrodinger-Poisson Drift Diffusion model is established and applied to study the electro optical characteristic of superlattice Si/h-BN exotic Avalanche Photodiode for application in IR detection. The effect of $h-B N$ in the superlattice structure of the device under test is studied through a comprehensive simulation modeling. This depicts the betterment of external and internal quantum efficiency compared to its flat profile counterpart. This study also reports the suitability of $\operatorname{Si} / \mathrm{h}-\mathrm{BN}$ exotic based APD photo sensors in terms of better photo-responsivity over its flat profile Si counterpart. Significant Noise reduction in case of superlattice Si/h-BN exotic Avalanche Photodiode would open its application possibility as low noise single photon detector. The validity of an indigenously developed Quantum Modified Schrodinger-Poisson Drift Diffusion model is established through experimental verification. To the best of authors’ knowledge this is the first research report on superlattice $\mathrm{Si} / \mathrm{h}$ BN exotic Avalanche Photodiode as IR detector.

Author Keywords: Quantum Modified Schrodinger-Poisson Drift Diffusion model

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of a Planar Multiband Antenna for Applications in Terahertz Spectrum
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A monolayer Graphene planar THz antenna is planned, the antenna consists of three layers that start with a ground plane, and a Silicon substrate and end with a monolayer graphene patch layer. The dimension of the silicon substrate is $25 \times 25 \mu \mathrm{~m}^{2}$ and this is also the same for the ground plane. The dimension of the graphene patch is $20 \times 20 \mu \mathrm{~m}^{2}$, and the thickness of the PEC, Silicon, and Graphene patch is $1 \mu \mathrm{~m}, 3 \mu \mathrm{~m}$, and 0.64 nm respectively. The designed antenna provides multiple bands in the THz frequency region the first band is 4.710842 THz to 6.060448, the second one is 6.452828 THz to 7.313617, and the last one is 8.5553 THz to 9.360948 THz. The bandwidths are 1.349606 THz, 0.860789 THz, and 0.805648THz, the Fractional bandwidths are 25.05%, 12.50%, and 8.99% for initial to third bands correspondingly. The maximum gain and directivity achieved are around 7.025 dBi and 7.242 dBi respectively. The antenna achieved a lower reflection coefficient of -25.89212 dB at the frequency 9.208484 THz. The designed Monolayer graphene planar THz antenna (MGTA) is suitable for many THz applications like THz wireless communications, THz imaging, Defense, Industrial applications, spectroscopy, and other THz applications.

articleTitle: A Metasurface-based Flexible Triple Bandpass Filter in ISM and IoT bands towards Wearable Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this paper, a single layered, flexible metasurface (MS)-based slot type triple bandpass filter has been proposed for the ISM and IoT bands. The unit cell of the proposed MS structure consists of three slots designed on a flexible jeans substrate viz., one rectangular ring, one inverted U-shaped slot and a circular slot at its centre. The proposed MS exhibits three distinct transmission bands at $2.4 \mathrm{GHz}, 5.28 \mathrm{GHz}$ and 5.82 GHz. In addition, two stop bands are also realized at 3.77 GHz and 5.67 GHz making the structure suitable for wearable antenna applications. The performance of the structure is analyzed under incident angle variation to find that the structure is angularly stable up to 45°. The electric field distributions have been studied at the frequencies of operation to find the roles of the various slots used in the MS design. The first and the last transmission bands have potential applications in the ISM domain while the middle one makes the transmission feasible for IoT applications. The low profile combined with the compact design make the MS structure useful for wearable spatial filter.

articleTitle: Time-Modulated Array for Direction of Arrival Estimation using Unipolar and Bipolar Pulse Sequences
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper explores the methods of estimating direction of arrival (DoA) using time-modulated array (TMA) controlled by two modulating pulse sequences, namely, unipolar and bipolar. The performances of the TMA based DoA estimators with unipolar and bipolar pulse sequences are compared and the detailed analysis of the obtained results are presented. The study with numerical results in terms of different DoA estimation parameters such as gain, scanning range, power spectrum under different SNR reveals that the TMA using bipolar pulse sequence performs better as compared to that of unipolar pulse sequence.

articleTitle: 3D Printed Cylindrical Luneburg Lens
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Two-dimensional (2D) Luneburg lenses are attracting increasing research interest due to their unique beam collimation and steering capabilities. This paper explores the design and potential applications of a 2D Luneburg lens using PLA (polylactic acid) as the 3D printing material. Unlike the conventional Luneburg lens with different dielectric layers, we propose a design that utilizes only one material, and the refractive indices are varied by introducing air voids inside the substrate without compromising the structural or mechanical integrity of the lens. When fed with a waveguide, the proposed lens works in the X-band with a combined gain of approximately 12.7 dBi when fed by a waveguide. The lens was fabricated and verified by measurements.

articleTitle: Real-time UAV Detection through RF Signal Analysis and Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper introduces a real-time detection of non-cooperating unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) using RF signal analysis and machine learning. The system features an RF transceiver module that detects signals as weak as -120 dBm over a 2 to 6 GHz range, with a focus on UAV communication frequencies at 2.4 and 5.8 GHz. An automated Pan and Tilt Unit (PTU) facilitates comprehensive spatial coverage with 360° azimuth and 75° elevation scanning to pinpoint the direction of maximum RF radiation. Machine learning algorithms, including Gaussian Naive Bayes, Neural Networks, and Support Vector Machines, are employed to accurately classify and differentiate UAV signals from other RF sources. Extensive testing confirms the system’s efficacy in real-time UAV identification and tracking, achieving a classification accuracy of 99.6%. This robust integration of RF signal processing and machine learning presents a significant advancement in UAV detection technology, addressing critical security and surveillance needs.

articleTitle: Generation of Custom Shaped Beams with Digital Beam Forming in Focal Array Fed Reflector Antenna Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents detailed design guidelines for generating custom-shaped beams using Digital Beam Forming (DBF) in focal array-fed reflector antennas. The DBF enabled antenna system has been demonstrated to generate beams of various shapes, sizes and quantity. This ensures that the payload is flexible and reconfigurable so that the antenna radiation pattern can be altered to meet the ever-evolving needs and demands of the users. The characteristics of the generated antenna radiation pattern are governed by the excitation coefficients generated by the DBF processor, which are fed to the input of each array element. An optimization algorithm has been developed to determine these coefficients and optimize them in order to generate the specific shape and size of the required beam. A focal arrayfed reflector has been designed and the formation of different custom shaped beams has been demonstrated in this work. Such reconfigurable and flexible payloads find applications in the fields of satellite communications, remote sensing, broadcast services and tracking techniques.

Author Keywords: Focal array fed reflector antenna systems

articleTitle: Design and assessment of low frequency synchronous demodulator in Dicke radiometer for passive tissue thermometry
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this paper we present the design and assessment of a low frequency synchronous demodulator circuit in a single reference Dicke microwave radiometer meant for tissue thermometry. In medical applications, microwave radiometry is used as a non-invasive method to estimate the core-bodytemperature (CBT) of a subject by integrating the total noise power emitted by the sub-cutaneous heat source. However, since the method is sensitive to ambient conditions and external noise, a bias cancellation system configuration known as Dicke radiometer is needed. This system configuration requires a synchronous demodulator which allows us to subtract the system bias signal from the noise signal of interest. Towards this goal, we have designed, simulated, fabricated, and tested a low frequency synchronous demodulator circuit. This circuit uses an analog SPDT switch to separate the source and reference signals from the modulated signal, integrates them and then uses a switched capacitor circuit to obtain the differential signal. Preliminary results show the ability to resolve signals with differences in amplitude of few millivolts over the narrow clinical temperature range of 35 to $42^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$.

articleTitle: Design and Development of Ultra-Wideband Receiver for Impulse Ground Penetrating Radar
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents the design and development of ultra-wideband receiver for impulse Ground Penetrating Radar. The developed miniaturised receiver operates over an ultra-wide bandwidth from 0.5 to 2 GHz and caters to large input dynamic range from $\mathbf{- 7 6} \mathbf{~ d B m}$ to $\mathbf{- 1 0} \mathbf{d B m}$, with capability of digitally controlled gain, while maintaining low noise figure. It has excellent temperature performance with variation in gain upto 0.6 dB only in the temperature range of $-10^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$ to $50^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$ achieved using passive temperature compensation network. The proposed receiver is realized in a compact size of $126 \mathrm{~mm} \times 120 \mathrm{~mm} \times 27 \mathrm{~mm}$ with weight of 350 grams and DC power consumption of 2.6 W.

articleTitle: Analysis of groundwater-induced land subsidence in Kolkata City using InSAR and Sentinel-1 data
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Kolkata is the capital city of West Bengal, India and an urban dense metropolitan city. The aim of the paper is to use PS-InSAR technique for analysis of time-series of 63 sets of C-Band Sentinel-1 images acquired in ascending pass from Jan 2019 - Mar 2024 to calculate the time-series of radar line of sight (LOS) displacement and the average LOS velocity. The results show the SD of mean LOS velocity to be in the range of 4.4 to $-7.7 \mathrm{~mm} / \mathrm{yr}$ in the city with majority of values less than $1.7 \mathrm{~mm} /$ year. Some areas to the north like DumDum and north west near Rajabagan have subsidence as high as $\mathbf{- 3 0} \mathbf{~ m m} / \mathbf{y r}$. The results were compared with 23 GWL observations from CGWB and DWRID, West Bengal for the same period and they were found in good agreement with a correlation of around 0.63, confirming the cause of the subsidence in the city.

articleTitle: High Efficient Low profile Metasurface for RF Energy Harvesting
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this article, a simple low-profile metasurface based RF energy harvester (MSEH) in microwave region is proposed. The unit cell structure consists of a metallic circular ring with two rectangular patches that can exhibits an electromagnetic (EM) wave absorptivity greater than $\mathbf{9 9 \%}$. The AC energy of each cell is pooled through the load resistance of $130 \Omega$ connected with via where efficiency is achieved up to 98.12% at 4.6 GHz. Simulation results are optimized at 4.6 GHz with different parameters. The performance of the proposed device is angularly stable up to $\mathbf{4 0}$ degree. The proposed device can be used for different application such as in radar, satellite, and wireless communication.

articleTitle: A Compact Fractal Microstrip Patch Antenna for Skin Cancer Detection Using Monostatic Radar-Based Microwave Imaging Technique
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: The inherent advantages of being non-invasive and non-ionizing have drawn the attention of cancer researchers to microwave imaging (MWI). Therefore, this study focuses on monostatic radar-based microwave imaging (MRMWI) of skin cancer using a compact Ultra-Wide Band (UWB) Hybrid Fractal Microstrip Patch Antenna (HFMPA). The HFMPA functions as a sensor and has dimensions of 24×20×0.8 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>. It comprises a combination of Pythagoras tree and Snowflake-shaped resonators alongside a defective ground surface (DGS) and a slotted microstrip feed line. It operates within the 5.71-16.94 GHz frequency range with a peak gain of 5.1 dB at 16 GHz. The performance analysis of the proposed HFMPA as a sensor for MRMWI has been carried out in the vicinity of a four-layered design bio-mimic of the forearm in Computer Simulation Technology (CST) Microwave Studio (MWS) software. The HFMPA is positioned 19 mm from the bio-mimic of the forearm to collect backscattered signals (S11) at different positions around it. The collected data is pre-processed and then used with the Coherent-Factor Delay Multiply and Sum (CF-DMAS) beamforming algorithm to generate images of the inspected regions. The antenna’s specific absorption rate (SAR) is 1.38 W/Kg for 1 g of tissue, indicating safe for human exposure.

articleTitle: Orthogonal Chirp Orbital Angular Momentum Beams
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this paper, orthogonal chirp orbital angular momentum (COAM) beams with a non-linear azimuthal spiral phase variation are introduced. The COAM beams have a linear spatial frequency variation in the azimuthal plane similar to chirp signals. This variation contrasts the constant spatial frequency variation in the case of conventional OAM beams. Thus, a COAM beam consists of a spread of multiple OAM modes. This mode-spreading makes the COAM beams resistant to spatial frequency distortions during propagation, which would otherwise adversely affect the mode orthogonality of conventional OAM beams at radio frequencies. It is shown that orthogonal COAM beams having the same linear spatial frequency variation are associated with an additional azimuthal phase variation of integer multiples of 360 degrees. Generation of COAM beams is demonstrated using uniform circular arrays (UCAs) with antenna element phase excitations that vary as the square of the element number. It is also shown that concentric UCAs can generate multiplexed orthogonal COAM beams. Several examples of such beams are generated using UCAs designed at 17.8 GHz operating frequency via full-wave simulations in the CST Microwave Studio software. Such COAM beams could enable robust OAM communications in turbulent propagation conditions.

articleTitle: Design, Simulation and Testing of Wave Collection and Transport System for Michelson Interferometer Diagnostic
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A Wave Collection and Transport System (WCTS) has been designed and simulated using CST Microwave Studio to transport electromagnetic waves from tokamak hall to the Michelson interferometer (MI) system. The MI system is the diagnostic used for plasma electron temperature profile measurement on the tokamak. Simulations were carried out in the frequency range $\mathbf{7 0 - 1 7 0} \mathrm{GHz}$ range for the transmission line components using CST microwave studio. To minimize propagation losses, oversized waveguides were chosen instead of fundamental. For selection of suitable oversized waveguide, simulations were performed in $S, X$ and Ka band and best performing band was selected for WCTS. These oversized waveguides not only reduce propagation losses but also decrease the group delay of the propagating wave as compared to fundamental waveguide. The primary components of the oversized WCTS include waveguides, miter bends in both $\mathbf{E}$ and H planes, and wire-grid polarizers (WGP) to select the polarization of electromagnetic waves from the plasma. While the use of oversized waveguides significantly reduces the overall transmission line losses, it also introduces the issue of higher-order modes. The transmission line components have been designed, simulated, and experimentally validated in the laboratory, and the results have been presented.

articleTitle: Wideband Lightweight Integrated Q-Band Up-Down Converters for Communication System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Design concepts of integrated, wideband multi-channel Q band up-down converters are described in this article. Integrated up-down converters are important part of ELINT systems to process/analyse HF/S band or millimetre wave signals to Q/S/C band signals. Frequency planning of up-down converters are carried out judiciously thus; in-band undesirable spurs can be avoided. Various S/C/X/Ku/K/Q band sharp rejection narrow/wide band filters are designed to get excellent harmonics, spurious, image, isolations and in/out of band features to meet the targeted specifications. Health monitoring status signals are generated for all signals including power supplies to control the system performances. Excellent signal flatness over the band, in-band matching, phase noise, image, in/out of band spurious performances are achieved over ESS $\left(-25^{\circ} \mathrm{C}\right.$ to $+55^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$ and pre-post temperature 3 axis RV) to prove the design concept.

Author Keywords: Random Vibration (RV) and Environmental Stress Screening (ESS)

articleTitle: Design of Low Noise Broadband Three Channel Receiver Front-end at X band with High Channel to Channel Isolation and High Image Rejection
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this paper, design of a three channel RF receiver front-end at X band is presented with more than 60 dB inter channel isolation and less than $\pm 1.5 \mathrm{~dB}$ gain variation over $8.5 \%$ bandwidth. An image rejection filter and 3-way Wilkinson power divider is designed and simulated for realization of the receiver. Incorporating simulated data of these components, system simulation is carried out to optimize channel to channel isolation, image frequency rejection and gain flatness. The receiver is realized in a compact size of 16 cm x $8.5 \mathrm{~cm} \times 1.8 \mathrm{~cm}$. Fabricated prototype has a conversion gain of $\mathrm{3 0 ~ d B}$, noise figure of 2.5 dB and image rejection of 100 dB.

articleTitle: A Novel Dual-Band Matching Circuit Covering Wide Frequency Ratio suitable for 5G applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents a novel structure for dual-band matching networks, designed specifically for RF applications. The proposed matching network employs a three-section structure, and analytical expressions to calculate the characteristic impedance and length of these sections are presented. The proposed structure is validated for matching the optimal impedance of the 6 W GaN device at two distinct frequencies, 0.85 GHz and 3.5 GHz, to a $50-\text{ohm}$ load. We achieved the S11 parameter below 20 dB in simulations at a frequency ratio of approximately 4. Measured results validate the effectiveness of the proposed design, demonstrating excellent impedance matching and potential for practical RF applications.

articleTitle: RF Power Characterization of Indigenously Designed and Fabricated 130 Watt GaN HEMT Power Bar in packaged form
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Electrical characterization of a power HEMT includes DC IV, Pulsed IV, S-parameter and Load-pull Characterizations. Characterization of large periphery GaN HEMT itself is a challenge. Devices having gate periphery more than $\mathbf{4 0 0} \boldsymbol{\mu \mathrm { m }}$ starts to oscillate as DC bias is applied. Once device starts oscillating it cannot be characterized as it gives power output without any input power. This phenomenon leads to burning of the device or may damage expensive measurement equipments. Analysis of these oscillations have been carried out and developed an electrical network to suppress such oscillations. RF Characterization of in-house developed large periphery GaN HEMT devices have been carried out with the designed electrical network. Based on these measured results GaN HEMT devices with inbuilt stabilization components have been designed, fabricated and characterized. Using these large periphery unit devices, GaN HEMT power bars, which can deliver more than 100 Watt power output have been designed and fabricated. During RF characterization of the designed power bar oscillation issues were faced. Technique of off chip isolation resistors in package have been used to overcome these oscillations, that arises due to combining of multiple unit devices. Power output of more than 130 Watt has been measured in the packaged GaN HEMT power bar.

articleTitle: Development of Ku-band Heterodyne Receiver for Space applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents the development of Spaceborne Ku-band scatterometer receiver. This scatterometer is follow-on mission of on-board scatterometer of EOS-6 satellite. Developed receiver has been characterized as per defined environmental test level specifications for space as a part of test and evaluation to ensure reliable performance. It operates at 13.515625 GHz, having low noise figure of 2.1 dB, high gain of 75 dB, 0.4 dB flatness, and output $\mathrm{P}_{1 \mathrm{~dB}}$ of $\mathbf{1 0 ~ d B m}$ over the operating temperature range of $-10^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$ to $50^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$. Integrated receiver package has dimensions of $212 \times 180 \times 63(\mathrm{~mm} \times \mathrm{mm} \times mm)$, weight of 3 Kg and power consumption of 2.7 W.

articleTitle: Four Port MIMO Frequency Tunable Dielectric Resonator Antenna for 5G Sub 6 GHz Application
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this work, a four-port multiple input multiple output (MIMO) Frequency Tunable (FT) Dielectric Resonator Antenna (DRA) with connected ground for 5G Sub 6 GHz is presented. The proposed antenna is designed on FR4 epoxy with a thickness of $\mathbf{1. 6} \mathbf{~ m m}$. The DRA is designed through Alumina materials. FT is achieved through the PIN Diode. The Tunable Range (TR) and Total Spectrum (TS) of the proposed antenna are 62.09% and 47.32%, respectively. The MIMO performance parameters Envelope Correlation Coefficient (ECC), Diversity Gain (DG), and Total Active Reflection Coefficient (TARC) are calculated and found within the acceptable limit. The values of ECC and DG are 0.0025 and 10 dB respectively. Hence, the proposed antenna is suitable for 5 G Sub 6 GHz.

articleTitle: Compact Dual Band Implantable Antenna for Bio-telemetry Application
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this paper, a compact dual-band implantable antenna working at 915 MHz and 2.45 GHz is presented. The proposed antenna consists of several horizontal and vertical slots along with the shorting pin and full ground plane. Due to the compact design along with the full ground plane, the structure became a good candidate for implantable devices. The proposed antenna has a compact size of $9.5 \times 9.5 \times 0.54 {~mm}^{3}$. Moreover, the estimated specific absorption rate (SAR) complies with the IEEE standard for human safety. Lastly, a prototype of the proposed dual-band implantable antenna configuration has been fabricated and tested, and the measured result shows a good degree of consistency with the simulated one.

articleTitle: Beam Tilting Phase Gradient Metasurface for mm-Wave Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A robust beam tilting tri-layered Phase Gradient Metasurface (PGMS) lens is proposed for Multiple Input Multiple Output (MIMO) applications. The PGMS unit cell has transmission coefficient $\gt0.7$ and transmission phase varies from $0^{0}$ to ${2 2 6. 2 5}$. An array of $5 \times 12$ unit cells lens is kept at a height of $0.46 \lambda_{0}$ to tilt the beams of Antenna 1 and Antenna 2 to $-24^{0}$ and $+24^{0}$ respectively in XZ-plane. The resonating frequency of proposed antenna is from 27.4 GHz to 28.26 GHz. The maximum gain is ${9. 7 1} \mathrm{~ d B i}$ at 28 GHz and the Efficiency of the antenna is 83.6%. The isolation between two MIMO antenna is 15.71 dB with PGMS lens. The total antenna profile with the lens is $0.71 \lambda_{0}$.

articleTitle: Circularly-polarized High Aperture Efficiency Multi-Section Smooth-walled Horn Antenna at Kaband for Space-Borne Beacon
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents design, analysis and realization of a Horn Antenna having high aperture efficiency and low axial ratio, for right hand circular polarization (RHCP) at Ka-band (19.2-20.2 GHz). Horn with septum polarizer is the key system to achieve circular polarization. In this paper the design of linear profile multi-modal horn and compact septum polarizer is proposed to full-fill the objective. Horn and septum polarizer are analyzed and optimized using mode-matching and method of moment-based software (CHAMP and microwave $\mu$-wave wizard). Phi-symmetric variation in radius along the length is provided uniformly to excite $\mathrm{TE}_{1 \mathrm{n}}$ and $\mathrm{TM}_{1 \mathrm{n}}$ modes only in desirable amplitude and phase to achieve a high gain and low cross-polarization level which will result high edge of coverage (EOC) gain and low cross-polarization level at given region.

Author Keywords: Righthand circular polarization (RHCP) & Left hand circular polarization (LHCP)

articleTitle: Characterizing RIS-Reflected EM Waves Based on Gaussian Beam Models
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper explores the reflection and propagation of EM waves by Reconfigurable Intelligent Surfaces (RIS) using Gaussian beam models. We characterize the impinging waveform by experimentally determining the beam width and phase distribution. Furthermore, we detail the experimental setup and show accurate curve-fitting using the Gaussian beam model. Finally, we solve an electrically large RIS problem semi-analytically. In particular, we use the experimentally obtained impinging wavefront to analyze the far-field behavior of large aperture metasurfaces in V band application. This method is applicable for RIS and passive reflect metasurfaces with nearly full phase coverage.
