articleTitle: A Metasurface based Dual Passband Filter with Sharp Rejection for L-band Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this paper, a dual passband filter has been proposed with an extremely sharp rejection band between them incorporating metasurface (MS) structure in L-band. A highly rejecting stopband of 20 dB has been achieved at 1486 MHz between the two closely spaced passbands located at 1211 MHz and 1761 MHz respectively. The top metallic pattern of the unit cell of the proposed MS structure has been designed on the top of a 1 mm thick FR4 dielectric comprising two inverted L slots arranged along the principal diagonal together with two ring slots. It is confirmed from the field analyses that the ring slots offer the two closely spaced passbands while the two inverted L slots are responsible for strong transmission zero at the stop band. The proposed structure offers polarization insensitive response as well as very good stability for oblique incidence up to 45°. Being electrically ultra-thin and compact in nature, the proposed structure can find potential applications in space communication and radar navigational systems at L-band.

articleTitle: Planar and Modular Silicon Package suitable for Future Large-Format 1.9 THz Heterodyne Arrays
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Heterodyne detection at sub-millimeter wavelengths is the preferred method for performing high-resolution spectroscopy on interstellar clouds. Realizing large-format heterodyne arrays would significantly improve mapping speed but has shown to be difficult due to the integration complexity of the traditional metal-machined mixer package. This paper discusses the design and performance of a planarly integrated silicon micromachined low-loss waveguide network suitable for use in multi-pixel heterodyne arrays. The network is based on a two-sided RF/LO signal coupling and a quadrature hybrid coupler to combine the two signals before mixing them to an intermediate frequency using two balanced Hot Electron Bolometer mixers. It is shown that the architecture is very suitable for realizing 7 -pixel hexagonal subarrays, and we discuss details of the fabrication, integration, and assembly of a 4-pixel demonstrator array.

articleTitle: Implementation of 2-Bit Intelligent Reflecting Surface (IRS) Tuned by Varactor Diode for Electronically Beam Steering Performance
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Reconfigurable Intelligent reflecting surface (IRS) is one of the encouraging and empowering technology for both academia and industrial research. IRS is a 2D planer surface, containing an array of a large number of passive tunable reflecting elements, capable of manipulating the reflected wave electronically. This paper focuses on the detailed study of IRS implementation to steer the IRS reflection dynamically. We proposed a design of 1-bit and 2-bit IRS unit elements at 6 GHz, integrated with a varactor diode. Then, designed and simulated a 2-bit IRS with $40 \times 40$-unit elements and analyzed its results compared with 1-bit IRS, where, the required optimal phase shift matrix is evaluated using 2D-DFT codebook-based MATLAB coding. 2-bit IRS eliminates the other additional radiated beam, coming from the IRS surface, and achieves improved HPBW and the SLL of 6° and -12 dB, respectively, whereas, for 1-bit IRS, it is 6.5° and -7.6 dB, respectively. The beam steering performance of 2-bit IRS has been verified along $0^{\circ}, 10^{\circ}, 20^{\circ}$ and 30° at the elevation plane where, ± 30° scanning angle is achieved. The 2-bit reconfigurable IRS with electronically beam steering performance has an impact usefulness in microwave wireless communication for dynamic imaging and digital modulation.

articleTitle: Flexible Dual Band Matching Solution for Diverse Complex Loads
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this work, we propose a scheme to match a wide range of complex loads at two uncorrelated frequencies to any standard loads. A wide range of frequency ratios is used for impedance matching here, which also accounts for unavoidable fabrication issues. The study utilizes two sections for the matching network where individual sections match the real and imaginary parts of the complex loads separately. The prototype, fabricated on RT/duroid 5880 substrates, lies in good proximity to the matching networks intended for the current 5G frequency band of 2.4 GHz as well as the coming $5 \mathrm{G}+/ 6 \mathrm{G}$ bands that are expected to operate on approximately 5.8 GHz commercially.

articleTitle: Low Insertion Loss 6-Bit Phase Shifter with Decoder Control for L-Band Radar
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents a low-loss and compact 6-bit electronically reconfigurable phase shifter optimized for phased array applications. The phase shifter incorporates decoderbased control circuitry specifically designed for L-band phasedarray IFF Radar antennas. Capable of achieving diverse phase shifts up to 360° with minimum LSB of 5.62° over a broad bandwidth, the design supports rapid prototyping. A prototype was fabricated, operating in the $1.03-1.09 \mathrm{GHz}$ frequency range, utilizing a Rogers 5880 substrate with a 0.78 mm thickness and a dielectric constant of 2.2. The prototype accurately produces phase differences as specified by the control signals, with phase ripples confined to within 7°. Experimental measurements demonstrate excellent agreement with simulation results, validating the proposed design methodology.

articleTitle: Passive UHF RFID-based sensor: Influence of electrical conductivity and localized surface cracks on industrial-grade metal specimens
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Early detection and localization of initial-phase surface cracks on metal structures is critical, as they can propagate and severely compromise the structural integrity of bridges, pipelines, rail, and aerospace structures. This paper presents the study of a passive wireless RFID-based crack sensor for in-situ surface crack detection on industrial-grade metal specimens of varying conductivity. A circular-shaped, symmetrical microstrip antenna-based RFID crack sensor was designed in the Ansys HFSS tool operating in the UHF region. Simulation analysis was performed for varying surface crack depths and widths in millimeter resolution for the most commonly used Aluminum Alloy 6061 and Hot-Rolled Steel 1084 grade metal specimen. It is observed that the sensor resonant frequency variation is different for varying crack depths and widths and also for varying metal specimen grades. Preliminary no-crack measurement results illustrate that the sensor RSSI and Phase change values are sensitive with respect to changes in metal specimen conductivity. It is observed that upon calibration, the sensor crack detection capability can be leveraged to diverse industrial-grade metal specimens.

articleTitle: Development of a Compact and Portable Terahertz Imaging System for Industrial Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Terahertz (THz) imaging, which employs THz radiation to see-through different materials, has a wide range of applications, from nondestructive evaluation to biomedical applications. However, typically, $\mathbf{T H z}$ imaging systems are limited to laboratory-level optical bench-based setups with sophisticated vibration isolators for efficient operation. The sensitive nature of various components of the THz imaging system has prevented its widespread usage in industrial in-field applications. Hence, the authors have developed a compact and portable terahertz imaging system suitable for in-field industrial applications. The various components of the system have been carefully selected, taking the ruggedness and low cost into consideration. The suitability of the portable THz imaging system to different application areas has been demonstrated, which includes security screening to detect concealing objects, nondestructive testing of composites, moisture detection in leaves, microplastics identification in soil, food quality assessment, porosity change assessment in pharmaceutical tablets, etc. These imaging results prove the capability of this system to be deployed in industrial field applications in the future.

articleTitle: Stepped Impedance Matching Network For The Design Of Harmonic Tuned RF Power Amplifier
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents the design of an efficient, second harmonic tuned RF Power Amplifier (PA) using stepped impedance matching networks. The stepped impedance microstrip line output matching network is designed to offer optimum impedances at fundamental $\left(f_{0}\right)$ as well as at second harmonic frequency $\left(2 f_{0}\right)$. On the other hand, the input matching network offers optimum impedance at fundamental whereas at second harmonic frequency, it differs from the impedance required for optimum performance of the Macom’s CG2H40010F GaN HEMT at $2 f 0$. This condition restricts the amplification of any unwanted signal at $2 f_{0}$. The designed PA delivers 12.4 W of CW power in Class-AB mode of operation at 2.45 GHz with measured Power Added Efficiency (PAE) and drain efficiency of $\mathbf{7 2. 2 \%}$ and $\mathbf{7 3. 1 \%}$ respectively. Measured Gain and input return loss of the amplifier are within $19 \pm 0.6 \mathrm{~dB}$ and better than 10 dB respectively, over $2.37 \mathrm{GHz}-2.65 \mathrm{GHz}$.

articleTitle: Optimization of Grid Parameters of Dual-Gridded Reflector Antenna to Improve Cross-polar Performance for Wide-Coverage Contoured-Beam
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A new method for getting improved cross-polar performance of Dual-Gridded Reflector (DGR) Antenna by optimization of grid parameters; has been described in this paper. The grid tilt angle, grid width and grid spacing of DGR have been optimized using Multi-level Optimization using ‘Minmax’ and Multi-level Coordinate Search (MCS) optimization algorithms. Better XPI (cross-polar isolation) performance has been achieved without affecting EoC (Edge of Coverage) Gain. The DGR antenna has been analyzed using PO (Physical Optics) & PTD (Physical Theory of Diffraction) and MoM (Method of Moments) of software Ticra Tool 24.0. Two corrugated linear-polarized horns (Lin-V and Lin-H) are used to illuminate rear and front shell of DGR, respectively. Beam has been shaped for India coverage area using ‘Minmax’ optimization algorithm for specified EoC (Edge of Coverage) Gain and XPI (cross-polar isolation). The grid parameters have been optimized after shaping of surfaces for front and rear shells for further improvement in XPI. However, it can be combined with surface-shaping. Major outcome of the grid optimization of DGR facilitate compliance of -35 dB XPI for Indian mainland for both polarization.

articleTitle: Circularly Polarized Cylindrical Dielectric Resonator Antenna with a New Rectangular-frame Aperture Feed for 5G Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper introduces a rectangular-frame aperture feed applied to a cylindrical dielectric resonator antenna (CDRA) to achieve circular polarization (CP). The CDRA has been placed on a square ground substrate to implement the antenna. A rectangular microstrip line is used to feed the aperture. The rectangular-frame aperture is oriented at a 45 degree angle relative to the microstrip line on the ground plane. This orientation generates the two orthogonal field components necessary for circular polarization within the CDRA. Based on the proposed theory, a right-hand circularly polarized (RHCP) antenna has been designed. The antenna structure was optimized and analyzed using high-frequency structure simulator (HFSS) software. The resulting design achieves an impedance bandwidth of 18.18% and a $3-\mathrm{dB}$ axial ratio bandwidth of 15.75%. Additionally, the antenna demonstrates a gain exceeding 6 dB across the operating bandwidth. The effective bandwidth of this design covers the 3.5 GHz band, which is critical for the mid-band spectrum in 5 G networks and other contemporary communication applications.

articleTitle: Low Profile Reconfigurable Metasurface in X-Band for Electronic Beam-steering
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A low profile reconfigurable metasurface (MS) with single X-Band antenna element, having fast electronic Beam-Steering (BS), is presented for low cost applications. The designed structure consists of a X-Band microstrip patch antenna with inset feed as the radiator, illuminating a MS layer containing $5 \times 5$ programmable closed square loop Unit Cells (UCs) as the superstrate layer. PIN diodes have been embedded in UCs to alter the electric field intensity within the MS layer in order to switch the radiation pattern in a given H-plane of the antenna. Proposed design not only reduces no. of PIN diodes to 16 from initial 100 to achieve BS in H-plane but also incorporates a optimized hybrid scheme for biasing diodes. As a proof-of-concept, a prototype antenna with MS is fabricated and measured. It achieves beam-steering upto 24° across frequency range of 500 MHz in a compact size of $1.2 \lambda_{0} \times 1.2 \lambda_{0} \times 0.12 \lambda_{0}$ (where $\lambda_{0}$ is the wavelength at 8.6 GHz). Good agreement between simulated and measured results for antenna input return loss validates the design principle across different directions. Furthermore, design also shows a considerable improvement in impedance bandwidth (BW) as well as in gain w.r.t. antenna radiator alone.

articleTitle: Optimization and mathematical analysis for mosaic patch antenna for improved gain
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This study introduces a novel idea of the Mosaic Patch Antenna, based on a calculus-based MIMO (Multiple Input, Multiple Output) antenna design customized for wireless transmission. These square-shaped cuts are arranged in a unique mosaic pattern, which has been patterned in three different iterations to optimize the performance of the patch antenna. This mosaic cut is performed on the top, bottom, and center of the patch, which leads to an increase in gain ranging from 0.02 to 0.035 dBi, culminating in a total gain of 3.2 dBi and a bandwidth of 3 GHz. Deriving exact formulas for the mosaic cut’s length and breadth allowed for this achievement by guaranteeing correct patch antenna dimensions and ideal design parameters. Due to mosaic cuts, it is operating in TE12 higher order mode, and its advantages are increased gain, directional radiation patterns, and enhanced beam shaping. These patch antennas enhance the performance of Radio Frequency Identification (RFID) systems, which often utilize patch antennas with a 2.4 GHz cut-off frequency and require a narrow bandwidth. The results show that the Mosaic Patch Antenna, which offers good performance in the $\mathrm{2. 4} \mathrm{~ G H z}$ frequency region, is a feasible solution for cutting-edge communication systems.

articleTitle: An X-Band RF Binary Phase Modulator Based on a Reflection-Type Phase Shifter
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents a high-speed wideband RF binary phase modulator based on a reflection-type phase shifter for X-band applications. A PIN diode in the shunt arm, connected with a transmission line of characteristic impedance Z and electrical length $\theta^{\circ}$, is used as a load at the through and coupling ports of a conventional 3 dB branch line hybrid coupler (BLC) to minimize the parasitic effects of the diode at X -band frequencies. The load impedance can be switched between low and high by applying forward and reverse bias to the PIN diode, causing the phase shift $\left(S_{21}\right)$ to change by 180° for BPSK modulation for a continuous wave frequency of 10 GHz. The load network is further modified with an additional series transmission line to maximize the load impedance ratio in the ON and OFF states of the diode. The measured insertion losses are 2.17 dB and 1.18 dB in the ON and OFF states of the PIN diode, respectively. The measured $\left|S_{11}\right|$ is below $\mathbf{- 1 5} \pm 5 \text{dB}$ over the $\mathbf{8 - 1 2} \mathbf{~ G H z}$ range, and the measured phase difference between the ON and OFF states remains at $180^{\circ} \pm 10^{\circ}$ over the $\mathbf{9. 4 2 - 1 0. 2 3 ~ G H z}$ range.

articleTitle: Compact Monopole MIMO Antenna with SRR and DGS for Satellite Communication
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This This paper proposes a design for a four-port Monopole MIMO antenna using a split ring resonator (SRR) and defective ground structure (DGS) for satellite communication. Single element Monopole antenna having SRR and feed line at the top of the substrate and bottom having DGS. The coupling capacitance between SRR and the feed line provides better impedance matching. In order to achieve low mutual coupling and enhanced isolation with high gain, In MIMO the elements with SRR and DGS are positioned orthogonal to one another. The frequency range covered by the Proposed MIMO antenna design is between $9.4 \mathrm{G H z}$ to 14.2 GHz and has an overall size $45 \text{mm} \times 45 \text{mm} \times 1.6 \text{mm}$. The recommended MIMO antenna has an isolation of $\gt15 \text{dB}$ between the elements with a gain of 4 dB and covers the Satellite communication range. The diversity performance metrics such as envelope correlation coefficient ($\mathrm{E C C}\lt0.001$), diversity gain (DG >9.95dB), Mean effective gain (MEG 1), and Total active reflection coefficient (TARC - 10dB) have been simulated and characteristic results as S parameters, radiation pattern are well pleased.

articleTitle: Microfluidic Sensor Based on SIW Self-Diplexer Antenna for Simultaneous Detection of Adulteration of Different Oils
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents a microfluidic sensor utilizing a substrate integrated waveguide self-diplexer antenna for simultaneous detection of adulteration of mustard oil with groundnut and coconut oils. The self-diplexing feature is achieved by loading a diagonal rectangular-shaped slot on the top metallic plane of the antenna. The diplexer resonates at two distinct frequencies, 4.53 GHz and 6.01 GHz, with a minimum isolation > 35 dB between the two antenna elements. Two microfluidic pockets, made from PDMS, are positioned on the antenna. One pocket is used for the detection of coconut oil adulteration in mustard oil and the other groundnut oil adulteration in mustard oil. The interaction of these oils with the electromagnetic fields causes shifts in the resonant frequencies of the antenna. The sensor enables both simultaneous detection of two different oils and individual liquid sensing. The frequency shifts observed are 840 MHz for pure mustard oil. The sensor achieves high sensitivities of 2.19 GHz/RIU for coconut oil adulteration in mustard oil and 2.77 GHz/RIU for groundnut oil adulteration in mustard oil. These features make the sensor well-suited for detection of adulteration of oils.

articleTitle: Optimal Design of Planar Log-periodic Array Antenna: A Revisit through Theory of Characteristic Modes
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this article, we presented the optimal design guidelines of planar log-periodic array antenna for UWB radio applications. Using CMA and full-wave analysis, the pLPA antenna’s characteristics were studied. It was observed that the growth rate of the pLPA determines many factors for the low-dispersive communication systems. For higher growth rates, $\tau \gt 0.6$, the resonances from multiple dipole elements are nearer and cover the spectrum with multiple bands. This phenomenon rewards for high-power end-to-end communication systems. Based on various observations, the design guidelines were framed to meet the industry requirements for few wireless technologies.

articleTitle: A C-Band 30W GaN MMIC PA With On-Chip Drain Pulse Modulator
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents the design, simulation and test results of C-Band 30W MMIC Power Amplifier with on-chip Drain Bias Modulator. Both RF power amplifier section and pulse modulator circuitry have been integrated within a single MMIC die of $6 \mathbf{m m} \times 6 \mathrm{~mm}$ size using 250 nm GaN on SiC HEMT process. Development of on-chip depletion mode HEMT based supply modulators on GaN paves the way for integration of high power PAs and modulators onto MMIC die that are especially suitable for AESA radars with large numbers of transmit modules.

articleTitle: A Methodology to Characterize the Virtual Gate Effect in a Power Amplifier
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: An experimental method to characterize the virtual gate effect in radio-frequency (RF) power amplifiers (PAs) based on high-electron-mobility transistors (HEMTs) is presented. The experimental setup ensures that the GaN device in an amplifier is at the same temperature and trap state every time the experiment is repeated. An algorithm is proposed to estimate multiple trapping time constants simultaneously from measured DC drain current transients of the PA in response to pulsed RF excitation. We observe that the time constants of the device recovery time remain constant over a range of power levels and are related to the shape of the load cycle of the device.

articleTitle: Design of Orthogonally Placed Trapeze-Spiral MIMO Antenna for Wireless LAN Applications.
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this article, an omnidirectional, circularly polarized MIMO antenna is discussed. An asymmetrical coplanar waveguide-based metamaterial MIMO antenna is modeled for 5G-WLAN applications. The antenna is etched on a low-cost lossy FR4 substrate with physical dimensions of (75×90×1.6) mm3. An asymmetric double split, split ring resonator is introduced in the antenna module to achieve port isolation of around −40 dB between the orthogonal ports. The realized gain is 2.8 dB with a fractional bandwidth of 4.1% resonating at 2.4 GHz. The proposed MIMO antenna’s diversity performances like correlation coefficient (ECC), diversity gain (DG), total active reflection coefficient (TARC), isolation, and MEG were estimated to be 0.03, 9.9 dB, −35 dB, −40 dB, and 2.3 dB respectively. The above-mentioned parameters along with the other performance attributes like reflection and transmission coefficients were analyzed and verified experimentally, which showed better similarity between them. This optimum performance of the discussed MIMO radiator makes it applicable for MIMO-based wireless applications.

articleTitle: Decade Bandwidth, Ultra-Compact, 2-Way Equal Power Divider for Space Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents a compact ultra-wide band 2-way equal power divider in the frequency range of $0.1-1 \mathrm{G H z}$. The proposed design employs 3 -section power divider in meandered microstrip configuration with optimum impedances for each stage in order to attain decade bandwidth in a compact size of $0.09 \lambda_{\mathrm{g}} \times 0.075 \lambda_{\mathrm{g}}$. Isolation performance is improved by judiciously optimizing isolation resistors. The overall dimension of the designed power divider is $25.4 \mathrm{~mm} \times 19.4 \mathrm{~mm}$ and simulated using 25 mil thick Alumina substrate. The fabricated prototype exhibits close matching with simulated ones. The measured return losses are better than 11 dB (for input port) & better than 18 dB (for output ports) and insertion loss is 0.45-0.9 dB over the frequency of operations. Realized power divider provides an isolation better than 20 dB over the frequency range of $0.27-1 \mathrm{GHz}$. To the best of authors’ knowledge, power divider with microstrip configuration exhibiting decade bandwidth in an ultra-compact size of $0.09 \lambda_{\mathrm{g}} \times 0.075 \lambda_{\mathrm{g}}$ has not been reported at this frequency band.

articleTitle: Miniaturization of CPW Fed Ultra-wideband Slot Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A technique for miniaturization of CPW-fed open-end semicircular slot UWB antenna is proposed in this paper. The size of any CPW-fed antenna can be reduced using this technique. The designed antenna has an impedance bandwidth (IMBW) from 3.09 to $\mathbf{1 4. 0 8} \mathbf{G H z}(\mathbf{1 2 8 \%})$ for $\left|S_{11}\right| \leq-10 \mathbf{d B}$ with a gain of $3 \pm 1 \mathrm{dBi}$ over the operating frequency range of $3.65-14.08 \mathrm{GHz}(117 \%)$. The proposed antenna is uniplanar with a compact size of $0.23 \lambda_{0} \times \mathbf{0. 2 5} \lambda_{0} \times \mathbf{0. 0 0 8} \lambda_{0}\left(\lambda_{0}\right.$ is the wavelength at the smallest frequency of operation in free space). The proposed antenna is suitable to mount on the metallic surfaces of wireless devices due to its small size. It has a small variation of group delay and radiation pattern with frequency. The prototype is developed and simulated and the measured results have a good match.

articleTitle: A Gain-Enhanced Wideband Metasurface-based Circularly Polarized Partially Grounded Patch Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper introduces a metasurface (MS)-based circularly polarized microstrip patch antenna with partial ground. The antenna consists of a square microstrip patch in a 1.6 mm thick FR-4 substrate with a cross-shaped slot. A metasurface layer, composed of a $5 \times 5$ square array, is designed on another $1.6 \mathbf{~ m m}$ thick FR-4 substrate placed above the host antenna as a superstrate layer. The proposed antenna demonstrates a $\mathbf{- 1 0} \mathbf{~ d B}$ impedance bandwidth spanning from 5.34 GHz to 7.80 GHz, along with an axial ratio (AR) bandwidth from 5.95 GHz to 6.29 GHz. At 6.20 GHz, the antenna achieves a maximum realized gain of 5.90 dBic, exhibiting a right-handed circular polarization (RHCP) feature. With its compact dimensions $\left(0.77 \lambda_{0} \times 0.77 \lambda 0 \times 0.032 \lambda_{0}\right.$ at 6.12 GHz), the circularly polarized antenna proposed here is well-suited for long range radio communication and in satellite for uplink transmission.

articleTitle: Wideband SIW Based Frequency Selective Surface Using Exponential Tapering Technique
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this paper, a new design approach is proposed for a Frequency Selective Surface (FSS) based on the Surface Integrated Waveguide (SIW) technique using exponential tapering. Here, the unit cell of the FSS is an exponentially tapered crossslot structure designed on either side of a low-loss substrate. The FSS element shows nearly 34% wide bandpass response in the X-band region i.e., $-3 \mathbf{d B}$ transmission bandwidth from $8.69 \mathbf{~ G H z}$ to 12.07 GHz, with low insertion loss of 0.1 dB and sharp roll-off characteristics. To validate the proposed FSS design, a low-cost FR4 substrate is used for fabrication, and the measured results are compared to the corresponding simulation results.

articleTitle: Cathodes for Futuristic THz VEDs
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: The development of terahertz (THz) technology has garnered significant attention due to its potential applications in communications, imaging, and spectroscopy. Central to the advancement of THz vacuum electron devices (VEDs) are electron emitters, which play a pivotal role in determining the efficiency and performance of these devices. This article details the advancements in electron emitter technology at CSIR-CEERI, focusing on thermionic and field emission cathodes essential for next-generation VEDs. The study examines Controlled Porosity Dispenser (CPD) cathodes, Nano-Scandate cathodes, and free-standing graphene film emitters. CPD cathodes demonstrate enhanced emission uniformity and efficiency through optimized pore structures. The fabrication of nano-scandate cathodes, utilizing scandia-doped tungsten nanoparticles, achieves high current densities at lower operating temperatures, extending the cathode’s lifespan. The introduction of tungsten-doped reduced graphene oxide (rGO) films as field emitters presents a significant improvement in emission performance, offering potential applications in advanced THz devices. Analytical and emission studies confirm the superior performance of these cathodes, positioning them as crucial components in the evolution of high-power, high-frequency VEDs.

articleTitle: A Broadband Metasurface Absorber Based on Indium-Tin-Oxide Thin Film
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents the design and measurement of a polarization-insensitive broadband metasurface absorber utilizing an indium tin oxide (ITO) resistive film. The metasurface, comprising an ITO conductive layer, effectively absorbs electromagnetic waves by generating ohmic losses, resulting in high absorption. The absorber demonstrates an absorption rate exceeding 90% across a frequency range of $18 \mathbf{~ G H z}$ to 22 $\mathbf{G H z}$, achieving a bandwidth of 4 GHz. The unit cell, with a period length of 0.37 wavelengths, consists of four rotated slotted patches and is polarization-insensitive to incident angles. The overall structure is composed of three layers: an ITO film layer, a PET film layer, and a Rogers RO4350B substrate. The reflection coefficient was measured using the rectangular waveguide method, showing good agreement with simulation results.

articleTitle: A 2.45 GHz Rectifier Matching Circuit for Radio Frequency Energy Harvesting
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents designing of rectifier matching circuit frequency at $\mathrm{2 . 4 5} \mathrm{~ G H z}$ for radio frequency energy harvesting applications. The circuit consists of a voltage doubler circuit, diode model SMS 7630005 LF Schottky diode is used for rectification purpose. An impedance matching network T type matching circuit is used and load resistance of $3 \mathrm{k} \Omega$. The matched rectifier constructed over Rogers RO4350 substrate with copper thickness $0.035 \mathrm{~mm}, \mathrm{0 . 7 6 2} \mathrm{~ m m}$ height, 0.004 loss tangent $\tan \delta$ and dielectric constant 3.66, -10 dbm to 8 dbm power levels. 1.624 V is Corresponding Vdc. Maximum efficiency found at $\mathrm{3 ~ d B m}$ which is $\mathrm{4 9 . 0 8 \%}$.

articleTitle: Modelling a Nonlinearly Spaced 24-Element Array Radio Telescope
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A computational electromagnetic (CEM) model of a Transient Array Radio Telescope (TART) is designed using nonlinearly spaced 24 GPS patch antennas configured in a spiral pattern. The new spiral layout of the TART model is similar to the actual TART deployed in Mauritius. Simulation results show that the far-field gain of the array at 1575 MHz is 20 dBi along the main beam and the side lobe level is 10.08 dB. The CEM model is an attractive option for analysing antenna properties such as the far-field radiation pattern of the array and can be used to optimise TART.

articleTitle: MIMO Antenna Performance Analysis with Realistic Bumper for Automotive Application
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this paper, the design and integration of 1D and 2D MIMO antennas in Automotive RADAR applications using realistic Bumpers are discussed. A 3Tx-5Rx 1D MIMO and a 4Tx-6Rx 2D MIMO antenna configuration are designed, with each Tx/Rx antenna being a seven-element series-fed binomial array. The angular resolution provided by 1D and 2D MIMO in the azimuth is 8.74 and 4.23 degrees respectively, and, an additional elevation resolution of 46.6 degrees is provided by the 2D MIMO. Two CAD models of car bumpers are used for simulation. The antennas are mounted behind the car bumper and the impacts of this integration are investigated using the S-parameter response and Antenna Array Ambiguity Function (AAAF) model. These analyses provide important insights into the comparative performance of 1D and 2D MIMO antennas in automotive RADARs, which can help evaluate appropriate remedial measures in real-time applications.

articleTitle: Modular Approach for Frequency Generation in an Airborne SAR System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: The paper presents the design and implementation of a compact and modular frequency generator (FG) for an Airborne Synthetic Aperture Radar system. This modular approach caters to the generation four different signal outputs along with chirp signal modulation, viz. 9600 MHz local oscillator (LO) signals for V & H receivers and transmit chirp signals at $9600 \pm 337.5 \mathrm{MHz}$ for V and H high power transmitter. The entire functionality is distributed across three modulesreceiver local oscillator signal generation module, baseband signal modulation module and modulated transmit signal generation module. Respective bias circuits are also in-built in these cards, further serving the cause of high integration. The modules are realized on a low cost commercially available hybrid substrate and uses commercial off the shelf components. The overall dimensions of the housing is $130 \mathrm{~mm} \times 104 \mathrm{~mm} \times$ 42.7 mm. The in-band spurious is better than 20 dBc, whereas out of band spurious rejection is better than 50 dBc.

articleTitle: Improvement of RF interference on DDR interface using tab-routed microstrip line
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: With various form factors like single board computers(SBC), mini-ITX form factor board, and micro-strip line (MSL) routing for DDR (Double data rate) is challenging to have minimum receiver sensitivity interference. Strip line (SL) is always preferred over MSL with losing a layer. This paper discusses tab-based routing, which helps signal quality while demonstrating good improvement over receiver sensitivity performance. The proposed structure shows the maximum improvement in eye height (EW) and eye width (EH) with 1.22% and 23.89 % respectively at 3200Mbps compared to conventional design. When the antenna is kept near the board’s periphery, MSL with tab routing shows a good improvement compared to the traditional MSL design, which is one of the challenges for meeting RFI requirements.

articleTitle: Design of Third-Order BPFs with Featured Transmission Zeros for Enhanced Selectivity
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This work proposes two third-order bandpass filters (BPFs): one with low-side transmission zero and the other with high-side transmission zero, to improve the selectivity of the passband. To generate the transmission zero, the structure relies primarily on the electrical coupling of two folded open-loop resonators that are internally coupled with a half-wavelength resonator. A half-wavelength resonator exhibits high-side transmission zero of the passband upon symmetric coupling and low-side transmission zero upon antisymmetric coupling. The proposed filters are designed using coupling matrix synthesis, considering the necessary parameters. Two example filters are designed and fabricated at a center frequency of 1.9 GHz, with a bandwidth of 230 MHz and a return loss of more than 20 dB.

articleTitle: Compact VHF/UHF Wideband Omnidirectional Antenna using a New Modified Reflective Ground Plane for Gain Enhancement
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A compact omnidirectional printed antenna working in the VHF/UHF range is discussed in this paper. The omnidirectional antenna structure includes a new closed-loop partial ground and a bevelled-shaped metal radiator. The antenna is fed by a tapered-shaped feed which improves the impedance matching with the return loss of at least 10 dB from 140 MHz to 1.4 GHz. The 3 dB gain bandwidth (GBW) of the proposed antenna is from 140 MHz to 840 MHz. The antenna is designed on a low-cost substrate, and the size of the omnidirectional antenna is approximately a quarter of the wavelength at the lowest operating frequency. A stable radiation pattern along with consistent gain with up to 5 dB gain enhancement is achieved over the entire bandwidth.

articleTitle: Class F Power Amplifier: Enhanced Analysis and Design through Integrated Reflected Wave Consideration
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper explores the operation of harmonically tuned power amplifiers (PAs), highlighting the importance of reflected waves in shaping the waveform. New equations for harmonically tuned PAs are proposed based on this wave shaping mechanism, addressing limitations of existing equations. These proposed equations account for factors like reflection coefficient. Validating these equations, a class F PA is examined, revealing two cases with the same voltage gain but differing fundamental power and drain efficiency due to reflections. This observation, unaddressed by existing equations, underscores the significance of the proposed mechanisms. Simulation results confirm the validity of the waveform shaping mechanism and derived equations, aligning well with theoretical expectations.

articleTitle: Study on the Microwave Disinfection of Food Grains using 42GHz Gyrotron Source
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: An experimental study has been carried out to explore the possibility of using high power microwave to disinfect the infected food grains. A $42 \mathrm{GHz}-500 \mathrm{~kW}$ Gyrotron based high power microwave source is used to carry out study on the microwave disinfection of food grains. The main idea is to expose the infected food grains to high power microwave for short duration and examine its effects on the mortality of insects in various food grains like wheat, rice and pulses. The $\mathbf{1 0 0 \%}$ mortality of all insects including its larvae is observed when we expose the infected food grains for 150 kW power only for 100 ms duration. The main observation during this disinfection of grain is that the temperature of food grains does not exceed 50 degree and almost 100% mortality is observed for all the insects. The similar experiments is carried out at low power $\sim 1 \mathrm{KW}$ at 2.45 GHz (Microwave oven) and in this case also the 100% mortality is observed when we exposed the food grains for more than 10 seconds but the temperature of food grains exceeds more than 70 deg, which is not desirable.

articleTitle: A Single Layer Broadband Conformal FSS based Absorber using Resistive Ink
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this study, the design and implementation of a Broadband conformal FSS based absorber using resistive ink is presented. The suggested absorber has broadband performance and high absorptivity. The usage of resistive ink on a single layered PLA (Polylactic Acid) substrate with an air gap between the substrate and ground plate is a novel feature of the design. The air gap makes the design lighter and more flexible, resulting in higher efficiency. With frequencies spanning from $4 \mathbf{~ G H z}$ to 14 GHz, the absorbers outstanding bandwidth exceeds 10 GHz, and absorption levels consistently exceed 90 percent. The design has extensive coverage, spanning the $\mathbf{C}, \mathbf{X}$, and upper Ku bands, and is effective with a wide range of incoming wave polarizations. An equivalent circuit model has been created, and various parametric modifications have been examined to investigate the absorption mechanism of the proposed design. It is additionally polarization insensitive. This absorber is especially helpful for a variety of real-world applications that demand flexible and conformal electromagnetic absorption since it can withstand transverse electric (TE) mode up to $\mathbf{4 5}$ degrees of incident angle.

articleTitle: Magnetic and Dielectric Loaded Miniaturized Ultra-Wide Band Spiral Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: The paper proposes a miniaturized Ultra-wide band Circularly Polarized Spiral Antenna for L/S/C/X/Ku-Band Interferometer based Direction Finding application. The spiral antenna utilizes a wide band microstrip balun to achieve impedance matching over multi-octave frequency band (1-18 GHz) by employing magnetic loading to absorb spurious radiation, achieving a Voltage Standing Wave Ratio (VSWR) less than 2:1. The antenna configuration incorporates a cavity structure to convert the Bi-directional radiation pattern to the Uni-directional radiation pattern. The cavity is loaded with a microwave absorber to suppress unwanted radiations, destructive interference between the backward waves and to absorb the back lobe, thereby achieving a symmetric radiation pattern with a good axial ratio of less than 2.5 dB over ultrawide bandwidth. Shaped dielectric loading is used on expanding outer spiral arms to improve the operational frequency bandwidth and the boresight radiation pattern at low frequency end. The simulated antenna performance was validated through measurement and is in good agreement with each other. The proposed design is a potential candidate for Direction Finding based on the Base Line Interferometer (BLI) technique for Electronic Warfare (EW) systems.

articleTitle: Design And Development of Compact Antenna for 5G Base Station with Stable Radiation Pattern
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this paper, a compact-sized narrowband dual-polarized antenna has been designed to operate in the n78 band (3.3 GHz - 3.8 GHz) with an operating frequency of 3.5 GHz. This antenna consists of crossed loops as radiating elements and parasitic elements are added to improve performance. This antenna aims to achieve a minimum cross-polarization of at least -20 dB and maintain stable gain over the entire bandwidth. This antenna could potentially be a suitable fit for 5G base stations, achieving a maximum cross-polarization of -20 dB. It has achieved a unidirectional gain of 5.2 dB and an almost constant gain of 5 dB over the bandwidth.

articleTitle: AMC based Antenna Sensor for Wireless Testing and Monitoring of Dielectric Materials
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A non contact artificial magnetic conductor (AMC)based antenna sensor is proposed for retrieving the permittivity of solid materials. The proposed sensor consists of a coplanar waveguide (CPW)-fed antenna with suppressed harmonics and a specially designed AMC reflector. The periodic AMC reflector having a wide bandwidth of 467.61 MHz is integrated with the antenna to increase the overall gain and the electric field strength in the sensing region. The overall antenna-based sensor structure is simulated using the CST Studio to optimize various parameters for the optimum performance. A numerical model is developed for the estimation of the permittivity of the test specimen in terms of its measured resonant frequency and the thickness. It is observed that the permittivity of the test specimen using the proposed scheme can be estimated with an average error of 5%. The proposed antenna sensor can be used for real-time wireless sensing and monitoring applications.

articleTitle: SIW-Based Monopulse Antenna for X-Band Tracking
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper introduces a low-profile monopulse array antenna using substrate-integrated waveguide (SIW) technology for X-band tracking applications. The entire antenna structure is composed of four TE 20 mode slotted SIWs, each containing eight inclined slots. Four slots are positioned above the central axis of the SIW, and the remaining four are below the central axis, spaced at intervals of $\lambda \mathrm{g} / 2$. Each of the four SIWs is excited by individual ports within a very compact space using coaxial-to-SIW transitions. Simultaneous excitation of these SIWs with various phase combinations at the four input ports generates a sum pattern, along with E-plane, H-plane, and bi-plane difference patterns. The antenna offers a broadside gain around 15.5 dBi with the sum pattern and achieves a null depth of $\mathbf{- 2 7} \mathbf{d B}$ with the difference patterns at a frequency of 8.04 GHz. It also delivers an impedance bandwidth of 1.3% and ensures inter-port isolation of more than $\mathbf{2 6} \mathbf{d B}$ throughout the entire operating band.

articleTitle: Self-Diplexing Antenna Design based on Substrate Integrated Waveguide (SIW) for 5G millimeter-wave applications.
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A Self-diplexing antenna based on Substrate Integrated Waveguide (SIW) technology for fifth generation (5G) millimeter(mm) wave applications is proposed. The proposed antenna design has an inset rectangular cavity inside a larger square cavity. Two unequal modified U-shaped slots are etched from the cavity to achieve self-diplexing. By integrating the design with a nested cavity, high isolation is achieved between the two ports at operating frequencies 25.68GHz and 29.34GHz when separately excited by port-1 and port-2 respectively. The antenna achieves an isolation of over 24dB between the two slots. It demonstrates peak gains of 5.58dB and 5.40dB at the above-mentioned operating frequencies.

articleTitle: A Miniaturized LTCC based Hermetically Sealed X-Band TR Module
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: We report a space grade miniaturized X-Band transmit receive (TR) module for a phased array antenna. The module has been developed using custom designed MMICs, which are packaged using LTCC based RF packaging technique. Assembly of LTCC is assembled on a higher thermal conductivity carrier plate ($\mathrm{C P}$) with MMIC attached to the $\mathrm{C P}$, resulting in better thermal management of the TR module. Hermetic sealing of the MMICs is done by laser sealing the LTCC module inside a drop-in-module with RF and DC interfaces through hermetically sealed glass beads. The entire design of the TR module is done by utilizing Indian foundry and technology. This development is an important milestone in the Government of India’s vision of Made in India and Atmanirbhar Bharat.

articleTitle: Metasurface Based Multi-Band Polarization Converter Using Subwavelength Stepped Impedance Resonator
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper introduces a novel multi-band reflective type metasurface design for polarization conversion operation. For this purpose a novel unit cell design has been proposed utilizing L-shaped resonators that can facilitate polarization conversion performance at $2.5 \mathrm{GHz}, 4 \mathrm{GHz}$ and 6 GHz respectively, with a wider band at the latest point, highlighting its multi-band feature of operation. Additionally, subwavelength Stepped Impedance Resonators (SIR) have been integrated to the design in four separate configurations to tune the frequencies of operation through tuning of the impedance ratios of the concerned components. High Polarization Conversion Ratio values ranging between $\mathbf{9 5 \%}$ to $\mathbf{9 9 \%}$ have been achieved through all the bands of operation. Moreover the design described stable angular performance for incidence angles as high as 20 degree over the observed tri-band region. Obtaining triband polarization conversion performance from a single-layer reflective design highlight its novelty of contribution, further suggesting its use for sub- 6 GHz technology applications, like V2X components (5.9-6 GHz), fixed wireless access devices (3.54.2 GHz) and future IoT designs ($\mathbf{(2.5 - 2.7 ~ GHz})$at this juncture.

articleTitle: Advances in Metasurface Antenna for Real-Time Biomedical Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A microstrip patch antenna with a $5 \times 5$ Metasurface (MS) is developed and examined for potential use in biomedical applications. A flexible, biocompatible substrate of Polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) is used to make the antenna. The proposed structure underwent testing on a synthetic phantom that accurately imitates the properties of human flesh. The return loss of the antenna is found to be 23.9 dB, which indicated good impedance matching at 2.45 GHz operating frequency with bandwidth of 6.2%. Besides, the realized gain and overall efficiency are 6.6 dBi and $\mathbf{6 9 \%}$ respectively indicating that there has been a significant improvement in directivity and efficiency after the application of MS on it. Evaluation of surface current distribution also confirms that MS optimization significantly improves radiating features of this antenna. This data shows how well-suited the previously indicated design of using such antennas is for biomedical applications due to its dependability and effectiveness when seen as a system unit.

articleTitle: Experimental Investigation of Electromagnetic (EM) Bridge for Deployable Antenna Array at P, L and S Band
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents the practical investigation and evaluation of a contactless low profile electromagnetic (EM) bridge, which is used to deploy direct radiating arrays placed on different panels. The RF connectivity is established using an EM bridge, which offers low loss, phase stability and low passive intermodulation, compared to the cable assembly. For the evaluation, an EM bridge integrated with microstrip lines on different panels is designed and developed at $P(450 \mathrm{MHz}), \mathrm{L}$ band $(1.5 \mathrm{GHz})$ and S -band $(\mathbf{2} .8 \mathrm{GHz})$. The RF characterization of the EM bridges with microstrip lines is carried at various folding angles of the panels. The measured results show $\leq 0.08$ dB insertion loss in $P, L$ and S bands. The measured RF performance has also been compared with that of the cable assembly. It is found that EM bridge has superior RF performance and low profile in comparison of coaxial assembly for RF connectivity of foldable antenna.

articleTitle: Wideband Meander Line Based Microwave Antenna for Head Imaging Application
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this work a compact meander line antenna is designed for head imaging application. The put forward model operates from 0.65 to 4.36 GHz, with a bandwidth percentage of 148.1%. The antenna has been designed keeping the head phantom near it to make a realistic head scanning arrangement at a later stage. The Specific Absorption Rate of the designed antenna is checked at several frequencies within its broadband. Also, all the performance parameters of the put forward structure is studied from the simulator. The antenna will be used to scan the head using a multistatic arrangement in future.

articleTitle: Ka Band IQ Modulator MMIC With An Integrated Amplifier For SATCOM Application
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This article presents a Ka band direct Up-converter (DUC) MMIC with an integrated amplifier realized using 130 nm GaAs/AIGaAs/InGaAs pHEMT process. The Up-converter comprises a IQ modulator as a mixer core and a single stage Ka band amplifier. This module operates with a LO signal within frequency band of 25.5 to 27 GHz and IF signal (I and Q) with a frequency DC to 1 GHz. Modulator chip is assembled in a space ready module for application in satellite datalink. The measured highest conversion gain of DUC is 1.53 dB with gain variation of $0.026 \mathrm{~dB} /{ }^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$ over temperature at LO power of 3 dBm. The measured carrier and harmonic suppression are better than 30 dBc and 17 dBc respectively. An input 1 dB gain compression level of 15 dBm and input IP3 of 21 dBm is achieved by MMIC.

articleTitle: A Dual Band Transmittive-type Linear to Circular Polarization Converter using Single Layer Metasurface
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This manuscript presents a novel metasurface (MS) based structure which can convert a transmittive-type linearly polarized incident electromagnetic (EM) wave into circularly polarized one in two distinct frequency bands incorporating a single layer of dielectric. The unit cell of the MS comprises six diagonally arranged metallic small square patches enclosed by a metallic square ring at the edge. The proposed structure has been designed on a $\lambda / 32$ thick dielectric substrate along with the periodicity of $\lambda / 5$ where $\lambda$ is free space wavelength with respect to the center frequency of the lower conversion band. The transmitted EM wave is circularly polarized (CP) in nature in C and Ku bands as the axial ratio is below 3 dB at 5.34 GHz to 6.8 $\mathbf{G H z}$ and 13.3 GHz to 16.01 GHz, being centered at 6 GHz and 14.5 GHz respectively. The chirality and surface current have been studied to confirm that the transmitted waves are respectively left-handed CP and right-handed $C P$ in C and $K u$ bands. The proposed structure can find potential applications towards space and satellite communications.

articleTitle: Design & Development of Space Qualified Modular Receiver for Synthetic Aperture RADAR Payloads
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents design and implementation of a compact and high gain receiver having modularity and hardware reconfigurability in the design architecture, to cater to space-borne Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) payloads operating in different frequency bands. The compactness and reconfigurability in the receiver are achieved by employing Monolithic Microwave Integrated Circuits (MMICs) for active circuits and Microwave Integrated Circuits (MICs) for passive circuits. The MMICs are packaged in standard metal ceramic packages, making the device footprint same for all the MMICs, thus adding modularity to the design. The measured gain and noise figure of Receiver configured for X-band SAR are 70dB and 4.65 dB respectively. The space worthiness of the proposed receiver is proven by successful completion of space qualification tests.

articleTitle: A Multi-Octave EW Receiver in VHF/UHF Band for Strategic Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper describes the design aspect of VHF/UHF Receiver covering VHF to UHF band with excellent selectivity, sensitivity and wide dynamic range. The principle of operation of this receiver is based on super heterodyne approach and is realized using super component integration with modular approach. A PIN diode based limiter is employed to protect Low Noise Amplifier (LNA) from high power emissions. LNA is employed to boost the incoming signal to a sufficient level with minimum inclusion of its internal thermal noise. Filter bank is realized using lumped components in channelized way in a compact size (60mm x 20mm), to achieve high rejection and to avoid cross talk between the channels. The VHF/UHF Receiver is designed for a survival input power of 5 Watts, effective gain of 40 dB, excellent sensitivity of 90 dBm and wide dynamic range of 60 dB over the VHF to UHF band in single compact housing of size 240 x 210 x 18 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>. It is being used for various strategic platform applications to accurately intercept, identify, locate the enemy radar.

articleTitle: Wearable Antenna Design and Analysis of Active Range of Motion for Upper Limb Movement using On-Body UWB Channel Parameters
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents a novel wearable antenna design which is used for analysis of Active Range of Motion (AROM) for upper limb movement using an ultra-wideband (UWB) technology ranging from $4-8 \mathrm{GHz}$. These analysis are done to monitor the movement of limbs. For the analysis, different onbody channel parameters are used, such as RMS delay spread ($\sigma \tau$) in nanoseconds (ns), Path loss (PL) in decibels (dB), and Coherence bandwidth (Bc) in MHz. To track the movement of the upper limb during physical exercises, the proposed antenna is mounted on both wrists. The analysis shows that limb movement has been tracked by three parameters, i.e., $\sigma \tau$, PL, and Bc. These UWB channel parameters provide AROM of upper limb for its monitoring in healthcare applications.

articleTitle: Dual Band Four Port MIMO Slot Antenna for 5G Millimeter Wave Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A dual band four port multiple input multiple output (MIMO) slot antenna designed for 5G millimeter (mm) wave application is presented in this paper. Initially, a single element antenna is developed to achieve resonance at 26 GHz with the purpose of comprehending and refining the specifications of a microstrip patch antenna operating in the mm-wave frequency range. To improve antenna performance in terms of gain and channel capacity, a MIMO structure is constructed with a rectangular patch antenna by carefully appending slots in them. In addition, to improve isolation between antenna elements and to get a compact size, a four-element MIMO antenna is oriented by arranging the antenna elements along the sides of the substrate which inhibits as sequentially rotating the single element patch antenna along the substrate. The proposed compact four-port MIMO antenna exhibits resonances at 26 and 30 GHz, with reflection coefficient values of −28 dB and −25 dB, respectively, and a gain of 9.8 dBi at both resonant frequencies. The MIMO antenna is also evaluated for parameters like Diversity Gain (DG), Envelope Correlation Coefficient (ECC), Mean Effective Gain (MEG) and Channel Capacity Loss (CCL).

articleTitle: Compact Wide Stop Band Quarter mode SIW Bandpass Filter
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A compact wide stop band substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) band pass filter is proposed in this paper. Compactness is achieved using quarter mode concept which involves using two magnetic walls, one placed vertically and another placed horizontal resulting reduction of component footprint by $75 \%$. For further reducing the device footprint, a via is used at diagonal of the quarter mode SIW along with a magnetic wall placed very close to the electric wall of the quarter mode SIW. Initially a second order chebyshev filter response is obtained without transmission zero (TZ) in the stop band. Non resonant node is used to enhance the source load cross coupling and place a TZ close to the pass band edge. Higher order spurious frequencies in the stop band are suppressed using two L shaped slots in the top plane of the filter. The proposed compact filter offers a wide stop band upto 4.6 times the pass band center frequency

articleTitle: Polarization Insensitive Near Unity Absorption FSS for RF Energy Harvesting Application
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A polarization insensitive frequency selective surface is designed by combining hexagonal resonator integrated with cross dipole resonator. The unit cell is designed for 2.45 GHz with an overall size of $\mathbf{3 8. 5} \text { mm } \times 3 8. 5 \text { mm }$. The load resistor for the unit cell is chosen to be $50 \Omega$ so that the design is compatible with the measurement instruments. Two vias have been used to achieve the polarization insensitive behavior. The structure is simulated in CST Microwave Studio. A prototype of $5 \times 5$ unit cells is fabricated and tested in anechoic chamber. The simulated and experimental results are found in close agreement. A shift of 40 MHz in the resonant frequency is observed in the fabricated structure. The unit cell captures 99.6 $\%$ of the incident power at the resonant frequency. The maximum Rad-to-RF efficiency is $\mathbf{6 7 \%}$.

articleTitle: SIW Cavity-Backed Semi-array Antenna for Dual-band MIMO applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents an SIW cavity-backed semi-array dual-band MIMO antenna designed for modern wireless communication systems. Utilizing SIW technology, the antenna achieves compact size, low profile, and seamless integration with planar circuits. The design methodology and measured results of the fabricated prototype are discussed, demonstrating stable radiation patterns, low cross-polarization levels, and isolation above 27 dB with the lower operating spectrum providing 4.9% FBW and the upper spectrum providing 6.7% FBW. It also provides ECC lower than 0.02 and stable DG, making it a promising solution for next-generation wireless applications.

articleTitle: Digital Implementation of Beam Squint Mitigation for Wide Band Active Phased Radars
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Beam squint occurs when the beam angle varies for wide bandwidth signals in phased array radars when steering is achieved with the help of phase shifters. The advancements in the digital technologies enable the mitigation of this effect with the help of Field Programmable Gate Arrays (FPGAs). Most of the modern active phased radars use digital beam forming for the formation of multi beams. In this work, we report on a FPGA based solution for beam squint correction by providing suitable corrections in the frequency domain using real time echo samples before forming the beams in the digital domain. Floating point operations are considered in this method to obtain better accuracy results with multiple computations. The beam squint effect is briefly explained by considering wide bandwidth signals. Further, the digital implementation of the beam squint mitigation method is proposed. The work is supported with various results obtained at different stages of analysis.

articleTitle: The miniature reconfigurable circular disc monopole antenna with tunable band-notch feature
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This manuscript presents a miniature reconfigurable circular disc monopole antenna with tunable band-notch feature. The impedance bandwidth (IBW) of the patch antenna is $2.95-19.9 \mathrm{GHz}$, which covers the full UWB frequency band $(\mathbf{3. 1 - 1 0. 6 ~ G H z})$. The modified circular patch has an inverted U-shaped slot with one PIN diode. The ground plane has a small rectangular center slot. The on/off switching configuration of the PIN diode provides frequency hopping of the notch band for $3.4-\mathbf{3. 6 9}$. $\mathbf{G H z}$ (WiMAX) band, the $3.8-4.2 \mathrm{GHz}$ (C-band), the $4.4-4.8 \mathrm{GHz}$ (INSAT and fixed satellite service band) and the $5.15-5.825 \mathrm{GHz}$ (WLAN band). The size of the antenna is $30 \times 40 \times 1.6 \mathrm{~mm}^{3}$. The designed antenna provides good simulated results in terms of return loss, realized gain, surface current and radiation pattern.

articleTitle: Reconfigurable Multifunctional Metasurface for Wideband Polarization Conversion
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Multifunctional polarization converters have been in high demand due to the lack of features for polarization conversion in the existing designs. The need for integration of active elements to develop reconfigurable metasurfaces helps develop multifunctional metasurfaces. However, the challenge still lies in developing a cost-efficient and feasible design that can operate over a very wide band of frequencies while providing multifunctional polarization conversion over the entire operating bandwidth. The design consists of three layers with a PIN diode integrated into the upper patch layer. Polarization conversion functionalities are obtained depending upon the state of the PIN diode. The proposed metasurface operates over 8.4 $\mathrm{GHz}-14.13 \mathrm{GHz}$ with a relative bandwidth of 50.87%. When the integrated PIN diode is turned OFF, cross-polarization conversion is obtained over this entire frequency range, exhibiting a conversion ratio (PCR) of $\mathbf{\gt 9 0 \%}$. When the PIN diode is switched ON, multiple polarization conversions are obtained within the frequency band of operation. Cross Polarization conversion is observed from 10.9 GHz to 14.2 GHz with a relative bandwidth of $\mathbf{2 6. 3 \%}$ and PCR $\gt \mathbf{9 0 \%}$, and linear to circular polarization is observed in two bands from 8.1277 GHz - 8.231 GHz and 9.23 GHz-10.4 GHz.

articleTitle: Pattern Synthesis of Linear Antenna Array using Honey Badger Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: The honey badger algorithm (HBA) is a nature inspired metaheuristic algorithm influenced by the foraging nature of honey badger. In this paper, HBA is applied for synthesizing the pattern of linear antenna array for peak and close in side lobe level (SLL) reduction, side lobe average power minimization with null positioning and beamwidth constraint by optimizing the excitation current of array elements. Four design examples are illustrated to demonstrate the effectiveness of HBA for pattern synthesis in comparison to the other state of art metaheuristic algorithms. The simulation result shows that HBA performs better than other algorithms in all the design examples. HBA also presents fast rate of convergence which demonstrates its utility in solving design optimization problems of electromagnetics.

articleTitle: Optimum RF carrier pair allotment based on IMD minimising strategies
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper addresses novel strategies for allotment of RF paired carriers. A practical and effective allotment strategy is introduced to reduce intermodulation distortion (IMD). Two strategies are presented: Sequential pairing and Selective pairing using Full Spectrum Examination Method (FSEM). Additionally, comparison of the two strategies is presented with regard to the number of intermodulation products. MATLAB is used to realize the respective algorithm. The reduction in IMD indicates the effectiveness of the proposed allotment method.

articleTitle: Wideband Electrically Tunable Metamaterial Absorber using Varicap and PIN Diode
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: We propose a tunable metamaterial absorber (MA) unit equipped with varactor and PIN diodes that is insensitive to polarization, aiming to significantly expand the metamaterial absorbers tunable bandwidth. Based upon hexagon split rings (HSRs), high absorptivity is demonstrated by the unit over a wide range of angles of incidence. By dividing the HSRs into two parts, the absorption frequency may be regularly adjusted within a predefined range via varying the voltage given to the varicap diodes. Through optimization of these parameters, simulation results show that the proposed MA achieves a significantly expanded tunable frequency range of 6.72-8.88 GHz, with a bandwidth of 2.16 GHz.

articleTitle: Design of X Band 40W GaN Power Amplifier
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This article describes the creation of an X-band high power monolithic microwave integrated circuit (MMIC) amplifier (HPA) with a maximum power of 50 W typical and a power added efficiency (PAE) better than $\mathbf{3 5 \%}$. It makes use of a SiC-based GaN field effect transistor (FET) with a $0.25 \mu \mathrm{~m}$ gate length. Without the need for additional circuitry, the three-stage high-performance amplifier for X band MMICs is intended to achieve a complete $50 \Omega$ input/output impedance. The manufactured amplifier has a power gain of 27 dB and chip measures $5.3 \times 4.9 \mathrm{~mm}^{2}$ overall.

articleTitle: High performance GaN LNA for space based radar front-end
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents the design and implementation of a high performance Gallium Nitride (GaN) High Electron Mobility Transistor (HEMT) based Low Noise Amplifier (LNA) for space-borne X-band radar applications, fabricated using the UMS foundry’s $0.25 \mu \mathrm{m}$ GaN-on-SiC process. The LNA demonstrates exceptional performance metrics, achieving a noise figure (NF) of less than 1.6 dB, gain greater than 18.5 dB and gain flatness of $\pm 0.25 \mathrm{~dB}$ across the frequency range of 9 to 10 GHz. The high linearity of GaN LNAs is exhibited through a P1dB of 20.5 dBm. The entire design is implemented in a compact die size of $2.46 \mathrm{~mm}~ X~ 1.79 \mathrm{~mm}$. A total of 27 dies were fabricated and measured, and the performance results were consistent across all samples, affirming the reproducibility and high yield of the design. This combination of low noise figure, high gain, good gain flatness, high linearity and compact chip size, which are otherwise contradictory requirements, represents the best-in-class performance reported to date for GaN LNAs operating in the specified frequency range.

articleTitle: Design of a Physics-Informed Learning Model for the Electromagnetic Modeling of Functional Materials
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: There is a crucial need for an intelligent system to assist material scientists in fabricating and testing functional materials, such as microwave-absorbing materials. Most researchers are searching for novel materials for reduced-size microwave absorbing materials needed in various civil and military applications. The existing models used by material scientists suffer from various challenges, such as trial and error, the requirement of large dataset, and sophisticated instrumentation. This paper proposes a physics-informed learning-based model to assist the researchers in selecting, modeling, and characterizing any material depending on the user-defined application. An example is demonstrated for dielectric material to achieve the minima of the reflection coefficient.

articleTitle: Bi-functional Wideband Switchable Metasurface for Cross and Circular Polarization Conversion
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this paper, a novel wideband switchable multifunctional metasurface polarizer is proposed, which can be switched from one function to another function by using a PIN diode. The meta-atom consists of two rotated rectangular copper patches placed on the copper-backed low-loss Rogers RT5880LZ dielectric substrate. Two PIN diodes are mounted in the gap between the two rectangular patches. When the diodes are in ON states, the patching arrangement of the meta-atom yields a linear to circular polarization conversion in a frequency range of $11.1-20.8 \mathrm{GHz}$ with a wide bandwidth of 9.7 GHz for axial ratio (AR) $\lt \mathbf{3 d B}$. But, when the diodes are in the OFF state, the metasurface behaves as a linear to cross-polarization conversion, and the polarization conversion ratio is observed more than $\mathbf{9 0} \%$ for the frequency range of $10.3-20.2 \mathrm{GHz}$ with a wide bandwidth of 9.9 GHz. Notably, we achieved wide bandwidth for both functions which was not presented previously. The designed metasurface can be for different applications such as polarization control devices, antennas, wireless communication, etc.

articleTitle: Assessment of binder aggregate behavior of bituminous mixes using log-periodic feedlines based microstrip filter
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive study on the characterization of bituminous mixes using microwave-based measurements. We investigated the electromagnetic properties of different samples, such as bituminous concrete (BC) and open-grade friction course (OGFC), using a novel two-port ring filter with log-periodic feedlines (operating from 0.35 - 0.65 GHz) designed on the RT/Duroid 5880 substrate. The specimens were evaluated based on average attenuation and group delay measurements, revealing distinct electromagnetic behaviors. The specimens’ calculated and measured flow rates were correlated to these factors (with an error of 0.05). This shows that the filter can accurately measure the flow rates needed to study how the binder and aggregate interact in bituminous mixes. Findings show that OGFC and BC samples are very different in how they respond to electromagnetic fields and how they flow. This shows how sensitive and valuable microwave techniques are for studying bitumen and building roads.

articleTitle: Around-the-corner Radar Sensing Using Reconfigurable Intelligent Surface
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Around-the-corner radar (ACR) sensing of targets in non-line-of-sight (NLOS) conditions has been explored for security and surveillance applications and look-ahead warning systems in automotive scenarios. Here, the targets are detected around corners without direct line-of-sight (LOS) propagation by exploiting multipath bounces from the walls. However, the overall detection metrics are weak due to the low strength of the multipath signals. Our study presents the application of reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS) to improve radar sensing in ACR scenarios by directing incident beams on the RIS into NLOS regions. Experimental results at 5.5 GHz demonstrate that micro-Doppler signatures of the walking motion of humans can now be captured in NLOS conditions through the strategic deployment of RIS.

articleTitle: A Low-Cost SIW-based Wideband H-plane Horn Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This study explores a budget-friendly $\boldsymbol{H}$-plane horn antenna based on a Substrate Integrated Waveguide (SIW) based technology for wideband applications. The antenna is designed using FR4 substrate material, which has a thickness of $1.6 \mathbf{~ m m}$. A small arc is placed at the front side of the antenna aperture for proper matching with the free space. It is found that the horn antenna can work from 6.39 to 19.15 GHz, which can cover X and $K_{u}$ - bands. In addition, the flaring angle of the H-plane horn antenna is adjusted to improve the gain. A conventional $\mathbf{5 0} \mathbf{~ o h m}$ coaxial probe is used as a feeding element for the antenna. The maximum gain obtained is 6.4683 dB as well as FBR is $\mathbf{2 2. 8 6} \mathrm{dB}$.

articleTitle: A Novel Reconfigurable Antenna Sensor Based on Microstrip Circuits for Environmental Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Microwave sensors based on the chipless radio frequency identification (CRFID) technology are well-suited for wireless sensing systems. However, developing CRFID sensors with controllable modes and integrated multi-parameter integration remains a significant challenge. In this paper, we propose a novel reconfigurable four-port antenna-based sensor with multiparameter characteristics. By integrating multiple sensor arrays designed with special sensitive materials on the same plane, we achieve flexible channel reuse and sensing mode reconstruction. The sensor is completely passive and reusable, enabling longterm synchronous sensing and information transmission in critical areas where power supply is difficult to obtain.

articleTitle: Miniaturized Multi Octave Quad Front-End with Built-in health check for Multi-channel Receivers
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: The design of a Quad Front-End Receiver (QFER) covering L to Ku band with excellent amplitude and phase tracking among the four channels is described in this paper. A two-stage pin-diode limiter is employed to protect the receiver from high-power signals. High rejection filters are used to suppress the out-of-band signals and wide-band low-noise amplifiers (LNA) for conditioning the incoming signal to meet the required receiver specifications like noise figure and linearity. The QFER employs an internal tunable frequency source, which is routed to all four channels using a novel vertical transition ensuring equal amplitude and phase, to check the health of the multichannel receiver. The QFER is realized with 20 dB effective gain and minimum return loss 10 dB over L to Ku band using super component integration in a compact size of 95x95x30 mm3.

articleTitle: Design of Dual-Polarized Active FSS Based Rasorber With Switchable Transmission
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents a dual-polarized active frequency selective surface (AFSS)-based rasorber, designed for switchable transmission operations. The proposed structure integrates an upper lossy layer with a lower switchable bandpass layer. The bandpass layer design comprises of aperture-based slots within which the PIN diodes are integrated. Metallic vias are inserted in the bandpass layer to maintain symmetry in the design and apply proper bias to the diodes. Further, chip resistors integrated lossy layer is integrated at the top of the active bandpass layer. In the absorption frequency band, the bandpass FSS acts as a reflecting ground layer to the lossy layer.
