The proposed rasorber realizes a switchable transmission between the two states of PIN diode at $9.7 \mathrm{GHz}(1.4 \mathrm{~dB})$, while for both states a broad absorption band exists at the lower frequency band ranging from 3.4 to 7.7 GHz (77.47%).

articleTitle: Analysis of Port Excitation using Finite-Difference Time-Domain (FDTD) Simulations
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This study investigates port excitation configurations in a rectangular cavity resonator, analyzing their impact on electromagnetic field distribution for biomedical waste treatment applications. Using the Finite-Difference Time-Domain (FDTD) method and CST simulations, we examine three port configurations: top, side, and center loadings, aiming to determine their effectiveness in achieving a uniform electric and magnetic field distribution, resonance characteristics, heating efficiency at 2.45 GHz—a key requirement for efficient waste treatment. Results show that single-port configurations often leave underexposed regions, or “dark zones,” within the cavity, while multiple orthogonal ports significantly enhance uniformity across the field distribution. Specifically, a three-port configuration demonstrates superior coverage, likely improving the efficiency of waste treatment by exposing a greater volume of material to electromagnetic radiation. This work underscores the importance of port configuration in cavity design for electromagnetic treatment systems, providing insights for optimized field distribution in biomedical waste processing and similar applications. Future work will explore 3D FDTD modeling to enhance precision in complex geometries.

articleTitle: A Quasi-Endfire Circularly Polarized Antenna for Surface-Mount Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This article presents a high gain quasi-endfire circularly polarized antenna for surface mount applications. The radiating structure is a half mode dielectric waveguide which is fed by a microstrip line from the bottom. The microstrip line is designed on a rohacell. To generate circular polarization in the endfire direction, an array of metallic strips are used above the dielectric slab and they are rotated by some angle $\theta$ with respect to the central axis of the slab. The proposed antenna is Right Handed Circularly Polarized (RHCP), has a common BW (impedance, gain, and AR) of around 2 GHz ranging from 18 GHz to 20 GHz. The maximum realized gain in this spectrum is 13.46 dBiC. The antenna is well suited for different surface mount endfire applications such as in rockets, missiles, CubeSats, and in UAVs.

articleTitle: A four leaf clover shape reflectarray antenna for X Band applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper communicates a design of a nature-inspired four-leaf clover shape radiating element and further incorporates it into making RA. It is a low-profile design on a single layer and possesses high gain. The radiating patch is a 1.56 mm thick Rogers RT/duroid 5880 of dielectric constant $\varepsilon_{\mathrm{r}}=2.2$ and $\tan \boldsymbol{\delta}=0.025$. It works well for the intended center frequency at 10 GHz of the X band (8 to 12 GHz). This circular aperture RA is of diameter 300 mm with 316 reradiating units arranged on it. From simulated results, the side lobe level and cross-polarization level in the E plane are below 13 dB and $\mathrm{6 0 ~ d B}$ separately for operating frequency. Further maximum gain of $\mathrm{2 5. 4 6} \mathrm{dBi}$ is obtained and aperture efficiency is $\mathrm{3 5. 6 8} \%$ at 10 GHz. While a 3 dB gain bandwidth of 18% is attained.

articleTitle: Enhanced RF performance on Graded-channel AlGaN/GaN HEMTs with Aerogel-Cavity for 6G Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this research work, graded-channel AIGaN/GaN HEMT with aerogel-cavity T-gate is investigated. The inclusion of aerogel under the field plates reduces parasitic capacitance due its low dielectric constant. This reduction in the parasitic capacitance shows significant improvement in cutoff frequency ${\mathrm {f_{T}}}$. The aerogel-cavity graded-channel device with a gate length of $\mathrm{5 0} \mathrm{n m}$ shows ${\mathrm {f_{T}}}$ of $193 \mathrm{G H z}$. The results exhibit a $\mathrm{1 2 \%}$ improvement in ${\mathrm {f_{T}}}$ compared with conventional graded-channel AIGaN/GaN device. These results promises that the proposed device have a greater potential for 6 G future communication networks.

articleTitle: A 14 GHz, 16 dBm Power Amplifier with 50% PAE in 130-nm CMOS for SATCOM Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents the measured performance of a fully matched single stage differential cascode power amplifier fabricated in $130-\mathrm{nm}$ bulk CMOS process for Ku-band satcom applications. The PA uses MCR based baluns for its input and output matching networks. The PA achieves 16dBm of saturated output power with 50% PAE and obtained 14.9 dBm output power with 45% PAE at 1dB compression point. This paper also discusses the small-signal and load-pull measured performance of two common-source (CS) power cells to demonstrate thin oxide device capability for medium power applications at these satcom frequencies.

articleTitle: Generation of Multi-modal Orbital Angular Momentum (OAM) wave at Millimeter-wave Frequency
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this article, a millimeter-wave multimodal OAM (Orbital Angular Momentum) wave antenna of two concentric Uniform Circular Array (UCA) comprised of identical rectangular patches has been presented. Said OAM array has been designed to operate at 60 GHz for next gen high data rate communication applications for short-distance. It can transmit $0, \pm 1$ and ± 2, OAM modes simultaneously in free space with a realized gain of $7.8 \mathrm{dBi}, 6 \mathrm{dBi}$, and 8.5 dBi, respectively. Presented work is capable to provide high order of spatial multiplexing and spectral efficiency with low beam divergence angle and high inter mode isolation (IMI)

articleTitle: A High Efficiency Truncated Square-Shaped Multifunctional Reflective Polarizer for Modern Satcom Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents a linear to linear (LTL) and linear to circular (LTC) polarization converter for potential satellite applications. Multi-functional polarization manipulation characteristics have been achieved due strong anisotropy offered by a diagonally oriented truncated square-shaped structure. It is studied that the amount of truncation is playing a prominent role in driving the bandwidth of LTL and LTC polarization conversions. Simulation results demonstrate that the suggested converter is capable to convert the linearly polarized wave to its cross counterpart over $8.74-13.71 \text{GHz}$ and 22.75-23.58 GHz. Moreover, this polarizer is proven to alter linearly polarized wave into the nearly perfect circularly polarized wave over the frequency range of $7.47-8.52 \text{GHz}$, $\mathbf{1 4 . 3 7 - 2 2 . 4 2 ~ G H z}$, and $\mathbf{2 3 . 6 8 - 2 4 . 7 1 ~ G H z}$. Favorably, it offers distinct type of circular polarization (both left and right hand) manipulation in the different bands which is crucial in reducing the interference in up-link and downlink frequencies. Many satellite and defence applications in the X -, Ku -, and K- bands are anticipated for this suggested polarizer because of its compact design, low profile, low cost, ease of fabrication, and multifunctional polarization transformation characteristics.

articleTitle: RFR-Based ML for Predicting Radiation Properties of MM Lens Antenna in Microwave WPT
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper introduces a machine learning (ML) method based on random forest regression (RFR) for predicting the radiation properties of a Metamaterial (MM) lens antenna. At $2.45 \mathbf{G H z}$, the proposed unit cell achieves a 99.6% transmittance with a positive refractive index (RI), $n=28.85$. Optimising the MM lens position and strip gap enhances gain and, hence, received power. The proposed ML approach evaluates radiation characteristics using strip gap and distance variables. Simulations for near and far-field MM lens placement are conducted to validate the results for three different gap values. Remarkably, a strong agreement between the ML predictions and the results obtained from CST simulations is observed, with an error margin of 3%. The proposed RFR-ML method enables the exploration of power-beaming applications in far-field wireless power transfer.

articleTitle: Design, Simulation and Stability Analysis of a MMIC Based W-Band Medium Power Amplifier
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: High power amplifier design always requires a detailed analysis of output power matching and stability. The goal is to design an amplifier that is stable under all operating conditions along with a medium power output at W-Band. This paper describes the design of a W-band GaAs Medium Power Amplifier MMIC and the simulation study on stability analysis and matching networks. The amplifier is designed to operate with an output power of 20 dBm and a gain of $10-11 \mathrm{~dB}$ in the frequency range of 88 to 96 GHz. The input and output power combining techniques along with even and odd mode stability analysis have been discussed.

articleTitle: A Wideband Photo Paper Based Microwave Absorber
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: The manuscript describes a wideband microwave absorber designed for efficient absorption of electromagnetic waves across the C-band frequency spectrum. The proposed absorber incorporates a resistive layer printed on photo paper using inkjet printing technology. The structure demonstrates a wide absorption bandwidth, achieving 90% absorption in the frequency interval of 3 GHz - 10.79 GHz. The unit cell of the absorber has a periodicity of 30 mm and a thickness of 10.175 mm. The absorber is capable of maintaining its 90% absorption bandwidth for all polarizations under normal incidence. The configuration maintains a stable 90% absorption bandwidth for large incident angles (45 degree) for transverse magnetic (TM) as well as transverse electric (TE) polarizations.

articleTitle: Detection of Cardiovascular Activities of Multiple Patients using MIMO mmWave Radar
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents the detection and analysis of cardiovascular activities for localisation of multiple patients using Doppler signals associated with their chest wall motion, heart beat and sleep disorder. The modeling of the vital signs has been carried out considering the vibrating surface of human body illuminated by a radar. The main challenge of a medical radar is the noncontact diagnosis of multiple people. MIMO radar has enormous potential in two areas: micro Doppler detection and fine angular resolution. In this work, MIMO radar is designed and analysis of micro Doppler due to (i) chest movement, (ii) heartbeat and (iii) tidal volume of patients in their sleeping conditions has been carried out using MATLAB models.

articleTitle: High-Performance Compact Lowpass Filter With Controlled Transmission Zeros
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents the design of a compact lowpass filter (LPF) using the transverse resonance method (TRM). Systematically, transmission zeros (TZs) are placed near the cut-off and away from the cut-off frequency to control the sharpness and stopband rejection bandwidth. The stopband $20 \mathrm{~dB}, 30 \mathrm{~dB}$ rejection bandwidth is widened by folding the capacitive and inductive lines, which will control the coupling of electric fields between the lines.LPF is designed on low-cost substrate FR-4 having thickness of $h=0.8 \mathrm{~mm}$, and $\tan \delta=$ 0.027, for 3 dB cut-off frequency (fc) $=2.5 \mathrm{GHz}$. The proposed LPF has less than 0.05 dB passband insertion loss; sharpness is $65 \mathrm{~dB} / \mathrm{GHz}$, and 30 dB rejection bandwidth is up to 11.6 GHz.

articleTitle: Optically Transparent Corrugated Substrate Integrated Waveguides
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Substrate integrated waveguides (SIWs) are a replacement for conventional rectangular waveguides that can offer planar architecture for easy integration within radio frequency (RF) circuits. They use an array of vias in the $\mathbf{H}$ plane that imitates a conductive wall and hence makes it impossible to create optically transparent waveguides. Corrugated SIWs (CSIW) are a new form of SIW that replaces array of vias with inductive corrugated stubs and offers a waveguide performance in the TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">10</inf> mode. In this paper, an optically transparent CSIW has been designed using indium tin oxide (ITO) as the conductor, and its performance is compared with a conventional SIW and CSIW. The proposed optically transparent CSIW offers a transmission loss of approx. 2.2 dB averaged over the operating bandwidth compared to 1.3 dB offered by conventional CSIWs. The optically transparent behavior makes the design highly suitable for new transparent circuits on glass windows or car windshields.

articleTitle: Study of Beam-Wave Interaction in W-Band Folded Waveguide Travelling Wave Tube
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Simulation study for W-band Folded Waveguide Travelling Wave Tube (FW-TWT) has been carried out. The study includes electromagnetic and particle-in-cell (PIC) simulation. The electromagnetic simulation is carried out without applying the electron beam. There are three aspects of study in electromagnetic simulation, the dispersion characteristics, the interaction impedance and the transmission characteristics. PIC simulation is carried out by applying the electron beam. The operating characteristics of the W-band FW-TWT have been studied to determine the bandwidth of the structure, the variation of output power versus input power for different cathode voltages.

articleTitle: Characterization of a Coaxially-fed MIMO Antenna for n257 mmWave IoT Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This work presents the design and characterization of a coaxially-fed multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) antenna for n257 band low-latency internet-of-things (IoT) applications. The proposed MIMO design offers -10 dB impedance bandwidth from 25.8 to 28.77 GHz, covering the globally designated n257 band. The design of the antenna is compact and architecturally simple and offers peak gain up to 9.8 dBi at a resonant frequency of 27 GHz, with a radiation efficiency of above 95% in the covered spectrum. Furthermore, the design features a compact inter-element spacing of $0.18 \lambda$ and a minimum isolation of 31 dB throughout the operational frequency band. The proposed MIMO antenna has an envelope correlation coefficient (ECC) value below 0.0002 and a mean effective gain (MEG) value less than -3 dB in the entire millimeter-wave (mmWave) n257 band spectrum, which renders it suitable for high-speed IoT applications.

articleTitle: Analysis of Bond Wires and Proposal for Compensation Circuits in 73 GHz Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This work investigates the problems associated with bond wire interconnection in millimeter wave applications. The deteriorating effect of bond wire caused by the inductance and other parasitic parameters in the bond wire is analyzed against frequency. To improve the insertion loss and matching associated with bond wire, an impedance compensation circuit is designed at $73 \mathbf{G H z}$ consisting of a radial stub and microstrip line. Furthermore, simulations shows that the degradation in transmission loss performance and matching can be minimized by reducing the overall length of bond wire and increasing the diameter. The proposed solution is verified by the measurements of a 25 um diameter bond wire with and without compensation structure. The measured insertion loss is reduced to $\mathbf{- 3. 5} \mathrm{dB}$, compared to the -6dB insertion loss in bond wire interconnect without compensation. Moreover, the input and output return loss are better than $\mathbf{- 1 0} \mathbf{d B}$ at $\mathbf{7 3} \mathbf{~ G H z}$. Significant improvements in terms of transmission performance and impedance matching are observed, compared with an unmatched bond wire.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of Non-Conventional Dielectric Dome Antenna for Scan Enhancement
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper investigates the design and performance of non-conventional dielectric dome antennas integrated with a 4x4 Microstrip Patch Antenna Array (MPAA). The primary objective is to enhance the wide-angle scanning capabilities of the antenna for modern communication and radar systems. Three distinct dome designs were analyzed: Design 1 and Design 2 prioritizing the maximization of scanning range, and Design 3 focusing on minimizing dome size and gain drop at boresight angles. The results indicate substantial improvements in beam shaping and scanning capabilities with the incorporation of dielectric domes. While the scanning ability of MPAA is limited to 45 degrees, all three dome designs significantly enhanced the scanning range and maintained acceptable gain levels. Notably, Design 2 achieved a Scanning range of upto 70 degrees and Design 3 showed 1 dB increase in boresight gain compared to other two domes.

articleTitle: Dual Wideband High Gain Moon-Shaped Antenna for 5G Millimeter-Wave Energy Harvesting Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this paper, a dual-band antenna is proposed for dual-band energy harvesting applications. A sectoring mechanism has been chosen for achieving dual-band characteristics at the millimeter-wave range. The offset feeding approach is investigated for exciting the antenna. The antenna is built on a substrate Rogers RT Duroid 5880TM of thickness 0.508 mm. The proposed antenna operates at 31.70GHz and 35.72 GHz frequencies. The antenna’s radiative properties indicate that it is appropriate for dual-band RF energy harvesting purposes in the millimetre wave range.

articleTitle: Holographic Metasurface Antennas using Complementary Yagi-Uda based Aperture Coupled Surface Wave Launcher
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A Holographic Metasurface Antenna (HMA) with a novel feeding technique is presented in this paper. A low-profile, highly directive HMA is designed using Aperture Coupled Feeding technique. A novel idea of incorporating complementary Planar Yagi-Uda structure in ground plane is presented in this paper. The radiation pattern maxima is achieved in the broadside direction $\boldsymbol{\theta}=0, \boldsymbol{\phi}=0$. A Phase Factor (PF) is incorporated in the surface to achieve circular polarization (CP). The CP-HMA is used to achieve a high gain of $\sim 19 \mathrm{~dB}$ and an axial ratio of $\sim \mathbf{0 . 6 d B}$. The Linearly Polarized (LP) HMA is designed to get a gain of $\sim 17 \mathrm{~dB}$ using this novel feeding technique.

articleTitle: Ultra-wideband Dual-Polarized Frequency Independent Reflective Metasurface for RCS Reduction
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this paper, a simple planar phase gradient metasurface based on phase discontinuity is presented for electromagnetic wave maneuvering. Due to the phase discontinuity of the Phase gradient metasurface (PGM), specular reflections diffused in multiple directions $\left(-30^{\circ}\right.$ to $\left.30^{\circ}\right)$ in both monostatic and bistatic situations by greatly lowering radar cross-section (RCS).The 8x8 array’s metasurface is produced by an electromagnetic simulator (EM). The simulation findings show that throughout a broad frequency range of the 10–20 GHz operating band, the reflective metasurface’s RCS value reduced (below –10 dB) in both of the aforementioned scenarios. In monostatic and bistatic designs over a wide incidence angle range, planar design, angular, frequency independency, and wide angle RCS reduction are exhibited. This illustrates the possibilities of the proposed surface in real-time scenarios requiring stealth applications.

articleTitle: Application of High Power Gyrotrons in the Field of Fusion Research, Deep Drilling and Space
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: The High Power Gyrotrons deliver megawatt level microwave power at very high frequency up to 202 GHz. The Gyrotrons are most demanding high power microwave source for Electron Cyclotron resonance Heating (ECRH) in the tokamak plasma. Since the coupling of EC waves is very efficient and highly localized in tokamak plasma, the ECR heating is most preferred in many tokamak devices. In the ITER, ECRH is being upgraded from 20MW to 47MW power. Several other fusion devices projecting 100s of megawatt ECRH power for DEMO fusion power plant. A $42 \text{GHz}-500 \text{kW}$ Gyrotron based ECRH system is being used continuously on tokamaks SST-1 and Aditya-U to carry out experiments related to plasma breakdown and heating. Another ECRH system ($82.6 \text{GHz}-400 \text{kW}$) would be commissioned on tokamak Aditya-U to facilitate the tokamak to carry out experiments at higher ECRH power. The high power Gyrotrons can also be used for other applications like deep earth drilling for geo-thermal energy and microwave beam assisted satellite launch. The paper discusses various applications of high power Gyrotrons.

articleTitle: Comparison of the Performance of Inline Filter Topologies Implementing Transmission Zeroes
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Advancements in compact, high-performance filtering structures are crucial for high performance communication systems. Applications such as massive MIMO antenna arrays require filters which are at the same time strongly selective and highly miniaturized. Traditionally, transmission zeroes in the filtering response have been obtained using cross-coupling between multiple resonators. Recently, techniques have been developed for the retrieval of transmission zeroes with inline topologies. In this work, two of such techniques are compared, the extracted-pole and the path filter. The size and performance of these topologies are evaluated by creating and comparing a test filter for each of them, working around 3.7 GHz with a 5.4% bandwidth. Substrate Integrated Waveguide (SIW) prototypes have been fabricated and measured.

articleTitle: FSS-based Rasorber with Wideband Absorption and Tunable Transmission
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A polarization-independent T-A type active frequency selective rasorber (AFSR) with a tunable transmission band and wideband absorption is presented in this paper. There are two layers in the proposed AFSR. The bottom layer is a bandpass frequency selective surface (FSS) integrated with a varactor diode-based active filter layer separated by an air spacer, and the top layer is a wideband quasi-single absorptive layer loaded with lumped resistors. A full wave simulation was carried out to analyze the proposed structure. The reflection coefficient of the proposed structure is observed to be less than $\mathbf{- 1 0} \mathrm{dB}$ from $4.43 \mathrm{GHz}-9.98 \mathrm{GHz}(77 \%)$. The absorption bandwidth spans a fractional bandwidth of 75.52% from 4.45 GHz to 9.85 GHz and permits over $\mathbf{9 0 \%}$ absorption. This range includes a portion of the X -band and nearly the whole C-band. Furthermore, the transmission band with the lowest possible insertion loss (IL) can be tuned between 2.7 and 4.3 GHz. The proposed geometry offers a stable response up to 40° to the oblique incidence for TE and TM polarized waves, with a thickness of $0.052 \lambda$ concerning the lowest frequency. The suggested AFSR could have practical uses in stealth and airborne applications.

articleTitle: Ultra-Wideband Tx and Rx Discone Antenna for Multi-frequency Operation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents design and development of ultrawide-band (UWB) discone antenna for both transmission and receiver/monitoring applications. The design focuses on achieving efficient operation across a wide range of frequencies, covering V/UHF bands. Simulation results from Ansys HFSS exhibit low VSWR and steady radiation patterns. Prototype antennas are fabricated. The transmission antenna covers 55 MHz to 570 MHz with a VSWR of $3: 1$, suitable for high power transmission application whereas the the receiver/monitoring antenna covers 30 MHz to 540 MHz, can also support to receive from 1 MHz onwards with a VSWR within 3.2:1. The measured results are in good agreement with simulated results. These antennas find applications in UWB communication and monitoring scenarios.

articleTitle: Prediction of 3D Printed Substrate’s Dielectric Constant Using Artificial Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: The article discusses the prediction of the dielectric constant of a material using an Artificial Neural Network (ANN). Here, a 2.4 GHz transmission line is designed on four different substrates namely, flame retardant 4 (FR4), polylactic acid (PLA), thermoplastic polyurethane (TPU), and cardboard paper followed by the transmission parameters measurement using a vector network analyzer (VNA). Later, the material characteristics are extracted using Kramer’s Kronig algorithm. The S-parameter values obtained during the measurement and the dielectric constant and permeability values extracted from Kramer’s Kronig algorithm are further used for training neural networks to predict the dielectric constant of an unknown material. In the validation stage, a patch antenna is designed, simulated, and fabricated on 3D-printed material using the dielectric constant predicted by the ANN. The simulation and measurement values are in good comparison.

articleTitle: Mechanically Reconfigurable Terahertz Quasi-Optical Components for Spectral Filtering and Polarization Control
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Terahertz technologies present unique opportunities for high throughput communications, short-distance high-resolution radar, and spectral sensing/imaging. This spectral range presents some interesting challenges in terms of tunability of transmissive quasi-optical components for spectral filtering or polarization control. The concept of multi-layer periodic structures with sub-wavelength elements, such as frequency-selective surfaces or metasurfaces, allows to create terahertz optical components with unique properties. In this context, this paper reviews three distinctive realizations of such multi-layer transmissive devices with reconfigurable properties. The controlled dynamic adaptation of transmission properties is achieved through mechanical reconfiguration based on relative translation or rotation of layers. These presented devices are illustrative of three efficient implementations based on different physical mechanisms, with application for tunable spectral filtering and dynamic polarization control.

articleTitle: Enhancement of Cut-off Frequency Beyond 2.5 THz by Optimization of Anode Area of Planar Schottky Barrier Diodes for MMIC Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Junction capacitance and series resistance play an important role in determining the cut-off frequency of planar THz Schottky barrier diodes. In this paper, the geometry dependence of anode area on junction capacitance and series resistance value has been studied using TCAD simulation to obtain cut-off frequencies of 2.5 THz or higher. The targeted cut-off frequencies were achieved after fabrication for the chosen rectangular anode geometries.

articleTitle: Implementation of Spectral Estimation with Wavelet Denoising Techniques for Advanced Indian MST Radar: A comparative Study
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: The Mesosphere-Stratosphere-Troposphere (MST) Radar, located at Gadanki, is a powerful tool for observing atmospheric phenomena across various altitudes. Recently upgraded to the Advanced Indian MST Radar (AIR) system, this radar significantly enhanced its capabilities. Spectral estimation is carried out to estimate the Doppler frequency, and from the estimated frequencies, the wind velocity components. This paper presents the implementation of various parametric, non-parametric, and semi-parametric spectral estimation techniques for Advanced Indian MST Radar (AIR) system time series raw data obtained from National Atmospheric Research Laboratory (NARL). It carries out a comparative study of performance of various spectral estimation techniques applied to MST Radar. Additionally, the study explores the application of various wavelet-based denoising techniques for preprocessing the data prior to spectral estimation. This preprocessing step is crucial for enhancing the data quality and subsequently improves the spectral estimation performance.

articleTitle: A Frequency Reconfigurable Magnetic Dipole Based Electrically Small Quasi-Isotropic Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This work presents a novel frequency reconfigurable electrically small antenna (ESA) with a quasi-isotropic radiation pattern for ISM band applications within the 2.4 GHz band. The key contribution of this work is that a split ring resonator (SRR) is used parasitically with the electric dipole to realize a magnetic dipole-type radiation pattern. In addition, the proposed configuration is further configured with two p-i-n diodes to facilitate frequency reconfigurability to the antenna within the 2.4 GHz band. The SRR is arranged orthogonally with an electric curved dipole to achieve a uniform or quasi-isotropic radiation pattern in 3D spatial coverage. The overall size of the fabricated prototype is $0.13 \lambda \times 0.13 \lambda \mathrm{~mm}^{2}$; here, λ is the free space wavelength that corresponds to operating frequencies. The proposed antenna offers 40MHz bandwidth centered at 2.44GHz when the diodes (D1 & D2) are ON and a 30MHz bandwidth centered at 2.47GHz when the diodes (D1 & D2) are OFF. In both states, the antenna exhibits a quasi-isotropic radiation pattern with over 60% efficiency.

articleTitle: On-Chip Terahertz Inverted E-Connected I-Shaped Plasmonic Waveguide Bandpass Filter
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents an advanced on-chip terahertz ($\mathrm{T H z}$) bandpass filter (BPF), uniquely designed with an Inverted E-Connected I-Shaped hybrid spoof surface plasmon polariton (SSPP) integrated with a substrate integrated waveguide (SIW). This design operates effectively across a frequency range of 276 GHz to 296 GHz, achieving a reflection coefficient $S_{11}$ better than $\mathrm{- 1 0} \mathrm{dB}$ and an insertion loss (IL) $S_{21}$ of $\mathrm{- 2. 4} \mathrm{~ d B}$. It features a 3 dB bandwidth of 20 GHz. Notably, the design excels in controlling bandwidth, maintaining a variance of less than 7%, highlighting the precision and innovation in its development and marking it as a significant contribution to THz technology.

articleTitle: A Compact In-Band Full-Duplex Antenna with Improved Performance for V2V/V2X Communications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this paper, a compact high gain in-band fullduplex (IBFD) antenna utilizing an upside-down transmitting and receiving antenna is presented. A V-shaped slot etched on a radiating surface is used to operate at 5.9 GHz, which covers the dedicated short-range communication (DSRC) frequency band $(5.85-5.925 \mathrm{GHz})$. The radiating patches are orthogonally oriented in a vertically-stacked antenna configuration while maintaining a small gap between their ground planes to obtain a large inter-port isolation of 51 dB between the transmitting and receiving system. Each of the antenna element provides a fractional impedance bandwidth (FIBW) of $\mathbf{2. 8 8 \%}$ from 5.815.98 GHz, a peak realized gain of 8 dBi, and a radiation efficiency of $\mathbf{9 6 \%}$. Furthermore, the geometry exhibits a cross-polarization level below -50.4 dB and a front-to-back ratio of 25 dB. The measured responses display a good resemblance with the simulated characteristics, thereby confirming the suitability of the proposed antenna for vehicular communication applications.

articleTitle: Design of a Compact Distributed-Lumped Ka-Band BPF with Wide Stopband in IPD Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This work presents a bandpass filter (BPF), centered at 27.6 GHz and a fractional bandwidth of 22% with a wide stopband using integrated passive device (IPD) technology. The filter is implemented by incorporating both distributed and lumped elements. The central component of the architecture is a $3^{\text {rd }}$ order Chebyshyev’s folded hairpin line tapped filter, which is followed by two lumped element based transmission zero networks(TZN) that enhances the rejection at $2 f_{0}$. Inter-digital capacitors and spiral inductors are used to realize the capacitors and inductors respectively in the TZNs. To the best knowledge of the authors lumped element based TZ have been realized for the first time in hairpin resonator based filter in Ka Band with a miniaturized configuration. Wide stopband rejection of more than 20 dB upto 60 GHz, with an insertion loss (IL) of 1.5 dB and return loss (RL) better than $\mathbf{- 1 9. 5} \mathbf{d B}$ across the band in a size of $0.93 \times 0.99 \times 0.1 \mathrm{~mm}^{3}$ is achieved.

articleTitle: Design & Development of L - Band Drop - In - Isolator for Space Application
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: The authors present microwave Drop-In-Isolator (DII) using Yittrium-Gadolinum (Y-Gd) ferrite and Neodymium (NdFeB) magnets for space applications. The DII is designed for L band, having center frequency of 1.9 GHz. The electric and magnetic circuits (EM-MCs) are designed, simulated and optimized in COMSOL Multiphysics. The dimensions of the DII are obtained theoretically and are presented in detail. The usual measurement process includes the stripline losses and fixture losses. In order to remove these losses, de-embedding method is implemented. The simulation RF performances of the DII are experimentally validated. The DII exhibits return loss more than 20 dB, insertion loss less than 0.4 dB and isolation more than 20 dB within the operating frequency band of $1.8-2.0 \mathrm{GHz}$. A stable performance of the DII is observed over cold $\left(-30^{\circ} \mathrm{C}\right)$ to hot (80°C) temperature range.

articleTitle: Harmonic Beam Steering with 2-Bit Equivalent Phases Using a 1-Bit Time-Domain Coding Metasurface
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents harmonic beam steering by employing 2 -bit equivalent phases from a 1 -bit time-coding element. The space-time-coding (STC) matrix is computed based on the fundamental frequency ($f_{c}$), the desired m th harmonic, and the desired beam angle ($\theta_{d}$). Scattering pattern plots illustrate the radiation pattern at $\theta_{d}$ for the frequency $f_{c}+m f_{0}$, and at $-\theta_{d}$ for $f_{c}-m f_{0}$, where $f_{0}$ is the modulation frequency. The symmetry observed in the radiation patterns for $\pm m$ th harmonics is attributed to the symmetry between their corresponding optimized 2-bit phase equivalents. However, while using the original 1-bit STC matrix, each harmonic produces symmetrically deflected dual beams directed at $\pm \theta_{d}$. The proposed concept and design can be applied to millimeter-wave (mmWave) sensing, communications, and imaging.

articleTitle: Performance Investigation of Triangular Lattice Arrangement Based UWB Phased Array for Electronic Warfare Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This research article investigates the performance of multilayer vivaldi antenna array arranged in triangular lattice. The main objective of this research work is to design ultrawideband (UWB) grating lobe free antenna array for electronic warfare (EW) applications. Proposed structure composed of 8×8 elements arranged in triangular lattice comprehensively analyzed for scattering parameters and farfield performance. Impedance bandwidth of antenna element used in the proposed structure is 15 GHz (120%) in the range of 5 GHz to 20 GHz. Improved radiation characteristics of complete array are observed at boresight with peak gain of 28 dBi at 18 GHz. Reduction in mutual coupling levels among the elements observed and maintained which makes it suitable for defense and aerospace applications.

articleTitle: Miniaturized Tunable Bandpass Filter for Sub-1 GHz Band Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this paper, a compact tunable band-pass filter (BPF) is presented. The filter is designed for the sub- $\mathbf{~ G H z}$ band applications where the measured tunable frequency range (TFR) extends from 0.4 GHz to 0.93 GHz. Its equivalent circuit (EC) model is developed for physical insight. The proposed filter uses a simple biasing arrangement with single voltage control for diodes. Thus, the basing complexity is reduced and it is a miniaturized BPF.

articleTitle: A Single Layer Multi-Functional Reflection Type Polarization Converter for C/X/Ku/K Band Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this paper, a design of multi-functional polarization converter has been proposed with high polarization efficiency, and wide cross converter bandwidth making it an ideal solution for diverse radio frequency (RF) applications. The compact unit cell, measuring $0.46 \lambda \times 0.46 \lambda$ in size, demonstrates a polarization conversion efficiency around $95 \%$. The proposed metasurface is engineered to concurrently convert linear to cross-polarization and circular polarization within C-band, X-band, majority of the Ku-band, also some parts of the K-band. It proficiently converts CPC across three bands with highest bandwidth of ${9 3 . 8 9 \%}$ and LTCP across 7 narrow bands wherein, a single band occupies the lower frequency range of $5.98-6.03 \text{GHz}$, while the others operate at higher frequencies (above 17 GHz) achieving both LHCP and RHCP.

articleTitle: Second Order Dual-Band Band Pass SIW Filter
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper introduces a second order dual bandpass substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) cavity. The cavity dimensions are enlarged to achieve the desired dual-band gap between the fundamental mode (TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">101</inf>) and the next higher mode (TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">102</inf>). Higher modes are suppressed by precisely adjusting the feed position, and a transmission zero is created between the two bands. Two cavities are magnetically coupled via gaps $g_{1}$ and $g_{2}$, forming a second order dual-band bandpass filter. The simulations are performed using Ansys HFSS.

articleTitle: A Large-Signal AlGaN/GaN HEMT model for Kuband applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this paper, the method for extracting the largesignal model of a $0.15 \mu \mathrm{~m}$ AlGaN/GaN HEMT device of size $6 \times 75 \mu \mathrm{~m}$ has been described. The extraction of small-signal parameters at different gate-drain voltages is based on getting reliable extrinsic parameter values from the measured passive pinch-off data, which are then optimized. The model coefficients for the drain source current model have been obtained using curve fitting of the measured I-V data. The model accuracy was verified by S-parameter matching, DC I-V matching and $P_{\text {out vs. Pin }}$ matching between the model and the measured data. The saturated output power of 30.8 dBm has been obtained from the device model in Ku-band.

articleTitle: Parametric Analysis and Design Methodology for Integrated Digitated Capacitor-based Corrugated Substrate Integrated Waveguides
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Standard substrate integrated waveguides (SIW) lack DC isolation making it difficult to place active elements for reconfigurability. Corrugated SIWs (CSIW) have been presented in the literature, using inductive stubs as a replacement of vias to introduce DC isolation, but they face high transmission losses. A new CSIW using integrated-digitated-capacitors (IDC) as corrugations was proposed in the literature that offers low transmission loss while maintaining a complete DC isolation. This paper demonstrates the parametric and modal analysis of the new IDC-based CSIW and compare its performance with classical CSIWs. The IDC-CSIW is shown to offer a reduction in transmission loss of 33% for CSIW to 13% for proposed IDC-CSIW. The paper offers a design methodology to develop such planar waveguides for any frequency bands.

articleTitle: A Novel Filtering Balun Implemented in Substrate Integrated Waveguide Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents a novel filtering balun implemented in substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) technology using modified coupling matrix. The filtering response is achieved using four SIW cavity resonators with iris openings. The balanced output ports (port 2 and port 3) are placed opposite to each other in different layers so as to achieve equal power division and out-of-phase characteristics when the signal is propagating from port 1. To verify the proposed design, SIW filtering balun is simulated at center frequency of 3.5 GHz with 150 MHz bandwidth. The simulated return loss obtained is 19 dB over the entire band and the peak insertion loss is 4.5 dB. As expected, there are no amplitude and phase imbalances in the simulated results. In addition, the design methodology is scalable to realize higher-order filtering response.

articleTitle: Multi Frequency Self Diplexing All Metal Ridge Waveguide Antenna for Cloud Radar Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This article demonstrates a novel dual-band linear polarised self-diplexing ridge waveguide antenna for $35 / 94 \mathrm{GHz}$ cloud radar applications. The structure consists of two waveguides, with the $\mathbf{W}$-band waveguide integrated into the Ka-band waveguide as an embedded ridge, allowing the $\mathbf{W}$-band waveguide to operate in a single mode. A GCPW (Grounded CoPlanar waveguide) to WR (Rectangular Waveguide) transition has been designed to feed the Ka-band waveguide, providing a good bandwidth of approximately 2.4 GHz at Ka-band. A single unit cell with 10 and 30 longitudinal slots exhibits peak gains of 15 dBi and 21 dBi at 35 and 94 GHz, respectively. Furthermore, a four-element configuration has been designed with a peak gain of 21 dBi and 28 dBi for the Ka and W bands respectively.

articleTitle: Flexible CPW-Fed Antenna for Ultra-wideband Wearable Application
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper introduces a compact, slotted coplanar waveguide (CPW)-fed antenna that exhibits a wide bandwidth (fractional bandwidth $\gt \mathbf{5 0 \%}$) within the ultra-wideband (UWB) range, and is also flexible. The antenna design features hexagonal rings that are cut and slotted on a polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) substrate to achieve these characteristics. The slotted hexagonal ring radiator is fed by a tapered CPW, positioned centrally on a trapezium-shaped ground plane. The antenna operates effectively over a frequency range of 1.68 to 9.03 GHz, achieving a total impedance bandwidth of 7.35 GHz ($\mathrm{S} 11\lt -10 \mathrm{~dB}$ for $1.68-9.03 \mathrm{GHz}$, VSWR <2). The peak gain across the band is $\mathbf{6. 7 1} \mathbf{~ d B i}$. Through various design iterations, the peak gain is observed to be 6.71 dBi at 6.5 GHz and 4.07 dBi at 2.4 GHz. Additionally, the antenna maintains an axial ratio $(\mathrm{AR})\lt 3 \mathrm{~dB}$ from 1.75 to 1.83 GHz, and a specific absorption rate (SAR) of $1.33 \mathrm{~W} / \mathrm{kg}$ for 1 g of tissue. The overall dimensions of the antenna are $95 \times 80 \mathrm{~mm}^{2}$.

articleTitle: A Single Complementary Split Ring Shaped fixed frequency SIW Resonator for Rotation Sensing Application
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Microwave sensors have recently evolved in the domain of displacement sensing applications, particularly utilizing the variations in the resonance frequency. However, this kind of approach poses certain challenges, viz. environmental factors as well as higher setup cost. Hence, this paper presents for the first time a newly designed substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) based rotation sensor loaded with single complementary split ring for fixed frequency operation. The parent SIW is designed to operate for the fundamental TE $\mathbf{1 0}_{10}$ propagation mode at a cutoff frequency of 2.4 GHz. The resonator model is loaded over the top surface of SIW to yield a resonance at a fixed frequency of 5.42 GHz for a rotation range of 0° to 50°. The sensor is implemented by making the resonator to rotate which displayed a fixed frequency notch. The sensing principle here depends on the variation of the notch depth at the resonance with respect to different rotation angles. This preliminary design is working well within a dynamic range of $0^{\circ}-50^{\circ}$ with a decent linearity. The proposed fixed frequency rotation sensor is exhibiting a sensitivity of $0.28 \mathrm{~dB} /{}^{\circ}$. These performance metrics are significantly good compared to the other available fixed frequency rotation sensors.

articleTitle: Microstrip Patch with Strategic Loading: A New Variant for Significant Improvement in the Polarization Purity
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This work explores a novel patch loading technique to effectively mitigate the cross-polarized (XP) radiation over both orthogonal (H-) and diagonal (D-) planes of a coaxial fed rectangular microstrip patch. PTFE based laminated strip, along with strategic steps, has been introduced to overcome the limitations posed by the higher order TM02 mode. To alleviate the field asymmetry imposed by the offset coaxial probe, the loading has been positioned at an offset point. A C-band patch ensures as much as 23 dB XP improvement over H-plane and 5 dB over the D-plane, keeping input impedance and primary radiation undisturbed.

articleTitle: Automated Design of Pixelated Metasurfaces using Particle Swarm Optimization for Diverse Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper introduces an automated methodology for designing pixelated metasurfaces for diverse application scenarios. Our approach dynamically adjusts pixel positions on the metaatoms of the metasurface to achieve specific functionalities. Based on Particle Swarm Optimization, the design algorithm minimizes the cost function to output optimal pixel configuration for the desired functionality. For definiteness, we focused on optimizing the Polarization Conversion Ratio and Transmission Efficiency at a target frequency $f_{0}$. We fabricated metasurface prototypes based on simulated meta-atoms and conducted experimental measurements to validate our approach. The experimental results are strongly correlated with the simulated responses, confirming the efficacy of our methodology for designing versatile metasurfaces with electromagnetic response characteristics that are desirable for specific application scenarios.

articleTitle: Enhanced Liquid Adulteration Detection Using a Novel CSRR-Loaded Planar Microwave Probe
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A new design for a complementary split ring resonator (CSRR) loaded planar microwave probe has been developed to improve sensitivity in liquid adulteration detection. Unlike traditional planar resonant sensors, these innovative two-port and single-port structures can be directly submerged in liquid samples. Sensor 1 features a microstrip line with CSRRs etched at the ground plane, creating a compact and highly sensitive probe. Sensor 2 features a microstrip patch with CSRRs etched at the points of the maximum electric field, creating a compact sensitive probe. The design, studied in CST Studio Suite Electromagnetic Solver and fabricated for testing, can distinguish between materials with similar dielectric constants. Sensor 1 operates in the $7.6-9.4 \mathrm{GHz}$ band and sensor 2 operates in the $\mathrm{1 2. 8} \mathrm{- 1 3. 8} \mathrm{~ G H z}$ band, the sensors effectively detect adulterants like mineral oil in high-quality edible oils, demonstrating its superior sensitivity and precision in measuring dielectric properties.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of Millimeter Wave Radar Waveforms for Integrated Sensing and Communication
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Next-generation intelligent transportation systems require both sensing and communication between road users. However, deploying separate radars and communication devices involves the allocation of individual frequency bands and hardware platforms. Integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) offers a robust solution to the challenges of spectral congestion by utilizing a shared waveform, hardware, and spectrum for both localization of mobile users and communication. Various waveforms, including phase-modulated continuous waves (PMCW) and frequency-modulated continuous waves (FMCW), have been explored for target localization using traditional radar. On the other hand, new protocols such as the IEEE 802.11ad have been proposed to support wideband communication between vehicles. This paper compares both traditional radar and communication candidate waveforms for ISAC to detect single-point and extended targets. We show that the response of FMCW to mobile targets is poorer than that of PMCW. However, the IEEE 802.11ad radar outperforms PMCW radar and FMCW radar. Additionally, the radar signal processing algorithms are implemented on Zynq system-on-chip through hardware-software co-design and fixed-point analysis to evaluate their computational complexity in real-world implementations.

articleTitle: Data-Driven BiLSTM Prediction Model for Dual-Band RF Power Amplifier
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This article proposes a Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (BiLSTM) model to capture nonlinear distortions in dual-band RF power amplification (PA) systems. It is important for advanced wireless communication systems, especially those with high peak-to-average power ratio (PAPR) waveforms, to characterize and linearize RF power amplifiers (PAs) despite deep learning’s success in various fields. This study employs BiLSTM neural networks to address memory effects in nonlinear PAs. This paper designed and tested a dual-band PA operating at 2.4 GHz, using the BiLSTM model to predict output power and linearity. Our BiLSTM-based modeling architecture effectively addresses non-causality concerns, achieving an R-Square ($R^{2}$) of 0.89, mean squared error (MSE) of 0.013, and mean absolute error (MAE) of $\mathbf{0. 0 7}$. Experimental results validate our approach’s effectiveness, demonstrating accurate PA characterization by the trained networks. The BiLSTM model also shows promising performance in linearizing tested PAs, addressing their inherent unpredictability. This work advances deep learning integration to enhance PA performance in future wireless communication systems.

articleTitle: A Tilted-modified Phi-shaped Reflective Type Polarizer for V/W-Band Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents a new unit cell named here as a ‘tilted modified Phi-shaped (TMPS)’ polarization converter. The proposed TMPS offers linear co- to linear cross-polarization at V - and W-band frequencies. The TMPS demonstrates a polarization conversion bandwidth of 78.12% $(52.63$ to 120.11 GHz) with a polarization conversion ratio (PCR) exceeding $\mathrm{9 0 \%}$. Furthermore, surface current distributions have been studied to analyse the wideband behaviour of the proposed converter. The ultrathin compact wideband TMPS polarization converter is suitable for applications in radar technology.

articleTitle: Bifunctional Metasurface for Linear Polarization Conversion and Absorption using Vanadium Dioxide
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Vanadium dioxide $\left(\mathbf{V O}_{2}\right)$ is a phase change material that exhibits reversible insulator-to-metal transition close to 68 °C. During the phase transition, VO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> shows more than three orders of resistance switching, changing its behavior to metallic at high temperature, which makes it suitable for RF switching and tunable microwave devices. Traditional metasurfaces are typically designed for a single application with fixed frequency response. This simulation work reports a VO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> based switchable bifunctional metasurface which can achieve polarization conversion and electromagnetic absorption through phase transition of VO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>. In the insulating state of VO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>, the proposed metasurface acts as a linear polarization converter from 17.9 GHz to 22.9 GHz with more than 90% polarization conversion ratio. Whereas, in the metallic state of VO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>, the designed metasurface acts as an absorber from 15.86 GHz and 23.02 GHz with less than -10 dB reflection. The presented approach to obtain dual functionality may stimulate new ideas to design multifunctional microwave devices.

articleTitle: A Triple Band Polarization Insensitive Graphene-Based Metasurface Absorber in Terahertz Gap
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper proposes a graphene-based metasurface absorber structure for low, mid, and trailing ranges of terahertz (THz) gap. The unit cell of the structure consists of a patterned graphene layer with simultaneous plus-shaped and swastika-shaped slots grown over a layer of amorphous silicon dioxide ($\mathbf{S i O}_{2}$) backed by a golden layer. The proposed structure offers three absorption bands having bandwidths of 0.83 THz, 0.96 THz and 0.48 THz with respective peaks at 3.03 $\mathrm{THz}, 6.06 \mathrm{THz}$, and 9.93 THz. The four-fold symmetry of the unit cell makes the structure polarization insensitive in nature. The structure offers angular stability for oblique incidents up to $\mathbf{4 0}$ degrees for both TE and TM modes of polarization. The structure is as thin as $\sim \lambda / 14$ concerning the frequency of first peak absorption, and the periodicity of the unit cell is $\sim \lambda / 16.5$ supporting effective homogeneity condition. The structure can be used for future implementable aspects that can apply to sensing, 6G communications and other biomedical applications.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of 5 Element C-band and 4 Group X-band Conformal Shared Aperture Antenna Array for Spaceborne SAR Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Synthetic aperture radar (SAR) generates high resolution images of Earth’s surface in day and night weather by using microwave signals. A dual-band C/X linear polarized conformal shared aperture antenna (SAA) for spaceborne SAR applications is presented in this paper. The five-element series feeding C-band and the four group X-band corporate feeding form the SAA structure. Each group of X-band consists of 4 elements $(2 \times 2)$. The antenna’s performance properties are evaluated. The proposed design achieved a bandwidth of 50 MHz and gain of 12.1 dBi for the C-band. For the X -band 305 MHz bandwidth and 12.7 dBi gain is attained. The proposed design works as radome due to conformal nature. The total size of the SAA array is $110 \times 106 \times 0.8 \mathbf{~ m m}$.

articleTitle: Optically-Driven RIS for Next-Generation 5G Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: -the paper presents an optically driven reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS) tailored for next-generation 5G sub-6 GHz applications. The unit cell employs a semicircle slot design on FR4 material, optimized using Finite Element Method (FEM) techniques. A PIN diode serves as the tuning element, modulating electromagnetic waves based on its on/off states controlled remotely by light. The unit cell demonstrates excellent reflection coefficient characteristics within the 3.3 to 3.5 GHz range typical of 5 G sub- 6 applications, providing a phase difference of $180^{\circ} \pm 20^{\circ}$ between diode states. A full-wave simulation of a 16x10 RIS array is conducted with excitation in x-polarization. The array effectively steers the beam to 18 degrees in normal incident $\left(\theta i=0^{0}\right)$ and 3 degrees under oblique incidence $\left(\theta i=30^{\boldsymbol{0}}\right.$) respectively. In first scenarios, the RIS achieves superior performance with a gain of 17.7 dBi, a halfpower beam width (HPBW) of 9 degree, and $\mathbf{- 1 0} \mathbf{d B}$ side lobe level (SLL) at 3.4 GHz. The characteristics of the proposed RIS enable perfect anomalous reflection of electromagnetic (EM) waves. Overall, these results demonstrate that the proposed design is well-suited for future 5G sub-6 applications in wireless communication.

articleTitle: Fully Balanced Ka-Band Up-Conversion Mixer MMIC with an Integrated Self Biased Amplifier
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This article presents a X band ($7-9 \mathrm{GHz}$) to Ka band $(25-29 \mathrm{GHz})$ frequency up-converter realized using 130 nm GaAs/AlGaAs/InGaAs pHEMT process. The mixer core includes on-chip transformers at all the ports which helps it to achieve excellent isolation and sideband suppression. The FET resistive mixer architecture is chosen because of its ability to operate with a very small LO power of 3 dBm. Besides the mixer circuit, a four stage self-biased amplifier to boost the RF signal is also implemented on the same chip. The measured conversion gain(CG) is $\gt15 \mathrm{~dB}$ over a wide bandwidth of 24 to 28 GHz with peak output power of 10 dBm for -8 dBm IF power input. The designed circuit offers greater than $\mathbf{2 0} \mathbf{d B c}$ harmonic suppression (HS) for the undesired tones. The proposed circuit consumes 80 mA current from 2 V single DC supply. The assembled chip in a hermetically sealed module qualifies for space applications.

articleTitle: Optimum Design of Non-Quadrature Phase Difference Coupler with Unequal Power Division using Coupled Lines
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In modern wireless technology, the compactness of the design is an essential factor to consider. A new non-quadrature, unequal power division coupler with an arbitrary coupling coefficient using coupled transmission lines is proposed in this work. As the designed coupler consists of only three coupled line sections, it requires less area than conventional branch-line couplers. For the optimum performance and errorfree transmission of signals, bandwidth should be as maximum as possible. In this designed coupler, one can get the maximum coupling coefficient bandwidth in amplitude response, phase imbalance, and amplitude imbalance graphs. The generalized phase difference coupled line coupler’s design equations are derived by even-odd mode analysis.

articleTitle: Gain and Bandwidth Enhancement of Printed Dipole Antenna for X-Band Applications by using 1-Bit Reflectarray
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This work presents an effective method for enhancing the bandwidth and gain of a printed dipole antenna by employing a 1-bit reflectarray. The dipole antenna (Antenna 1) has a bandwidth of 4.6 GHz, covering the range from 4.01 GHz to 5.41 GHz, and a gain of $\mathbf{2. 6} \mathbf{~ d B i}$. Three circular radiators were placed at the bottom of the substrate of the printed dipole antenna to enhance both gain and bandwidth. In addition, two resonances were generated in the X -band at 8.4 GHz and 10.6 GHz. A bandwidth of 3.7 GHz was obtained over a range from 7.2 GHz to 10.9 GHz, while the lower resonance frequency shifted from 4.6 GHz to 4.69 GHz, with a bandwidth of 4.3 GHz to 5.1 GHz and a gain of $\mathbf{3. 1} \mathbf{~ d B i}$. The $16 \times 16$ element 1-Bit Reflectarray antenna was illuminated to enhance the gain from 3.1 dBi to 25.1 dBi for X-band applications. The cross-polarization level of the proposed Reflectarray was - 22 dB.

articleTitle: Implementation of Ladder Decoupling Structure to Enhance Isolation in Slotted Rhombic Shaped Multi-Band (SRSM) MIMO Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this research article, a novel compact 2-port slotted rhombic shape multi-band (SRSM) Multiple-Input Multiple-Output (MIMO) antenna, measuring $\mathbf{4 8} \times \mathbf{3 8} \times \mathbf{1. 6} \mathrm{mm}^{\mathbf{3}}$ is designed and analyzed the performance. The antenna functions across four distinct frequency bands: 4.35 GHz (C-band), $\mathbf{1 2. 3 5 ~ G H z ~ (K u - b a n d), ~} \mathbf{1 7. 5} \mathbf{~ G H z}$ (Ku-band), and 22.7 GHz (K-band), achieving a maximum return loss of 34.8 dB at 4.35 GHz. The associated impedance bandwidths are 7.05 GHz, $2.1 \mathrm{GHz}, 3.5 \mathrm{GHz}$, and 3.7 GHz, respectively. To improve isolation, a ladder-shaped decoupling structure is integrated into the ground plane, resulting in isolation $\geq \mathbf{2 5} \mathbf{~ d B}$. The antenna shows impressive performance metrics, including an Envelope Correlation Coefficient (ECC) $\leq 0.001$, Total Active Reflection Coefficient (TARC) <-10 dB, a gain of 7.39 dBi, and a diversity gain of $\cong \mathbf{9. 9 9 9} \mathbf{~ d B}$. These frequency bands support a range of applications such as satellite communication, military radar, 5G, and future wireless communication systems. Both simulated and measured results are in agreement, highlighting the antenna’s suitability for advanced wireless communication applications with high isolation, low correlation, and efficient multi-band functionality.

articleTitle: Ultra Wide-band Circularly Polarized Graphene Tunable SIW-CDRA for 6G THz Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: The present investigation introduces a novel cylindrical dielectric resonator antenna (CDRA) for 6 G THz applications based on a Substrate-Integrated Waveguide (SIW). Operating in the 9.72 THz to $\mathbf{1 2 . 4 8} \mathbf{~ T H z}$ frequency band, the antenna exhibits Ultra-Wide-Band (UWB) characteristics. This SIW-CDRA structure is esteemed for its Circular Polarization (CP) capability and graphene-based tunability. Graphene integration atop the CDRA enables altering the antenna’s resonance frequency, whereas controlled changes in graphene potential achieve CP tuning. The configuration generates an Impedance Bandwidth (IBW) of -10 dB covering 24.82% (9.72 $\mathrm{THz}-12.48 \mathrm{THz}$), with a peak radiation efficiency of 67.6% and a maximum gain of $\mathbf{1 0 . 1 3 \mathrm { dB }}$. The antenna provides a bandwidth of 2.39%(10.32 THz-10.57 THz) at a 3 dB Axial Ratio (AR). These results demonstrate the unique features of the suggested SIW-CDRA for THzapplications.

articleTitle: Continuous Temperature Monitoring of Substation Switchgear Using PassiveWireless RFID Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This work presents the design and development of an Ultra High Frequency (UHF) RFID sensor tag for continuous temperature monitoring in switchgear substations. The tag antenna of dimension, $69 \times 15 \text{mm}^{2}$ designed on a 1.52 mm thick FR-4 substrate using EM simulation software HFSS $^{\circledR}$, Ansys Inc., USA, achieved a gain of $1.8 \mathrm{d B i}$ at $915 \mathrm{~ M H z}$. Simulation and measurement results demonstrated a reflection coefficient of $\mathrm{- 1 3 . 7 6 ~ d B ~ a n d } \mathrm{- 1 2 . 2 6 ~ d B}$, respectively, with a maximum read rate of 1.5 m. Real-time temperature measurement under actual switchgear conditions validated the sensor's suitability for condition monitoring applications.

articleTitle: Thermo-Mechanical Design and Analysis of W-Band Sheet Beam Electron Gun Assembly for Efficient Heat Dissipation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This article reports, thermo-mechanical analysis of a sheet beam electron gun compatible with vacuum electronic devices operating in $\mathbf{W}$ band frequencies. Thermal analysis of the electron gun has been carried out to estimate temperature distribution at different parts of the electron gun assembly which in turn dictates possible geometrical alternations of electron gun components and crucial inter-component geometrical dimensions. The electrode geometries, support structures, cathode heat shield and joints have been optimized to minimize thermal drain in operating condition of the device. Estimation of the optimal heater power has been done to achieve proper uniform temperature across the cathode surface using transient and steady state simulation. Thermal deformation of electrodes has been computed in order to evaluate the spacing between electrodes in operating condition which is crucial to estimate realistic beam current during operating conditions.

articleTitle: Sub-Arrays using CSRR Loaded Dual-band Microstrip Patch Antennas for MIMO and Phased Array Applications in 6G FR3 Band
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this paper, sub-arrays using a CSRR (complementary split-ring resonator) loaded microstrip patch antennas are proposed for MIMO and phased array applications in 6 G wireless communication systems. The CSRR-loading on the microstrip patch antenna leads to simultaneous miniaturization and dualband performance spanning center-frequencies of 11 GHz and 13 GHz, making the antenna element suitable for operation in the 6G FR3 band advocated by 3GPP. The CSRR-loaded dual-band microstrip patch is used to first realize a $2 \times 2$ subarray (configuration-I) with an inter-element spacing of $0.5 \lambda_{0}$, where $\lambda_{0}$ is the free-space wavelength at 13 GHz, which shows a grating lobe free beam steering up to 80°. The sub-array achieves a satisfactory impedance matching of $\leq-20 \mathrm{~dB}$ and inter-port isolation $\geq 16 \mathrm{~dB}$. Another sub-array (ConfigurationII) is then configured using the dual-band patch and sequential rotation principle for polarization diversity MIMO application. The proposed sub-arrays configurations using CSRR-loaded dualband microstrip patches are further fabricated, and the results are experimentally validated.

articleTitle: Miniaturized Dual-band 2.5D Reconfigurable Frequency Selective Surface for Switching Between Passband and Microwave Absorption
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper showcases a novel 2.5D architecture-based dual-band multifunctional active frequency selective surface (AFSS). The designed AFSS exhibits passband filter response in the transmission mode operation and microwave absorption at dual frequencies in the reflection mode operation. Electronic switching between two operating modes was realized by adequate biasing of the PIN diodes in ON and OFF states. The unit element of the AFSS consists of multilayer 2D periodic metasurfaces (MS) arranged in a back-to-back manner. The top MS is a combination of 2.5D via enabled resonators, and the bottom MS is made of a pair of metal strips and T-shaped structures integrated with PIN diodes. The air-spacer of thickness 1 mm is sandwiched between the two MSs. The AFSS exhibits a highly stable response at different oblique incidences.

articleTitle: A New Reconfigurable Intelligent Surface featuring Amplification Capabilities for 6G Communication
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents an active reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS) integrated with a power amplifier (PA) to enhance the reflected electromagnetic wave. The new patch design and the slotted hourglass plane improve the bandwidth in conjunction with the microstrip line. A 2x2 ARIS subarray is designed, incorporating a power combining and dividing network along with a single PA to reduce both cost and complexity of the ARIS. The ARIS achieved a gain from 0.04 dB to 0.45 dB over the frequency range of 4.5 GHz to 5.5 GHz. The proposed Active RIS is well-suited for Interference Management and Low-Latency Communications.

articleTitle: Design and Realization of small S-Band Ground Station Antenna using ADE Geometry
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Design, fabrication and realization of a four element helical array feed for 2.7 m axially displaced ellipse (ADE) reflector is demonstrated in this article. Profile for the antenna with optimized optics is generated with close form equations and analyzed in TICRA. Approximate gain of the primary pattern is derived for optimized optics with the help of TICRA simulation. A 14-turn helical antenna array, which resembles desired gain of the primary pattern is designed in HFSS for optimum secondary pattern. The helical array is arranged in $2 \times 2$ configurations. Inter-element spacing of the array elements is optimized to obtain desired pattern. Designed elements are fabricated with the help of local vendor and later they are characterized in CATF for radiation pattern. Measured radiation pattern resembles with the simulated pattern. A suitable dome shaped low-loss radome is fabricated covering four elements. The Radome is characterized in CATF and measured loss is less than 0.2 dB in the operating frequency band. The feed along with other feed electronics integrated with 2.7 m ADE reflector antenna system. Overall performance is validated by measuring G/T using sun and receiving real time satellite data. The antenna system is currently operational at international ground station.

articleTitle: A Wideband Dual-Feed Microstrip Antenna With Pattern Diversity
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Pattern diversity antennas can be used in both communication and sensing applications. However, ensuring both the pattern diversity and a wideband response together with a single antenna is challenging. To this end, a novel, dual-feed microstrip antenna fed by a ratrace coupler has been designed and fabricated here. A wideband impedance matching and a good isolation between the ports are experimentally validated. Pattern diversity is observed on the two ports of the antenna, which have broadside and conical patterns.

articleTitle: A 3-W, 25 dB Gain, 40 % PAE Three-Stage Ka-Band MMIC Power Amplifier
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents the design performance continuous wave (CW) Monolithic Microwave Integrated Circuit (MMIC) Power Amplifier (PA) with greater than 3 Watt output power, implemented in a 150 nm GaN-grown on-SiC HEMT process. The power amplifier (PA) features three cascaded stages, each progressively increasing the RF power level from 10 dBm to 35 dBm, while maintaining over 40% power added efficiency (PAE) over the frequency range of 24 to 26 GHz. This proposed 3-stage mmic is realized in UMS 150-nm GaN on SiC process.

articleTitle: A QMSIW Based Antenna Sensor for Breast Tumor Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This study introduces a small, lightweight, Quarter Mode Substrate Integrated Waveguide (QMSIW) cavity-backed antenna as a near field microwave sensor for breast tumor detection. The proposed sensor operates at $2.4 \mathbf{~ G H z}$ ISM band and exhibits good sensibility in identifying the abnormalities in the dielectric characteristics of breast tissues. The proposed antenna is fabricated on RT Duroid 5880 with overall footprint of $\mathbf{3 3} \mathbf{~ m m} \times \mathbf{2 6} \mathbf{~ m m}$. The sensor is validated through experimental testing using realistic heterogeneous breast phantoms both with and without a tumor. At the outset, the sensor is placed 2 mm from the healthy breast phantom and the resonant frequency is measured to be 2.43 GHz. Following that, the sensor’s performance is assessed by systematically modifying the position and sizes of the tumor. The simulated and measured reflection coefficient results demonstrate a significant discrepancy between healthy and malignant tissues. Furthermore, the SAR analysis is performed to investigate the disparities between normal breast tissues and cancerous tissues.

articleTitle: Radar Based Vital Sign Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents study on a microwave frequency system specifically crafted for non-contact monitoring of vital signs. The system employs a radar to transmit modulated wave signals towards the target object. Through the analysis of transmission and interference signals at varying levels, crucial information pertaining to the movement of vital signs is extracted and discerned. The paper focuses on data processing utilizing the Doppler effect. Subsequently, the obtained results will be meticulously scrutinized with reference values to assess their efficacy in accurately extracting vital sign movements. This research significantly contributes to the progress of non-invasive biomedical diagnostics by enhancing our comprehension of microwave system functionality for vital sign measurement.

articleTitle: Realization of True Time-delay based Transmit Modules for EW applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Active electronically scanned array (AESA) technology has reached a mature level over many years of development for RADAR applications that have traditionally been steered with phase shifters but it suffers from beam squinting over wide bandwidths. In AESA based EW Applications which require to handle wide instantaneous bandwidth waveforms and operate with narrow beam widths, this beam squint is good enough to steer off of the target, depending upon the frequency. This problem can be solved by using True Time Delay(TTD) devices in place of Phase Shifter which reduces beam squint, increases based on bandwidth and also provides frequency independent beam scanning. In this paper we discuss in detail about fully integrated ultra-wideband 4-channel and 8-channel timed array which has been designed and developed to establish the feasibility of crucial and critical hardware critical aspects. The TTD element used in each channel has a resolution of 3.125ps and can provide maximum delay of 197 ps. The design bandwidth is from C-Ku band in CW which corresponds to less than 1 cm inter channel spacing.

articleTitle: A Frequency switchable Multiband Microstrip Patch Antenna using Two P-I-N diodes for X/Ku Band Communication
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: The communication antenna in modern communication systems should dynamically change the operating frequency to ensure optimal performance under a variety of scenarios. The design of a frequency reconfigurable Patch antenna (FRPA) with a height of 1.5 mm in RT Duroid Roger 5880 substrate is discussed in this paper. The proposed antenna with a dimension of $38.5 \times 38 \times 1.5 \mathrm{~mm} 3$ is designed with two PIN diodes with four tunable modes in the frequency of operation through the status of PIN diodes. The designed antenna is a rectangular patch antenna with circular slots in it and a T-shaped patch is used as an extension in the regular rectangular patch with a PIN diode as a switch. The patch antenna is slotted to get the desired radiation pattern for the frequency of operation at a range of $(5 \mathrm{GHz}-20 \mathrm{GHz})$ which covers partial X-band and Ku band. The simulation of the proposed antenna can provide a gain of 9.02 dB with high radiation efficiency. The VSWR is below 2 and $S_{11}{\lt}-10 \mathrm{~dB}$ for all the resonating frequencies of different modes of operations.
