The antenna design satisfies the requirements of contemporary radar communication, which includes weather and air traffic control (ATC), Broadcasting, VSAT, and Earth observation.

articleTitle: Multi-Temperature RF GaN HEMT Model Using the ASM Industry Standard
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this paper, we discuss the methodology for the extraction of DC parameters and RF parameters of normally-on Gallium Nitride-based high electron mobility transistors (GaNHEMT). The industry standard ASM GaN HEMT model is used to model the bias dependency of intrinsic capacitances and resistances of the small signal equivalent circuit by fitting the DC characteristics. The extrinsic parameters are then extracted using Scattering parameters for a broad frequency range. Through validation with measured data at multiple biases and temperatures, our methodology demonstrates accurate and reliable parameter extraction for developing large-signal models of GaN-HEMTs. Given the need for GaN RF products in harsh environments, this model serves as a facilitator for the design of future GaN RF applications for deployment at elevated temperatures.

articleTitle: Design and PIC Simulation of Klystron like RBWO with Four Premodulation Cavities
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: An X-band Klystron like Relativistic Backward Wave Oscillator, with four pre-modulation cavities, has been designed and simulated for its beam-wave interaction behavior using FDTD-based electromagnetic code. A maximum RF output power of $\sim 2.91 \mathrm{GW}$ at operating frequency of $\sim 9.48$ GHz was predicted by the present simulation, given an applied input DC voltage of 570 kV, a beam current of about $\sim 6.7 \mathrm{kA}$, and a magnetic field of 2.7 T. Other factors such as $\mathrm{R} / \mathrm{Q}$, surface power loss, stored electromagnetic energy, and electron power were observed across pre-modulation cavities. The power conversion efficiency was calculated to be $\sim 76 \%$ and pulse length of $\sim 100 \mathrm{~ns}$.

articleTitle: Investigation of Resonance De-tuning In Scalable All Metal-patch Phased Array Radar Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: The paper presents the investigation of the detuning of all-metal scalable Phased Array Antenna (PAA). A $4 \times 4$ tile array configuration using a suspended metal patch is studied to operate at L-Band. The metal patch is optimized to achieve 50 MHz of bandwidth at the center frequency of $1620 \mathbf{~ M H z}$. The detuning of the antenna resonance is investigated in the array environment and corrected by following a reverse engineering approach. The reverse engineering approach follows active investigation of the field distribution and optimizes the performance, thus reducing the development cost by 50%. The maximum gain of $4 \times 4 \mathbf{P A A}$ is $18 \mathbf{d B i}$, with a reduced mutual coupling of $\geq 20 \mathrm{~dB}$. The beam steering performance of the allmetal $4 \times 4 {\text { PAA }}$ is demonstrated up to ± 50°. The performance of the simulated antenna was validated by measurement and agrees well with each other. The proposed design is a potential candidate for large-scale phased array radar systems.

articleTitle: Hairpin Resonator Based Non-invasive EM Biosensor For Lung Health Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This work presents the design and evaluation of a novel wearable microwave sensor for real-time monitoring of lung health using a modified hairpin microwave resonator. The proposed sensor operates at a center frequency of 2.2 GHz and is capable of detecting shifts in the resonant frequency due to the changes in permittivity for different lung abnormalities. The proposed sensor provides a significant shift of 515.5 MHz for pulmonary edema and 435 MHz for emphysema, demonstrating its high sensitivity to detect aforementioned respiratory environment. The sensor exhibits a sensitivity of 8.2% and a figure of merit (FOM) of 18.164, along with a Q-factor of 227, indicating its high-performance capabilities. The simulated results of the hairpin resonator integrated with real characteristics of human tissue mimic, demonstrate its potential as a sensor for real-time monitoring of lung functions, which could aid in the early detection and management of respiratory conditions.

articleTitle: Ultra-Wide Band Dual-Polarized Transceiver Antenna Module for Buried Target Detection In Lossy Medium
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper proposes a miniaturized transceiver antenna module for buried target detection in a lossy medium. The transceiver antenna module is configured using a vivaldi boxshaped antenna array, where the Transmitter(Tx) and Receiver $(\mathbf{R x})$ antenna array module are separated with a $0.6 \lambda_{0}$ distance to achieve an isolation of below $-20 d B$, where $\lambda_{0}$ is the freespace wavelength at 1 GHz. Each antenna array comprises seven ultra-wideband Vivaldi antenna elements operating at $1-4 \mathrm{GHz}$ and equal amplitude power combiner. The array configuration is optimized to achieve a peak gain of $12 \mathbf{d B i}$, maintaining an average angular coverage of 30° for perfect penetration in a lossy medium. The simulated antenna performance was validated through measurement, and they are in agreement with each other. The proposed transceiver model is highly potent in defense and military systems.

articleTitle: Design and Development of a Truncated Patch Antenna with slot loading for Wearable Devices
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This study introduces the design and development of a truncated compact patch antenna featuring a button-slot, aimed at wearable technology. Specifically designed for the ISM band and WBAN, the antenna measures $42 \text{mm} \times 40 \text{mm} \times 1.6$ mm. A microstrip line powers the button-slot equipped truncated patch, constructed on an FR4-Epoxy substrate. Operating within the ISM band from 2.21 GHz to 3.15 GHz, the antenna achieves a reflection coefficient of $\mathbf{- 2 6 . 4 5} \mathbf{~ d B}$. It offers a bandwidth of 940 MHz, and a gain of $\mathbf{3 . 8 5} \mathbf{~ d B i}$. The specific absorption rate (SAR) is maintained below $1.6 \text{W} / \text{Kg}$, ensuring user safety. Simulation was conducted using HFSS software, and the fabricated antenna exhibits considerable gain. This antenna is an excellent choice for ISM band applications, including Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, WBAN, and other wearable technologies.

articleTitle: A Multi-functional Single-Layer Polarization converter with High-Efficiency
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this paper, a simple design of multi-functional polarization converter has been proposed with good angular stability, high polarization efficiency, wide bandwidth performance features, making it an ideal solution for diverse radio frequency (RF) applications. The proposed metasurface is engineered to concurrently convert linear to cross-polarization and circular polarization within the C-band and partially within the X-band. It proficiently converts a linearly polarized wave to a circularly polarized wave across two distinct frequencies, both right-hand circular polarization and left-hand circular polarization is achieved.The compact unit cell, measuring $0.24 \lambda \times 0.24 \lambda$ in size, demonstrates a conversion efficiency exceeding 90% for incident angles up to 50 degrees.

articleTitle: Wideband Monopole Antenna for Medical Imaging Application
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this work a compact monopole antenna is designed for breast tumor imaging. The put forward model operates from 1.62 to 11.13 GHz, with a maximum gain of 5.32 dBi at 7.6 GHz. The Specific Absorption rate (SAR) of the designed antenna is checked at several frequencies within its broadband. This is done by separately designing breast model. All the performance parameters of the put forward structure is studied from the simulator. Also multiple copies of the designed antenna are placed around the modelled breast phantom for getting adequate data for imaging the embedded tumor at a later stage.

articleTitle: Highly miniaturized SIW-based self-multiplexing antenna for pentaband applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This communication presents a highly miniaturized SIW self-multiplexing antenna for penta-band applications. The proposed design utilizes K-shaped and Yshaped slots on a half-mode (HM) SIW cavity to form five independent radiators with high isolation between the ports. The antenna radiates at $2.42 \mathrm{GHz}, 3.55 \mathrm{GHz}, 4.45 \mathrm{GHz}, 5.2 \mathrm{GHz}$, and 5.81 GHz, covering WLAN bands. The proposed selfpentaplexing SIW antenna (SPSIWA) is compact, has high isolation ($27-41 \mathrm{~dB}$), acceptable peak realized gain (3-5 dB), and unidirectional radiation pattern.

articleTitle: Design of Meta Surface based Monopole Antenna Sensor for Breast Cancer Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents the design of a meta surface-based monopole antenna sensor intended for breast tumor detection, operating at a resonant frequency of 2 GHz. The miniaturization of the proposed antenna-sensor is achieved around 37% after introducing two pairs of rectangular slots on the length edge of the patch. The overall footprint of the proposed antenna is $0.3 \lambda_{g} \times 0.45 \lambda_{g}$. The monopole antenna is designed on Rogers RT5880 material with a thin profile of 0.787 mm thickness. A meta surface acting as a reflector is designed with intention to increase gain. After placing the meta surface, the antenna gain is enhanced from 2.13 dBi to 6.9 dBi. The proposed antenna is an efficient radiator maintain radiation efficiency $88-99 \%$ in the operating bandwidth 1.94 GHz to 2.06 GHz. Later, we have used the proposed design to detect the presence of tumor in a heterogeneous female breast-equivalent phantom. The meta-surface combined with antenna improves the sensor performance to receive the reflected/transmitted EM-wave.

articleTitle: Multi-Facet Loaded Quad-Band Dielectric Resonator Antenna for Self-Sustainable Smart City Applications Using RF Energy Harvesting
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this paper, a quad-band dielectric resonator antenna (DRA) with dual-polarization characteristics for RFEH applications is stated. A spiral facet approach has been investigated and it is employed on four faces of the proposed DRA for obtaining multi-band characteristics. The antenna with four spiral facets on the left-bottom-top and rear surfaces offers better results over all other multi-facet combinations, and that design is considered the optimized one. A rectangularly shaped dielectric resonator ($13 \times 11 \times 6.3 \mathrm{~mm} 3$) has been chosen for designing a DRA on a low-cost FR4 substrate ($66 \times 68 \times 1.6$ mm 3). The proposed antenna covers $5.0 \mathrm{GHz}, 5.5 \mathrm{GHz}, 5.8 \mathrm{GHz}$, and 6.2 GHz bands. The proposed spiral facet technique offers an additional feature of providing Omni-directional characteristics.

articleTitle: Performance Comparison of Time-Modulated Linear Antenna Arrays Using Various Switching Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents a comparative analysis of random and constant instances with different switching schemes in a time-modulated linear antenna array (TMLAA). This work focuses on radiated power in the fundamental and harmonic frequencies using various switching schemes in TMLAA. Simulations are conducted using an 8-element TMLAA implemented in MATLAB to examine the performance of Bidirectional Phase Center Motion (BPCM), Unidirectional Phase Center Motion (UPCM), and Variable Aperture Size (VAS) schemes with varied and constant instances.

articleTitle: Investigation of Dual-Band Dual-sense Circularly Polarized MIMO DRA for 5G millimetre wave Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this study a dual-band, dual-sense circularly polarized (CP) dielectric resonator (DR) based multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) antenna for 5G millimeter-wave applications is designed. This design combine two cylindrical DRs with varying radii stacked above one another, each excited by a Z-shaped slot embedded in the ground plane to obtain CP. The stacking mechanism enables the dual-band feature, while the Z-shaped slot is responsible for $\mathbf{C P}$ characteristics. In the lower frequency range, the antenna is configured for left-hand circular polarization (LHCP), and in the upper frequency range, right-hand circular polarization (RHCP). The orthogonal configuration of the antenna elements ensures an isolation exceeding 20 dB. The antenna features dual impedance bandwidths of $\mathbf{1 7. 9 6 \%}$ ($\mathbf{2 6. 2 0 - 3 1. 3 7} \mathbf{~ G H z)}$) and 21.15% (35.71-44.16 GHz), along with $3-\mathrm{dB}$ axial-ratio (AR) bandwidths of $\mathbf{3. 1 6 \%}$ and 0.5%. The antenna also exhibits peak gains of 8.2 dBi and 8.3 dBi in the lower and higher frequency spectrum, respectively.

articleTitle: Mitigating EMI due to Inductively Coupled Plasma Excitation in Rubidium Atomic Clocks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Rubidium (Rb) based atomic clocks are critical components in navigation satellite programs, forming the backbone of space-based navigation systems due to their exceptional precision and reliability. To maintain their optimal performance, the internal temperature of these clocks must be controlled within milli kelvin levels. However, electromagnetic interference (EMI) from inductively coupled plasma (ICP) circuits used to glow electrodeless lamps can disrupt the temperature sensors, leading to temperature fluctuations and performance degradation. This study investigates practical solutions to EMI mitigation that do not compromise the precision of temperature control. Through this, we aim to enhance the performance and reliability of rubidium-based atomic clocks in navigation satellite systems by ensuring precise thermal management despite the presence of ICP-induced electromagnetic radiation.

articleTitle: A Novel Frequency-Reconfigurable Antenna Employing Solid Dielectric Variation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: The paper proposes a frequency reconfigurable microstrip patch antenna with a novel passive tuning technique for mechanical tuning of its resonant frequency. It also intricately explores the operational mechanisms of the proposed antenna, highlighting its effective utilization of layered dielectric substrates for precise tuning of the resonant frequency. Through a meticulous analysis of capacitance, effective radiating length, and the strategic variation of dielectric materials, this study reveals the inherent capacity of reconfigurable antennas to seamlessly adapt to dynamic communication scenarios, ultimately augmenting wireless communication performance. Additionally, this paper derives and proposes an equation for calculating the resonant frequency based on the varying effective permittivity resulting from the variation of dielectric materials. These antennas play a crucial role in modern wireless systems due to their adaptability to various conditions. Their ability to dynamically control operational frequency range by leveraging the concept of layered dielectric substrates constitutes a compelling approach, culminating in tangible enhancements in communication efficiency and efficacy.

articleTitle: Design of a Compact 2-Bit PIN Diode Reflection Type Phase Shifter using Radial Stub
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: The goal of this research is to create an optimized hybrid coupler structure for a PIN diode reflection type phase shifter (RTPS) operating at microwave frequencies. To date, no phase shifter has been reported with the proposed technique, compactness, minimum phase error and balanced amplitude. Another limitation of designing such structures at such high frequency range, is that the $50 \Omega$ impedance lines’ width approaches its length for given substrate thickness, that is undesirable. This study introduces a new method of developing a module at $100 \Omega$ and translating it back to $50 \Omega$ at the input and output terminals. Moreover, the proposed design is highly resilient to manufacturing constraints owing to the addition of radial stubs instead of lumped components, as reflective loads. Its performance with respect to its bandwidth coverage is better with 15% bandwidth enhancement, insertion loss around 3 dB, and reflection co-efficient at all ports is better than $\mathbf{- 1 5 d B}$ over the whole operating bandwidth. The simulated and measured results validate the proposed design effectively.

articleTitle: Flat Gain Antenna with 3D Printed Metastructure for 5G Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this article, A Planar Dipole Antenna (PDA) is proposed with a flat gain of 11 dBi over the bandwidth of 4.6 GHz. The PDA antenna is operating from 22 GHz to 26.6 GHz. A 3D printable Poly Lactic Acid (PLA) material is used as 3D structure for gain enhancement by a little more than 5dBi and to tilt the main beam from end-fire to +21°. The dimensions of 3D Structure is 6×4×3 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> and height of substrate is 0.254 mm. The maximum gain achieved is 11.45 dBi and minimum gain is 11.07 dBi. The gain variance is reduced from 3 dB to 0.45 dB after incorporating 3D printed Metastructure to PDA. With the appropriate gain the proposed antenna is suitable for 5G communication with a compact profile of 30×33×3.254 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> only.

articleTitle: Analysis and Mitigation of Undesirable Harmonics in CMOS-based Integrated Frequency Doublers
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper comprehensively analyses the nonidealities associated with CMOS-based integrated Frequency Doublers (FD), which are essential components in high-frequency synthesis. While Phase-Locked Loops (PLLs) are commonly employed for frequency generation, frequency doublers are necessary when the application demands a much higher output frequency than a PLL can produce with a reasonable phase noise performance. For performing extensive characterization on the impact of input amplitude and phase mismatches on the output harmonic leakages, a frequency doubler working at $2.3-\mathrm{GHz}$ frequency was designed in a $180-\mathrm{nm}$ CMOS technology. The use of a CML buffer and switch-tunable capacitors with this doubler provides an excellent rejection of undesirable harmonics generated by amplitude and phase mismatches.

articleTitle: Mutual Coupling Reduction between the Closely Placed Patch Antennas
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this article, an inductive microstrip line and capacitive slot combination-based decoupling technique is presented. A very high, strong mutual coupling is reduced by varying the inductance and capacitance of the proposed microstrip line and capacitive slot, respectively. To provide detailed design instructions for implementing the decoupling method, a synthesis of an equivalent circuit is demonstrated. The decoupling method provides 13.5 dB isolation enhancement between the nearly placed antennas $\left(\right. {\mathrm {gap}} \left.=0.012 \lambda_{g}\right)$ without occupying extra space. Further, the extension of the claimed decoupling method is examined for the linear 1-D array. Thus, the suggested simple structure of compact dimensions possesses a high ability to reduce strong mutual coupling, which makes it a good candidate for MIMO and array applications.

articleTitle: A 27 dBm 5-18 GHz Multifunction Bidirectional amplifier using GaAs pHEMT process
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Design and realization of a 27 dBm broadband multifunction bidirectional amplifier (BDA) using GaAs pHEMT process in the frequency range $\mathrm{5 - 1 8} \mathrm{~ G H z}$ is presented in this article. The proposed design consists of combination of feedback and stacked non-uniform distributed power amplifier(SNDPA) in the transmit mode(Tx), a receive protection limiter, a 4 stage low noise amplifier and a digitally controlled attenuator in the receive mode $(\mathrm{R x})$ integrated in a single chip. It also features an on-chip power detector to sense the functioning of the power amplifier (PA). The transmit and receive path is isolated by a high power handling switch at the output end. The resulting BDA gives a small signal gain of $30 \pm 1$ dB and delivers a saturated output power of $27 \mathrm{dBm}(0.5 \mathrm{~W})$ in the Transmit mode. In the Receive mode, a small signal gain of 30 dB with maximum noise figure of 6 dB is achieved over the entire bandwidth. On-chip TTL drivers are integrated to ease the control of attenuator bits and switch direction. The current consumption in the transmit and receive modes are 500 mA and 135 mA respectively. The size of core chip is around $5.3 \times 3.4$ $\mathrm{m m}^{2}$.

articleTitle: A SIW Backed Compact Self-Quadruplexing Antenna for C-band and X-band Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A compact all-planar-fed substrate integrated waveguide backed (SIW) self-quadruplexing antenna (SQA) is configured for quad-band operation simultaneously. The key advantages of the SIW-oriented design are low loss, less design complexity, improved port isolations, and low-cost implementation. The antenna is fabricated on low loss RT/Duroid 5880 substrate and suitable for high-frequency applications. The model comprises an SIW cavity, a modified cross-shaped slot, and 4 planar ports placed across each other, two on each side. The hybrid slot is designed and placed so as to operate at 4 different frequencies in the C -band and X -band ranges $6.58 \mathrm{GHz}, 10.14 \mathrm{GHz}, 7.96 \mathrm{GHz}$, and 8.94 GHz by maintaining proper isolation (> 24 dB) among the ports. The layout supports independent frequency tuning using a single parameter. The antenna is prototyped and characterized for validation.

articleTitle: A 81.2-83.1 GHz Differential Pulsed Millimeter Wave Voltage-Controlled Oscillator on a 65 nm CMOS Process for Radar and Imaging Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: A differential pulsed millimeter wave (mm-wave) voltage-controlled oscillator (VCO) is proposed and designed on a 65 nm 1 -poly 10 -metal ($1 \mathrm{P10M}$) CMOS process for radar and imaging applications. The features of VCO and pulsed oscillators are integrated together. The losses offered by the on-chip inductor are compensated with a widely used NMOS cross-coupled pair by providing a sufficient amount of negative resistance-the feature of pulsed RF oscillations achieved by using a PMOS head switch. The controllability of the oscillation frequency is achieved by using tuning transistors. The tuning range of the proposed pulsed RF VCO is 1.9 GHz, from 81.2-83.1 GHz. The input pulse signal provides bias to the PMOS head switch when its amplitude is zero volts. The proposed pulsed RF VCO occupies an area of $\mathbf{1 7 5} \mathbf{u m} \times 130 \mathrm{um}$. The proposed design results in a phase of $\mathbf{- 8 7. 2 1 ~ d B c / H z}$ at $1 \mathbf{M H z}$ offset for the oscillation frequency of 83.1 GHz. The DC power consumption of the design varies from $8.6-11.6 \mathrm{~mW}$.

articleTitle: Design of Digitally Reconfigurable Bandwidth and Center Frequency Bandpass Filter
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents design and development of a digitally reconfigurable bandwidth and center frequency bandpass filter for variable data rate communication systems. Bandwidth and center frequency of bandpass filter are reconfigured using varactor diodes present in the lumped tubular filter topology. The proposed filter offers high selectivity with symmetrical pass band over the wide tuning range. Reconfigurable bandwidth and center frequency are achieved by varying the capacitances of series and shunt varactor diodes present in the circuit. Reverse bias voltage of varactor diodes is controlled by digital control circuit. Digital control circuit comprising of a controller and a multi-channel digital to analog converter which enables different combinations of bias voltages required to configure the bandwidth and center frequency of the filter. Fractional bandwidth can be configured from 4 to 20 percent of the center frequency by sending digital control word through serial port interface. Also, center frequency of the filter can be tuned from 140 MHz to 180 MHz. The measured performance of the filter shows good agreement with the simulation.

articleTitle: Contoured-Beam Transmitarray Antenna for Satellite Communication
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: In this paper, we have reported design and optimization of a new Offset-fed Transmit-array antenna for wide contoured beam for satellite communication. Offset geometry of Transmit-array facilitates single supporting structure for both feed and planer antenna for accommodation at spacecraft, causing minimized scattering. The Transmitarray antenna has been analyzed using periodic-method of moment (pMoM) of software Ticra Tool 24.0. Smooth-walled RHCP-polarized horn is used to illuminate the transmit-array. Beam has been shaped for wide coverage area using ‘minimax’ optimization algorithm for specified EoC (Edge of Coverage) Gain and XPI (cross-polar isolation). Twin-layer unit cell of double square loop Unit Cell has been taken for transmit-array antenna. Horn and transmit-array combination along-with another shaped main reflector can optimized to get tailored RF performance.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of a Modified Compass-Cross-Slot Frequency Selective Surface (FSS)
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents a design and analysis of a modified compass-cross slot etched on a low-profile single-cladded FR4 substrate. The proposed Frequency Selective Surface is designed to function as a bandstop filter in the X band and a bandpass filter in the Ku-band. The designed FSS achieves transmission zeros at 8.2-12.2 GHz and transmission poles at $13.6-18.8 \mathrm{GHz}$. The unit cell dimension of the FSS is $0.2 \lambda_{0} \times 0.2 \lambda_{0}$, providing 50° angular stability and 90° polarization insensitivity performance for both TE and TM modes. Theoretical analysis is validated through Equivalent Circuit Modelling (ECM) and simulations using Ansys HFSS software. Thus, the X -band is shielded, and the Ku-band is passed through, improving satellite communication performance.

articleTitle: High Gain Beam Steering 3D printed Digital Metasurface Lens Antenna for W-Band 6G Terahertz Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents a novel digital metasurface lens antenna designed to achieve a high gain and dynamic beam-steering for 6 G communication systems operating in the W-band ($75-110 \mathrm{GHz}$). Utilizing the capabilities of additive manufacturing, a complex metasurface structure is created featuring intricately designed 3-bit quantized unit cells to precisely manipulate phase shifts. Each unit cell incorporates air voids at the top and bottom to function as anti-reflection structures, while the middle section comprises a dielectric grating with variable heights, achieving a phase gradient of 45°. The material used for unit cell is ABS with a dielectric constant of 3.6 and a loss tangent of 0.015 at 110 GHz. The proposed metasurface lens has an overall dimensions of $28 \mathrm{~mm} \times 28 \mathrm{~mm} \times 5 \mathbf{~ m m}$. It is excited using a WR-10 waveguide feed with cross-sectional dimensions graded metasurface lens antenna achieves a maximum gain of 24.6 dBi and a beam-steering capability of 51° at 110 GHz. These results demonstrate the potential of 3D-printed metasurfaces for high-performance 6 G applications.

articleTitle: Dispersion Relation of a Cylindrical Dielectric Coated Conductor
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Theoretical investigation of an infinitely long Goubau line or Cylindrical Dielectric Coated Conductor (CDCC) is presented here. Literature survey shows that the CDCC has been investigated for fundamental transverse magnetic (TM) and transverse electric (TE) mode only. In this work, the contributions of TE and $T M$ modes are utilized to find the solution of different $H E M$ modes. Theoretical results are verified with earlier published work. Modal charts are given here for $\varepsilon_{r}=20$ and 38.

articleTitle: A Novel LTCC Based Temperature Compensated Transmit Receive Module for Space borne Earth Observation Microwave Sensor
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents the design, main features and measured performance of a C-Band Miniaturized Transmit Receive integrated Module. The novel approach utilized for compensation of RF performance over a wide temperature range and integration of dual polarization capability with integrated controller module’s main features along with low noise reception, 10 W transmit power and gain and phase control with high accuracy. Each TRiM consists of two T/R Modules and a TR controller housed in a single package for miniaturization. The TR Modules have been realized using Low Temperature Co-fired Ceramic based packaging for miniaturization and are hermetically sealed for high reliability. The TRiM has been successfully qualified, and more than 288 such TRiMs have been developed and used for the realization of active phased array antenna of RISAT-1A/EOS-04 synthetic aperture radar (SAR) payload having multi-mode imaging capability along with single/dual/hybrid/full polarization capability. RISAT-1A/EOS-04 was launched on February 14, 2022, and RISAT-1B, a repeat mission of RISAT-1A, is currently under realization.

articleTitle: Analysis of Analog Radio-Over-Fiber Link for 5G NR Fronthauling in N258 Frequency Band
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: We present the design and performance analysis of an analog radio over fiber (ARoF) link in the N 258 frequency band of 5G new radio (NR) based on numerical simulations. The link is designed to operate in the frequency range of 24.25 GHz to 27.5 GHz with a gain of $0 \mathrm{~dB} \pm 1 \mathrm{~dB}$. The simulation model includes the impact of the various sources of noise and nonlinearity in the link that affect the link performance in terms of noise figure, saturation, spurious-free dynamic range (SFDR) etc. The designed link exhibits an SFDR of $\gt95 \mathrm{~dB} / \mathrm{Hz}^{2 / 3}$ with an input 1 dB saturation power (P 1 dB) of $\mathrm{- 3. 6} \mathrm{dB}$ and a noise figure of 34 dB. The simulation model is capable of scaling to higher or lower frequencies of operation and is also extendable to multichannel DWDM ARoF links.

articleTitle: X/Ka Dual band Dual Circularly Polarized Reflector Antenna System for Deep Space Satellite TT&C and Data Transmission Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Design of dual band (X/Ka) dual circularly polarized Reflector antenna system with common phase center for deep space satellite TT&C and data Transmission applications is presented. The antenna consists of a 2 meter Axially Displaced Ellipsoidal (ADE) Reflector with a coaxially fed horn antenna as feed. This antenna is planned for Telemetry, Tracking and Telecommand (TT&C) as well as payload Data transmission application from deep space orbiting spacecraft to ground communication. The performance of simultaneous excitation of X and Ka band antenna feed assembly with ADE reflector is simulated and results show that a very good performance can be achieved in both the bands.

articleTitle: Federated Learning and LiDAR Data-Assisted Ground Station Selection for Autonomous Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This study uses deep learning to improve transmitter selection for autonomous vehicles. We use a federated learning algorithm to reduce the communication overhead by broadcasting the transmitter’s position to all nodes. The simulation results show that the proposed algorithm performs significantly better, with an accuracy of 1.7 times better than the global positioning system (GPS)-based selection. Moreover, federated learning-based selection reduces the overall data size by 96.38%, significantly reducing communication overhead. This study further tests the generality of the proposed model using techniques like transfer learning, which successfully handled variations in the number of samples for training, the city used for simulation, and the number of base stations.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Analysis and Frequency Response of Plasma Medium for High Power Microwaves
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Plasma is a dispersive medium that has shown peculiar properties when exposed to electromagnetic energy, especially for high-power microwaves. The main design parameters of plasma include gas type, gas pressure, and electron mobility. In specific enclosed conditions, the gas type and pressure remain fixed. At the same time, electron density can be controlled with an external power supply. In this paper, the properties of plasma parameters are studied and investigated at different power levels of electromagnetic energy. The frequency response and electromagnetic behaviours of plasma are analysed using a circuit model and verified by full-wave simulations. Finally, the performance of the plasma structure is verified experimentally.

articleTitle: Cylindrical DRA Array MIMO System with High Isolation for mm-Wave Band 5G Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents a Dielectric resonator antenna (DRA) array multi-input-multi-output (MIMO) system with high inter-element isolation characteristics for millimeter wave (mm-Wave) band applications. The DRA consists of an orthogonally placed interconnected dielectric resonator array excited by an aperture-coupled microstrip feed line. This arrangement provides a standard inter-element isolation by depressing the out-of-phase current distribution. Further, the inter-element isolation is enhanced by inserting the metallic via in the dielectric arm of interconnected DRA. The metallic via confined the field distribution around it, eliminating field coupling. In turn, the isolation is improved significantly $(\gt20 \mathrm{~dB}$ at 27.5 GHz and $\gt15 \mathrm{~dB}$ in the desired band) without compromising the radiation performance of the antenna. The measured 10 dB fractional impedance bandwidth is $13.8 \%(27-31 \mathrm{GHz})$, and isolation is more than 20 dB. The realized peak gain is 6.7 dBi at 27.5 GHz, and the overall gain is $\gt5.3 \mathrm{dBi}$ in the desired band. The antenna is designed, fabricated, and measured at mm-Wave band (26-31 GHz) to demonstrate the idea. Moreover, the MIMO performance parameters are estimated to validate the applicability of the proposed MIMO system for mm-Wave band 5G application.

articleTitle: Innovative Methodology for Developing Frequency Selective Surfaces on Arbitrary Curved Surfaces
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This article presents a novel technique for designing frequency selective surfaces (FSS) on arbitrary surfaces based on the computer-aided design (CAD) model. Utilizing the ray triangle intersection algorithm and the Riemann sum technique ensures uniform unit cell placement by computing equidistant points across complex surfaces. This innovative approach has a profound advantage in the design of conformal FSS, eliminating the need for surface equations and time-consuming parametric variation. For demonstration, a unit cell is designed with a bandstop filter response at 10 GHz in the X -band along with an insertion loss of 20 dB, and its performance is checked under normal and oblique incidence. Then an arbitrary surface is developed, and its CAD model is determined. Subsequently, the unit cell is uniformly placed on the surface using the proposed technique. The efficacy of the technique is validated through simulation using a finite element boundary integral (FEBI) setup, followed by the prototype fabrication using a 3-D printer and the electromagnetic (EM) response measurement of the designed FSS.

articleTitle: Co-existence Filter Analysis of FSS-ES and 5G Base Stations
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents a method for deriving the co-existence filter requirements of a 5G base station and a fixed satellite service earth station. A comparison of the co-existence filter rejection levels for classes of base stations operating in FR-1 and FR-2 ranges is also presented. A detailed analysis of the impact of the separation distance on natural co-existence and the effect of additional filtering is demonstrated. Finally, the minimum rejection required for different classes of base stations to co-exist with the corresponding FSS for distances under two km is presented.

articleTitle: A High Performance 5-6 GHz GaAs MMIC Beamforming Core Chip for Active Phased Arrays
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Design and development of a beamforming MMIC core chip, in 5-6 GHz frequency band for active phased array application along with measured performance is presented in this paper. Multiple Transmit/Receive Module (TRM) functions including digital phase shifter, digital attenuator, TR switches, low noise amplifier, medium power amplifier, linear gain amplifiers and LVTTL driver are integrated onto a single MMIC. The core chip is realized using a $0.5 \mu \mathrm{~m}$ GaAs pHEMT process technology in chip area of $22.5 \mathrm{~mm}^{2}$ making it a compact and cost-effective option. The measured performance achieves a gain of 25dB (min.) in both Transmit (Tx-) & Receive (Rx-) mode with 21 dBm output power and 5 dB (max.) noise figure. The chip features 6-bit phase control for range of 360° with resolution of 5.625° and 6 -bit amplitude control for range of 31.5 dB with resolution of 0.5 dB respectively making it a high-performance beam forming core chip for active phased arrays. The chip is operated at power supply voltages of $\pm 5 \mathrm{~V}$ and consumes +ve supply currents of 250 mA in Tx mode and 200 mA in $R x$ mode with 25 mA of -ve supply current.

articleTitle: Design and analysis of compact antenna for 5G bands for V2X wireless telemetry and IoT multiband applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: Modern communication demands antennas with multi-band, high gain, and compact size for enhanced performance across the mid 5 G and sub 6 GHz frequency spectrum. This study presents a compact antenna comprising three steps achieved by strategically rectangular slots of varying positions to enhance current density strategically, alongside additional modifications. The antenna is designed on a FR4 substrate measuring 24 mm by 28 mm, with a height of 1.6 mm and a patch size of 20 mm by 24 mm. Notably, the antenna exhibits multi-band features concerning notches around 3.38 and 4.54 GHz, with minimum reflection coefficient of -26.3 dB, respectively, achieving a high peak gain of 5 dBi. It effectively covers 5 G applications within the $3-3.6 \mathrm{GHz}$ range, functioning as a multi-band antenna with a wide bandwidth spanning 3-3.6 GHz and $4.4-4.8 \mathrm{GHz}$, respectively. Moreover, it covers 5G mid and sub $6 \mathrm{G H z}$ bands, including V2X wireless telemetry, IoT multi-band applications, and ground-based navigation frequencies. The antenna’s performance was successfully verified through implementation using IE3d simulation software and experimentally validated through the vector network analyzer in presence of absorber, respectively.

articleTitle: An Innovative Approach for Microwave Circuit Design and Analysis Using Fully Symmetrical Planar Smith Chart
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper discusses the graphical procedures for designing and analyzing any active and/or passive microwave circuit using a fully symmetrical planar Smith Chart based on Mercator projection. To illustrate it with the examples, an equivalent circuit of tunnel diode having a negative resistance is considered. The second example elaborates on the design of an L-section impedance matching circuit. These graphical procedures can be used to design and analyze, hence, to calculate the equivalent impedance and/or admittance of any microwave active/passive circuit consisting of lumped and/or distributed elements.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic and Particle-in-Cell (PIC) Simulation of L-Band Tunable Pulsed Magnetron
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper presents the electromagnetic, and particle-in-cell (PIC) simulation of a 300 kW, L-Band tunable pulsed magnetron using 3D PIC code CST microwave studio. The operating frequency of the magnetron can be tuned from 818-892 MHz with the help of tuning plunger axially inserted between the annular shaped straps. The resonant structure of this magnetron is a hole and slot type of structure having eight numbers of holes and slots and double ring strapping on both sides of anode block. During the stable operation of magnetron four numbers of space charge spokes are formed which confirms $\boldsymbol{\pi}$-mode of operation in a magnetron with eight numbers of hole and slot cavities. A single peak in frequency spectrum at 868.93 MHz is observed when the tuner cup is in plane with the tuner end anode surface. The tunability of the magnetron has been verified by inserting tuner ring back and forth inside the straps.

articleTitle: 1D-FDTD Formulation with NARX Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Microwaves, Antennas, and Propagation Conference (MAPCON)
abstract: This paper hybridizes the 1D-FDTD formulation of Maxwell’s equation with the NARX (nonlinear autoregressive network with exogenous inputs) recurrent neural network. An object in FDTD is divided into a large number of cells. FDTD characterizes an electromagnetic interaction by updating fields at each node in an iterative manner using Maxwell’s equations. This iterative process leads to large simulation time and storage. The proposed method reduces the storage requirement and, hence, the pressure on computing resources and time by treating the fields as time series. This method updates the field values for a few iterations using FDTD. Then, the NARX networks, trained through these fields, predict the remaining iterations autonomously.
